\chapter*{About this edition}
This book compiles every tracked Markdown document under \path{docs/design/}, including the nested byte-packed Surface record and the design-directory index. It preserves design history rather than presenting every proposal as shipped behavior. GitHub issues and milestones own current roadmap and release scope.

The eight Mermaid source diagrams are redrawn as native TikZ. The component atlas contains vector SVG projections generated from actual DOGFOOD \texttt{Surface} cells at a fixed time, viewport and shipped theme. Source hashes, figure provenance and the complete chapter inventory accompany this edition.

The book palette derives from \texttt{\#F7685F}. Dark coral headings and links contrast at 8.60:1 against white; charcoal body text contrasts at 14.69:1. The anchor coral is used as a field and graphic accent, with dark text at 4.97:1. Component colours retain the actual application theme.

Jacquard 24 and IBM Plex Mono are distributed by \href{https://fonts.google.com}{Google Fonts}. Their SIL Open Font Licenses are included with the font files. DejaVu Sans supplies missing technical symbols. Workstation paths are normalized to portable workspace labels, and selected emoji markers receive plain-language labels. Historical repository links resolve to the archived base revision where applicable.

\chapter{DF-001 --- Show DOGFOOD Coverage Progress}\label{record-001}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-001-show-dogfood-coverage-progress.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF --- DOGFOOD Field Guide}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-001-why-this-cycle-exists}

We want to release Bijou without pretending DOGFOOD is already a complete reference.

The honest answer is not to block release forever. It is to make DOGFOOD visibly truthful about its current documentation coverage.

This cycle exists to put that truth directly into the initial docs experience:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a progress indicator
\item
  an explicit ratio
\item
  a defensible denominator tied to the canonical component-family reference
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope of this cycle}\label{record-001-scope-of-this-cycle}

This cycle intentionally covers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a canonical DOGFOOD coverage metric based on documented component families
\item
  mapping current DOGFOOD stories onto that coverage model
\item
  a docs-pane progress bar and ratio
\item
  tests that prove the landing surface reflects real coverage instead of a hand-wavy claim
\end{itemize}

It does \textbf{not} include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  expanding story coverage itself
\item
  claiming feature completeness
\item
  a broader release-management dashboard
\item
  automatic release gating
\end{itemize}

\section{Human users}\label{record-001-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-001-primary-human-user}

A user opening DOGFOOD to decide how complete and trustworthy the field guide currently is.

They need:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a clear signal that DOGFOOD is still in progress
\item
  an honest coverage ratio
\item
  enough context to understand that the metric is about documented component families
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-001-human-hill}

A user can open DOGFOOD and immediately see that it is a living field guide with explicit progress, not a silently incomplete reference pretending to be finished.

\section{Agent users}\label{record-001-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-001-primary-agent-user}

An agent maintaining DOGFOOD story coverage over time.

It needs:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a stable coverage model
\item
  a defensible denominator
\item
  a way to add stories later and have the landing progress move automatically
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-001-agent-hill}

An agent can add or remove DOGFOOD story coverage and see the docs-pane progress update from real source data rather than manual copy edits.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-001-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A user launches DOGFOOD.
\item
  The landing screen shows the normal hero treatment.
\item
  The initial docs content pane shows a progress bar and ratio for current DOGFOOD documentation coverage.
\item
  The user understands that DOGFOOD is in progress and can see how much of the canonical family map is currently covered.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Agent playback}\label{record-001-agent-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent opens the DF-001 cycle doc.
\item
  It sees that the denominator is the canonical component-family reference, not a vague export count.
\item
  It runs the cycle and app tests.
\item
  It can verify that the docs-pane copy and progress bar are driven from real story coverage data.
\item
  It can point to the next backlog item for actually expanding coverage.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Linked invariants}\label{record-001-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are the Spec}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/visible-controls-are-a-promise.md}{Visible Controls Are a Promise}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/docs-are-the-demo.md}{Docs Are the Demo}
\end{itemize}

\section{Invariants for this cycle}\label{record-001-invariants-for-this-cycle}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD must not imply fuller coverage than it actually has
\item
  the coverage denominator must be explicit and stable
\item
  adding story coverage later should update the progress metric automatically
\item
  the title screen must not present documentation coverage as though it were a loading state
\item
  the docs-pane coverage UI must remain secondary to the primary onboarding content
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation outline}\label{record-001-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Create a DOGFOOD legend and coverage-focused cycle doc.
\item
  Define the canonical coverage denominator from the design-system component-family reference.
\item
  Map current DOGFOOD stories onto that family coverage model.
\item
  Write failing cycle and app tests for the new landing progress treatment.
\item
  Render a progress bar and ratio in the initial docs content pane.
\item
  Close the cycle and spawn the next DOGFOOD coverage backlog item.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests to write first}\label{record-001-tests-to-write-first}

Under \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the active cycle doc includes the required workflow sections
\item
  DOGFOOD coverage resolves from canonical family reference data
\item
  the initial docs content surface shows the coverage ratio and percent
\item
  the next DOGFOOD backlog item exists
\end{itemize}

\section{Risks}\label{record-001-risks}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  choosing a denominator that feels arbitrary or magical
\item
  making the title screen feel like a loading screen when it is actually a title screen
\item
  hardcoding a number that will drift the moment a new story lands
\end{itemize}

\section{Out of scope}\label{record-001-out-of-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  story authoring for additional families
\item
  docs completeness gating in CI
\item
  release automation
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-001-retrospective}

\subsection{What landed}\label{record-001-what-landed}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a new DOGFOOD legend
\item
  a real coverage model based on canonical component families
\item
  story-to-family coverage mapping
\item
  a docs-pane progress bar and ratio that update from the current story set
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Drift from ideal}\label{record-001-drift-from-ideal}

This cycle does not improve DOGFOOD coverage itself.

That is intentional. The goal here is honesty first, not pretending that a progress indicator is the same thing as documentation work.

\subsection{Debt spawned}\label{record-001-debt-spawned}

Spawned:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/method/graveyard/legacy-backlog/DF-002-expand-dogfood-component-family-coverage.md}{DF-002 --- Expand DOGFOOD Component Family Coverage}
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DF-003 --- Enforce DOGFOOD Coverage Floor}\label{record-002}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-003-enforce-dogfood-coverage-floor.md}\par}\smallskip

\emph{Cycle for turning DOGFOOD coverage honesty into a CI-enforced release gate instead of a passive progress display}

Legend:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF --- DOGFOOD Field Guide}
\end{itemize}

Depends on:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-001-show-dogfood-coverage-progress.md}{DF-001 --- Show DOGFOOD Coverage Progress}
\end{itemize}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-002-why-this-cycle-exists}

DF-001 made DOGFOOD honest about how incomplete it currently is.

That honesty should not remain a purely visual promise. The repo should also enforce a minimum documentation floor so DOGFOOD cannot quietly regress or ship while pretending its progress bar means something.

This cycle exists to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  make the minimum acceptable DOGFOOD coverage explicit
\item
  enforce that minimum in CI and release-readiness flows
\item
  document the ratchet policy for future DF cycles
\end{itemize}

\section{Human users / jobs / hills}\label{record-002-human-users-jobs-hills}

\subsection{Primary human users}\label{record-002-primary-human-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  maintainers shipping Bijou releases
\item
  contributors expanding or touching DOGFOOD docs coverage
\item
  reviewers deciding whether a cycle improved or regressed documentation completeness
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human jobs}\label{record-002-human-jobs}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Ship Bijou without accidentally letting DOGFOOD coverage slip below the current honest bar.
\item
  See the current floor and next expected target without reverse-engineering old commits.
\item
  Treat docs completeness as a real quality gate, not a vague aspiration.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-002-human-hill}

DOGFOOD coverage progress is not just displayed in the app; it is enforced in the repo and raised deliberately over time.

\section{Agent users / jobs / hills}\label{record-002-agent-users-jobs-hills}

\subsection{Primary agent users}\label{record-002-primary-agent-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  agents expanding DOGFOOD stories
\item
  agents preparing release candidates
\item
  agents auditing whether documentation completeness is meeting the current floor
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent jobs}\label{record-002-agent-jobs}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Compute the current DOGFOOD family-coverage ratio from source data.
\item
  Compare that ratio against an explicit floor.
\item
  Fail deterministically when the floor is not met.
\item
  Surface the next required target so future cycles know the next ratchet point.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-002-agent-hill}

An agent can determine from source-controlled policy whether the current DOGFOOD story set is acceptable for CI and release without heuristics or manual judgment.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-002-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer opens the repo after a coverage-expansion cycle.
\item
  The DOGFOOD coverage floor is explicit in source control.
\item
  CI checks the current real story coverage against that floor.
\item
  If coverage drops below the floor, CI fails before merge or release.
\item
  The maintainer can also see the next target to raise by in the next dedicated DOGFOOD coverage cycle.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Agent playback}\label{record-002-agent-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent computes DOGFOOD coverage from \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} and the canonical component-family reference.
\item
  The agent reads the explicit floor and next target from the shared policy module.
\item
  The agent runs the coverage gate script.
\item
  If coverage is below the floor, the script fails with the measured percent, floor, and next target.
\item
  If coverage meets the floor, CI proceeds and the next ratchet remains visible for future cycles.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Linked invariants}\label{record-002-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are the Spec}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/docs-are-the-demo.md}{Docs Are the Demo}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/visible-controls-are-a-promise.md}{Visible Controls Are a Promise}
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation outline}\label{record-002-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a shared DOGFOOD coverage-policy module with:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    explicit floor percent
  \item
    explicit +5-point ratchet increment
  \item
    explicit next target
  \item
    helpers for evaluating/asserting the floor
  \end{itemize}
\item
  Add a \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e} script that computes real coverage and fails when the floor is not met.
\item
  Add focused tests for the policy and gate behavior.
\item
  Wire the gate into CI and release-readiness flows.
\item
  Update DF legend/changelog and spawn the next backlog item for actually raising the floor.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests to write first}\label{record-002-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  cycle doc regression for DF-003 and its follow-on backlog item
\item
  policy/gate tests proving:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    current coverage meets the current floor
  \item
    the next target is exactly floor + 5
  \item
    the gate fails when the floor is set above current coverage
  \end{itemize}
\item
  release-readiness regression proving the new gate runs as part of the plan
\end{itemize}

\section{Risks / unknowns}\label{record-002-risks-unknowns}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  CI can enforce the current floor, but it cannot infer from git history whether maintainers actually raised the floor every time they should have
\item
  the initial floor needs to be set to the current honest value, not an aspirational one that would immediately fail the repo
\item
  the meaningful follow-on is expanding DOGFOOD coverage itself, not only adding more policy
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-002-retrospective}

What landed:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  explicit DOGFOOD coverage floor policy in source control
\item
  a reusable coverage gate script
\item
  CI/release hooks enforcing the current floor
\item
  an explicit next target to make the next +5-point ratchet visible
\end{itemize}

What did not land:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  actual new DOGFOOD component-family stories
\item
  automatic historical enforcement of ``every cycle raised by 5'' beyond the explicit next-target ratchet
\end{itemize}

Follow-on:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/method/graveyard/legacy-backlog/DF-004-raise-dogfood-coverage-floor-to-next-target.md}{DF-004 --- Raise DOGFOOD Coverage Floor to the Next 5-Point Target}
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DF-004 --- Raise DOGFOOD Coverage Floor to the Next 5-Point Target}\label{record-003}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-004-raise-dogfood-coverage-floor-to-next-target.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF --- DOGFOOD Field Guide}
\end{itemize}

Depends on:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-003-enforce-dogfood-coverage-floor.md}{DF-003 --- Enforce DOGFOOD Coverage Floor}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/method/graveyard/legacy-backlog/DF-002-expand-dogfood-component-family-coverage.md}{DF-002 --- Expand DOGFOOD Component Family Coverage}
\end{itemize}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-003-why-this-cycle-exists}

DF-003 made the current DOGFOOD coverage floor executable.

That was necessary, but it still left the honest next step untouched:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD only documents 3 of 35 component families
\item
  the enforced floor is 9\%
\item
  the next declared target is 14\%
\end{itemize}

This cycle exists to earn that next target honestly by documenting enough additional component families that the floor can be raised without gaming the metric.

\section{Scope of this cycle}\label{record-003-scope-of-this-cycle}

This cycle intentionally covers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  adding enough real DOGFOOD component stories to move coverage from 3 to 5 families
\item
  raising the enforced floor from 9\% to 14\%
\item
  raising the next declared target from 14\% to 19\%
\item
  proving the result through cycle tests and the existing gate script
\end{itemize}

It does \textbf{not} include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  pretending every component now has full docs coverage
\item
  changing the canonical family denominator
\item
  inventing placeholder stories with no real use/avoid/lowering guidance
\item
  broad DOGFOOD shell or navigation redesign
\end{itemize}

\section{Human users}\label{record-003-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-003-primary-human-user}

A builder evaluating whether DOGFOOD is becoming meaningfully more complete over time.

They need:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the progress bar and ratio to move for a real reason
\item
  newly documented families to be legitimate, not filler
\item
  the CI gate to reflect actual content growth
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-003-human-hill}

A user can see that DOGFOOD is more complete than before, and the reported progress corresponds to real newly documented families they can browse.

\section{Agent users}\label{record-003-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-003-primary-agent-user}

An agent tasked with growing DOGFOOD coverage while preserving honesty.

It needs:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  an explicit target to hit
\item
  a clear smallest honest route to that target
\item
  tests that prove the new stories count toward canonical family coverage
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-003-agent-hill}

An agent can raise the DOGFOOD floor to the next target only by adding real story coverage that the gate and docs app both recognize.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-003-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A user enters DOGFOOD.
\item
  The docs pane reports a higher coverage percentage than before.
\item
  The higher value corresponds to newly browseable component stories instead of a policy-only change.
\item
  The user can open those new stories and see real usage guidance, variants, and lowering notes.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Agent playback}\label{record-003-agent-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent opens the DF-004 cycle doc.
\item

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-006-why-this-cycle-exists}

This cycle exists to earn that next target through real feedback-history coverage: one low-level transient overlay family and one activity-stream family.

\item

\item
  raising the enforced floor from 24\% to 29\%
\item
  raising the next declared target from 29\% to 34\%

\item
  changing the canonical component-family denominator

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-008-why-this-cycle-exists}

DF-008 made DOGFOOD feel more like a field guide by documenting bounded prose and explicit linked destinations.

The next promised step is now explicit:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD currently documents 13 of 35 component families
\item
  the enforced floor is 34\%
\item
  the next declared target is 39\%
\end{itemize}

This cycle exists to earn that next target through two core form families that make DOGFOOD more credible as a guide to real decisions and set-building flows: \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.

\section{Scope of this cycle}\label{record-008-scope-of-this-cycle}

This cycle intentionally covers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  adding enough real DOGFOOD component stories to move coverage from 13 to 15 families
\item
  documenting \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as the binary-decision family
\item
  documenting \texttt{m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as the multiple-choice family
\item
  raising the enforced floor from 34\% to 39\%
\item
  raising the next declared target from 39\% to 44\%
\end{itemize}

It does \textbf{not} include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  full form-group or wizard coverage
\item
  replacing the docs app with live interactive form execution
\item
  changing the canonical denominator
\item
  pretending DOGFOOD now covers the whole form system
\end{itemize}

\item
  one story that shows \texttt{m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as a real set-building flow with keyboard toggling and fallback semantics
\item
  coverage progress that rises only because those families are genuinely present
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-008-human-hill}

A user can open DOGFOOD, learn when to use \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, and see the coverage number rise because the field guide now actually covers those decision/input families.

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-010-why-this-cycle-exists}

DF-010 made DOGFOOD more credible around one-choice prompts and peer navigation.

The next promised step is now explicit:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD currently documents 17 of 35 component families
\item
  the enforced floor is 44\%
\item
  the next declared target is 49\%
\end{itemize}

This cycle exists to earn that next target through two deeper form families that move DOGFOOD closer to real application-building guidance instead of stopping at one-off prompts:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} / \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for \textbf{Text entry}
\item
  \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} / \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for \textbf{Multi-field and staged forms}
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope of this cycle}\label{record-010-scope-of-this-cycle}

This cycle intentionally covers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  adding enough real DOGFOOD component stories to move coverage from 17 to 19 families
\item
  documenting \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} / \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as the \textbf{Text entry} family
\item
  documenting \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} / \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as the \textbf{Multi-field and staged forms} family
\item
  raising the enforced floor from 44\% to 49\%
\item
  raising the next declared target from 49\% to 54\%
\end{itemize}

It does \textbf{not} include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  live embedded text-entry execution inside DOGFOOD
\item
  every remaining form-adjacent family like breadcrumbs, steppers, or progress trackers
\item
  changing the canonical denominator
\item
  pretending DOGFOOD now covers the whole input stack
\end{itemize}

\section{Human users}\label{record-010-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-010-primary-human-user}

A builder evaluating whether DOGFOOD can now teach richer data-entry flows instead of stopping at choice prompts and passive documentation surfaces.

They need:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  one story that shows \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as honest short-form versus multiline text-entry work
\item
  one story that shows \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as related-input flows with grouping or step progression
\item
  coverage progress that rises only because those deeper form families are genuinely present
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-010-human-hill}

A user can open DOGFOOD, learn when to use \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} / \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} / \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, and trust the higher coverage number because those families are actually represented in the field guide.

\subsection{Drift from ideal}\label{record-010-drift-from-ideal}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-011-why-this-cycle-exists}

DF-011 made DOGFOOD more credible around text entry plus grouped and staged form flows.

The next promised step is now explicit:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD currently documents 19 of 35 component families
\item
  the enforced floor is 49\%
\item
  the next declared target is 54\%
\end{itemize}

This cycle exists to earn that next target through two calmer structural teaching surfaces that make the field guide feel broader and more production-like instead of only deeper on forms:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for \textbf{Explainability walkthroughs}
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} / \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for \textbf{Dividers}
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope of this cycle}\label{record-011-scope-of-this-cycle}

This cycle intentionally covers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  adding enough real DOGFOOD component stories to move coverage from 19 to 21 families
\item
  documenting \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as the \textbf{Explainability walkthroughs} family
\item
  documenting \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} / \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as the \textbf{Dividers} family
\item
  raising the enforced floor from 49\% to 54\%
\item
  raising the next declared target from 54\% to 59\%
\end{itemize}

It does \textbf{not} include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a full AI-docs or assistant workflow inside DOGFOOD
\item
  every remaining structure/navigation family like breadcrumbs, timelines, or disclosure stacks
\item
  changing the canonical denominator
\item
  pretending DOGFOOD now covers the full shell and block language
\end{itemize}

    coverage of \texttt{K\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} and \texttt{N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m}
  \item
    an enforced floor of 59 with a next target of 64
  \item
    real help and notification-system stories in DOGFOOD
  \end{itemize}
\item

\subsection{What landed}\label{record-012-what-landed}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a new real help story teaching \texttt{h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} under the \texttt{K\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} family
\item
  a new real notification-system story teaching stacked live notifications and archived notification history through the actual TUI notification APIs
\item
  canonical family coverage increased from \texttt{2\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}5} to \texttt{2\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}5}
\item
  DOGFOOD docs coverage now resolves to \texttt{6\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}\%}, which safely clears the \texttt{5\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}\%} floor
\item
  the enforced floor moved from \texttt{5\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}\%} to \texttt{5\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}\%}
\item

\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} / \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} / \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for \textbf{App shell}
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} / \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for \textbf{Workspace layout}
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope of this cycle}\label{record-013-scope-of-this-cycle}

This cycle intentionally covers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  adding the app-shell family to DOGFOOD
\item
  adding the workspace-layout family to DOGFOOD
\item
  moving the field guide from \texttt{2\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}5} families to at least \texttt{2\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}5}

\chapter{DF-021 --- Shape DOGFOOD As Terminal Docs System}\label{record-019}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF --- DOGFOOD Field Guide}

\section{Sponsor human}\label{record-019-sponsor-human}

A builder or maintainer who expects DOGFOOD to behave like Bijou's terminal-native documentation site, not only a component-story browser.

\section{Sponsor agent}\label{record-019-sponsor-agent}

An agent that must answer, from repo artifacts alone:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  what DOGFOOD is supposed to document
\item
  which parts of the repo must be reachable inside DOGFOOD before \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} ships
\item
  which missing docs surfaces are now release blockers
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-019-hill}

DOGFOOD is shaped as a terminal documentation system for Bijou, with the current component-library explorer treated as one important section inside a broader docs site rather than the whole product.

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-019-why-this-cycle-exists}

DOGFOOD has crossed an important threshold:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  all \texttt{3\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}5} canonical component families are now represented
\item
  the shell and landing surfaces are strong enough to feel like a real product
\item
  the docs app is already the proving surface for Bijou's shell, design-language, and component work
\end{itemize}

But the scope is still too narrow for what the repo now claims DOGFOOD to be.

Today, DOGFOOD is still mostly a \textbf{components docs view}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  it has a landing screen
\item
  it has a component-family explorer
\item
  it can show component story docs and variants
\item
  it does \textbf{not} yet act like a terminal-native documentation site for the repo as a whole
\end{itemize}

That gap is now release-shaping:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  there is no real viewer for prose docs from \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}
\item
  there is no DOGFOOD section for repo/package documentation
\item
  there is no DOGFOOD section for Bijou's philosophy, architecture, and doctrine docs
\item
  the current shell structure still assumes ``components'' is the whole docs product
\end{itemize}

If \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} ships while DOGFOOD remains component-only, Bijou will still have a strong component field guide, but it will not yet have the terminal docs surface that the repo increasingly implies exists.

\section{Human users}\label{record-019-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-019-primary-human-user}

A builder evaluating Bijou as a framework, not just as a pile of widgets.

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-019-human-hill}

A user can open DOGFOOD and browse:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  what Bijou is
\item
  how it is organized
\item
  what each package is for
\item
  how the component library works
\item
  what philosophical and architectural ideas shape the repo
\end{itemize}

without leaving the terminal to read the main docs corpus.

\section{Agent users}\label{record-019-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-019-primary-agent-user}

An agent tasked with extending DOGFOOD, importing docs, or explaining Bijou's public surface to users.

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-019-agent-hill}

An agent can recover the expected DOGFOOD information architecture from repo docs and can see exactly which missing docs surfaces block \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}.

\section{Playback questions}\label{record-019-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  If a user asks ``where do I read real Bijou docs in the terminal?'', does DOGFOOD have a clear answer beyond component stories?
\item
  Can a user browse both the component library and the non-component docs corpus without the app pretending they are the same thing?
\item
  Can a user find package-level explanations for \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u}, \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i}, the i18n packages, and the app template?
\item
  Can a user read Bijou's philosophy, architecture, and doctrine docs from inside DOGFOOD?
\item
  Can an agent point to explicit \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker items for those gaps?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility / assistive reading posture}\label{record-019-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

This cycle is prose-heavy. The docs shell must preserve legible reading in plain text, keyboard navigation, and scrollable surfaces that do not depend on screenshots, pointer-only interaction, or color alone to communicate structure.

\section{Localization / directionality posture}\label{record-019-localization-directionality-posture}

The docs shell should stay localization-ready, but this cycle does not block \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} on translating the entire imported prose corpus. The important requirement is that section metadata and reader structure do not hard-code LTR-only assumptions.

\section{Agent inspectability / explainability posture}\label{record-019-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

The DOGFOOD docs-site shape must be explicit in repo artifacts:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  this cycle doc
\item
  release blocker backlog files in \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}/}
\item
  signposts such as \texttt{P\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{B\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
\end{itemize}

Agents should not have to infer from chat memory that DOGFOOD is supposed to grow beyond the component explorer.

\section{Non-goals}\label{record-019-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  importing every markdown file in the repo into DOGFOOD for \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}
\item
  full website parity with static docs tools
\item
  full-text search across every prose page
\item
  a general GSAP-like text-effects API for the entire framework
\item
  eliminating every piece of bespoke DOGFOOD chrome before \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}
\end{itemize}

The immediate requirement is a real docs-site shape and a non-embarrassing minimum corpus, not infinite scope growth.

\section{Evidence}\label{record-019-evidence}

\subsection{Current DOGFOOD shape}\label{record-019-current-dogfood-shape}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD already has a strong landing screen and framed docs shell
\item
  the current explorer is fundamentally centered on component families, component docs, and variants
\item
  the existing app still treats that component explorer as the main docs product
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Current repo docs shape}\label{record-019-current-repo-docs-shape}

Bijou's actual docs corpus already exists outside DOGFOOD:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}/}
\item
  package READMEs and repo-facing top-level docs
\end{itemize}

So the missing work is not ``write every thought from scratch.'' The missing work is exposing the right corpus and navigation structure inside DOGFOOD itself.

\section{Decision}\label{record-019-decision}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DOGFOOD's \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} role}{DOGFOOD's  role}}\label{record-019-dogfoods-4.1.0-role}

For \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, DOGFOOD should be treated as a \textbf{terminal documentation site for Bijou}, not only a component gallery.

\subsection{Expected top-level sections}\label{record-019-expected-top-level-sections}

At minimum, DOGFOOD should visibly distinguish these sections:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Start Here / Guides}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    what Bijou is
  \item
    how to get oriented
  \item
    how to start building
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Components}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    the current family/story/variant explorer
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Packages}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    what each shipped package is for
  \item
    when to reach for each one
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Philosophy / Architecture}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    design doctrine, architecture, and repo philosophy
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Release / Migration}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    what changed in the current line
  \item
    how to move between major versions
  \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

The current components view remains important, but it becomes one section of the docs system instead of the whole app.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker stance}{ blocker stance}}\label{record-019-blocker-stance}

These gaps are now \textbf{release blockers} for \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  no prose-doc reader plus top-level docs navigation
\item
  no repo/package docs inside DOGFOOD
\item
  no philosophy/architecture/doctrine docs inside DOGFOOD
\end{itemize}

If those remain absent, the release would still ship a strong component field guide, but not the terminal docs system Bijou increasingly claims to have.

\section{Deliverables from this shaping cycle}\label{record-019-deliverables-from-this-shaping-cycle}

This cycle should spawn three explicit \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blockers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-022-build-prose-docs-reader-and-top-level-dogfood-nav.md}{DF-022 --- Build Prose Docs Reader And Top-Level DOGFOOD Nav}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-023-publish-repo-package-and-release-guides-in-dogfood.md}{DF-023 --- Publish Repo, Package, And Release Guides In DOGFOOD}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-024-publish-philosophy-architecture-and-doctrine-guides-in-dogfood.md}{DF-024 --- Publish Philosophy, Architecture, And Doctrine Guides In DOGFOOD}
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation outline}\label{record-019-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Shape a top-level DOGFOOD docs-site IA instead of treating ``components'' as the only section.
\item
  Add a prose-doc reader path so markdown- and guide-like pages can be read inside the app.
\item
  Expose a minimum set of repo/package/release pages in that reader.
\item
  Expose a minimum set of philosophy/architecture/doctrine pages in that reader.
\item
  Keep component stories as the ``Components'' section rather than letting them keep masquerading as the whole docs product.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests to write first}\label{record-019-tests-to-write-first}

Under \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the cycle doc exists and names the missing docs-site sections
\item
  a \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}/} lane exists
\item
  the three blocker items exist in that lane
\item
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{B\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} acknowledge reopened \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blockers around DOGFOOD scope
\end{itemize}

\section{Risks}\label{record-019-risks}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  treating DOGFOOD's component explorer as ``good enough docs'' and shipping a narrower product than the repo's own story implies
\item
  reopening the \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} boundary without making the new blockers explicit in METHOD signposts
\item
  trying to solve search, docs import, architecture writing, and motion APIs all at once instead of defining a credible minimum docs-site contract
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-019-retrospective}

\subsection{What landed}\label{record-019-what-landed}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD's next shape is now explicit: terminal docs system, not only component gallery
\item
  the missing \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} docs-site surfaces are named as concrete blockers
\item
  the release boundary is narrowed around a more honest docs promise
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Debt spawned}\label{record-019-debt-spawned}

Follow-on work such as generalized text-motion APIs, richer search, and deeper bespoke-chrome cleanup may still matter, but they should not hide the more important docs-site gaps that now block \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}.

\chapter{DF-022 --- Build Prose Docs Reader And Top-Level DOGFOOD Nav}\label{record-020}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-022-build-prose-docs-reader-and-top-level-dogfood-nav.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF --- DOGFOOD Field Guide}

Depends on:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-021-shape-dogfood-as-terminal-docs-system.md}{DF-021 --- Shape DOGFOOD As Terminal Docs System}
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsor human}\label{record-020-sponsor-human}

A builder or maintainer who expects DOGFOOD to behave like a real docs site shell instead of only a component-family browser.

\section{Sponsor agent}\label{record-020-sponsor-agent}

An agent that must inspect DOGFOOD and answer:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  where the top-level docs sections live
\item
  whether DOGFOOD can read prose docs inside the app
\item
  whether the component explorer is still being mistaken for the whole docs product
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-020-hill}

DOGFOOD visibly behaves like a terminal-native docs shell with top-level section tabs and a real prose-doc reader, while keeping the component explorer as one important section rather than the whole app.

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-020-why-this-cycle-exists}

\texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}1} reframed the release honestly: DOGFOOD had enough shell and component breadth to feel substantial, but it still behaved like a components-only product.

That meant \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} still lacked a visible docs-site shell:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  there was no top-level section navigation
\item
  there was no prose-doc reader inside the app
\item
  users could not tell where non-component docs were supposed to live
\end{itemize}

This cycle closes that shell-shape gap without pretending the full repo, package, release, doctrine, and architecture corpus has already landed.

\section{Playback questions}\label{record-020-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Does DOGFOOD now expose top-level docs navigation instead of a single component-only page?
\item
  Is the default docs route a prose-reader-oriented section rather than dropping directly into the component explorer?
\item
  Can a user visibly switch between \texttt{G\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}, \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}, \texttt{P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}, \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y}, and \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e}?
\item
  Does the component browser still work as one section inside the docs shell?
\item
  Is the remaining \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker work now clearly about publishing the real corpus rather than inventing the shell shape?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility / assistive reading posture}\label{record-020-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

The new reader must stay keyboard-first and text-legible. It cannot rely on screenshots, pointer-only interaction, or color alone to communicate the new section structure.

\section{Localization / directionality posture}\label{record-020-localization-directionality-posture}

Section titles and shell hints should stay localizable. This cycle does not block on translating the starter prose corpus, but the shell shape must not hard-code a components-only reading model.

\section{Agent inspectability / explainability posture}\label{record-020-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

The repo should make the new shell shape explicit in:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  this cycle doc
\item
  the DOGFOOD app implementation
\item
  the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker lane
\item
  the release signposts and tests
\end{itemize}

An agent should be able to prove that \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}2} closed and that the remaining blocker work is now corpus publication.

\section{Non-goals}\label{record-020-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  importing the full repo docs corpus in this cycle
\item
  closing package, release, doctrine, or architecture content gaps
\item
  replacing every bespoke DOGFOOD surface
\item
  inventing a general animation or text-effects API as part of this work
\end{itemize}

\section{Decision}\label{record-020-decision}

For \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, DOGFOOD should expose the full section map immediately:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{G\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y}
\item
  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e}
\end{itemize}

\texttt{G\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} becomes the default docs route and carries the initial prose reader foundation. The other non-component sections get a visible home now, even if their deeper corpus still lands in follow-on blocker cycles.

\section{Implementation outline}\label{record-020-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Promote DOGFOOD from a one-page framed app to a top-level tabbed docs shell.
\item
  Add a prose-reader page model with guide navigation and scrollable main-doc surfaces.
\item
  Keep the existing component explorer intact as the \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} tab.
\item
  Seed DOGFOOD with starter markdown pages that explain the docs map and make the missing sections visible.
\item
  Reduce the remaining \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blockers to real corpus publication: \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}3} and \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}4}.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Evidence}\label{record-020-evidence}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the docs app now defaults to \texttt{G\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  the framed header exposes multiple top-level docs sections
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} still contains the family/story/variant explorer
\item
  DOGFOOD can render prose markdown pages from a starter corpus
\item
  the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker lane now only carries the remaining corpus work
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-020-retrospective}

The important correction here is architectural, not decorative: DOGFOOD stops overclaiming that ``component docs'' equals ``the whole Bijou docs product.''

The remaining release blocker work is now narrower and more honest:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}3} should publish repo/package/release guidance into the visible shell
\item
  \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}4} should publish philosophy/architecture/doctrine guidance into the visible shell
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DF-023 --- Publish Repo, Package, And Release Guides In DOGFOOD}\label{record-021}

\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsor human}\label{record-021-sponsor-human}

A builder or evaluator who expects DOGFOOD to explain the Bijou repo, its published packages, and the current release line without sending them back out into scattered repo files.

\section{Sponsor agent}\label{record-021-sponsor-agent}

An agent that must answer:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  what packages ship in the workspace and what each one is for
\item
  where the repo says to start reading
\item
  what changed in \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}
\item
  how a \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} user should approach the \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} upgrade
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-021-hill}

DOGFOOD stops treating \texttt{P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} and \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e} as placeholder tabs and starts acting like a real terminal docs product for those topics. A user can reach repo orientation, package explainers, and \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release/migration material from inside the app.

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-021-why-this-cycle-exists}

\texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}2} gave DOGFOOD the shell shape of a docs site, but it still only proved the shape. The newly visible \texttt{P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} and \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e} sections were honest placeholders, not the actual corpus.

That was good enough to clarify the next blocker, but not good enough to ship \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} honestly.

If DOGFOOD is the canonical docs surface for this release, it cannot keep outsourcing repo/package/release understanding to filesystem spelunking.

\section{Playback questions}\label{record-021-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Can a user open a repo-orientation page inside \texttt{G\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}?
\item
  Does \texttt{P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} now expose explainer pages for the shipped workspace packages instead of only an overview placeholder?
\item
  Does \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e} now expose the actual \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} long-form \texttt{W\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}'\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w} and migration guidance inside the docs app?
\item
  Do the signposts and blocker lane stop pretending \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}3} is still open?
\item
  Is the remaining \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} DOGFOOD blocker work now narrower: philosophy/doctrine corpus plus the examples/smoke posture shift?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility / assistive reading posture}\label{record-021-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

The newly published corpus must remain keyboard-first, scrollable, and text-legible inside the existing three-pane reader. No screenshot-only or color-only explanation is allowed.

\section{Localization / directionality posture}\label{record-021-localization-directionality-posture}

This cycle does not translate the new prose corpus, but it must keep the reader on the same localizable shell and section model established in \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}2}.

\section{Agent inspectability / explainability posture}\label{record-021-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

An agent should be able to prove closure by inspecting:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the DOGFOOD app corpus declarations
\item
  the new cycle doc
\item
  the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker lane
\item
  the release signposts
\item
  the cycle tests
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-goals}\label{record-021-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  closing the philosophy/architecture/doctrine blocker (\texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}4})
\item
  replacing the package READMEs or release docs as their own repo-owned sources
\item
  finishing the examples-to-DOGFOOD posture shift
\item
  changing the \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} version decision
\end{itemize}

\section{Decision}\label{record-021-decision}

For \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, DOGFOOD should publish the existing repo/package/release corpus through the prose-doc reader instead of keeping those sections as stubs.

The source of truth remains the repo-owned docs and package READMEs. DOGFOOD is the canonical human-facing reading surface for them.

\section{Implementation outline}\label{record-021-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a repo-orientation page under \texttt{G\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Publish package explainer pages for the shipped workspace packages in \texttt{P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Publish the \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} long-form \texttt{W\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}'\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w} and migration guides in \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  Update the starter overview pages so they no longer claim that the package and release corpus is missing.
\item
  Move \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}3} from the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker lane into \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/} and update the signposts/tests.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Evidence}\label{record-021-evidence}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD now exposes a \texttt{D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p} guide
\item
  the \texttt{P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} section contains per-package explainer pages
\item
  the \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e} section contains \texttt{W\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}'\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} and \texttt{M\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}
\item
  the active \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker lane no longer lists \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}3}
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-021-retrospective}

The important correction is not just ``more text exists.'' The correction is that DOGFOOD now behaves more like a real docs product:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  repo orientation lives inside the app
\item
  package understanding lives inside the app
\item
  release understanding lives inside the app
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsor human}\label{record-022-sponsor-human}

A builder or maintainer who wants DOGFOOD to explain not just what Bijou exports, but why the framework is shaped the way it is.

An agent that must answer:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  what doctrine governs Bijou runtime and modeling decisions
\item
  how the repo is architected
\item
  which invariants matter
\item
  where the design-system and UX stance live

\section{Hill}\label{record-022-hill}

The \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y} section in DOGFOOD stops being a placeholder and becomes a real reader-first home for doctrine, architecture, invariants, and design-system guidance.

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-022-why-this-cycle-exists}

After \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}3}, DOGFOOD could explain the repo, the package line, and the release line, but it still could not explain Bijou's design stance without sending users back into raw repo docs.

That was the last major corpus gap keeping DOGFOOD from acting like a real docs product for \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}.

\section{Playback questions}\label{record-022-playback-questions}

\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

  Does the \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y} section now expose more than an overview page?
\item

\item
  Can a user read runtime-truth doctrine, architecture, invariants, and design-system guidance without leaving DOGFOOD?
\item
  Do the blocker lane and signposts stop pretending \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}4} is still open?
\item
  Are the remaining \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blockers now only the examples/smoke posture items?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility / assistive reading posture}\label{record-022-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

The newly published corpus must remain scrollable, keyboard-first, and text-legible inside the existing prose-reader shell.

\section{Localization / directionality posture}\label{record-022-localization-directionality-posture}

This cycle does not translate the doctrine corpus, but it must keep the same localizable shell and section posture established in \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}2}.

\section{Agent inspectability / explainability posture}\label{record-022-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

An agent should be able to prove closure by inspecting:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the new \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y} guide entries in the DOGFOOD app
\item
  the cycle doc
\item
  the updated \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker lane
\item
  the release signposts
\item
  the cycle tests
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-goals}\label{record-022-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  replacing the source docs under \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}
\item
  finishing the examples-to-DOGFOOD posture shift
\item
  replacing the release smoke contract
\item
  changing the \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} version decision
\end{itemize}

\section{Decision}\label{record-022-decision}

For \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, DOGFOOD should publish the key doctrine and architecture corpus through the \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y} section instead of treating that section as an empty promise.

The repo-owned docs remain the source of truth. DOGFOOD becomes the canonical human-facing reading surface for them.

\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

  Keep the \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y} overview page, but update it to describe the now-published corpus.

  \item

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-022-retrospective}

\chapter{DF-025 --- Make DOGFOOD The Only Human-Facing Docs Surface}\label{record-023}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-025-make-dogfood-the-only-human-facing-docs-surface.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF --- DOGFOOD Field Guide}
