  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-021-shape-dogfood-as-terminal-docs-system.md}{DF-021 --- Shape DOGFOOD As Terminal Docs System}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-022-build-prose-docs-reader-and-top-level-dogfood-nav.md}{DF-022 --- Build Prose Docs Reader And Top-Level DOGFOOD Nav}
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsor human}\label{record-023-sponsor-human}

A builder or maintainer who should have exactly one obvious answer to ``where do I go to learn Bijou?''

\section{Sponsor agent}\label{record-023-sponsor-agent}

An agent that must determine, from repo artifacts alone, whether the public docs surface is DOGFOOD or the \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/} tree.

\section{Hill}\label{record-023-hill}

DOGFOOD is the only human-facing docs surface for Bijou. The \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/} tree remains useful, but only as a secondary/internal reference, regression, and migration substrate rather than a competing public docs front door.

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-023-why-this-cycle-exists}

The repo currently carries two conflicting truths:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  strategy docs say DOGFOOD should replace example sprawl as the living docs system
\item
  front-door docs and release validation still treat \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/} as a first-class public teaching path
\end{itemize}

That is not a harmless wording issue.

If humans still have to browse \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} to understand the product, then DOGFOOD is not actually the docs surface yet. It is just a better example.

For \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, Bijou needs a sharper stance:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD is where humans should learn Bijou
\item
  example programs are secondary and should not compete with DOGFOOD for repo-front-door authority
\item
  release smoke should follow the same truth instead of continuing to bless the broad examples tree as the main proving surface
\end{itemize}

\section{Human users}\label{record-023-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-023-primary-human-user}

A curious builder evaluating Bijou and trying to find the canonical docs path quickly.

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-023-human-hill}

A human can read the root docs surfaces and recover one clear story:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  start with DOGFOOD
\item
  use package docs and design docs as supporting corpus
\item
  treat \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/} as secondary reference material, not as the main product documentation surface
\end{itemize}

\section{Agent users}\label{record-023-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-023-primary-agent-user}

An agent updating docs, release automation, or backlog placement.

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-023-agent-hill}

An agent can point to explicit repo artifacts showing:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD is canonical
\item
  example inventory is secondary
\item
  the remaining release blockers needed to make runtime smoke and docs posture match that decision
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback questions}\label{record-023-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  If a human asks ``where do I start learning Bijou?'', do the front-door docs point to DOGFOOD first?
\item
  Does \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} clearly read as a secondary/internal inventory instead of a public docs hub?
\item
  Do METHOD signposts and release blockers explicitly say that \texttt{s\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}*} is no longer acceptable as the release-facing end state?
\item
  Does the repo have a clear blocker capturing the remaining work to demote examples behind DOGFOOD?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility / assistive reading posture}\label{record-023-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

This is a docs-information-architecture cycle. The important accessibility requirement is clarity: people using plain-text docs, terminal readers, or agent tooling should not have to infer canon from inconsistent link placement or filenames.

\section{Localization / directionality posture}\label{record-023-localization-directionality-posture}

This cycle does not add new localized copy requirements. It does require that section naming and docs routing remain cleanly separable from English-only filesystem trivia such as \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s}.

\section{Agent inspectability / explainability posture}\label{record-023-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

The DOGFOOD-only decision must be visible in:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  this cycle doc
\item
  the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker lane
\item
  signposts such as \texttt{P\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{B\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
\item
  front-door docs such as \texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
\end{itemize}

Agents should not have to rely on chat memory to learn that \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/} has been demoted.

\section{Non-goals}\label{record-023-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  deleting the entire \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/} tree immediately
\item
  pretending every example should disappear
\item
  relocating every implementation file currently under \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}
\item
  eliminating every migration/reference example before \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}
\end{itemize}

The immediate requirement is policy honesty and release-blocker clarity, not blind deletion.

\section{Evidence}\label{record-023-evidence}

\subsection{Current contradiction}\label{record-023-current-contradiction}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} says DOGFOOD should stop docs, demos, examples, and tests from drifting apart
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} already says DOGFOOD is the primary living-docs surface
\item
  but the root docs still expose \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} as a public map, and release readiness still depends on \texttt{s\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}*}
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Why that matters}\label{record-023-why-that-matters}

If examples remain both:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a public docs front door
\item
  and the main release smoke contract
\end{itemize}

then DOGFOOD cannot honestly be called ``the only way'' yet.

\section{Decision}\label{record-023-decision}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{Public-docs rule for \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}}{Public-docs rule for }}\label{record-023-public-docs-rule-for-4.1.0}

For \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, DOGFOOD is the only human-facing docs surface.

That means:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  root docs should send humans to DOGFOOD first
\item
  package/design/release corpus should be reachable through DOGFOOD
\item
  the example inventory should read as secondary/internal/reference material
\item
  release smoke should move off the broad \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/} tree
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Example posture}\label{record-023-example-posture}

Examples still matter, but their role is narrower:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  migration references
\item
  isolated API seam proofs
\item
  targeted regression fixtures
\item
  implementation sandboxes
\end{itemize}

They do \textbf{not} get to remain a competing public docs navigation layer.

\section{Deliverables from this shaping cycle}\label{record-023-deliverables-from-this-shaping-cycle}

This cycle should tighten the \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker lane by:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  keeping \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-023-publish-repo-package-and-release-guides-in-dogfood.md}{DF-023 --- Publish Repo, Package, And Release Guides In DOGFOOD} as a release blocker
\item
  keeping \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-024-publish-philosophy-architecture-and-doctrine-guides-in-dogfood.md}{DF-024 --- Publish Philosophy, Architecture, And Doctrine Guides In DOGFOOD} as a release blocker
\item
  moving \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/WF-003-replace-smoke-examples-with-smoke-dogfood.md}{WF-003 --- Replace \texttt{s\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}*} With \texttt{s\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d}} into the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker lane
\item
  spawning \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-026-demote-examples-to-secondary-reference-status.md}{DF-026 --- Demote Examples To Secondary Reference Status} as an explicit docs-surface blocker
\end{itemize}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist

  Publish a repo-owned DOGFOOD entrypoint under \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}.

\item

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}

\chapter{DF-026 --- Demote Examples To Secondary Reference Status}\label{record-024}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF --- DOGFOOD Field Guide}

\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsor human}\label{record-024-sponsor-human}

A learner or evaluator who should get one clear answer about where to start reading Bijou docs, instead of being bounced between DOGFOOD and a parallel example hub.

\section{Sponsor agent}\label{record-024-sponsor-agent}

An agent that must tell the difference between:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the canonical docs surface
\item
  the internal example inventory
\item
  migration/reference fixtures
\item
  smoke and regression substrate
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-024-hill}

The repo stops presenting \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/} as a competing docs product. DOGFOOD is the canonical human-facing path. Examples remain valuable, but only as secondary/internal/reference material.

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-024-why-this-cycle-exists}

\texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}5} set the policy direction, but policy alone was not enough.

If DOGFOOD says ``start here'' while the example inventory still reads like a second docs hub, the public posture is still split.

This cycle exists to make the repo-facing surfaces honest before \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}.

\section{Playback questions}\label{record-024-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Do front-door docs still clearly tell humans to start with DOGFOOD?
\item
  Does the example inventory now read as secondary/internal/reference instead of a public docs hub?
\item
  Can a user open DOGFOOD itself and understand why examples are secondary?
\item
  Do release-facing docs stop treating the example inventory as equal public navigation?
\item
  Is \texttt{W\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3} now the only remaining \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility / assistive reading posture}\label{record-024-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

The examples posture should be stated in text, not implied by color, layout, or repo folklore.

\section{Localization / directionality posture}\label{record-024-localization-directionality-posture}

This cycle does not translate the example posture copy, but it must keep the explanation inside the same localizable DOGFOOD shell.

\section{Agent inspectability / explainability posture}\label{record-024-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

An agent should be able to prove closure by inspecting:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
\item
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
\item
  the DOGFOOD guide corpus
\item
  the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker lane
\item
  the cycle tests
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-goals}\label{record-024-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  deleting the whole \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/} tree
\item
  replacing the release smoke contract
\item
  erasing migration or isolated API seam references that still matter
\end{itemize}

\section{Decision}\label{record-024-decision}

For \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, DOGFOOD is the only human-facing docs surface. The example inventory remains, but it should read as:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  secondary/internal reference
\item
  migration substrate
\item
  isolated API proof
\item
  regression/smoke substrate
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation outline}\label{record-024-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Publish the secondary-example posture inside DOGFOOD itself.
\item
  Tighten \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} so it reads as an internal reference map.
\item
  Tighten \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} so it does not read like a docs hub.
\item
  Move \texttt{D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}6} from the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} blocker lane into \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/} and update the signposts/tests.
\end{enumerate}

  DOGFOOD now exposes a \texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p} guide

\chapter{DF-027 --- Storybook-Style Tool for Bijou}\label{record-025}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-027-storybook-style-tool-for-bijou.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: "DF-027 — Storybook-Style Tool for Bijou"
legend: DF
lane: design

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-025-framing}

Bijou already has the pieces of a Storybook-style workflow: structured \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y} records, DOGFOOD's component explorer, story capture matrices, fixture-promotion records, and MCP-facing docs payloads. The missing piece is a standalone workstation that developers can use without entering the full docs app, backed by a stable model that tooling can consume without scraping DOGFOOD.

This cycle adds the first dedicated Storybook workstation slice. It includes an interactive TUI for local component browsing and development, plus the deterministic model/index and matrix capture path for agents, CI, MCP exports, block tooling, screenshots, and schema-bound controls.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-025-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Bijou builders browsing first-party components and shells by family.
\item
  Maintainers auditing variant and output-mode coverage before release.
\item
  Tooling authors who need a stable story index and capture path for docs, MCP, screenshots, fixtures, or future block workstations.
\item
  Agents selecting stories without reverse-engineering the DOGFOOD shell.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-025-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder can run \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k} and enter a standalone Storybook-style workbench over the story catalog, with variants, profiles, package/source facts, and a preview surface.
\item
  A maintainer can capture a selected story across every variant/profile pair using the same \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x} substrate as existing docs tooling.
\item
  A future UI or MCP tool can consume a stable workstation model instead of scraping \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} or re-parsing story docs.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-025-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does the workstation index every DOGFOOD story without duplicating story truth?
\item
  Does it group stories by family and expose variants, profile modes, package, tags, and source path?
\item
  Can callers capture a selected story's variant/profile matrix?
\item
  Does the capture path render real story previews instead of placeholder text?
\item
  Does the tool reuse \texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} rather than creating a second matrix format?
\item
  Is there a simple command for humans and agents to run?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-025-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a standalone interactive Storybook workstation app.
\item
  Add a DOGFOOD storybook workstation module for deterministic tooling.
\item
  Add a text index renderer for the story catalog.
\item
  Add a selected-story matrix capture helper.
\item
  Reuse \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y} and \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x} contracts.
\item
  Add root scripts for the interactive workbench and text-first workstation.
\item
  Keep both paths on the same story catalog instead of duplicating story truth.
\end{itemize}

  The workstation model covers every \texttt{C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}S} entry.

\end{enumerate}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-025-drift-check}

The current DOGFOOD app remains the canonical human-facing docs surface. This slice does not fork story data or add a browser dependency. The standalone workbench and text-first workstation both read the existing \texttt{C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}S} catalog and use the existing story protocol plus \texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.

The result is a narrow, reusable tooling seam: deterministic enough for agents and CI, but still powered by the same story records humans browse in DOGFOOD.

  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} launches a standalone interactive TUI over the same story catalog, with catalog navigation, profile/variant switching, preview, and test-matrix panes.
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k} now targets the standalone interactive workbench instead of opening DOGFOOD on the components page.
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x} provides the text-first command path, while \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k} remains available for existing docs and users.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-025-retrospective}

The right Storybook-style tool has two layers: a standalone interactive workbench for humans and a stable model/capture path for CI, MCP, release audits, agents, and future block tooling. Both layers stay useful because they share the same story records instead of minting a second registry.

\chapter{DF-028 Story Capture Matrix}\label{record-026}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-028-story-capture-matrix.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DF-028 Story Capture Matrix
legend: DF
lane: design

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-026-framing}

Bijou's best components are not single screenshots. They have rich, interactive, static, pipe, and accessible renderings, often across multiple variants and widths. Docs and tests need one place to see that matrix without copying examples by hand.

DF-028 adds a pure story capture matrix. The first slice accepts story profiles, variants, and a renderer callback, captures every profile/variant combination, and renders deterministic text. It is intentionally renderer-neutral: callers can use core components, TUI frames, fixtures, or DOGFOOD stories around it.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-026-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Maintainers auditing multi-mode component stories.
\item
  Docs authors promoting regression fixtures into readable examples.
\item
  MCP/tooling authors exporting the same capture facts to agents.
\item
  Accessibility reviewers comparing lowerings without opening a TUI.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-026-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer can capture every variant across interactive, static, pipe, and accessible profiles from one renderer callback.
\item
  A reviewer can see missing required modes before accepting a story capture.
\item
  A docs surface can render the captured matrix as stable text.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-026-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does the helper invoke the renderer once for every profile/variant pair?
\item
  Does each capture preserve story id, profile id, variant id, mode, width, and output?
\item
  Can callers require specific modes and get deterministic missing-mode output?
\item
  Does matrix text group captures by variant and profile?
\item
  Can the matrix carry component metadata from DX-025 without owning that metadata contract?
\item
  Does \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u} export the story capture API from the root barrel?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-026-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add \texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Add \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Support profiles with id, label, mode, and width.
\item
  Support variants with id, label, and optional description.
\item
  Support optional component metadata.
\item
  Support \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} and expose missing modes.
\item
  Keep outputs as strings in this slice; surface-specific capture can build on top later.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-026-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED tests fail before implementation and pass after.
\item
  Captures are deterministic and cover the profile/variant cross product.
\item
  Missing required modes are stable and sorted by output-mode order.
\item
  Text output is suitable for docs, test failures, and agent reports.
\item
  Docs and changelog describe the helper.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-026-implementation-outline}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Implement the helper in \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Export it from \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Keep rendering caller-owned; this helper records and formats the matrix.
\end{itemize}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-026-drift-check}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Scope stayed renderer-neutral. The helper executes a caller-provided renderer and records string output, leaving surface conversion and runtime/test adapter orchestration to future wrappers.
\item
  The matrix can carry DX-025 component metadata but does not validate or own it.
\item
  Missing required modes are sorted by Bijou output-mode order.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback}\label{record-026-playback}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} invokes the renderer once for each profile/variant pair and stores story id, profile id, variant id, mode, width, and output.
\item
  \texttt{m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} reports required modes absent from the supplied profiles.
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} renders profile ids, variant ids, missing modes, and each captured output grouped by variant and profile.
\item
  Optional \texttt{m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a} lets DOGFOOD/MCP/docs consumers attach the shared component metadata contract without duplicating fields.
\item
  \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u} exports the story capture API from the root barrel.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-026-retrospective}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Keeping rendering caller-owned makes the helper useful in core tests, DOGFOOD, TUI fixtures, and MCP payload generation without importing runtime adapters.
\item
  The next useful layer is a fixture/story wrapper that supplies profiles and renderer contexts automatically, then writes the matrix into docs artifacts.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DF-029 Fixture-to-Docs Promotion Path}\label{record-027}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-029-fixture-to-docs-promotion-path.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DF-029 Fixture-to-Docs Promotion Path
legend: DF
lane: design

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-027-framing}

Good Bijou examples often start as regression fixtures. Good docs examples often become the clearest regression fixtures. Today the promotion path between those surfaces is mostly manual, which means provenance, story ids, component metadata, and capture outputs drift.

DF-029 adds a pure promotion record that links fixture, docs, story, example, or MCP artifacts. The first slice is not a file-writing CLI; it is the canonical record and text report that future commands can emit, review, and preserve.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-027-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Maintainers promoting stable fixtures into docs and DOGFOOD stories.
\item
  Docs authors linking examples back to executable regression coverage.
\item
  MCP/tooling authors reusing example provenance in agent-facing payloads.
\item
  Agents proposing docs updates from failing or useful fixtures.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-027-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer can record a fixture-to-docs promotion with source artifact, target artifact, component metadata, story matrix, tags, and notes.
\item
  A docs author can reverse that record when a docs story should become a regression fixture.
\item
  A reviewer can read a deterministic report that preserves provenance without inspecting multiple files.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-027-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does the record support fixture, docs, story, example, and MCP artifacts?
\item
  Does the helper preserve metadata and story capture matrix references?
\item
  Are tags normalized deterministically?
\item
  Can the promotion direction be reversed without losing provenance?
\item
  Does report text include id, source, target, component, matrix, tags, and notes?
\item
  Does \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u} export the promotion API from the root barrel?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-027-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Add \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}?\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Add \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Support artifact kinds \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}, \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}, and \texttt{m\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}p}.
\item
  Support optional \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a} and \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x}.
\item
  Keep the first slice pure and deterministic; no filesystem writes.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-027-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED tests fail before implementation and pass after.
\item
  Promotion records keep source, target, metadata, matrix, tags, and notes.
\item
  Reverse promotion swaps source/target and preserves provenance.
\item
  Report text is stable and suitable for docs, review comments, and agent output.
\item
  Docs and changelog describe the helper.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-027-implementation-outline}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist

\item
  Keep artifact paths as caller-owned strings; path validation belongs to a future CLI/adapter.
\end{itemize}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-027-drift-check}

\begin{itemize}

\item

\item
  Tag normalization is deterministic: trimmed, de-duplicated, and sorted.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-027-retrospective}

\end{itemize}

\chapter{DF-030 Dogfood Docs Surface Block}\label{record-028}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-030-dogfood-docs-surface-block.md}\par}\smallskip

Status: landed for \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} Issue: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/244}{\#244} PR: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/pull/258}{\#258}

\section{Framing}\label{record-028-framing}

DOGFOOD is already the human-facing documentation app and proving ground, but its docs experience was still described as several nearby surfaces: navigation, article reader, search, proof panels, and footer/status evidence. DF-030 makes that product truth explicit as one inspectable Block contract.

This cycle lands \texttt{D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} as the canonical DOGFOOD docs workspace Block. It does not replace the existing leaf Blocks. Instead, it anchors them under one docs-surface identity so humans and agents can inspect the full documentation experience without reconstructing it from scattered rendering code.

\section{Sponsored Perspectives}\label{record-028-sponsored-perspectives}

Sponsored Human:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer wants DOGFOOD to be the first-class documentation experience, not a secondary demo app.
\item
  A reader wants navigation, article content, search, and proof artifacts to feel like one documentation surface.
\end{itemize}

Sponsored Agent:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent auditing docs truth needs one Block tree and stable lowering facts for the selected route, heading, search hit count, and proof artifacts.
\item
  An agent should not need provider handles, global app state, or rendered cell parsing to know what DOGFOOD is showing.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-028-hill}

A maintainer can open DOGFOOD and treat the docs app as the canonical Bijou documentation surface, with route, reader, search, and proof evidence exposed as typed Block metadata, schema-bound input, command intents, registry inventory, and stable lower-mode facts.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-028-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Can DOGFOOD name its full docs workspace as one Block?
\item
  Can unknown docs-surface input be validated before rendering?
\item
  Do route, heading, search-hit-count, and proof-artifact facts survive every output mode as stable identities?
\item
  Does the DOGFOOD Blocks inventory show this surface as product truth?
\item
  Can lower modes explain the docs surface without borders, color, or terminal layout?
\end{itemize}

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-028-lower-modes}

Pipe mode:

\begin{CodeBlock}
route   heading search-hit-count    proofs
blocks  blocks  2   table-demo.gif
\end{CodeBlock}

Accessible mode:

Search query table has 2 hits. Proof artifacts: table-demo.gif.
\end{CodeBlock}

The lower-mode invariant is semantic parity. The route, heading, hit count, and proof artifact facts are inspected from \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}, not parsed from terminal layout.

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-028-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

\texttt{D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} must preserve docs meaning without relying on position, borders, color, or animation. Accessible mode lowers the selected route, reader heading, search summary, and proof artifact list into readable sentences, while facts preserve the same semantic payload for assistive and agent consumers.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-028-localization-and-directionality-posture}

The registry description for \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} is catalog-backed through the DOGFOOD string table. This slice adds English source rows plus generated German, Spanish, and French runtime catalog entries for the docs-surface description and rendered-preview label. Any untranslated neighboring strings remain explicit catalog debt rather than hidden selected-locale fallback. The Block contract itself carries ids, routes, counts, and artifact labels as data so future locale and directionality adapters can format presentation without changing the semantic facts.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-028-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

Agents should inspect this surface through typed Block metadata, view data requirements, command intents, schema-bound input, registry ownership, and mode-lowering facts. The registry intentionally remains render-free and avoids provider handles, subscriptions, mutable dispatch callbacks, or global Block lookup.

\section{Closeout}\label{record-028-closeout}

DF-030 moves DOGFOOD one step closer to being the canonical docs surface rather than a collection of adjacent examples. The useful boundary is the typed Block: metadata, schema-bound input, command intents, registry evidence, and lower-mode facts. The runtime app remains free to render through its existing TUI machinery, but the product truth is inspectable as a Block.

\section{Framing}\label{record-029-framing}

The v6 block floor already proved \texttt{A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l}, \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}, and \texttt{I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l}. The next useful slice is the product feedback layer: inline state, in-flow notices, transient overlays, activity history, shortcut cues, and progress.

This cycle turns issues \#220 through \#225 into first-party standard Blocks in \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u}. The work uses the current typed Blocks API: \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, validated metadata, view data contracts, command intents, story ids, deterministic render output, and stable lowering facts. It does not introduce a new YAML or JSON runtime IR. Declarative YAML/JSON can become an adapter later, but it should compile into the typed contract this slice proves.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-029-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  TUI app authors who need reusable status and feedback semantics instead of bespoke strings inside pages.
\item
  DOGFOOD maintainers who need status surfaces to lower truthfully across interactive, static, pipe, and accessible modes.
\item
  Tooling authors who want block metadata, data contracts, command intents, and stories to describe feedback surfaces before rendering them.
\item
  Future IR authors who need a typed target for YAML/JSON block declarations.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-029-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder can import one of the standard feedback Blocks and immediately inspect its metadata, data requirements, command intents, and ready story.
\item
  A reader can move between rich, static, pipe, and accessible profiles and still get the same feedback meaning, even when visual chrome disappears.
\item
  A maintainer can run one focused cycle test that proves the status and feedback slice is catalogued, rendered, and lowering-stable.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-029-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Which feedback surfaces are common enough to become first-party Blocks now?
\item
  Do these Blocks declare data contracts and command intents without taking on provider subscriptions or command dispatch?
\item
  Do visual modes render as surfaces while pipe and accessible modes preserve meaning as text?
\item
  Do lowerings carry stable facts so tests and tools do not parse terminal drawings?
\item
  Does this slice make room for a future YAML/JSON declaration format without inventing a second runtime contract?
\end{itemize}

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-029-lower-modes}

Static mode preserves the same surface structure as interactive mode while remaining deterministic and render-only.

Pipe mode lowers every Block to a compact record:

\begin{CodeBlock}
InlineStatusBlock | label=docs | status=ok | message=synced
\end{CodeBlock}

Accessible mode lowers every Block to a readable sentence list:

\begin{CodeBlock}
InlineStatusBlock
- label: docs
- status: ok
- message: synced
\end{CodeBlock}

The lower-mode invariant is semantic parity, not visual parity. Pipe and accessible consumers should not need box drawing, row positions, or color to understand status.

\section{Requirements}\label{record-029-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Export all six Blocks from the package barrel and standard catalog.
\item
  Include all six Blocks in \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}.
\item
  Give each Block valid metadata across interactive, static, pipe, and accessible modes.
\item
  Give each Block at least one ready story id.
\item
  Attach view data contracts so tooling can inspect required slot data without provider handles.
\item
  Attach schema adapters and schema-bound block exports so callers can validate plain input before binding render slots.
\item
  Attach command intents for selecting the block, copying facts, and opening a story, without command callbacks.
\item
  Render interactive/static output as surfaces and pipe/accessible output as text.
\item
  Preserve \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}, \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y}, \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e}, selected identity, and \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}*} facts across modes.
\end{itemize}

\section{Future Declarative Shape}\label{record-029-future-declarative-shape}

The old Bijou IR idea still fits, but this slice keeps it as a declaration format over the typed API:

\begin{CodeBlock}
block: InlineStatusBlock
package: "@flyingrobots/bijou"
story: inline-status.ready
modes:
  - interactive
  - static
  - pipe
  - accessible
data:
  inlineStatus.label: docs
  inlineStatus.status: ok
  inlineStatus.message: synced
commands:
  - inlineStatus.select
  - inlineStatus.copyFacts
  - inlineStatus.openStory
facts:
  block: InlineStatusBlock
  block.family: status
  block.variant: ready
  semanticValue.label: docs
\end{CodeBlock}

A future declaration adapter can parse this shape, route it through \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}, and build typed \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} input or story fixtures. The runtime source of truth remains the typed Block contract.

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-029-drift-check}

The original DX-031 release floor was correct to limit itself to the first three Blocks. Drift appeared later when issues \#220 through \#225 became clear v6 candidates but ROADMAP and BEARING still left them in the v7 queue. This cycle corrects the tracker mirror and makes the expansion explicit, issue-backed v6 work.

No new follow-on debt is deferred by this slice. Broader component-family audits remain separate issues after \#225.

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-029-retrospective}

The useful move was not to invent a new IR under pressure. The useful move was to land the feedback vocabulary as typed, tested Blocks, then leave YAML/JSON as a future authoring adapter. That keeps the v6 release boundary concrete: geometry and Blocks continue to be inspectable package truth, not untyped story prose.

\chapter{DF-036 Audit loading placeholders family across real surfaces}\label{record-030}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-036-audit-loading-placeholders-family-across-real-surfaces.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DF-036 Audit loading placeholders family across real surfaces
legend: DF
lane: design
priority: medium
keywords:
  - component-audit
  - dogfood
  - lowerings
  - skeleton

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-030-framing}

The loading placeholder family is intentionally small: \texttt{s\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} should cover short-lived, known-shape loading gaps and should not become a generic decorative filler. Because skeletons exist to preserve layout truth, they are a good v6 release proof point: rich/static output can preserve shape, but pipe and accessible lowerings must preserve meaning without relying on placeholder glyphs.

This audit verifies the family against the real DOGFOOD story protocol, component-family doctrine, and mode-aware runtime behavior.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-030-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  TUI app authors deciding whether a known-shape loading gap should use \texttt{s\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, or explicit prose.
\item
  Docs readers switching the loading story across rich, static, pipe, and accessible profiles.
\item
  Maintainers who need a focused regression proving DOGFOOD and design-system guidance match current runtime truth.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-030-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder can inspect the DOGFOOD loading placeholder story and see both form-shaped and card-shaped placeholder regions.
\item
  A reader can switch the story through interactive, static, pipe, and accessible profiles without decorative placeholder glyphs leaking into constrained output.
\item
  A maintainer can run one cycle test that ties \texttt{s\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} behavior, DOGFOOD story metadata, and component-family guidance together.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-030-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does DOGFOOD expose the loading placeholder family through the \texttt{s\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} story?
\item
  Do the story variants cover both field/form and region/card skeleton usage?
\item
  Do interactive and static profiles preserve the placeholder shape?
\item
  Do pipe and accessible profiles avoid placeholder glyph leakage?
\item
  Do the design-system docs still describe skeletons as short-lived, known-shape placeholders rather than generic loading decoration?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-030-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Keep the existing \texttt{s\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} story identity and \texttt{l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s} coverage family id.
\item
  Render every skeleton story variant in every canonical story profile.
\item
  Treat rich/static placeholder glyphs as allowed only in visual profiles.
\item
  Treat pipe output as label/context preserving, not placeholder-glyph preserving.
\item
  Treat accessible output as explicit loading-state language.
\item
  Confirm \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} still matches the runtime story posture.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-030-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} proves the cycle doc carries the modern playback sections.
\item
  The test locates the DOGFOOD \texttt{s\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} story and verifies the expected variants.
\item
  Every variant renders non-empty output in every documented profile.
\item
  Rich/static output includes placeholder shape; pipe output does not include placeholder glyphs; accessible output includes explicit loading text.
\item
  Component-family docs retain the known-shape, short-lived loading guidance.
\end{itemize}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-030-drift-check}

No runtime drift was found in this slice. \texttt{s\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} already lowers to visual placeholder bars in interactive/static modes, no output in pipe mode, and explicit \texttt{L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.} text in accessible mode. DOGFOOD wraps those primitives with labels and region titles, so pipe output remains meaningful without copying decorative placeholder glyphs.

No follow-on backlog item is needed for this slice.

The audit confirmed that the smallest block families still need first-class mode tests. There was no need to expand \texttt{s\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} itself; the valuable work was pinning its semantic limits so future loading-screen or block work cannot quietly turn skeletons into decorative filler.

The work follows a Design Thinking loop:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  observe the real DOGFOOD surface families instead of trusting isolated fixtures
\item
  frame each family as a reusable Block contract with explicit data and facts
\item
  prototype the TUI and lower-mode shapes as ASCII mockups before treating the implementation as landed
\item
  test the contract through catalog, schema, render, and lowering proof
\end{itemize}

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-031-lower-modes}

Static mode keeps the same surface structure as interactive mode and stays render-only.

Pipe mode lowers every Block to a compact record:

\begin{CodeBlock}
FramedGroupBlock
title: Release Checks
items: tests green; docs updated; PR linked
selected: tests green
mode: review
\end{CodeBlock}

Accessible mode lowers every Block to label-first prose:

\begin{CodeBlock}
FramedGroupBlock
Title: Release Checks
Items: tests green; docs updated; PR linked
Selected: tests green
Mode: review
\end{CodeBlock}

Every lower mode carries inspectable facts:

\begin{CodeBlock}
block = FramedGroupBlock
block.rendered = true
block.family = grouping
block.variant = ready
block.mode = pipe
block.selected = tests green
semanticValue.title = Release Checks
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Accessibility And Directionality}\label{record-031-accessibility-and-directionality}

The first slice does not add bespoke focus behavior. The Blocks expose semantic labels and section values so accessible output can preserve meaning when visual grouping, rules, and input chrome are removed. Text is stored as plain strings or string arrays, leaving locale, bidirectional rendering, and translation concerns to callers and localization adapters.

\section{Agent Inspectability}\label{record-031-agent-inspectability}

Agents and tests should inspect metadata, data contracts, schema descriptions, command intent ids, ready story ids, and lowering facts. They should not scrape terminal boxes or infer meaning from row positions.

\section{Declarative IR Note}\label{record-031-declarative-ir-note}

The old Bijou IR idea still fits as a declaration format over this typed API. This cycle does not introduce a new YAML or JSON runtime, but it gives future IR work concrete targets:

\begin{CodeBlock}
block: FramedGroupBlock
package: "@flyingrobots/bijou"
story: framed-group.ready
data:
  title: Release Checks
  items:
    - tests green
    - docs updated
    - PR linked
  selected: tests green
  mode: review
commands:
  - framedGroup.select
  - framedGroup.copyFacts
  - framedGroup.openStory
facts:
  block.family: grouping
  block.variant: ready
  semanticValue.title: Release Checks
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Framing}\label{record-032-framing}

\texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} is the canonical compact side-panel surface for the currently selected thing. It should keep one active value obvious while supporting sections stay calmer and structured. That makes it a first-blocks proof point: an inspector panel is a reusable block-shaped composition, not an arbitrary box with hand-written strings.

This audit verifies the inspector family against real DOGFOOD story rendering, component-family doctrine, and mode-aware runtime behavior.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-032-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  TUI app authors building side panels for selected packages, records, rows, or rollout slices.
\item
  Docs readers checking how an inspector panel lowers when borders, color, and side-panel layout are not available.
\item
  Maintainers who need a focused regression proving inspector story metadata and design-system guidance stay aligned with runtime truth.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-032-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder can inspect the DOGFOOD inspector story and see current-selection emphasis plus compact supporting sections.
\item
  A reader can switch inspector variants through interactive, static, pipe, and accessible profiles while preserving the same semantic fields.
\item
  A maintainer can run one cycle test that ties \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} behavior, DOGFOOD story metadata, and component-family guidance together.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-032-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does DOGFOOD expose the inspector family through the \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} story?
\item
  Do variants cover both package-summary and rollout-review side-panel usage?
\item
  Do rich/static previews preserve titled containment and section rhythm?
\item
  Do pipe lowerings produce labeled plain text with one obvious current selection?
\item
  Do accessible lowerings linearize the same fields without relying on borders, color, or pane position?
\item
  Do component-family docs still position \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as side-panel context rather than a full guided recommendation or complex nested workflow?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-032-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Keep the existing \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r} story identity and \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s} coverage family id.
\item
  Render every inspector story variant in every canonical story profile.
\item
  Treat borders and box-drawing characters as visual-profile affordances only.
\item
  Keep pipe and accessible lowerings field-label-first and meaning-preserving.
\item
  Confirm \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} still matches the runtime story posture.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-032-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} proves the cycle doc carries the modern playback sections.
\item
  The test locates the DOGFOOD \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} story and verifies expected variants.
\item
  Every variant renders non-empty output in every documented profile.
\item
  Rich/static output includes titled box containment; pipe and accessible output do not depend on box drawing.
\item
  Pipe and accessible output preserve current selection, context, and section labels.
\item
  Component-family docs retain side-panel, current-selection, and compact section guidance.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-032-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist

  Add a DF-041 cycle test that renders the \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r} DOGFOOD story through the shared story protocol.
\item
  Read-test the inspector section in \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}.

\item
  Record any drift as follow-on backlog debt instead of widening this audit.

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-032-drift-check}

No runtime drift was found in this slice. \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} already renders boxed, titled containment in interactive/static profiles, lowers to labeled grouped text in pipe mode, and linearizes the same fields in accessible mode.

No follow-on backlog item is needed for this slice.

The inspector component did not need runtime changes. The important release work was turning current story truth into executable proof so future block and workspace work cannot quietly turn inspector panels into generic nested boxes or mini dashboards.

This follow-on six-pack turns choice, decision, peer navigation, progressive disclosure, and path progress audits into reusable Block contracts with schema-bound input and lower-mode facts.

The work follows a Design Thinking loop:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  observe DOGFOOD choice and navigation surfaces as product semantics, not visual widgets
\item
  frame each family as a named Block contract with explicit state and facts
\item
  prototype TUI and lower-mode shapes before treating implementation as landed
\item
  prove catalog, schema, render, command, story, and lowering behavior in tests
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-033-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  TUI authors who need reusable semantics for choices, decisions, peer navigation, disclosure state, and path progress.
\item
  DOGFOOD maintainers who need the Blocks preview page to show the next real component-family slice.
\item
  Tooling authors who need to inspect selection, current-step, checked-state, and disclosure facts without scraping terminal chrome.
\item
  Future declaration authors who need YAML or JSON IR targets over typed Block APIs rather than a second runtime.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-033-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder can import all six Blocks and inspect metadata, data requirements, command intents, schema descriptions, and ready story ids from the public barrel.
\item
  A reader can compare interactive/static output with pipe/accessibility lowerings and recover option identity, selected state, current route, disclosure state, and current step.
\item
  A maintainer can run one DF-046 cycle test that proves the six-pack is catalogued, schema-bound, rendered, documented, and lowering-stable.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-033-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-033-lower-modes}

Static mode keeps the same section structure as interactive mode and stays render-only.

Pipe mode lowers every Block to compact records:

\begin{CodeBlock}
SingleChoiceBlock
label: Output mode
options: interactive; pipe; accessible
selected: pipe
mode: radio
\end{CodeBlock}

\begin{CodeBlock}
PathProgressBlock
path: Setup; Blocks; Preview
current: Blocks
step: 2
total: 3
status: current
\end{CodeBlock}

Accessible mode lowers every Block to label-first prose:

\begin{CodeBlock}
SingleChoiceBlock
Label: Output mode
Options: interactive; pipe; accessible
Selected: pipe
Mode: radio
\end{CodeBlock}

\begin{CodeBlock}
PathProgressBlock
Path: Setup; Blocks; Preview
Current: Blocks
Step: 2
Total: 3
Status: current
\end{CodeBlock}

Every lower mode carries inspectable facts:

\begin{CodeBlock}
block = SingleChoiceBlock
block.rendered = true
block.family = input
block.variant = ready
block.mode = pipe
block.selected = pipe
semanticValue.label = Output mode
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Accessibility And Directionality}\label{record-033-accessibility-and-directionality}

The first slice does not add bespoke focus handling. The Blocks expose labels and section values so accessible output preserves choice state, current route, hidden-count state, and current-step state when visual affordances are removed. Text is stored as plain strings or string arrays, leaving locale and bidirectional rendering concerns to callers and localization adapters.

\section{Agent Inspectability}\label{record-033-agent-inspectability}

Agents and tests should inspect metadata, data contracts, schema descriptions, command intent ids, ready story ids, and lowering facts. They should not infer selected state, checked state, or current step from visual markers.

\section{Declarative IR Note}\label{record-033-declarative-ir-note}

The Bijou IR idea remains an adapter layer over this typed API. This cycle does not introduce a new YAML or JSON runtime, but it gives future IR work concrete targets:

\begin{CodeBlock}
block: SingleChoiceBlock
package: "@flyingrobots/bijou"
story: single-choice.ready
data:
  label: Output mode
  options:
    - interactive
    - pipe
    - accessible
  selected: pipe
  mode: radio
commands:
  - singleChoice.select
  - singleChoice.copyFacts
  - singleChoice.openStory
facts:
  block.family: input
  block.variant: ready
  semanticValue.label: Output mode
\end{CodeBlock}
