\chapter{DF-049 Audit multi-field and staged forms family across real surfaces}\label{record-034}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-049-audit-multi-field-and-staged-forms-family-across-real-surfaces.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DF-049 Audit multi-field and staged forms family across real surfaces
legend: DF
lane: design
priority: medium
keywords:
  - component-audit
  - dogfood
  - lowerings
  - forms

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-034-framing}

\texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} are the smallest form blocks that prove Bijou can model related user input as one coherent task. A group keeps related fields in one focused packet. A wizard keeps step boundaries and progress explicit when the task should unfold over time.

This audit verifies the existing \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d} DOGFOOD story against real story rendering, component-family doctrine, and mode-aware lowerings. It does not redesign the form runtime; it turns current story truth into executable release proof.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-034-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  TUI app authors composing setup, deploy, checkout, sign-up, and settings flows from first-party blocks.
\item
  Docs readers checking how grouped and staged forms behave when borders, color, and interactive focus are unavailable.
\item
  Maintainers who need a focused regression tying form-block story metadata, variants, and component-family guidance to real output.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-034-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder can inspect the DOGFOOD forms story and understand when to use a single grouped form versus a staged wizard.
\item
  A reader can switch both variants through interactive, static, pipe, and accessible profiles while preserving labels, values, summaries, and step state.
\item
  A maintainer can run one cycle test that proves form-block story metadata and design-system guidance have not drifted away from runtime behavior.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-034-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does DOGFOOD expose the family through the \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d} story?
\item
  Do variants cover both single-step grouped fields and staged wizard progress?
\item
  Do rich/static previews preserve visual containment and field rhythm?
\item
  Do pipe lowerings preserve sequential prompts, labels, values, summaries, and step intent?
\item
  Do accessible lowerings linearize labels and wizard progress without relying on borders, color, or visual grouping?
\item
  Do component-family docs still position \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as related data-collection blocks rather than generic layout containers?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-034-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Keep the existing \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d} story identity and \texttt{m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}s} coverage family id.
\item
  Render every grouped/staged form story variant in every canonical story profile.
\item
  Treat box drawing as visual-profile chrome only.
\item
  Keep pipe and accessible lowerings field-label-first and semantic-preserving.
\item
  Confirm \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} still matches the runtime story posture.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-034-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} proves the cycle doc carries the modern playback sections.

\item

\item
  Rich/static output includes visual containment; pipe and accessible output do not depend on box drawing.
\item
  Pipe and accessible output preserve form titles, labels, values, summaries, and wizard step state.
\item
  Component-family docs retain grouped form, staged flow, progress, summary, and accessibility guidance.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-034-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}

\item
  Read-test the multi-field and staged forms section in \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}.
\item
  Move the backlog note into \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/} and update the v6 lane pointer.
\item
  Record any drift as follow-on backlog debt instead of widening this audit.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-034-drift-check}

No runtime drift was found in this slice. The existing \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d} story already distinguishes grouped forms from staged flows, renders boxed field rhythm in interactive/static profiles, lowers to sequential labeled prompts in pipe mode, and linearizes step state in accessible mode.

No follow-on backlog item is needed for this slice.

\section{Playback}\label{record-034-playback}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED: the release lane had only a backlog note; no DF-049 playback test tied grouped and staged forms to real mode lowerings.
\item
  GREEN: the new cycle test renders both \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p} and \texttt{r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d} variants across interactive, static, pipe, and accessible profiles.
\item
  Rich/static previews preserve visual containment and field rhythm.
\item
  Pipe previews preserve labels, values, summaries, and wizard step intent without box drawing.
\item
  Accessible previews linearize the same facts with explicit current-step language for the wizard variant.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-034-retrospective}

The forms story did not need runtime changes. The useful release work was codifying the first-blocks contract: grouped and staged forms are semantic data-collection compositions, not string dumps or decorative boxes.

\section{Framing}\label{record-035-framing}

Motion and shader effects have become a real authoring surface, not a demo side quest. \texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} now has quad, Braille, and glyph-fit resolution modes, the raytrace helpers are available for app-owned shader scenes, and spring animation is stable under slow terminal pulses.

The DOGFOOD docs still treat that family as a small animated field. That is too thin for current repo truth. The story should prove the full family against real runtime behavior instead of trusting isolated fixtures or prose alone.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-035-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  TUI app authors who want expressive terminal visuals without inventing their own canvas, ray, or animation substrate.
\item
  Documentation readers evaluating whether motion, shader, and transition effects lower honestly across rich, static, pipe, and accessible output.
\item
  Maintainers who need regression tests that keep examples, docs, and exported APIs aligned as the rendering stack evolves.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-035-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist

\item

\item
  A maintainer can run a focused cycle test that proves \texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, transition shaders, \texttt{a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}/spring motion, and \texttt{t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} remain represented by real examples and DOGFOOD previews.
\end{enumerate}

The work follows a Design Thinking loop:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  observe the remaining DOGFOOD component families as reusable product semantics instead of visual one-offs
\item
  frame each family as a named Block contract with explicit data fields and facts
\item
  prototype interactive, static, pipe, and accessible shapes before treating the implementation as landed
\item
  prove catalog, schema, render, story, command, preview, and lowering behavior in tests
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-036-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  TUI authors who need reusable semantics for branding, primitives, comparisons, hierarchies, exploratory lists, and dependency views.
\item
  DOGFOOD maintainers who need the Blocks preview page to show the remaining component-family families as real examples, not future-audit placeholders.
\item
  Tooling authors who inspect selected ids, semantic values, and family facts without scraping terminal layout.
\item
  Future declarative IR authors who need stable typed targets for YAML or JSON declarations.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-036-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder can import all six Blocks and inspect metadata, data requirements, command intents, schema descriptions, and ready story ids from the public barrel.
\item
  A reader can move between visual, static, pipe, and accessible modes and recover brand, primitive, comparison, hierarchy, list, and dependency meaning without ANSI, borders, color, or animation.
\item
  A maintainer can run one DF-054 cycle test that proves the six-pack is catalogued, schema-bound, rendered, documented, and lowering-stable.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-036-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does each late-family audit now have a named Block contract instead of a broad review note?
\item
  Are required fields concrete enough for DOGFOOD previews and small enough for reuse?
\item
  Do lower modes expose stable facts for block identity, family, variant, mode, selected value, and semantic values?
\item
  Does the DOGFOOD Blocks page have sample slots for every new definition?
\item
  Does this keep future YAML/JSON IR as an adapter over typed Block APIs?
\end{itemize}

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-036-lower-modes}

Static mode keeps the same surface structure as interactive mode and stays render-only.

Pipe mode lowers every Block to a compact record:

\begin{CodeBlock}
BrandEmphasisBlock
brand: BIJOU
tagline: Terminal-native app blocks
decoration: accent rule
role: nonessential
selected: BIJOU
\end{CodeBlock}

\begin{CodeBlock}
TemporalDependencyBlock
title: Timeline
events: 09:00 build; 09:05 test; 09:10 publish
dependency: publish waits for test
selected: publish
dependsOn: test
\end{CodeBlock}

Accessible mode lowers every Block to label-first prose:

\begin{CodeBlock}
BrandEmphasisBlock
Brand: BIJOU
Tagline: Terminal-native app blocks
Decoration: accent rule
Role: nonessential
Selected: BIJOU
\end{CodeBlock}

\begin{CodeBlock}
TemporalDependencyBlock
Title: Timeline
Events: 09:00 build; 09:05 test; 09:10 publish
Dependency: publish waits for test
Selected: publish
Depends on: test
\end{CodeBlock}

Every lower mode carries inspectable facts:

\begin{CodeBlock}
block = BrandEmphasisBlock
block.rendered = true
block.family = branding
block.variant = ready
block.mode = pipe
block.selected = BIJOU
semanticValue.brand = BIJOU
\end{CodeBlock}

\begin{CodeBlock}
block = TemporalDependencyBlock
block.rendered = true
block.family = graph
block.variant = ready
block.mode = accessible
block.selected = publish
semanticValue.title = Timeline
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Accessibility And Directionality}\label{record-036-accessibility-and-directionality}

The first slice does not add bespoke focus behavior. The Blocks expose labels, selected values, and section values so accessible output preserves meaning when visual emphasis, indentation, dense columns, list focus, and graph arrows are removed. Text is stored as plain strings or string arrays, leaving locale, bidirectional rendering, and translation concerns to callers and localization adapters.

\section{Agent Inspectability}\label{record-036-agent-inspectability}

Agents and tests should inspect metadata, data contracts, schema descriptions, command intent ids, ready story ids, and lowering facts. They should not infer hierarchy depth from indentation, compare values from column positions, or dependency meaning from arrows.

\section{Declarative IR Note}\label{record-036-declarative-ir-note}

The Bijou IR idea remains an adapter layer over this typed API. This cycle does not introduce a new YAML or JSON runtime, but it gives future IR work concrete targets:

\begin{CodeBlock}
block: TemporalDependencyBlock
package: "@flyingrobots/bijou"
story: temporal-dependency.ready
data:
  title: Timeline
  events:
    - 09:00 build
    - 09:05 test
    - 09:10 publish
  dependency: publish waits for test
  selected: publish
  dependsOn: test
commands:
  - temporalDependency.select
  - temporalDependency.copyFacts
  - temporalDependency.openStory
facts:
  block.family: graph
  block.variant: ready
  block.selected: publish
  semanticValue.title: Timeline
\end{CodeBlock}

\chapter{DF-060 Audit viewport masking and scrollable inspection panes family across real surfaces}\label{record-037}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-060-audit-viewport-masking-and-scrollable-inspection-panes-family-across-real-surfaces.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DF-060 Audit viewport masking and scrollable inspection panes family across real surfaces
legend: DF
lane: design
priority: medium
keywords:
  - component-audit
  - dogfood
  - lowerings
  - viewport

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-037-framing}

Viewport masking is the family that proves overflow is owned by bounded panes, not by callers slicing strings after rendering. \texttt{v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} is the base masking primitive for structured surfaces, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} adds long-document position context, and \texttt{f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} adds workspace focus ownership. Their string counterparts remain explicit text-lowering paths.

This audit verifies the DOGFOOD \texttt{v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} story against real story rendering, component-family doctrine, and mode-aware lowerings. It also closes the story drift where DOGFOOD taught only the base viewport mask even though the family doc already included pager and focus-area panes.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-037-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  TUI app authors wrapping existing surfaces in bounded scroll regions.
\item
  Docs readers checking the distinction between masking, paging, and focused inspection panes.
\item
  Maintainers who need one focused regression tying viewport story metadata, variants, and design-system guidance to real output.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-037-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder can inspect DOGFOOD and see viewport mask, structured stack, pager, and focused pane variants in one family.
\item
  A reader can switch every variant through interactive, static, pipe, and accessible profiles while preserving scroll and focus context.
\item
  A maintainer can run one cycle test that proves viewport-family story metadata and family guidance have not drifted away from runtime behavior.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-037-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does DOGFOOD expose the family through the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} coverage id?
\item
  Do variants cover pure viewport masking, structured masking, pager status, and focus-area chrome?
\item
  Do rich/static previews keep bounded pane chrome visible?
\item
  Do pipe lowerings preserve sequential content and scroll/focus context without pretending hidden regions are interactive?
\item
  Do accessible lowerings linearize pane content with explicit position or focus facts?
\item
  Do component-family docs still cover viewport, pager, focus area, and the row-aware holdout boundary?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-037-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Keep the existing \texttt{v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} story identity and coverage family id.
\item
  Render every viewport-family story variant in every canonical story profile.
\item
  Treat scrollbars, gutters, and box drawing as visual-profile chrome only.
\item
  Keep pipe and accessible lowerings scroll-context-first and semantic-preserving.
\item
  Confirm \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} still matches the runtime story posture for viewport, pager, and focus-area primitives.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-037-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} proves the cycle doc carries the modern playback sections.
\item
  The test locates the DOGFOOD \texttt{v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} story and verifies expected variants.
\item
  Every variant renders non-empty output in every documented profile.
\item
  Rich/static output includes structured visual containment; pipe and accessible output do not depend on box drawing.
\item
  Pipe and accessible output preserve viewport scroll, pager line, and focus pane context.
\item
  Component-family docs retain viewport, pager, focus area, content guidance, lowering guidance, and the domain-specific row-aware boundary.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-037-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Extend the existing \texttt{v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} DOGFOOD story with pager and focused pane variants.
\item
  Add mode-aware constrained lowerings for the story so pipe/accessibility profiles expose scroll/focus facts as text rather than visual chrome.
\item
  Add a DF-060 cycle test that renders every variant through the shared story protocol.
\item

\end{enumerate}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-037-drift-check}

Runtime support already existed for the full family. The drift was in DOGFOOD: the story represented only \texttt{v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} while the design-system family also documented \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.

This slice fixes that by extending the story instead of filing follow-on debt. No runtime API changes were required.

\section{Playback}\label{record-037-playback}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED: the release lane had only a backlog note, and the DOGFOOD story did not visibly exercise pager or focused-pane variants.
\item
  GREEN: the new cycle test renders \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w}, and \texttt{f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e} variants across interactive, static, pipe, and accessible profiles.
\item
  Rich/static previews preserve scrollbars, status lines, focus gutters, and nested surface masking.
\item
  Pipe previews preserve viewport scroll, pager line, and focus context without box drawing.
\item
  Accessible previews linearize the same pane facts in reading order.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-037-retrospective}

The runtime did not need another overflow abstraction. The useful release work was making DOGFOOD tell the whole family story: mask structured surfaces, page long linear documents, and mark focused inspection panes without letting scroll chrome become semantic content.

The design follows a Design Thinking loop:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  observe the remaining release gaps through the live GitHub tracker instead of stale roadmap prose
\item
  frame the work around user-visible release truth and agent-inspectable release proof
\item
  prototype the title screen, BlockLab labels, table parity, lower modes, and workflow guards before treating the cycle as landed
\item
  prove the result with rendered DOGFOOD tests, package/API tests, docs tests, localization gates, and parsed workflow assertions
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-038-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer preparing v7 needs the issue tracker, roadmap, BEARING, title surface, and release proof to agree without manual reconciliation.
\item
  A TUI builder needs \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} to obey the same width constraints and lower-mode semantics already proven by \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  A component author needs the preview workstation to use a project-owned name, BlockLab, while legacy commands remain available during migration.
\item
  A review agent needs structured workflow assertions, stable release-title facts, and lower-mode output instead of brittle prose or raw string scans.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-038-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A DOGFOOD reader can open the docs app and see a v7 title surface that names the release identity, proof lanes, and navigation options at wide and narrow terminal widths.
\item
  A TUI author can use \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} with explicit width constraints and get output that fits like \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} while preserving row, column, value, and selected-cell facts in lower modes.
\item
  A maintainer can close the v7 issue lane with GitHub, BEARING, ROADMAP, CHANGELOG, workflow tests, BlockLab names, and docs all pointing to the same release truth.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-038-lower-modes}

The title surface should be backed by release metadata so every mode lowers from the same truth.

Static mode:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Bijou DOGFOOD release title. Release V7 Product Truth. Proof lanes: table parity, scoped Node I/O, BlockLab, release title.
\end{CodeBlock}

Pipe mode:

\begin{CodeBlock}
release_id  v7
release_title   V7 Product Truth
proof_lane  table parity
proof_lane  scoped Node I/O
proof_lane  BlockLab
proof_lane  release title
navigation_available    true
\end{CodeBlock}

Accessible mode:

\begin{CodeBlock}
DOGFOOD title screen for V7 Product Truth. Current release proof lanes are table parity, scoped Node I/O, BlockLab, and release title. Navigation remains available after the title.
\end{CodeBlock}

\texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} is the surface-native path, so this cycle proves bounded surface width rather than adding a new lowering contract. Semantic table facts remain owned by \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}:

\begin{CodeBlock}
row-id  bijou
column-id   status
cell-value  ready
layout-variant  fitted
selected-cell   bijou/status
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Runtime And API Contracts}\label{record-038-runtime-and-api-contracts}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD release title metadata should be a typed local data structure, not scattered strings in the renderer.
\item
  DOGFOOD visible title strings must go through the DOGFOOD localization catalog.
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} should share, reuse, or faithfully mirror the fitted table model already used by \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} instead of growing a second width algorithm.
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} docs must state that returned paths can be realpath normalized and that symlink escapes are rejected even when lexical prefixes appear valid.
\item
  Workflow tests should parse \texttt{.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}l} as YAML and inspect \texttt{j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s} structurally.
\item
  BlockLab should become the canonical human-facing name and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}*} the canonical agent-facing token family, while old \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k} scripts remain as compatibility aliases during this migration window.
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility, Localization, And Inspectability}\label{record-038-accessibility-localization-and-inspectability}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The title screen must expose release title and proof lanes as text, not only border art or color.
\item
  New DOGFOOD strings require \texttt{e\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{f\allowbreak{}r}, \texttt{e\allowbreak{}s}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e} catalog values.
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e} and \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} are part of the merge gate.
\item
  Agent-facing facts should include release id, release title, proof lane ids, navigation availability, table row ids, table column ids, and selected cell identity.
\item
  No title-screen behavior should depend on wall-clock time, network state, or live GitHub API data.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DF-061 Audit overlay primitives family across real surfaces}\label{record-039}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-061-audit-overlay-primitives-family-across-real-surfaces.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DF-061 Audit overlay primitives family across real surfaces
legend: DF
lane: design
priority: medium
keywords:
  - component-audit
  - dogfood
  - lowerings
  - overlays

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-039-framing}

Overlay primitives are the family for layered UI that is not ordinary document flow: \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, and \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}. They differ by interruption level. Tooltips explain locally, drawers supplement, modals block, and toasts announce transiently.

This audit verifies overlay primitive stories against real story rendering, component-family doctrine, and mode-aware lowerings. It also closes the story drift where DOGFOOD already had modal and toast examples, but did not visibly exercise drawer or tooltip primitives as part of the same overlay family.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-039-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  TUI app authors choosing the right overlay primitive instead of overusing modals or toasts.
\item
  Docs readers checking how layered UI lowers when z-order is unavailable.
\item
  Maintainers who need one focused regression tying overlay story metadata, variants, and design-system guidance to real output.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-039-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder can inspect DOGFOOD and see tooltip, drawer, modal, and toast primitives side by side as one overlay family.
\item
  A reader can switch every overlay primitive through interactive, static, pipe, and accessible profiles while preserving the right interruption level.
\item
  A maintainer can run one cycle test that proves overlay story metadata and design-system guidance have not drifted away from runtime behavior.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-039-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does DOGFOOD expose all four overlay primitives?
\item
  Do variants cover explanatory, supplemental, blocking, and transient overlay jobs?
\item
  Do rich/static previews keep layering and containment visible?
\item
  Do pipe lowerings avoid fake z-order and preserve plain prompt/event text?
\item
  Do accessible lowerings linearize overlay relationships to their owning context?
\item
  Do component-family docs still separate primitive overlays from the full notification system?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-039-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Keep \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l} and \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t} story identities while adding missing drawer and tooltip story coverage.
\item
  Ensure \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t} participates in the \texttt{o\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} coverage family while still retaining its lower-level transient-overlay coverage.
\item
  Render every overlay primitive story variant in every canonical story profile.
\item
  Treat borders, dimmed backdrops, anchor placement, and z-order as visual-profile chrome only.
\item
  Keep pipe and accessible lowerings plain, explicit, and semantic-preserving.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-039-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} proves the cycle doc carries the modern playback sections.
\item
  The test locates DOGFOOD stories for \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, and \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Every documented overlay variant renders non-empty output in every profile.
\item
  Rich/static output includes structured visual containment; pipe and accessible output do not depend on box drawing.
\item
  Constrained lowerings preserve blocking modal prompts, supplemental drawer context, local tooltip explanation, and transient toast events.
\item
  Component-family docs retain overlay primitive guidance and the boundary with notification system behavior.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-039-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add drawer and tooltip DOGFOOD stories under the overlay primitive family.
\item
  Add mode-aware constrained lowerings to modal and toast story variants.
\item
  Add a DF-061 cycle test that renders every overlay primitive through the shared story protocol.
\item
  Move the backlog note into \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/} and update the v6 lane pointer.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-039-drift-check}

Runtime support already existed for all four primitives. The drift was in DOGFOOD: \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} were visible, but \texttt{d\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} were only documented indirectly.

This slice fixes the drift by adding the missing stories and making constrained lowerings explicitly textual. No runtime API changes were required.

\section{Playback}\label{record-039-playback}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED: the release lane had only a backlog note, and DOGFOOD did not visibly exercise every overlay primitive.
\item
  GREEN: the new cycle test renders modal, drawer, tooltip, and toast stories across interactive, static, pipe, and accessible profiles.
\item
  Rich/static previews preserve layering, borders, anchors, and backdrop context.
\item
  Pipe previews preserve prompt, supplemental, explanation, and event content without box drawing.
\item
  Accessible previews linearize the same overlay facts in reading order.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-039-retrospective}

The useful release work was not inventing another overlay. It was making DOGFOOD teach the existing overlay hierarchy honestly: explain with a tooltip, supplement with a drawer, block with a modal, and announce briefly with a toast.

This audit verifies the family against real story rendering and runtime behavior. The point is not to invent another notice component. The point is to prove that \texttt{p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, and framed runtime notification routing all still describe one coherent system.

This audit verifies the existing DOGFOOD \texttt{a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l} story against real story rendering, component-family doctrine, and mode-aware lowerings. The existing \texttt{w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t} story already distinguishes split-pane context from grid dashboard composition, renders structured region geometry in interactive/static profiles, and lowers to region summaries in pipe/accessibility modes.

No follow-on backlog item is needed for this slice.

\section{Framing}\label{record-044-framing}

The data visualization family proves that Bijou can render dense numeric signals without making glyph art the only source of truth. \texttt{s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{b\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, and \texttt{p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} should use rich terminal geometry when available, then lower to explicit numeric summaries when visual density is unavailable.

This audit verifies the existing DOGFOOD data visualization stories against real story rendering, component-family doctrine, and mode-aware lowerings. It does not redesign charting; it turns current data-viz runtime truth into executable release proof.

\chapter{DF-067 Prove Responsive DOGFOOD Layout Variants}\label{record-045}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-067-prove-responsive-dogfood-layout-variants.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DF-067 Prove Responsive DOGFOOD Layout Variants
legend: DF
lane: design
priority: high
keywords:
  - dogfood
  - responsive
  - layout
  - variants
  - resize

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-045-framing}

DOGFOOD already responds mechanically to terminal resize events: the runtime updates viewport dimensions, the framed shell recomputes body geometry, and the current grid primitives solve new integer rectangles.

That is not enough.

The current docs shell keeps fixed sidebars and asks the middle track to absorb whatever space remains. That is valid geometry, but below useful widths it turns the app into a technically present three-column surface whose content is no longer the primary thing.

This cycle keeps the work DOGFOOD-scoped. It does not wait for the full RE-035 layout envelope runtime. It proves the editorial layer first: resize handling is mechanical, responsive layout is editorial.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-045-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Readers opening DOGFOOD in small terminals.
\item
  Maintainers validating layout doctrine against a real product surface.
\item
  Agents checking whether DOGFOOD remains useful at constrained sizes instead of merely nonblank.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-045-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  At wide sizes, a reader sees navigation, content, and metadata/variant context together.
\item
  At standard sizes, a reader keeps navigation and content while secondary metadata folds away.
\item
  At narrow sizes, content becomes primary while navigation remains reachable.
\item
  At tiny sizes, DOGFOOD becomes a single useful pane instead of a crushed multi-column layout.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-045-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does DOGFOOD classify terminal size into explicit layout variants?
\item
  Does \texttt{1\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}0} keep the wide three-region docs/product shape?

\item
  Does \texttt{7\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0} keep content primary and navigation reachable?
\item
  Does \texttt{5\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}4} render a single useful pane with no fake sidebars?
\item
  Do the guide pages and component explorer both obey the same variant policy?
\item
  Does resize update the variant and viewport state without requiring a restart?
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a pure \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})} helper returning: \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w}, or \texttt{t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}y}.
\item
  Store the current layout variant in DOGFOOD page models so framed page layout functions can select a layout tree without depending on render-time hacks.
\item
  Keep current wide layouts intact.
\item
  Fold guide metadata and component variants out of \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d} and \texttt{n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w} layouts.

\chapter{DF-069 - Block-Authored DOGFOOD}\label{record-046}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-069-block-authored-dogfood.md}\par}\smallskip

Linked legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF - DOGFOOD Field Guide}

\section{Sponsor human}\label{record-046-sponsor-human}

DOGFOOD should prove that Bijou applications can be authored from Blocks, not only that Blocks can be previewed inside DOGFOOD.

\section{Sponsor agent}\label{record-046-sponsor-agent}

An agent should be able to inspect DOGFOOD and identify the semantic blocks that make up the product surface without reverse-engineering bespoke render helpers.

\section{Hill}\label{record-046-hill}

DOGFOOD becomes a block-authored application at the semantic surface boundary: title screen, shell regions, navigation, articles, settings, story previews, block previews, and inspector panes are declared as Blocks. Components remain the lower-level rendering vocabulary inside those Blocks.

\section{Core Rule}\label{record-046-core-rule}

Blocks own product semantics. Components own leaf rendering.

That means this work should create and consume Blocks for surfaces such as:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  \texttt{N\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  \texttt{D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  \texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  \texttt{G\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}
\end{itemize}

It should not wrap every \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, or list row in a Block.

\section{Architecture}\label{record-046-architecture}

The target composition is:

\begin{CodeBlock}
DOGFOOD app
  -> AppFrame / AppShell composition
    -> page and region Blocks
      -> components
        -> surfaces
\end{CodeBlock}

The existing unidirectional data-binding rule still applies:

\begin{CodeBlock}
business logic / providers
  -> immutable snapshots
  -> binding frames
  -> blocks and views render
  -> command intents
  -> business logic owns the next state
\end{CodeBlock}

Block-authored DOGFOOD must not introduce hidden provider registries, callback backchannels, render-time refresh hooks, mutable view stores, or direct provider reads from rendering code.

\section{Storybook Implication}\label{record-046-storybook-implication}

The standalone Storybook app should stop being a parallel bespoke TUI. It should use the same framed shell path as DOGFOOD and expose a \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} contract so story preview work exercises the product composition model.

\section{Non-goals}\label{record-046-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  no full visual redesign of DOGFOOD
\item
  no attempt to convert every low-level component into a Block
\item
  no new provider lifecycle system
\item
  no new localization runtime
\item
  no hidden global block registry
\item
  no rendered AppShell policy invented outside existing contracts
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Posture}\label{record-046-accessibility-assistive-posture}

Block-authored DOGFOOD should make semantic regions easier to lower across interactive, static, pipe, and accessible modes. Blocks should preserve facts about navigation, content, settings, previews, and inspector state without requiring agents or assistive modes to parse terminal art.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-046-localization-directionality-posture}

Blocks should receive localized labels and copy through DOGFOOD's localization port, not through direct catalog access. Block metadata may describe the surface, but runtime-visible labels remain localized app data.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-046-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

Agents should be able to ask which DOGFOOD Blocks are active, what data requirements they declare, which command intents they expose, and which surface they render into.

\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/commands-change-state-effects-do-not.md}{Commands Change State, Effects Do Not}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are the Spec}
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-046-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Update BEARING so the next product gravity is block-authored DOGFOOD.
\item
  Add DOGFOOD-local block registry helpers for semantic app surfaces.
\item
  Add \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} and move Storybook toward the framed shell.
\item
  Add DOGFOOD Blocks for title, navigation, documentation article, settings, block preview, and guide inspector surfaces.
\item
  Prove the block-authored registry without rendering every block during discovery.
\item
  Keep visual changes incremental and scoped.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-046-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  behavior tests proving the BlockLab app is framed rather than bespoke
\item
  behavior tests proving DOGFOOD block registry discovery does not call render
\item
  behavior tests proving core DOGFOOD surfaces have Block definitions
\item
  behavior tests proving localization and command intent boundaries stay declarative
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback}\label{record-046-playback}

DF-069A lands the block-authored DOGFOOD contract layer:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD has a local, branded \texttt{D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}.
\item
  Registry discovery rejects loose block-shaped objects.
\item
  Registry discovery records surface ownership without calling \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  BlockLab now has a \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} contract and the interactive BlockLab entrypoint uses the AppFrame shell.
\item
  DOGFOOD surface blocks now cover title, navigation, documentation article, block preview, guide inspector, settings, and BlockLab workbench surfaces.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-046-retrospective}

This slice deliberately stops at semantic surface contracts and the BlockLab frame migration. It does not rewrite every DOGFOOD renderer yet, does not move provider lifecycle policy, and does not convert leaf components into Blocks.

The final review gate also tightened the DOGFOOD i18n debt scanner so framed BlockLab machine tokens such as key names, event discriminants, mode literals, pane overflow policy, tones, and internal thrown errors do not count as visible English copy. BlockLab labels and rendered text still count as localization debt until they move behind a localization port.

\chapter{DF-070 - DOGFOOD Block Product Polish}\label{record-047}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-070-dogfood-block-product-polish.md}\par}\smallskip

Linked legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF - DOGFOOD Field Guide}

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-047-sponsor-human}

DOGFOOD should stop feeling like a contract debugger for Blocks and start feeling like a terminal product authored from Blocks.

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-047-sponsor-agent}

An agent should be able to inspect DOGFOOD and see that semantic Blocks own the major product surfaces, while prose, navigation, preview, and settings behavior remain observable through tests instead of hand-audited screenshots.

\section{Hill}\label{record-047-hill}

DOGFOOD moves from ``Blocks are documented here'' toward ``DOGFOOD is materially built from Blocks.'' The first proof is product polish: word-aware prose wrapping, block-owned documentation and navigation surfaces, block-owned inspector/settings surfaces, and block/story preview parity without inventing new provider, lifecycle, localization, or callback rules.

\section{Core Rule}\label{record-047-core-rule}

Rendered DOGFOOD polish must consume existing contracts.

That means:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  prose wrapping belongs at text/prose boundaries, not arbitrary surface clipping
\item
  Blocks own semantic product regions
\item
  components remain the leaf rendering vocabulary
\item
  localization goes through the localization port
\item
  data flow stays unidirectional
\item
  story and block previews should share the same shell assumptions
\end{itemize}

\section{Ten-Slice Plan}\label{record-047-ten-slice-plan}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Refresh BEARING and cycle truth after DF-069 and DX-035 merged.
\item
  Add word-boundary prose wrapping behavior.
\item
  Route DOGFOOD prose surfaces through the word-aware wrapper.
\item
  Move \texttt{D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} onto the real DOGFOOD article render path.
\item
  Move \texttt{N\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} onto the real DOGFOOD navigation render path.
\item
  Move \texttt{G\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} onto the real DOGFOOD inspector render path.
\item
  Move \texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} onto the real DOGFOOD settings surface.
\item
  Persist DOGFOOD's selected locale behind the existing localization boundary.
\item
  Expand localization catalog coverage for the block-authored surfaces touched by this cycle.
\item
  Align DOGFOOD Blocks preview and Storybook preview posture so both expose rendered product examples without debug-only wrapper clutter.
\end{enumerate}

The cycle pauses after slice 5 for drift review before continuing.

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-047-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  no new provider lifecycle system
\item
  no hidden global block registry
\item
  no broad visual redesign
\item
  no conversion of every leaf component into a Block
\item
  no AppFrame rewrite
\item
  no localization runtime rewrite
\item
  no tests that assert prose documentation wording instead of rendered behavior
\end{itemize}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-047-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  behavior tests proving prose wrapping breaks at word boundaries where possible
\item
  behavior tests proving DOGFOOD article/navigation surfaces use the same rendered output paths their Blocks publish
\item
  behavior tests proving block discovery and preview indexing do not execute unrelated render paths
\item
  behavior tests proving locale persistence and catalog coverage changes remain behind the localization port
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-047-retrospective}

Not started.

\chapter{DF-071 - DOGFOOD Block-Authored Surfaces}\label{record-048}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-071-dogfood-block-authored-surfaces.md}\par}\smallskip

Linked legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF - DOGFOOD Field Guide}

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-048-sponsor-human}

DOGFOOD should increasingly feel like an app authored from semantic Blocks, not an app that has a Blocks documentation page on the side.

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-048-sponsor-agent}

An agent should be able to inspect DOGFOOD's product surfaces and understand which Block owns each semantic region without executing provider lifecycle, hidden registries, or view mutation paths.

\section{Hill}\label{record-048-hill}

DOGFOOD uses Blocks for visible app semantics across shell, docs, preview, settings, and workbench surfaces while preserving the existing component layer as the leaf rendering vocabulary.

DF-071 is not a visual redesign. It is a product-boundary pass: more visible DOGFOOD surfaces should be described, rendered, and verified through Blocks where the Block boundary is already stable.

\section{Core Rule}\label{record-048-core-rule}

Blocks own product semantics.

Components own leaf rendering.

Runtime and provider systems own lifecycle.

Localization owns text lookup through a port.

DF-071 may connect these layers, but it must not collapse them.

\section{Fifteen-Slice Plan}\label{record-048-fifteen-slice-plan}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Refresh BEARING after DF-070 landed.
\item
  Land this design checkpoint.
\item
  Add missing block-authored surface coverage for shell footer/status hints.
\item
  Route docs footer hint text through the footer/status Block.
\item
  Add block-authored landing/title behavior proof.
\item
  Route the landing DOGFOOD panel through \texttt{T\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} data.
\item
  Add a registry-backed DOGFOOD surface Block inventory page.
\item
  Add block-authored search surface coverage.
\item
  Route search chrome title text through the search Block seam without changing search mechanics.
\item
  Add block-authored notification center coverage.
\item
  Add block-authored performance HUD coverage.
\item
  Add block-authored keyboard help coverage.
\item
  Add block-authored command palette coverage.
\item
  Update docs and changelog with the shipped public DOGFOOD surface posture.
\item
  Run full validation, push, and open a PR.
\end{enumerate}

The plan can adapt if the code reveals a cleaner seam, but each slice must keep the same separation of concerns.

\section{Adaptation Note}\label{record-048-adaptation-note}

The top navigation seam is owned by the generic \texttt{A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} tab renderer. DF-071 therefore did not fork tab rendering inside DOGFOOD. Instead, it covered the frame-owned surfaces that already have stable semantic boundaries:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  footer hints
\item
  search title
\item
  notifications
\item
  performance HUD
\item
  keyboard help
\item
  command palette
\end{itemize}

The actual overlay renderers remain in \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i}. DOGFOOD now publishes local block contracts for those surfaces so the app can be inspected as a block-authored product without duplicating frame runtime behavior.

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-048-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  no new provider lifecycle system
\item
  no command dispatch rewrite
\item
  no hidden global block registry
\item
  no localization runtime rewrite
\item
  no conversion of leaf components into Blocks
\item
  no broad visual redesign
\item
  no metadata-only tests standing in for rendered behavior
\end{itemize}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-048-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  behavior tests proving routed surfaces render the user-visible text they claim to own
\item
  behavior tests proving block registries expose the new semantic surfaces without discovery-time rendering
\item
  behavior tests proving routed surfaces still preserve lowered-mode behavior
\item
  behavior tests proving localization access stays behind the existing port
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-048-retrospective}

DF-071 landed the first broad pass over DOGFOOD block-authored product surfaces. It added or routed:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}

  \texttt{N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}

  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} landing title data
\item
  a registry-backed DOGFOOD surface inventory page
\end{itemize}

The key restraint held: frame runtime surfaces remain rendered by \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i}, while DOGFOOD owns the semantic block contracts, data requirements, command intents, and visible documentation inventory.

\chapter{DF-072 DOGFOOD Release Title Artifact Gallery}\label{record-049}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-072-dogfood-release-title-artifact-gallery.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DF-072 DOGFOOD Release Title Artifact Gallery
legend: DF
lane: cool-ideas
priority: medium
issue: https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/289
keywords:
  - dogfood
  - release
  - release-title
  - title-gallery

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-049-framing}

Issue \#289 asks DOGFOOD to treat release title screens as first-class release artifacts instead of replacing the last title treatment in place. V7 shipped with \texttt{V\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h}; this follow-up adds a unique post-release treatment and keeps both artifacts visible through the Release page.

The design follows a Design Thinking loop: observe that release identity is valuable after the release lands, frame titles as reusable proof artifacts, prototype a gallery that keeps the newest treatment first, and prove every title through interactive, static, pipe, accessible, and localized output.

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-049-sponsor-human}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer reviewing the release wants to see that v7 was published and that follow-up work is intentionally tracked instead of silently changing the historical title.
\item
  A DOGFOOD reader wants the Release page to open with the current title while still making the original release title discoverable.
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-049-sponsor-agent}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A review agent needs release-title metadata, lower-mode facts, and localization keys in one typed structure instead of scattered prose.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-049-hill}

A DOGFOOD reader can open the Release guide and see a latest-first title gallery whose current item is a unique \texttt{V\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e} post-release title screen, while the original \texttt{V\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h} artifact remains available with its own lower-mode facts.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-049-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does the Release guide open with the current title treatment?
\item
  Does the historical \texttt{V\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h} artifact remain selectable?
\item
  Do static, pipe, and accessible modes all lower from the same typed release-title record?
\item
  Does every new visible string have source rows and generated catalogs for all supported DOGFOOD locales?
\item
  Does compact interactive rendering stay within the caller's requested width?
\end{itemize}

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-049-current-truth}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} is already published.
\item
  The strict \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} GitHub milestone has no open issues.
\item
  Issue \#289 is open in the Beyond milestone and already describes the gallery shape this patch should land.
\item
  DOGFOOD currently has one release-title metadata object, one Release guide, and localized strings for that single title.
\end{itemize}

\section{Product Shape}\label{record-049-product-shape}

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-049-lower-modes}

Static mode keeps the title useful without border art:

Navigation remains available after the title.
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Runtime And API Contract}\label{record-049-runtime-and-api-contract}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Release-title data is represented by typed \texttt{D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} records.
\item
  \texttt{D\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}Y} is latest-first.
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}E} points at the current title treatment.
\item
  Rendering defaults to the current title but accepts an explicit historical title for stable artifact playback.
\item
  DOGFOOD Release guides are generated from the gallery, not manually copied per title.
\end{itemize}

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-049-linked-invariants}

\chapter{DF-073 Raster-to-Glyph Title Art}\label{record-050}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-073-raster-to-glyph-title-art.md}\par}\smallskip
