\section{Framing}\label{record-050-framing}

Issue \#303 asks the current DOGFOOD landing screen to carry a unique \texttt{V\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e} release identity. The first prototype used a textual wake ribbon; the current direction is stronger: render a deterministic stacked sine-wave wake as the animated title background and use the committed \texttt{B\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}g} wordmark as a background-transparent glyph mask in complementary colors.

The design follows a Design Thinking loop: observe that terminal title art is most useful when it can be generated, inspected, tested, and lowered; frame the problem as a reusable raster adapter rather than a one-off DOGFOOD paint pass; prototype a deterministic \texttt{R\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} filter for vector and image masks; rasterize the committed SVG wordmark without adding a browser canvas dependency; and prove the result with synthetic-frame tests plus DOGFOOD rendered-frame tests.

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-050-sponsor-human}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer opening DOGFOOD after \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} wants the first screen to feel release-specific without becoming a blocking splash page.
\item
  A visual designer should be able to provide an image, generated frame, or procedural RGBA buffer and choose the terminal character set used to render it.
\item
  A reader should still see the normal DOGFOOD entry point, prompt, footer controls, and release documentation route.
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-050-sponsor-agent}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A review agent needs the release title, raster filter contract, renderer mode, charset, pulse behavior, and lower modes to remain inspectable through existing artifacts and tests.
\item
  A future capture/export agent should be able to feed decoded frames through the same primitive without depending on browser canvas or VHS.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-050-hill}

A DOGFOOD reader can open the landing title screen and see \texttt{V\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e} named in the entry panel while stacked sine-wave glyph strata fill the terminal and the \texttt{B\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}g} wordmark tints those foreground glyphs in complementary colors without painting an opaque background box. Braille is one supported glyph mode, but the renderer can also use custom density character sets such as \texttt{/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{}Z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}?\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}.}. The screen remains pulse-driven, deterministic, bounded by the current landing quality profiles, and lowerable through existing release-title facts.

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-050-current-truth}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{V\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e} is already the current release-title artifact.
\item
  The landing renderer is already pulse-driven, cached, and quality-bucketed.
\item
  \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i} already has shader-based \texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} output for cell, quad, Braille, and fitted-glyph resolutions.
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} already establishes density ramps and coverage fitting.
\item
  Static, pipe, and accessible release-title output already comes from \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\end{itemize}

\section{Product Shape}\label{record-050-product-shape}

\subsection{Wide Landing Screen}\label{record-050-wide-landing-screen}

The stacked sine-wave wake occupies the first-viewport title surface. It uses the existing landing pulse shader and quality buckets, so the field stays animated without adding a new image decode path or GPU dependency. Wake colors are written into cell backgrounds while the density glyphs keep the surface geometry stable with matching foreground colors. The visible Bijou wordmark is rasterized from \texttt{a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}g}, fit to the terminal cell aspect, and used as a background-transparent mask that writes SVG glyphs without replacing existing backgrounds. The wordmark letters ride a staggered sine wave and tint their foreground fill from the landing ramps, so the logo can animate without owning a rectangular background. The lower FlyingRobots wordmark is read from \texttt{a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t}, treats Braille blank cells as transparent holes, fits the visible logo glyphs to the available landing width, preserves the underlying cell background, and paints visible Braille glyphs with the opposite foreground color of that preserved background. This keeps the mark transparent through modal dimming because the logo does not own a rectangular background fill. FlyingRobots fades away after the first three seconds, leaving the Bijou wordmark, wake, release panel, prompt, footer, and version marker as the stable title composition.

The title screen owns only title-screen controls. \texttt{E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r} is the only key that continues into the DOGFOOD documentation shell; backtick toggles the perf HUD in place, \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} / \texttt{q} use the shell quit policy, arrows and number keys adjust landing presentation, and other keys do not secretly route into docs. Pressing \texttt{E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r} switches the model directly to the docs route without a title-to-docs transition. That hard cut keeps the first documentation frame legible instead of briefly painting decorative raster residue over product content.

\begin{CodeBlock}
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                         BIJOU                                                |
|                                                                              |
|  ░░░████░░░░████░░████░░░░████░░░░████░░████░░░░████░░░░████░░              |
|  ░███░░░████░░░░████░░░████░░░████░░░░████░░░████░░░████░░░                 |
|  █░░████░░░████░░░░████░░░████░░░████░░░░████░░░████░░░████                |
|                                                                              |
|  + DOGFOOD / V7 Launch Wake ----------------------------------------------+ |
|  | Documentation Of Good Foundational Onboarding and Discovery             | |
|  +-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ |
|                                                                              |
|                              Press [Enter]                                  |
| Esc/q quit ...                                      60 fps - auto/full v7.0.0 |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
\end{CodeBlock}

The prompt keeps the localized \texttt{P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}]} text while using a stronger foreground gradient over the \texttt{E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r} letters than over the surrounding line.

\subsection{Small Landing Screen}\label{record-050-small-landing-screen}

Small terminals keep the title identity and use fewer glyph cells.

\begin{CodeBlock}
+------------------------------------------+
|    ░░████░░███░░████░░███░░████        |
|    ██░░░████░░███░░████░░███░░█        |
| + DOGFOOD / V7 Launch Wake ------------+ |
| | Documentation Of Good Foundational... | |
| +---------------------------------------+ |
|              Press [Enter]               |
| Esc/q quit                auto/compact    |
+------------------------------------------+
\end{CodeBlock}

\subsection{Lower Modes}\label{record-050-lower-modes}

The art is decorative. Lower modes keep exposing semantic release facts.

\begin{CodeBlock}
pipe:
  release_id=v7.0.0
  release_title="V7 Launch Wake"
  release_motif="launch wake"

accessible:
  DOGFOOD opens on the V7 Launch Wake release title. The interactive
  screen includes decorative raster title art rendered as terminal glyphs.
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Raster Adapter}\label{record-050-raster-adapter}

The primitive belongs in \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i} so DOGFOOD is only the first consumer.

\begin{CodeBlock}
RgbaFrame
  -> fit source pixels into target cell grid
  -> sample brightness/alpha/color per cell or sub-cell
  -> choose renderer:
       charset: density ramp from custom characters
       braille: 2x4 dot mask
       quad:    2x2 quadrant mask
  -> emit Bijou Surface
\end{CodeBlock}

\subsection{Input}\label{record-050-input}

\begin{CodeBlock}
interface RgbaFrame {
  width: number;
  height: number;
  data: Uint8ClampedArray | readonly number[];
}
\end{CodeBlock}

The public TUI primitive accepts already-decoded RGBA. DOGFOOD keeps SVG rasterization in the example app layer so the core package contract stays deterministic and dependency-free.

\subsection{Renderer Modes}\label{record-050-renderer-modes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t}: render each output cell with a density ramp. The caller can pass a custom glyph string such as \texttt{/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{}Z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}?\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}.} and choose whether it is ordered dark-to-light or light-to-dark.
\item
  \texttt{b\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}: render each output cell with a 2x4 Braille mask sampled from darkness/alpha.
\item
  \texttt{q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d}: render each output cell with a 2x2 quadrant mask sampled from darkness/alpha.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Fit Modes}\label{record-050-fit-modes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t}: preserve aspect ratio, fill the target, crop overflow, and center both axes.
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n}: preserve aspect ratio and letterbox with empty cells.
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h}: map the frame directly into the requested grid.
\end{itemize}

\texttt{c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o} is the visual width divided by height of one terminal cell. The default is \texttt{1} for square-cell math. DOGFOOD uses \texttt{0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}5} for the V7 SVG wordmark mask so the rendered logo fits the visible iTerm-style viewport instead of looking vertically stretched.

\subsection{Color Modes}\label{record-050-color-modes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e}: only glyphs.
\item
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}g}: average visible source pixels into foreground RGB.
\item
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g}: average visible/dark pixels into foreground and light pixels into background when available.
\end{itemize}

\section{Determinism And Performance}\label{record-050-determinism-and-performance}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  No browser canvas, wall clock, external image decoder, or GPU dependency is required.
\item
  DOGFOOD uses the existing pulse timestamp and quality frame-step quantization.
\item
  DOGFOOD computes the stacked sine-wave wake from quantized landing pulse time and current terminal dimensions, then paints it through the existing landing shader.
\item
  DOGFOOD reads \texttt{a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}g} once, rasterizes the wordmark into a cached mask per terminal size, and uses the mask to write foreground glyphs without replacing the underlying backgrounds.
\item
  DOGFOOD derives the Bijou logo row offsets, fill colors, FlyingRobots fade, and prompt gradient from quantized landing pulse time.
\item
  Target dimensions are bounded by landing quality profiles before rendering.
\item
  Cache keys include viewport, theme, quality, quantized time, and FPS badge state, preserving the existing landing frame cache behavior.
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Posture}\label{record-050-accessibility-assistive-posture}

The raster title art is decorative in interactive mode. Assistive output must not depend on parsing glyph art. It continues to rely on the release title, motif, proof lanes, and accessible release prose.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-050-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

Agents should be able to prove the slice by checking:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the current release title appears on the landing frame;
\item
  raster art uses the configured renderer and charset;
\item
  pulse changes the title art deterministically;
\item
  raw RGBA filter tests cover charset, Braille, quad, fit, color, and invalid charset behavior;
\item
  the stacked sine-wave wake remains the visible landing background;
\item
  pipe/accessibility release facts remain sourced from release-title metadata.
\end{itemize}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-050-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED: \texttt{r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} does not exist or is not exported.
\item
  RED: custom charset rendering cannot map a synthetic black/white frame.
\item
  RED: invalid charsets are not rejected.
\item
  RED: Braille rendering cannot map a single top-left subpixel to dot 1.
\item
  RED: terminal \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t} mode stretches or letterboxes instead of centered fill-cropping.
\item
  RED: terminal \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t} mode assumes square cells and crops the wrong axis in typical tall-cell terminals.
\item
  RED: DOGFOOD landing frame does not render enough stacked sine-wave glyph art.
\item
  RED: the committed \texttt{B\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}g} wordmark is not rasterized into the rendered landing frame.
\item
  RED: the committed \texttt{B\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}g} wordmark replaces backgrounds or paints transparent SVG pixels instead of acting as a background-transparent mask.
\item
  RED: the lower FlyingRobots wordmark is generated from the old wide text assets instead of \texttt{a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t}.
\item
  RED: pressing backtick on the landing title enters the docs instead of toggling the shell perf HUD in place.
\item
  RED: the landing title perf HUD omits shell HUD rows or reports a permanently zero frame time because the root DOGFOOD render loop is not hydrating timing telemetry.
\item
  RED: DOGFOOD landing still paints the old procedural BIJOU title over the wake field.
\item
  RED: non-Enter keys route from the title screen into the docs shell.
\item
  RED: the lower FlyingRobots wordmark stays visible after the three-second fade window.
\item
  RED: the Bijou SVG title mask is static instead of moving each letter through a staggered sine-wave row offset and animated fill color.
\item
  RED: the \texttt{P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}]} prompt does not draw attention to \texttt{E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r} with a gradient foreground.
\item
  RED: pressing Enter leaves any title-to-docs transition state or decorative transition artifact instead of hard-cutting to docs.
\end{itemize}

\section{Validation}\label{record-050-validation}

\section{Playback}\label{record-050-playback}

This slice lands when DOGFOOD has a visible, localized \texttt{V\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e} landing identity and a deterministic raster-to-glyph title treatment, without adding new strings, bypassing the landing cache, adding image decoding dependencies, or changing lower-mode release facts.

\section{Linked Work}\label{record-051-linked-work}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  GitHub Issue: \#321
\item
  Inspiration: \url{https://github.com/javierbyte/fluid-triangle}
\item
  Prior title art: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-073-raster-to-glyph-title-art.md}{DF-073 Raster To Glyph Title Art}
\item
  Portable rendering direction: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-042-shared-ui-scene-ir-and-bijou-render-target.md}{DX-042 Shared UI Scene IR And Bijou Render Target}
\item
  Portable endpoint direction: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-043-portable-bijou-blocks-and-multi-endpoint-ir.md}{DX-043 Portable Bijou Blocks And Multi-Endpoint IR}
\item
  Related renderer experiments: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/RE-031-raytrace-shader-kernel.md}{RE-031 Raytrace Shader Kernel}, \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/RE-032-fit-cell-glyphs-from-coverage.md}{RE-032 Fit Cell Glyphs From Coverage}
\end{itemize}

This document is a planning artifact. It does not claim a GPU renderer, Geordi packed-cell target, browser endpoint, or new title screen implementation already exists in this repository.

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-051-decision-summary}

Bijou should design a future DOGFOOD title screen around a live fluid field moving around a triangular obstacle, rendered as terminal glyphs. The immediate Bijou work should define the title-scene contract, deterministic CPU fallback, theme-token policy, and cell-level proof. The high-end renderer should be Geordi-backed when the shared render pipeline is ready.

The intended long-term flow is:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Fluid Title Scene Spec
  -> deterministic field state
    -> Bijou CPU glyph renderer
      -> Bijou Surface
        -> terminal

Fluid Title Scene Spec
  -> Geordi fluid/shader endpoint
    -> PackedBijouCells or image witness
      -> Bijou Surface or browser/image output
\end{CodeBlock}

The goal is not to copy a browser demo into DOGFOOD. The goal is to turn the idea into a Bijou-native release-title system with deterministic witnesses and a future GPU render endpoint.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-051-sponsored-human}

A Bijou maintainer wants a memorable title screen that feels alive, branded, and release-specific without making DOGFOOD startup flaky, slow, or impossible to test.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-051-sponsored-agent}

An agent wants a deterministic scene description, frame inputs, glyph outputs, and render receipts so it can explain title-screen pixels and terminal cells without depending on screenshots or manual terminal observation.

\section{Hill}\label{record-051-hill}

DOGFOOD can show a fluid triangle title screen where the fluid motion, glyph density, color tokens, and input behavior are deterministic under test, while the production renderer can later upgrade from a Bijou CPU path to a Geordi-backed GPU path without changing the title scene's product contract.

\section{Inspiration Boundary}\label{record-051-inspiration-boundary}

The reference project is useful because it combines:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  fluid-like motion
\item
  a triangular obstacle
\item
  ASCII rendering
\item
  per-column character sequences
\item
  a playful launch-screen posture
\end{itemize}

Bijou should borrow the interaction and rendering concept, not the browser runtime assumptions.

The reference README states that its simulation code comes from Ten Minute Physics and that the project is MIT licensed. If Bijou ports substantial code from the reference or from the underlying Ten Minute Physics simulation, the ported file must preserve the relevant MIT attribution and copyright notice. The preferred first implementation is an original Bijou renderer inspired by the concept.

\section{Title Concept}\label{record-051-title-concept}

The title screen should feel like a fluid gate opening around a triangle:

\begin{CodeBlock}
..............................................................................
....@@@@@###WWWW9876????abc;:+=-,._       _.,-=+:;cba????6789WWWW###@@@@@....
...@@@###WWW9876????abc;:+=-,._          /\          _.,-=+:;cba????6789W....
..@@###WW9876????abc;:+=-,._            /  \            _.,-=+:;cba????67....
..@###W9876????abc;:+=-,._             /    \             _.,-=+:;cba????....
..@@###WW9876????abc;:+=-,._           \    /           _.,-=+:;cba????67....
...@@@###WWW9876????abc;:+=-,._         \  /         _.,-=+:;cba????6789....
....@@@@@###WWWW9876????abc;:+=-,._      \/      _.,-=+:;cba????6789WWW....
..............................................................................

                                  BIJOU
                              Press [Enter]
\end{CodeBlock}

The actual renderer should not draw this literal mockup. This is a spatial intent sketch:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  fluid surrounds a central triangular collider
\item
  density changes map to glyph ramps
\item
  the BIJOU mark remains readable above or inside the field
\item
  the Enter prompt remains clear and localized
\item
  the perf HUD and quit controls keep their existing ownership
\end{itemize}

\section{Scene Model}\label{record-051-scene-model}

The title should be modeled as data before it is rendered.

\begin{CodeBlock}
type FluidTitleSceneSpec = {
  id: 'dogfood.fluid-triangle-title';
  version: 1;
  seed: number;
  cols: number;
  rows: number;
  quality: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'auto';
  themeMode: 'dark' | 'light';
  triangle: {
    centerX: number;
    centerY: number;
    radius: number;
    rotation: number;
  };
  glyphRamps: readonly string[];
  titleKey: 'dogfood.title.bijou';
  promptKey: 'dogfood.title.pressEnter';
};
\end{CodeBlock}

The scene spec owns intent. Renderers own lowering.

\section{Renderer Targets}\label{record-051-renderer-targets}

\subsection{Bijou CPU Renderer}\label{record-051-bijou-cpu-renderer}

The first implementation should be a deterministic Bijou CPU renderer. It does not need to be a full fluid solver. It needs to produce the right motion language, stay bounded, and be testable.

Acceptable first algorithms:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  advected scalar density field
\item
  curl-noise-like deterministic flow
\item
  lightweight particle splat field
\item
  simplified stable fluid pass
\end{itemize}

The CPU renderer should emit:

\begin{CodeBlock}
FluidTitleSceneSpec + frame index
  -> FluidTitleFrame
    -> Surface
    -> FluidTitleReceipt
\end{CodeBlock}

\subsection{Geordi GPU Renderer}\label{record-051-geordi-gpu-renderer}

The intended high-end path is Geordi-rendered:

\begin{CodeBlock}
FluidTitleSceneSpec
  -> Geordi fluid/shader endpoint
    -> rgba image target
    -> PackedBijouCells target
    -> frame witness
\end{CodeBlock}

The Geordi endpoint should be allowed to compute richer fluid motion, higher resolution fields, better collider interaction, and image/video witnesses. Bijou should consume its output through a declared target profile rather than special-case a browser canvas.

\subsection{Low Mode}\label{record-051-low-mode}

Low mode must remain useful without GPU support.

\begin{CodeBlock}
seeded density wave
  -> glyph ramp
    -> token colors
      -> Surface
\end{CodeBlock}

Low mode should be cheap enough for CI snapshots and slow terminals.

\section{Quality Modes}\label{record-051-quality-modes}

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Mode
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Renderer
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Purpose
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\texttt{l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w} & Bijou CPU density wave & CI, SSH, constrained terminals \\
\texttt{m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m} & Bijou CPU particle or scalar field & default local terminal \\
\texttt{h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h} & Geordi GPU endpoint when available & release capture, browser/image witness \\
\texttt{a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o} & runtime choice & best available mode under frame budget \\
\end{longtable}
}

\texttt{a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o} must degrade deterministically by recorded facts:

\begin{CodeBlock}
{
  "requestedQuality": "auto",
  "selectedQuality": "medium",
  "reason": "geordi-endpoint-unavailable",
  "frameBudgetMs": 16
}
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Theme And Color Policy}\label{record-051-theme-and-color-policy}

The renderer must use theme tokens rather than raw title-screen colors.

Candidate tokens:

\begin{CodeBlock}
title.fluid.bg
title.fluid.low
title.fluid.mid
title.fluid.high
title.triangle.edge
title.triangle.fill
title.logo.fg
title.prompt.fg
title.prompt.enter.fg
\end{CodeBlock}

The glyph ramp and color ramp should be separate:

\begin{CodeBlock}
density -> glyph
density -> token/color
\end{CodeBlock}

This avoids the prior title-screen failure mode where a visual layer appeared to set the wrong background because glyph, foreground, and background channels were not explicit enough.

\section{Input Contract}\label{record-051-input-contract}

The title screen must keep the current input discipline:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r} proceeds to DOGFOOD.
\item
  Backtick toggles the normal shell perf HUD.
\item
  \texttt{q} opens the normal quit confirmation.
\item
  Theme or quality controls may remain title-owned only if documented.
\item
  No other ordinary key should accidentally skip the title.
\end{itemize}

Future optional interactions can perturb the field:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  mouse move nudges velocity
\item
  arrow keys shift the triangle
\item
  terminal resize reseeds layout while preserving deterministic frame facts
\end{itemize}

Those interactions are not required for the first slice.

\section{Localization And Directionality}\label{record-051-localization-and-directionality}

The visible title and prompt must be localization-backed strings. The fluid field itself is visual and does not require localization, but lower modes should expose the string keys.

RTL posture:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The prompt should use the app's existing text direction rules.
\item
  The fluid field can remain spatially symmetric.
\item
  Per-column glyph ramps should not encode English-only words in default mode.
\end{itemize}

The reference project's per-column letter sequences are useful as a visual trick, but a Bijou default should not rely on hidden English text in the fluid field.

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-051-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

The title screen must not be the only source of release information.

Required posture:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  prompt remains static enough to read
\item
  low-motion mode can freeze or heavily slow the field
\item
  status/lower-mode facts identify the release title
\item
  perf HUD remains accessible from the title screen
\item
  the screen does not flash at unsafe contrast/frequency patterns
\end{itemize}

\section{Agent Inspectability}\label{record-051-agent-inspectability}

Every deterministic render pass should be able to emit a receipt:

\begin{CodeBlock}
{
  "sceneId": "dogfood.fluid-triangle-title",
  "frame": 120,
  "seed": 700,
  "renderer": "bijou-cpu-density",
  "quality": "medium",
  "triangle": { "centerX": 80, "centerY": 18, "radius": 9 },
  "glyphRampHash": "fnv1a32:...",
  "surfaceHash": "fnv1a32:...",
  "tokenRefs": [
    "title.fluid.low",
    "title.fluid.mid",
    "title.fluid.high",
    "title.prompt.enter.fg"
  ]
}
\end{CodeBlock}

For Geordi output, the receipt should add endpoint facts:

\begin{CodeBlock}
{
  "renderer": "geordi-fluid-gpu",
  "endpoint": "packed-bijou-cells",
  "shaderHash": "sha256:...",
  "packedCellsHash": "fnv1a32:...",
  "witnessHash": "sha256:..."
}
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-051-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Does the first frame read as Bijou before animation is observed?
\item
  Does \texttt{E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r} remain the only key that proceeds to DOGFOOD?
\item
  Does the prompt stay legible at 80x24 and larger terminals?
\item
  Can the title run in low mode without Geordi?
\item
  Can a test prove the triangle collider leaves a stable void or edge?
\item
  Can a receipt explain the selected renderer, quality, seed, tokens, and output hash?
\item
  Can the Geordi endpoint later replace the high-quality renderer without changing title-screen input behavior?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-051-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add the scene spec and receipt types.
\item
  Add a deterministic CPU low-mode density renderer.
\item
  Add glyph-ramp and theme-token lowering into \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  Add title-screen integration behind a release-title switch.
\item
  Preserve existing perf HUD, quit, and Enter-only routing contracts.
\item
  Add a low-motion/frozen frame path.
\item
  Add tests for frame determinism, prompt visibility, key routing, and token use.
\item
  Add Geordi endpoint target profile once packed-cell or image witness support is ready.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-051-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Given the same spec, seed, size, and frame, the CPU renderer produces the same \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h}.
\item
  Given different frame indexes, at least one fluid-region cell changes while the prompt remains stable.
\item
  Given 80x24, the prompt and title are visible and not overwritten by fluid cells.
\item
  Given non-Enter printable key input, DOGFOOD remains on the title route.
\item
  Given \texttt{E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}, DOGFOOD proceeds to the main docs route.
\item
  Given backtick, the normal perf HUD toggles while the title route remains active.
\item
  Given low-motion mode, repeated frames produce either identical output or a documented bounded change.
\item
  Given missing Geordi endpoint, \texttt{a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o} selects a Bijou CPU renderer and emits a reason fact.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-051-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  No browser canvas dependency in DOGFOOD startup.
\item
  No required GPU path for CI.
\item
  No direct code port from the reference project in the design slice.
\item
  No change to the public title-screen skip contract beyond preserving Enter-only proceed.
\item
  No claim that this implements shared UI scene IR.
\end{itemize}

\section{Slice Plan}\label{record-051-slice-plan}

\section{Closeout Notes}\label{record-051-closeout-notes}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-075-dogfood-post-release-polish.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF - DOGFOOD}

\section{Linked Work}\label{record-052-linked-work}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  GitHub Issue: \#334
\item
  Related future release-story work: \#335
\item
  Related future affordance work: \#336
\end{itemize}

This document scopes a bounded post-release polish cycle. It does not reopen the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} feature train and it does not claim the broader V8 Runtime Graph and Scene IR product surface.

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-052-decision-summary}

DOGFOOD should absorb the three most visible post-release polish findings from the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} sanity pass without expanding into a broad shell redesign:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Disable the hidden double-\texttt{T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b} footer toggle until the AppShell has a visible command, animation, and restore affordance.
\item
  Restyle the quit confirmation so it is compact, themed, aligned, and easy to answer in the default theme.
\item
  Make the Blocks section lead with \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}, because that is the most alive interactive proof of what Blocks are.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-052-sponsored-human}

A DOGFOOD user wants the docs app to feel deliberate after \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}: no hidden state that leaves terminal background behind, no awkward quit prompt, and a Blocks page that immediately demonstrates an interactive block instead of starting on descriptive prose.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-052-sponsored-agent}

An agent wants deterministic behavior to assert: footer visibility should not change through undocumented key timing, the quit dialog should have stable themed geometry, and the Blocks default route should identify the same guide id that renders the interactive counter proof.

\section{Hill}\label{record-052-hill}

DOGFOOD can start the post-\texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} era with a cleaner shell and a stronger Blocks first impression while keeping the patch small, testable, and isolated from V8 product-contract work.

\section{Scope}\label{record-052-scope}

\subsection{Disable Hidden Footer Toggle}\label{record-052-disable-hidden-footer-toggle}

The current hidden double-\texttt{T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b} footer toggle is not discoverable. When hidden, it can expose uncolored terminal background and does not explain how to recover the footer. This cycle should remove that key path from normal DOGFOOD/AppShell input handling. \texttt{T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b} should remain the normal focus traversal key.

This does not forbid a future footer command. A future version can reintroduce footer visibility as an explicit command with visible state, animation, help text, and theme-safe repaint behavior.

\subsection{Restyle Quit Confirmation}\label{record-052-restyle-quit-confirmation}

The quit confirmation should render as a compact modal rather than a tall, skinny prompt. Its background, border, title, body, and actions should use the selected frame theme instead of leaving unthemed terminal patches.

The action labels must be readable in the default DOGFOOD theme. The dialog should keep the existing command contract: confirm quits, reject closes the dialog, and normal app state remains underneath.

\subsection{Counter-First Blocks}\label{record-052-counter-first-blocks}

The Blocks section should open directly on \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}. Selecting the \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w} parent row should also route to \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}, making the preview group demonstrate an interactive block first.

Static and descriptive block previews remain available below it. The prior navigation fix that lets focus move from the first preview child back to the \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w} parent row must not regress.

\section{Out Of Scope}\label{record-052-out-of-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \#335 release-story surfaces: What's New, GraphQL proof, and CHANGELOG viewer.
\item
  \#336 future affordances: theme hotkey, tab badges, tutorial, and achievements.
\item
  A full AppShell animation or layout redesign.
\item
  A new \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} feature train.
\item
  Broad V8 Runtime Graph and Scene IR product-contract work.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-052-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Does pressing \texttt{T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b} repeatedly leave the footer visible and themed?
\item
  Does the quit confirmation render with compact themed geometry and readable \texttt{Y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}Q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t} / \texttt{N\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y} actions?
\item
  Does opening Blocks, or activating \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w}, show \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} first?
\item
  Does arrow navigation still allow the \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w} parent row to receive focus from the first standard block preview child?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Test Plan}\label{record-052-test-plan}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add or update DOGFOOD Blocks tests in \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} for initial Blocks selection and \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w} activation.
\item
  Add AppShell regression coverage proving \texttt{T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b} no longer emits a hidden footer toggle path.
\item

\chapter{DF-076 - BlockLab Demo Readiness Navigation}\label{record-053}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-076-blocklab-demo-readiness.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
id: DF-076
title: BlockLab Demo Readiness Navigation
status: active
lane: asap
github_issue: 338
legend: DF

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-053-decision-summary}

BlockLab is a focused app/workbench surface. Its story navigation keys must win over generic framed-shell scroll bindings.

\section{Problem}\label{record-053-problem}

\texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b} runs through \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}. The frame shell defaults to \texttt{k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}"}, so story-navigation keys such as \texttt{u\allowbreak{}p}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{j}, and \texttt{k} are consumed by generic frame scroll bindings before BlockLab sees them.

That makes BlockLab unusable in the release-video path and contradicts the workbench contract: when the app advertises story navigation keys, those keys must move the selected story.

\section{Scope}\label{record-053-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Configure the BlockLab framed app to prefer page-owned keys.
\item
  Add a regression that sends navigation keys through the framed-app runner path and asserts selected-story movement.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-053-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Change the default key priority for all framed apps.
\item
  Redesign BlockLab.
\item
  Add Theme Lab, localization, or GraphQL demo surfaces.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback}\label{record-053-playback}

Run \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b}, press \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n} or \texttt{j}, and verify the selected story moves from \texttt{a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} to \texttt{b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} without a frame key-shadowing warning.

\texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} is now ESLint-clean and no longer owns the landing or theme-token subsystems, but it remains both a file/context exception and a hard code-size exception. The next respectful step is still structural: move coherent docs explorer subsystems out until the main DOGFOOD app file stops being a review and iteration bottleneck.

\section{Problem}\label{record-054-problem}

The DOGFOOD app main file mixes content catalog setup, landing animation and theme rendering, framed docs explorer state, pane layout, mouse routing, and application lifecycle wiring. That makes behavior changes expensive even when lint is clean because reviewers and agents must reason across thousands of unrelated lines.

The landing surface is the best first extraction target: it owns a large set of theme tokens, glyph rendering, animated background, quality controls, caches, and overlays while depending on only a small part of the root model. Pulling it behind a typed module boundary reduces the monolith without changing the visible DOGFOOD route.

\section{Scope}\label{record-054-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Extract the landing surface/theme/rendering subsystem from \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} into focused module(s) under \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}.
\item
  Preserve existing landing route behavior, theme choices, quality controls, prompt rendering, performance HUD, and DOGFOOD panel output.
\item
  Keep the extracted module typed through explicit interfaces instead of importing the whole root model shape.
\item
  Tighten \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} file/context and code-size baselines after the extraction.
\item
  Keep all touched DOGFOOD i18n debt flat or lower. Any user-facing landing copy touched by this cycle must remain catalog-backed or reduce counted raw strings.
\item
  Update the changelog and Code Dojo exception ledger with landed counts.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DF-078 DOGFOOD Release Story Surfaces}\label{record-055}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-078-dogfood-release-story-surfaces.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}

  - dogfood
  - release

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF - DOGFOOD}

\section{Linked Work}\label{record-055-linked-work}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  GitHub Issue: \#335
\item
  v7.2 umbrella: \#354
\item
  GraphQL fixture lineage: \#329
\item
  Blocks app-binding lineage: \#342
\item
  Current release docs: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/releases/7.1.0/README.md}{docs/releases/7.1.0}
\end{itemize}

This document shapes \#335 into a bounded v7.2 demo-integrity pull. It does not turn v7.2 into a broad release-story product, and it does not pull the V8 Runtime Graph product contract forward.

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-055-decision-summary}

DOGFOOD already publishes release notes and migration docs in the Release section, but the app does not yet explain the post-v7.1 proof chain as a first-class product story. A presenter still has to narrate the important relationship manually:

\begin{CodeBlock}
GraphQL SDL fixture
  -> bijou-block/1 artifact
    -> ui-scene-ir/1 scene
      -> terminal Surface proof
        -> graphql-bijou-block-debug/1 facts
\end{CodeBlock}

The v7.2 repair is to add release-story surfaces that make that chain visible inside DOGFOOD:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A concise release-story entry point from the DOGFOOD home or Release page.
\item
  A ``What's New'' path that foregrounds the current release story, not only a Markdown document.
\item
  A GraphQL proof walkthrough tied to the real \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l} fixture.
\item
  A CHANGELOG viewer that preserves version boundaries, headings, and keyboard navigation.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-055-sponsored-human}

A release-video viewer needs DOGFOOD to show why Bijou's v7 proof matters without requiring a source-code tour. The presenter should be able to open one release-story path and walk from source SDL to rendered terminal proof.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-055-sponsored-agent}

An agent needs deterministic text and model witnesses for the release story: which version is being described, which GraphQL fixture carries the proof, which artifact and scene facts are inspectable, and which changelog section bounds the claim.

\section{Hill}\label{record-055-hill}

After this cycle, DOGFOOD can tell the current release story from inside the app: current ``What's New'' copy is discoverable, the real GraphQL block proof is inspectable step by step, and the changelog can be navigated by version without losing Markdown heading structure.

\section{Scope}\label{record-055-scope}

\subsection{Release Story Entry Point}\label{record-055-release-story-entry-point}

Add a compact entry point that is visible from normal DOGFOOD navigation. The entry should name the current release story and point to deeper pages rather than becoming another long landing section.

Acceptable first placement:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a Release page overview card, or
\item
  a concise home-page section that links into Release.
\end{itemize}

The implementation should not add a first-run takeover until there is a clear version-memory port and deterministic dismissal state.

\subsection{What's New Surface}\label{record-055-whats-new-surface}

The current Release section already reads \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}\$\allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}J\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}\}\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}. This cycle should make the surface easier to present by adding a short release-story summary before the long Markdown body or by adding a sibling guide that routes directly to the current ``What's New'' page.

The source of truth remains the versioned release document. DOGFOOD should not fork release claims into a second hand-maintained copy.

\subsection{GraphQL Proof Walkthrough}\label{record-055-graphql-proof-walkthrough}

Add a DOGFOOD guide that explicitly walks the checked-in fixture through the proof chain:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  source fixture path: \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l}
\item
  compiled artifact kind: \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}
\item
  lowered scene kind: \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}
\item
  terminal proof surface
\item
  debug fact kind: \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}
\end{itemize}

The guide must link the proof to the real \texttt{N\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} fixture and to the DOGFOOD navigation surface instead of describing a synthetic example.

\subsection{CHANGELOG Viewer}\label{record-055-changelog-viewer}

Add a first-class DOGFOOD path for \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} that preserves:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  version boundaries
\item
  Markdown headings
\item
  keyboard navigation through sections
\item
  readable current and historical release claims
\end{itemize}

The first slice may reuse the existing Markdown reader. A custom changelog index is acceptable only if it does not duplicate changelog content or invent a second release-history source of truth.

\section{Out Of Scope}\label{record-055-out-of-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  First-run modal or full-screen takeover with persisted dismissal state.
\item
  Runtime storage, host preferences, or cross-session version memory.
\item
  Rewriting the release docs pipeline.
\item
  Moving the broad \#302 Runtime Graph tracker into v7.2.
\item
  Migrating more DOGFOOD blocks to GraphQL.
\item
  Building a source-code browser or full artifact inspector.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-055-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Can a presenter reach the current release story from DOGFOOD without knowing a source file path?
\item
  Can the presenter open a GraphQL proof walkthrough and point to the real \texttt{N\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} SDL fixture?
\item
  Can a viewer see the sequence \texttt{G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}Q\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} inside DOGFOOD?
\item
  Can a viewer open the changelog and move between version boundaries without losing headings?
\item
  Can tests prove these routes from model state and rendered text rather than screenshots?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-055-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

The release story must work as text. Color may support hierarchy, but the proof chain, version names, fixture path, artifact kinds, and changelog boundaries must be visible in plain text and preserved in accessible lower modes where applicable.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-055-localization-and-directionality-posture}

The first implementation may use English-source Markdown, matching the existing Release section behavior. If new DOGFOOD chrome labels are added, they must use catalog keys and keep all supported locale rows current. The design introduces no new right-to-left layout behavior.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-055-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

Agents should be able to inspect:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the Release navigation guide ids
\item
  the rendered release-story text
\item
  the GraphQL fixture path and proof-chain labels
\item
  the changelog guide id and version-boundary headings
\item
  the tests that pin the routes
\end{itemize}

The proof must not depend on screenshots, timestamps, process ids, or local absolute paths.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-055-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/graceful-lowering-preserves-meaning.md}{Graceful Lowering Preserves Meaning}: the release story must remain meaningful as text, not only styled terminal layout.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/buffer-holds-facts.md}{The Buffer Holds Facts}: the GraphQL proof route should expose inspectable artifact and debug-fact labels.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are the Spec}: the release-story route is not complete until scripted DOGFOOD tests prove navigation and text witnesses.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-055-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a focused DOGFOOD release-story guide under the Release page.
\item
  Add a GraphQL proof walkthrough that references the real NavigationListBlock SDL fixture and proof-chain labels.
\item
  Add a CHANGELOG guide or changelog subsection that reads from \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}.
\item
  Add scripted DOGFOOD tests for the Release route, GraphQL proof text, and changelog version-boundary headings.
\item
  Add any new DOGFOOD localization keys needed for navigation chrome.
\item
  Update \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} with the landed v7.2 release-story status.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Test Plan}\label{record-055-test-plan}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add or extend \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} or a new DF-078 test file for the Release route.
\item
  Add a text assertion for the GraphQL proof chain and fixture path.
\item
  Add a text assertion for at least \texttt{[\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}]} and \texttt{[\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}]} changelog boundaries.
\item
  Run focused DOGFOOD release tests, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}, DOGFOOD i18n gates if chrome labels change, \texttt{g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}, and the normal pre-push gate before review.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-055-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD has a visible release-story entry point.
\item
  DOGFOOD can show the current ``What's New'' release story from the Release section.
\item
  DOGFOOD can show a GraphQL proof walkthrough tied to the real NavigationListBlock SDL fixture.
\item
  DOGFOOD can show changelog content with version boundaries intact.
\item
  First-run modal behavior is deliberately deferred unless a deterministic version-memory port is added in the same cycle.
\item
  \#335 has enough scoped design detail to leave \texttt{n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n}.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DF-150 - DOGFOOD Terminal Guardrails}\label{record-056}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DF-150-dogfood-terminal-guardrails.md}\par}\smallskip

Linked issues: \#150, \#151, \#152

Linked legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DF-dogfood-field-guide.md}{DF - DOGFOOD Field Guide}

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-056-sponsor-human}

A learner launching DOGFOOD from a terminal who needs to know that it will take over the screen and how to leave it.

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-056-sponsor-agent}

A docs-surface verification agent that can prove the DOGFOOD entrypoint behaves deterministically in TTY and non-TTY contexts.

\section{Hill}\label{record-056-hill}

DOGFOOD announces its full-screen behavior, prints explicit quit controls, and refuses to launch through non-interactive stdin/stdout paths that cannot host the TUI.

\section{Scope}\label{record-056-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a terminal readiness helper for the DOGFOOD entrypoint.
\item
  Require both stdin and stdout to be TTYs before launching DOGFOOD.
\item
  Print a short full-screen notice and exit controls before \texttt{r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Point scripted callers to the existing smoke command instead of failing silently through a pipe or redirected output.
\item
  Cover the guard in docs preview tests.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-056-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Does DOGFOOD tell the user it is about to launch a full-screen TUI?
\item
  Are the quit controls visible before terminal takeover?
\item
  Does a non-TTY stdin or stdout path fail with a useful message?
\item
  Does the message direct automation to the smoke command instead?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Reading Posture}\label{record-056-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

The warning is plain text on stderr before alt-screen rendering, so screen readers and logs can capture it without needing the TUI frame.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-056-localization-directionality-posture}

This launch warning is host-entrypoint English text in this cycle.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-056-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

The readiness helper is a pure function over \texttt{c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e}, so tests can assert TTY and non-TTY behavior without spawning a terminal.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-056-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Full-screen apps should declare terminal takeover before entering the app.
\item
  Non-interactive execution should point to scripted verification paths.
\end{itemize}

\section{Verification}\label{record-056-verification}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g}
\end{itemize}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-056-tests-to-write-first}
