\chapter{DX-001 --- Type Framed App Messages and Updates End-to-End}\label{record-057}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-001-type-framed-app-messages-and-updates-end-to-end.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DX-developer-experience.md}{DX --- Developer Experience}

\section{Historical note}\label{record-057-historical-note}

This slice is already landed.

It originally lived as a backlog capture and was promoted into \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/} during METHOD adoption so the active backlog would stop advertising completed work as upcoming queue. The file is lighter than newer cycle docs for that reason.

\section{Why this cycle existed}\label{record-057-why-this-cycle-existed}

Remove the \texttt{a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}y} cascade around \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and framed-page update flows.

\section{Why}\label{record-057-why}

Current framed-app typing forces consumers into casts and lint debt:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e} effectively types page \texttt{m\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}g} as \texttt{a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}y}
\item
  framed update results are difficult to type from the outside
\item
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}>} exists, but the consumer-facing API does not make it easy to stay fully typed
\end{itemize}

The result is that a strongly typed app can lose its message-model precision at the shell seam.

\section{Captured feedback}\label{record-057-captured-feedback}

From \texttt{w\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}d} TUI development:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p} page update typed as \texttt{(\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{})}
\item
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} returns an effectively untyped tuple
\item
  these two seams were the biggest source of lint violations
\end{itemize}

\section{Likely scope}\label{record-057-likely-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  make framed-page message typing generic and public
\item
  make framed update return types explicit and consumable
\item
  remove or reduce the need for external \texttt{a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}y} casts at the shell seam
\item
  add tests proving end-to-end typed message unions survive framed app composition
\end{itemize}

\section{Outcome}\label{record-057-outcome}

This work landed and is reflected in \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/CHANGELOG.md}{CHANGELOG.md}.

The public framed-shell surface now exports explicit typed message and update result helpers, and page updates keep custom message unions typed through the shell seam.

\section{Follow-on}\label{record-057-follow-on}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/method/graveyard/legacy-backlog/DX-003-rationalize-table-apis-and-public-table-types.md}{DX-003 --- Rationalize Table APIs and Public Table Types}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/method/graveyard/legacy-backlog/DX-004-smooth-surface-and-string-composition-seams.md}{DX-004 --- Smooth Surface and String Composition Seams}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/method/graveyard/legacy-backlog/DX-005-polish-small-component-and-import-ergonomics.md}{DX-005 --- Polish Small Component and Import Ergonomics}
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DX-002 --- Reconcile Cmd Typing With Cleanup and Effect Patterns}\label{record-058}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-002-reconcile-cmd-typing-with-cleanup-and-effect-patterns.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DX-developer-experience.md}{DX --- Developer Experience}

\section{Historical note}\label{record-058-historical-note}

This slice is already landed.

It originally lived as a backlog capture and was promoted into \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/} during METHOD adoption so the active backlog would stop advertising completed work as upcoming queue. The file is lighter than newer cycle docs for that reason.

\section{Why this cycle existed}\label{record-058-why-this-cycle-existed}

Make command typing match the cleanup-function and runtime-effect patterns Bijou actually encourages.

\section{Why}\label{record-058-why}

The current \texttt{C\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}>} typing does not line up cleanly with real usage:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the pulse timer pattern returns a cleanup function
\item
  the existing type expects \texttt{P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}Q\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}>}
\item
  consumers end up casting to \texttt{a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}y} to express documented patterns
\end{itemize}

This is both a DX problem and a runtime-model problem, because it blurs the line between commands and effects.

\section{Captured feedback}\label{record-058-captured-feedback}

From \texttt{w\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}d} TUI development:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the pulse timer cleanup pattern required \texttt{a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}y}
\item
  the types do not reflect the documented pattern
\end{itemize}

\section{Likely scope}\label{record-058-likely-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  audit current \texttt{C\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} definitions and real runtime usage
\item
  decide whether cleanup handles, effects, and commands need clearer separation
\item
  align public typing with the documented timer/cleanup pattern
\item
  add tests proving the typed API supports cleanup-producing runtime work without casts
\end{itemize}

\section{Outcome}\label{record-058-outcome}

This work landed and is reflected in \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/CHANGELOG.md}{CHANGELOG.md}.

\texttt{C\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}>} now matches the cleanup-capable runtime patterns Bijou actually uses, and the runtime retains and disposes cleanup results instead of forcing those paths through fake message contracts.

\section{Follow-on}\label{record-058-follow-on}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/method/graveyard/legacy-backlog/DX-003-rationalize-table-apis-and-public-table-types.md}{DX-003 --- Rationalize Table APIs and Public Table Types}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/method/graveyard/legacy-backlog/DX-004-smooth-surface-and-string-composition-seams.md}{DX-004 --- Smooth Surface and String Composition Seams}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/method/graveyard/legacy-backlog/DX-005-polish-small-component-and-import-ergonomics.md}{DX-005 --- Polish Small Component and Import Ergonomics}
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DX-022 Layout Inspector Overlay}\label{record-059}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-022-layout-inspector-overlay.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DX-022 Layout Inspector Overlay
legend: DX
lane: design

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-059-framing}

Layout and overlay issues are hard to inspect in situ. Bijou now retains enough runtime geometry that pane bounds, clipping, scroll regions, focus ownership, and z-layer ordering should not stay invisible during development.

DX-022 adds a first-party layout inspector overlay. The first slice is a pure surface helper: apps or framed shells can pass the retained regions they already know about and get a visible overlay plus a plain text report.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-059-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  App authors debugging split panes, clipped viewports, and mouse hit regions.
\item
  Maintainers investigating shell focus or overlay layering regressions.
\item
  Agent workflows that need a text report of layout truth without screenshot inspection.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-059-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A developer can composite an inspector over any surface and see region borders, ids, and dimensions without changing the app layout itself.
\item
  A maintainer can mark one region as focused and visually distinguish it from sibling regions.
\item
  A test can ask for a text report that includes rects, clip rects, scroll offsets, focus, and layer ordering.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-059-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does the overlay draw region bounds on top of an existing surface?
\item
  Does the overlay clip labels and borders to the target surface dimensions?
\item
  Does focused geometry stand out from non-focused geometry?
\item
  Does the text report preserve region ids, roles, rects, clips, scroll offsets, focus, and layers?
\item
  Does \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i} export the inspector API from the source barrel?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-059-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}?\allowbreak{})} helper.
\item
  Add a \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})} helper.
\item
  Support region \texttt{i\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t}, optional \texttt{r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}, optional \texttt{c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p}, optional \texttt{s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l}, optional \texttt{f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}, and optional \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}.
\item
  Draw only within the background surface bounds.
\item
  Keep the helper independent of \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} internals so raw runtime apps can use it too.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-059-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Focused tests fail before implementation and pass after.
\item
  The overlay draws borders and labels for visible regions.
\item
  The overlay clips off-screen regions without throwing.
\item
  The text report includes all supplied geometry facts.
\item
  Docs and changelog describe the helper.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-059-implementation-outline}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Implement the helper in \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Export it from \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Keep drawing intentionally simple: ASCII borders, compact labels, and explicit text reports are more useful in debug output than elaborate chrome.
\end{itemize}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-059-drift-check}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Scope stayed on the first pure helper slice. The runtime did not grow a global toggle, because callers can now compose the inspector over any retained geometry they already own.
\item
  The implementation accepts both debug-friendly \texttt{\{\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\}} rectangles and Bijou-native \texttt{\{\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\}} rectangles. That keeps the public helper ergonomic without forcing app-frame internals into the design contract.
\item
  Styling stayed out of the first pass. Plain ASCII borders make the overlay stable in tests, logs, and pipe captures.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback}\label{record-059-playback}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} draws clipped borders and compact labels over an existing surface.
\item
  Focused regions are distinguishable through the \texttt{*} label prefix.
\item
  Off-screen regions clip to the target surface instead of throwing.
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} emits ids, roles, rects, clip rects, scroll offsets, focus, and layer facts as deterministic text.
\item
  \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i} exports the new API from the source barrel.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-059-retrospective}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  This is useful as a small diagnostic primitive rather than a shell feature. Apps can opt in during tests, demos, or debug modes without changing runtime ownership.
\item
  The native \texttt{L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t} mismatch was caught by package typecheck after the RED tests went green. Accepting both shapes is the right boundary behavior: app-frame can pass retained layout rects directly, while external tests can use x/y terminology.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DX-023 Input Routing Inspector}\label{record-060}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-023-input-routing-inspector.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DX-023 Input Routing Inspector
legend: DX
lane: design

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-060-framing}

Key swallowing and priority mistakes are hard to diagnose from outside the runtime. Frame/page binding warnings already proved this seam needs stronger observability; developers should not have to infer routing truth from visible state changes alone.

DX-023 adds a first-party input-routing inspector. The first slice is a pure history and report helper around existing \texttt{R\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t} facts. Shell integration can feed it live records later without changing the core router.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-060-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  App authors debugging key priority, shell/page routing, and swallowed input.
\item
  Maintainers investigating runtime routing regressions.
\item
  Agent workflows that need text output for recent input-routing facts.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-060-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A developer can append routing records to a bounded history and inspect the last N events.
\item
  A maintainer can read a text report that shows event kind, visited views, handler owner, hit target, commands, effects, swallowed input, and no-op handlers.
\item
  A test can render the same report as a surface for docs or debug panes.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-060-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does the helper retain only the configured number of events?
\item
  Does the text report distinguish key and pointer events?
\item
  Does the report expose visited views, handled/stopped owner, and hit target?
\item
  Does the report flag swallowed input when routing stops unhandled?
\item
  Does the report flag no-op handlers when an event is handled without commands or effects?
\item
  Does \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i} export the inspector API from the source barrel?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-060-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add \texttt{a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}?\allowbreak{})}.

\item
  Keep the first slice pure and shell-agnostic.

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-060-acceptance-criteria}

\item
  Text reports include routing facts, swallowed status, and no-op status.
\item
  Surface reports render the same text into a bounded \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  Docs and changelog describe the helper.
\end{itemize}

\item
  Keep command/effect labeling explicit: callers can pass labels, otherwise the report shows counts instead of guessing object meaning.
\end{itemize}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-060-drift-check}

\begin{itemize}

\item

\item
  Live shell integration remains follow-on work; the first slice provides the data model, bounded history, text report, and surface rendering.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback}\label{record-060-playback}

  \texttt{a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} keeps a deterministic bounded history.
