  \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} renders the same report into a bounded \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i} exports the new API from the source barrel.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-060-retrospective}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  This complements the layout inspector without coupling to it. Layout explains geometry; input routing explains priority and ownership.
\item
  Keeping labels explicit prevents the inspector from turning command objects into misleading strings.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DX-024 Surface Diff Viewer}\label{record-061}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-024-surface-diff-viewer.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DX-024 Surface Diff Viewer
legend: DX
lane: design

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-061-framing}

Render debugging still depends on ad hoc inspection and text dumps. That is especially painful when a frame regression changes only a few cells, or when the character looks correct but a style changed underneath it.

Bijou already has a strong \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} truth object. DX-024 makes that truth inspectable with a first-party diff model and viewer surface.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-061-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Maintainers investigating visual regression failures in frame tests.
\item
  App authors debugging composed surfaces where nested layout masks or overlays changed a small region.
\item
  Agent workflows that need a compact, plain-text rendering of surface truth without manually dumping raw cells.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-061-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer can diff two surfaces and immediately see changed cell counts, style-only changes, and the smallest changed bounds.
\item
  An app author can render the same diff side-by-side or as an overlay surface without writing custom inspection code.
\item
  A test can print a plain-text diff summary that preserves the same changed cell facts when rich terminal rendering is unavailable.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-061-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does the diff distinguish char changes from style-only changes?
\item
  Does the diff include cells added by width or height differences?
\item
  Does the viewer produce both side-by-side and overlay renderings?
\item
  Does the plain-text rendering include counts and per-cell coordinates?
\item
  Does the package export the diff model and viewer from \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i}?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-061-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a pure \texttt{d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{})} model.
\item
  Add \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})} for rich viewer output.
\item
  Add \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})} for test and pipe output.
\item
  Support \texttt{s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e} and \texttt{o\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y} modes.
\item
  Count changed cells, character deltas, and style-only deltas separately.
\item
  Include a changed bounds rectangle when any cell differs.
\item
  Avoid changing existing surface or differ semantics.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-061-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Focused \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f} tests fail before implementation and pass after.
\item
  Cycle tests confirm the design doc sections and root package export.
\item
  Docs and changelog describe the new viewer.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-061-implementation-outline}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Implement the diff model and renderers in \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Export the new API from the \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i} source barrel.
\item
  Keep rendering intentionally plain: labels, counts, and simple ASCII markers are more useful in failure output than decorative chrome.
\end{itemize}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-061-drift-check}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The implementation stayed in \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i} because the model is useful for tests, but the viewer is a TUI authoring/debug component.
\item
  No existing surface or differ semantics changed; DX-024 only reads \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} cells and builds a separate report/view.
\item
  The side-by-side renderer intentionally keeps output plain and copyable for failure logs. Overlay mode applies simple highlight styles for rich surfaces.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback}\label{record-061-playback}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED: focused tests failed on the missing \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f} module and missing source-barrel exports.
\item
  GREEN: \texttt{d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} now reports changed counts, char deltas, style-only deltas, changed bounds, and per-cell coordinates.
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} renders both \texttt{s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e} and \texttt{o\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y} views.
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} renders a plain coordinate report for pipe/test output.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-061-retrospective}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The useful split was model first, viewer second. That keeps tests and future tooling from needing to parse the visual surface.
\item
  Style-only changes are first-class because they are a common terminal UI regression and invisible in simple text snapshots.
\item
  A future follow-on could wire this into frame-regression failure output, but the reusable primitive is now available.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DX-025 Component Metadata Contract}\label{record-062}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-025-component-metadata-contract.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DX-025 Component Metadata Contract
legend: DX
lane: design

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-062-framing}

Bijou has component facts scattered across package docs, strategy docs, examples, tests, DOGFOOD stories, and MCP-facing payloads. Those surfaces should not each invent a slightly different idea of what a component is.

DX-025 adds a pure component metadata contract in core. The first slice defines the runtime shape, validates common drift, and renders a deterministic summary. It does not build the story workstation; it gives that workstation, DOGFOOD, MCP docs, and agent workflows one shared object to consume.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-062-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Maintainers curating first-party component docs and examples.
\item
  Tool builders generating DOGFOOD pages, MCP payloads, or story indexes.
\item
  Third-party authors who want extension metadata without copying internal docs.
\item
  Agent workflows that need stable facts about component modes and invariants.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-062-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer can describe a component's package, family, modes, args, variants, invariants, docs, examples, and source path in one runtime object.
\item
  A tool can validate metadata and get deterministic issue paths for duplicate ids, missing required fields, and empty required lists.
\item
  A docs or agent surface can render a compact summary without parsing markdown.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-062-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does the contract capture package name, component name, family, modes, docs, args, variants, invariants, examples, and source path?
\item
  Does validation reject blank required fields and empty mode lists?
\item
  Does validation report duplicate mode names and duplicate ids deterministically?
\item
  Can variants and invariants attach semantic facts for mode-lowering checks?
\item
  Does a helper throw on invalid metadata for authoring-time guardrails?
\item
  Does \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u} export the contract and helpers from the root barrel?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-062-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a} and related runtime types.
\item
  Add \texttt{v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Add \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{})} for authoring-time validation.
\item
  Add \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Keep the contract pure and package-neutral enough for third-party components.
\item
  Reuse \texttt{O\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e} and \texttt{M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t} types where metadata touches modes and semantic facts.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-062-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED tests fail before implementation and pass after.
\item
  Valid metadata reports no issues and produces a stable summary.
\item
  Invalid metadata reports deterministic issue paths and messages.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} throws on invalid metadata.
\item
  Docs and changelog describe the metadata contract.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-062-implementation-outline}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Implement the helper in \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Export it from \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Keep validation strict enough to catch drift but not so broad that it becomes a schema language.
\end{itemize}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-062-drift-check}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Scope stayed on the contract and validation layer. The story workstation and DOGFOOD migration remain follow-up work that can consume this object.
\item
  Validation catches required-field drift, empty mode lists, duplicate modes, duplicate arg names, and duplicate ids across variants, invariants, and examples. It does not become a schema language or a docs parser.
\item
  Variants and invariants can carry \texttt{M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t} records, connecting this contract to DX-026 without coupling metadata to rendered output.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback}\label{record-062-playback}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a} captures package name, component name, family, modes, docs, args, variants, invariants, examples, tags, and source path.
\item
  \texttt{v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} returns deterministic issue paths and messages.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} throws with the report text when metadata contains errors.
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} renders a compact, stable summary for docs, agents, and MCP payloads.
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} renders validation output in review-friendly text.
\item
  \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u} exports the contract and helpers from the root barrel.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-062-retrospective}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  This gives DOGFOOD and MCP tooling a shared object without forcing either surface to own the component taxonomy.
\item
  Keeping semantic facts attached to variants and invariants should make future story audits and mode-lowering checks cheaper: metadata can describe the intended truth, and render-specific tooling can prove it.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DX-026 Mode-Lowering Linter}\label{record-063}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-026-mode-lowering-linter.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DX-026 Mode-Lowering Linter
legend: DX
lane: design

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-063-framing}

Bijou treats \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e}, and \texttt{a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} as real output contracts, not skins. Rich output can use layout, color, borders, animation, and symbols, but lower modes still need to preserve the semantic truth a human or agent needs to understand the component.

DX-026 adds a pure diagnostic helper for mode-lowering fidelity. The first slice does not parse rendered text or own component rendering. Instead, component authors supply the semantic facts each mode promises to preserve, and Bijou reports missing or collapsed facts in a stable format.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-063-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Component authors proving a custom component lowers honestly.
\item
  Maintainers reviewing regressions in \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e} and \texttt{a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} output.
\item
  Agent workflows that need deterministic diagnostics instead of screenshots.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-063-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A component author can compare semantic facts across rich, static, pipe, and accessible outputs without matching visual text.
\item
  A maintainer can identify which mode dropped a required entity, count, state, label, edge, or custom fact.
\item
  A test can assert a compact report, then render that report as stable text for docs or review comments.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-063-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Can a caller define a baseline mode and compare every other mode to it?
\item
  Does the helper report missing facts per mode with fact kind and key?
\item
  Does the helper report changed fact values for counts, states, or other value-bearing facts?
\item
  Does the helper report collapsed duplicate facts inside a mode?
\item
  Can callers mark a fact as optional so intentional omissions do not warn?
\item
  Can callers add component-specific assertion results to the same report?
\item
  Does \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u} export the helper and its report types?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-063-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add \texttt{l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})} to \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u}.
\item
  Add \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{})} for deterministic diagnostics.
\item
  Support fact kinds for \texttt{e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y}, \texttt{e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e}, and \texttt{c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m}.
\item
  Treat baseline facts as required unless \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  Report missing required baseline facts in lower modes.
\item
  Report changed required fact values in lower modes.
\item
  Report duplicate fact keys inside a mode as collapsed semantics.
\item
  Accept custom assertion results so component tests can attach domain-specific failures without a second reporting format.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-063-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED tests fail before implementation and pass after.
\item
  Reports include checked modes, issue severities, fact keys, and messages.
\item
  Optional facts are ignored when absent from a lower mode.
\item
  Duplicate facts are reported deterministically.
\item
  Docs and changelog describe the helper.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-063-implementation-outline}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Implement the helper in \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Export it from \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Keep the API pure and string/symbol independent; semantic facts are explicit runtime objects supplied by callers.
\end{itemize}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-063-drift-check}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Scope narrowed from a static source-code linter to a pure semantic diagnostic helper. That is the right first slice because components already know their runtime semantic facts, while parsing rendered text or source files would add brittle inference.
\item
  The helper reports missing facts, changed fact values, duplicate facts, and custom assertion failures. It does not try to decide whether a glyph or phrase is visually equivalent.
\item
  \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e} is the default baseline when present; otherwise the first supplied mode becomes the baseline.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback}\label{record-063-playback}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} compares supplied mode facts against a baseline and returns a structured report with checked modes, issue severities, fact kinds, fact keys, and pass/fail status.
\item
  Optional baseline facts with \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e} can be omitted by lower modes without warning.
\item
  Duplicate fact identities inside a mode are reported as collapsed semantics.
\item
  Failed custom assertions are folded into the same report.
\item
  \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} renders deterministic text for tests, docs, and review comments.
\item
  \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u} exports the helper and report types from the root barrel.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-063-retrospective}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The important boundary is explicit runtime truth. Component authors supply facts like \texttt{e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} or \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}3}; the helper checks fidelity without coupling itself to a renderer, AST, or screenshot.
\item
  This composes with DOGFOOD stories and future replay tooling: both can attach semantic facts to rendered variants and use the same report format.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DX-030 Add boundary-aware pointer selection and copy}\label{record-064}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-030-add-boundary-aware-pointer-selection-and-copy.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DX-030 Add boundary-aware pointer selection and copy
legend: DX
lane: design
priority: high
keywords:
  - dogfood
  - pointer
  - selection
  - clipboard
  - geometry

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-064-framing}

DOGFOOD currently depends on terminal-native selection. That is acceptable as a host fallback, but it is not the Bijou model. A drag gesture in a framed docs surface should not copy whatever cells happen to be painted across the whole terminal. It should resolve the owning pane, clamp the drag to that pane's geometry, and reconstruct text from the component's semantic content model.

This cycle defines the contract and lands the pure selection coordinator in \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u}. The runtime primitive consumes retained rectangles, viewport transforms, semantic content models, higher-priority blockers, and pointer ranges, then returns selected text plus an inspectable clipboard-effect record. It still does not implement OS clipboard writes, full app-frame drag capture, or cross-pane rich extraction. Those pieces remain host/runtime adapters rather than render logic.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-064-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD readers who want to drag-copy docs text without selecting shell chrome, neighboring panes, or visual gutters.
\item
  App authors who need copy behavior to respect pane and component boundaries.
\item
  Maintainers who need a stable target for later pointer-routing, clipboard, and semantic extraction work.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-064-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A reader can expect selection to stay inside the pane or component that owns the drag start.
\item
  A builder can declare selection metadata on a surface or layout node without giving rendering authority over geometry.
\item
  A maintainer can implement runtime selection later by following an explicit hit-test, range, extraction, and clipboard-effect protocol.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-064-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  What metadata can a surface or layout node expose for selection?
\item
  How does retained layout geometry map a pointer drag to one owning component?
\item
  How is copied output reconstructed for prose, tables, and mixed panes?
\item
  How does the shell arbitrate selection against existing mouse routing?
\item
  Where does clipboard IO live so copying remains an effect, not render logic?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-064-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Selection ownership is opt-out default behavior for framed docs-style panes, but interactive controls may explicitly opt out or override drag handling.
\item
  Hit-testing must start from retained layout geometry, not rendered strings.
\item
  A drag starts from one \texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r} and remains bounded to that owner unless a future explicit multi-owner policy allows otherwise.
\item
  Extraction reconstructs output from semantic content metadata, paragraph spans, table cells, or component-provided extractors, not raw terminal rows.
\item
  Viewports must map screen coordinates through scroll offsets before forming content ranges.
\item
  Copying to an OS clipboard is a host effect. Runtime selection should emit a command/effect fact; renderers should never write the clipboard.
\end{itemize}

\section{Contract}\label{record-064-contract}

The contract introduces six conceptual records.

\texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}

The component, pane, or layout node that owns a selectable region.

Required facts:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  stable owner id
\item
  retained layout node id
\item
  assigned screen rect
\item
  optional viewport transform
\item
  selection policy
\item
  content model reference
\end{itemize}

\texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}

The concrete selectable rectangle derived from layout truth.

Required facts:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  owner id
\item
  screen rect
\item
  content rect
\item
  clipping rect
\item
  z/layer order
\item
  enabled/disabled state
\end{itemize}

\texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e}

The normalized content-space range derived from a pointer drag.

Required facts:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  owner id
\item
  anchor point
\item
  focus point
\item
  normalized start/end points
\item
  content-space clipping rect
\item
  direction
\item
  drag source device
\end{itemize}

\texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l}

The semantic model used to reconstruct selected text.

Supported first models:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e}: paragraph and wrapped-line spans
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}: cell spans with optional semantic line grouping
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}: row and column cells with header context
\item
  \texttt{m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}: ordered child regions with their own extractors
\end{itemize}

\texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r}

The pure function that turns a \texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e} and content model into copied text.

Rules:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  prose unwraps soft wraps while preserving hard paragraph breaks
\item
  tables preserve cell boundaries with tabs or another declared delimiter
\item
  mixed panes concatenate child extractions in semantic order
\item
  decorative chrome, gutters, scrollbars, and focus rails are excluded by default
\item
  extraction must be deterministic and inspectable
\end{itemize}

\texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r}

The runtime service that arbitrates pointer selection.

Responsibilities:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  receive pointer down/drag/up facts
\item
  hit-test the topmost retained layout region
\item
  choose the nearest selectable owner
\item
  respect higher-priority mouse handlers such as split dividers, buttons, drag/drop targets, and active overlays
\item
  clamp movement to the owner region
\item
  request extraction on release
\item
  emit a clipboard effect or copy result command
\end{itemize}

The shipped \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} primitive covers this flow in pure package space. It does not own pointer capture or host clipboard IO; it gives those adapters a deterministic contract to call.

\section{Runtime Flow}\label{record-064-runtime-flow}

\begin{center}
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[booknode/.style={draw=BookHeading,line width=.6pt,fill=BookPanel,rounded corners=1.5pt,align=center,text width=29mm,minimum height=10mm,inner sep=5pt,font=\small},bookedge/.style={-{Latex[length=2mm]},draw=BookHeading,line width=.65pt},every edge quotes/.style={font=\scriptsize,fill=white,inner sep=2pt,text=BookMuted}]
\node[booknode] (P) at (0,0) {Pointer event};
\node[booknode] (H) at (0,-1.5) {Retained layout hit-test};
\node[booknode] (O) at (0,-3) {Nearest Selection\allowbreak{}Owner};
\node[booknode] (A) at (0,-4.7) {Higher-priority mouse handler?};
\node[booknode] (M) at (5,-6.4) {Route existing mouse command};
\node[booknode] (S) at (0,-6.4) {Start selection capture};
\node[booknode] (D) at (0,-7.9) {Drag updates Selection\allowbreak{}Range};
\node[booknode] (C) at (0,-9.4) {Clamp through owner rect and viewport transform};
\node[booknode] (X) at (0,-10.9) {Selection\allowbreak{}Extractor reconstructs text};
\node[booknode] (E) at (0,-12.4) {Clipboard effect or copy result command};
\draw[bookedge,] (P) to (H);
\draw[bookedge,] (H) to (O);
\draw[bookedge,] (O) to (A);
\draw[bookedge,] (A) to node[midway,fill=white,inner sep=1.5pt,font=\scriptsize,text=BookMuted] {yes} (M);
\draw[bookedge,] (A) to node[midway,fill=white,inner sep=1.5pt,font=\scriptsize,text=BookMuted] {no} (S);
\draw[bookedge,] (S) to (D);
\draw[bookedge,] (D) to (C);
\draw[bookedge,] (C) to (X);
\draw[bookedge,] (X) to (E);
\end{tikzpicture}}
\end{center}

Selection is a pointer interaction that uses layout truth. It is not a render phase and not a terminal-row scrape.

\section{Arbitration}\label{record-064-arbitration}

Mouse routing keeps the same priority model as the rest of Bijou:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Active modal or overlay captures first.
\item
  Explicit drag handles and resize controls win over selection.
\item
  Component-owned pointer handlers win when the component declares a drag gesture, such as sliders, split panes, or draggable tabs.
\item
  Otherwise, the nearest selectable owner may start a selection capture.
\item
  Terminal-native selection remains a host fallback when Bijou is not in mouse mode or the app opts out.
\end{enumerate}

The rule is deliberately conservative: selection should never steal a gesture from an interactive control that already owns that drag.

\section{Extraction Rules}\label{record-064-extraction-rules}

Prose extraction:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  maps pointer positions to paragraph spans
\item
  unwraps soft wraps
\item
  preserves hard line breaks, blank lines, and list boundaries
\item
  excludes visible borders, scrollbars, and status gutters
\end{itemize}

Table extraction:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  maps selected cells through row and column coordinates
\item
  preserves headers when the selection crosses enough columns to need context
\item
  emits tab-delimited text by default
\item
  leaves room for CSV/TSV policy later
\end{itemize}

Mixed pane extraction:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  clips each child to the owner range
\item
  extracts children in semantic order
\item
  inserts declared separators only where the component model says they exist
\item
  refuses to infer meaning from visual adjacency alone
\end{itemize}

Viewport extraction:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  maps screen coordinates into content coordinates with scroll offsets
\item
  respects clipped content
\item
  may expose current scroll context in accessible copy, but copied prose should be the selected content, not the scrollbar state
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-064-non-goals}

This cycle does not:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  implement OS clipboard adapters
\item
  implement drag selection in \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}
\item
  define multi-pane selection
\item
  define cross-pane rich extraction
\item
  define rich clipboard formats
\item
  define image or shader-region copying
\item
  make terminal-native selection disappear
\end{itemize}

Those are follow-on implementation slices once host and framed-app adapters are ready to consume the pure coordinator.

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-064-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The contract names selection owners, regions, ranges, content models, extractors, and the coordinator.
\item
  The contract states that hit-testing uses retained layout geometry.
\item
  The contract states that copied output comes from semantic extraction, not raw terminal rows.
\item
  The contract defines arbitration against overlays, drag handles, component pointer handlers, and terminal-native fallback.
\item
  \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u} exports a pure selection coordinator that uses retained geometry and semantic extraction.
\item
  The v6 release lane points at this design closure instead of the backlog note.
\item
  The DX legend records this as the latest completed selection/copy closure.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-064-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Promote the backlog item into this design-cycle contract.
\item
  Add \texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}, \texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l}, \texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}, and clipboard-effect records to \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u}.
\item
  Implement \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, and \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as pure primitives backed by retained geometry and semantic content.
\item
  Add package and Method-cycle tests that prove bounded prose extraction, table extraction, topmost owner selection, higher-priority blocker arbitration, terminal-native fallback, and v6 closeout evidence.
\item
  Update the v6 lane, roadmap, bearing, changelog, and backlog anchors so issue \#186 closes through implementation rather than contract-only deferral.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback}\label{record-064-playback}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED: the backlog named the need, but no stable design artifact defined the selection owner, range, extraction, and clipboard-effect contract; the new package and Method-cycle tests failed because no public selection module or v6 closeout evidence existed.
\item
  GREEN: this cycle defines the records, exports the pure selection coordinator, and proves semantic copy behavior without terminal-row scraping.
\item
  The contract keeps selection bounded by retained layout truth.
\item
  The contract keeps copying semantic and inspectable.
\item
  The contract keeps clipboard writes outside render logic.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-064-retrospective}

DX-030 is landed for the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release boundary.

The implementation intentionally stops at the pure selection coordinator because that is the correct package boundary for v6: layout truth and semantic content can now decide what would be copied, while host clipboard writes and framed-app drag capture remain explicit adapters. That keeps boundary-aware copy inspectable, deterministic, and test-protected without smuggling terminal row scraping into the renderer.

\chapter{DX-031 Standard Bijou Blocks}\label{record-065}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-031-standard-bijou-blocks.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DX-031 Standard Bijou Blocks
legend: DX
lane: design

\end{RecordMeta}

\emph{Cycle for declaring reusable app-building blocks that compose Bijou components into standard, inspectable surface patterns}

Legend:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DX-developer-experience.md}{DX - Developer Experience}
\end{itemize}

Depends on:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-025-component-metadata-contract.md}{DX-025 - Component Metadata Contract}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-031F-block-tree-rendering.md}{DX-031F - Block Tree Rendering}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-028-story-capture-matrix.md}{DF-028 - Story Capture Matrix}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-029-fixture-to-docs-promotion-path.md}{DF-029 - Fixture-to-Docs Promotion Path}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/RE-035-mandatory-layout-envelope-and-constraint-negotiation.md}{RE-035}
\end{itemize}

\section{Why This Cycle Exists}\label{record-065-why-this-cycle-exists}

Bijou has many capable components, but app builders still need to assemble common surfaces by hand: shells, readers, inspectors, command palettes, settings, modal stacks, notifications, and authentication flows.

Blocks standardize those common compositions without turning them into new primitives.

A block is a named composition of Bijou components with a documented layout, focus, input, mode-lowering, and semantic contract. Blocks are the layer a builder reaches for when they want to build an app quickly without re-deciding the same shell and workflow patterns every time.

\section{Boundary}\label{record-065-boundary}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Blocks compose primitives.
\item
  Blocks expose slots and semantic facts.
\item
  Blocks lower across interactive, static, pipe, and accessible modes.
\item
  Blocks do not mutate layout directly.
\item
  Blocks do not replace RE layout primitives.
\item
  Blocks do not become a hidden window manager.
\end{itemize}

\section{Relationship To RE-035}\label{record-065-relationship-to-re-035}

Blocks depend on layout truth, but they do not define it.

Each block should compile into ordinary visible nodes with mandatory layout envelopes. The block owns composition, slot names, default behavior, and semantic facts. The layout engine owns constraints, preferences, assigned rectangles, and explanations.

That keeps the boundary simple:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  blocks choose what app surface exists
\item
  layout chooses where each visible node fits
\item
  focus and input consume retained layout facts
\item
  renderers paint assigned rectangles
\item
  modes lower semantic block facts
\end{itemize}

\section{Runtime Truth Vs App Truth}\label{record-065-runtime-truth-vs-app-truth}

Blocks must preserve a hard boundary between primitive runtime truth and semantic app truth.

Primitive runtime truth belongs to RE and adjacent runtime layers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  layout envelope
\item
  constraints
\item
  preferences
\item
  assigned rectangles
\item
  fit policy
\item
  focus regions
\item
  hit regions
\item
  viewport facts
\item
  layer order
\item
  command and effect facts
\end{itemize}

Semantic app truth belongs to blocks and app code:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}
\item
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w}
\item
  \texttt{D\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l}
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d}
\item
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l}
\item
  domain entities, statuses, actions, and relationships
\end{itemize}

The dependency direction only goes one way:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  semantic blocks compile into primitive runtime truth
\item
  runtime primitives do not learn product, commerce, docs, or chat semantics
\item
  app semantics do not mutate runtime geometry directly
\item
  inspectors may relate both layers, but must label which layer they explain
\end{itemize}

This prevents business semantics from leaking into the layout engine and keeps runtime primitives from becoming app-shaped.

\section{Human Users / Jobs / Hill}\label{record-065-human-users-jobs-hill}

\subsection{Primary Human Users}\label{record-065-primary-human-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  App builders assembling Bijou tools from common surface patterns.
\item
  DOGFOOD maintainers turning docs, inspectors, settings, and command surfaces into reusable examples.
\item
  Component authors who need a standard target for real-world composition stories.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human Jobs}\label{record-065-human-jobs}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Pick a block for a common app surface instead of starting from blank layout.
\item
  Fill named slots with app-owned content.
\item
  Trust the block's default focus, input, responsive, and mode-lowering behavior.
\item
  Inspect how a block composes lower-level components.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Human Hill}\label{record-065-human-hill}

A builder can create a useful Bijou app shell with navigation, content, settings, help, notifications, and modal behavior by composing documented blocks instead of hand-rolling every surface.

\section{Agent Users / Jobs / Hill}\label{record-065-agent-users-jobs-hill}

\subsection{Primary Agent Users}\label{record-065-primary-agent-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Agents generating Bijou app scaffolds.
\item
  Agents upgrading examples into DOGFOOD stories.
\item
  Agents explaining how an app surface is composed.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent Jobs}\label{record-065-agent-jobs}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Select an appropriate block from a stable catalog.
\item
  Fill required slots and avoid unsupported private layout behavior.
\item
  Generate tests against block contracts instead of snapshot-only output.
\item
  Preserve semantic facts when lowering to pipe and accessible modes.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Agent Hill}\label{record-065-agent-hill}

An agent can inspect a block definition, identify its slots and mode behavior, and generate type-safe app code that uses the block without inventing new layout or input conventions.

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Posture}\label{record-065-accessibility-assistive-posture}

Blocks must preserve semantic meaning when visual chrome lowers away.

Every standard block should identify:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  named regions
\item
  active item or selected entity, when relevant
\item
  available actions
\item
  validation or warning facts
\item
  modal or focus-trap state, when relevant
\item
  whether hidden visual content remains available in accessible mode
\end{itemize}

Auth blocks must never expose secrets in accessible, pipe, static, or diagnostic output.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-065-localization-directionality-posture}

Blocks should describe layout in logical terms and inherit direction from the host context unless a block explicitly owns a local direction boundary.

The first catalog should avoid physical left/right naming in slot contracts. For example:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  use \texttt{n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} instead of \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v}
\item
  use \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r} instead of \texttt{r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e}
\item
  use \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} and \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s} instead of button order names
\end{itemize}

Text, bidi, and locale-specific formatting stay outside this first blocks cycle, but block slots must not make later localization harder.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-065-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

Blocks should be inspectable as data before rendering. An agent should be able to answer:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  which block is this?
\item
  which slots are required?
\item
  which slots are filled?
\item
  which lower-level components does it compose?
\item
  what semantic facts does it expose?
\item
  how does it lower by mode?
\item
  what are the expected focus and action surfaces?
\end{itemize}

The first implementation should prefer metadata and story captures over snapshot-only proof.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-065-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist

\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/commands-change-state-effects-do-not.md}{Commands Change State, Effects Do Not}

  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are the Spec}
\end{itemize}

\section{Block Contract}\label{record-065-block-contract}

Every standard block should declare:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  purpose
\item
  required slots
\item
  optional slots
\item
  variants
\item
  configurable options
\item
  composed components
\item
  layout posture
\item
  focus posture
\item
  input posture
\item
  responsive posture
\item
  mode-lowering posture
\item
  accessibility facts
\item
  examples and story ids
\item
  tests that define the contract
\end{itemize}

The eventual metadata can align with \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and story capture records, but this cycle starts by standardizing the human-readable catalog.
