  Done: formalize the active binding lifecycle before runtime subscriptions or rendered AppShell begin.
\item
  Done: add binding lifecycle primitives as immutable transition-algebra value objects.
\item
  Done: add active binding collection primitives for declared owner and requirement pairs.
\item
  Done: add active-view binding collection over the existing view-stack model.
\item
  Done: add invalidation flow from provider snapshot updates to new immutable binding frames.
\item
  Done: add Command intent dispatch proof through the runtime command buffer.
\item
  Done: prove rendered AppShell with provider-bound navigation, content, inspector, and status blocks.
\item
  Done: add DOGFOOD stories and captures for ready, loading, stale, empty, and error binding states through the standard block story and DOGFOOD preview surface.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-069-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Behavioral tests proving public binding frames expose immutable data without provider handles.
\item
  Behavioral tests proving binding snapshots are immutable and versioned.
\item
  Behavioral tests proving command intents are metadata, not callbacks.
\item
  Behavioral tests proving provider scopes are explicit local registries without hidden globals.
\item
  Cycle tests proving the active hierarchy owns active binding lifetime, provider subscriptions belong to runtime lifecycle, and binding frames remain immutable render inputs.
\item
  Behavioral tests proving lifecycle records are immutable transition-algebra facts with active, suspended, disposed, and invalidated states.
\item
  Behavioral tests proving active binding collections bind declared requirements to explicit lifecycle owners without rendering, subscribing, or dispatching.
\item
  Runtime tests proving active view-stack layers determine active bindings without rendering, subscribing, or dispatching.
\item
  Runtime tests proving provider scopes resolve nearest-provider wins without hidden globals.
\item
  Runtime tests proving active views create bindings and inactive views dispose or suspend them.
\item
  Runtime tests proving provider updates create new binding frames instead of mutating the current frame.
\item
  Runtime tests proving views can emit Commands but cannot mutate provider data.
\item
  Runtime tests proving Commands flow to business logic and produce later snapshots through the normal update loop.
\item
  Mode-lowering tests proving ready, loading, stale, empty, and error binding states survive in pipe and accessible output.
\item
  DOGFOOD tests proving AppShell nests provider-bound blocks through named logical regions.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-069-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Bijou has a documented data-binding architecture before expanding the block API further.
\item
  Data flow is one-way from business logic/providers into immutable view snapshots.
\item
  Views communicate user intent only through Commands.
\item
  Providers are explicit, scoped, and free of import-time global registration.
\item
  Active view hierarchy controls which data bindings are active.
\item
  Active binding collections expose active owner/requirement pairs and lifecycle ownership records before runtime provider integration.
\item
  Provider updates produce new immutable binding frames.
\item
  Command intent emissions enter the runtime command buffer without embedding business logic callbacks in views.
\item
  Binding status is visible to tooling and lower modes.
\item
  Schema-bound blocks compose with provider-bound views but do not replace the provider lifecycle.
\item
  AppShell is designed around nested provider-bound blocks in logical slots.
\end{itemize}

\section{Risks / Unknowns}\label{record-069-risks-unknowns}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The first API could accidentally expose provider handles to views. That would violate the core rule.
\item
  The provider lifecycle could duplicate existing runtime command/effect buffering if it is not layered carefully.
\item
  If provider scopes are too implicit, debugging active data flow will become difficult.
\item
  If binding frames are only TypeScript shapes, they will not satisfy the repo's runtime-truth standard.
\item
  Schema binding, provider binding, and slot binding can blur together. The architecture should keep them separate:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    schemas validate data shape
  \item
    providers deliver immutable snapshots
  \item
    slots compose views and blocks
  \item
    Commands express user intent
  \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-069-retrospective}

DX-034A landed the primitive contract layer first. The important restraint is that \texttt{B\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} is not a provider scope, subscription manager, active-view resolver, schema adapter, or AppShell slot model. It is only the immutable data frame views can read during render.

DX-034B then landed explicit provider/scope metadata. The restraint remains the same: \texttt{P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e} says which providers are locally available, but it still does not perform nearest-scope resolution, subscribe to backing sources, invalidate views, or dispatch Commands.

DX-034C landed structural AppShell composition. It proves semantic slots and nested block introspection, but still does not render AppShell or invent binding lifecycle policy.

DX-034D formalized active binding lifecycle ownership before runtime code. The important restraint is that active hierarchy, provider subscriptions, invalidation, and command dispatch are runtime responsibilities; views still receive immutable frames and emit intent only.

DX-034E landed binding lifecycle primitives as transition algebra. The restraint is that lifecycle records are immutable facts, not managers: they do not subscribe, refresh, dispatch, traverse the active hierarchy, render AppShell, retain caches, or bind schemas.

DX-034F landed active binding collection primitives. The restraint is that collections inspect declarations and produce active lifecycle ownership records; they do not subscribe, refresh, dispatch, render, cache, resolve provider scopes, traverse the real TUI runtime tree, bind schemas, or integrate DOGFOOD.

DX-034G landed active view-stack binding collection in \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i}. The restraint is that the runtime stack only decides which declared binding sources are active; it still does not render, subscribe, refresh, dispatch, resolve provider handles, or retain caches.

DX-034H landed provider-update invalidation and frame assembly as a pure contract helper. The restraint is that snapshot updates create new immutable frames and lifecycle invalidation facts; no provider manager or subscription loop exists yet.

DX-034I landed command intent emission and runtime command-buffer routing. The restraint is that command routes map intent records to command values; business logic still applies commands later through the existing runtime command buffer.

DX-034 is landed for the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release boundary. The shipped release floor is the explicit data-binding contract layer: immutable snapshots and frames, provider scopes, view data contracts, structural AppShell composition, active binding lifecycle facts, active runtime binding collection, provider-update frame assembly, command intent routing, and closeout proof that a provider-bound AppShell can render \texttt{n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r}, and \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s} regions from immutable binding frames without exposing provider, subscription, refresh, or dispatch handles to rendered output.

Provider-bound AppShell proof is present in the DX-034 closeout cycle test. The proof intentionally stays pure: provider subscriptions and cache policy remain runtime/provider responsibilities, while the release contract proves the boundary that views consume immutable frames and emit command intents.

DOGFOOD binding-state proof is present through the standard block story states and Blocks preview lowering checks for ready, loading, stale, empty, and error states. Broader production AppShell behavior can now build on the landed contract without keeping issue \#182 open.

\chapter{DX-036 Responsive Table Layout and Variants}\label{record-070}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-036-responsive-table-layout-and-variants.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DX-036 Responsive table layout and variants
legend: DX
lane: design
priority: medium
keywords:
  - table
  - layout
  - responsive
  - lowering
  - developer-experience

\end{RecordMeta}

Make \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} behave more like builders expect from a table: it should fit the available width by default, wrap cell content intelligently, and expose named style variants without forcing users to choose a separate component.

Legend:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DX-developer-experience.md}{DX - Developer Experience}
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-070-sponsor-human}

App builders using \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for command output, reports, diagnostics, and docs snippets should get readable tabular output without hand-calculating column widths for every terminal size.

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-070-sponsor-agent}

Agents generating Bijou CLI output should be able to choose a table variant and pipe format declaratively, while trusting the component to fit the viewport, wrap cells, preserve data in machine modes, and remain inspectable through tests.

\section{Hill}\label{record-070-hill}

A builder can render dense comparison data with \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and get responsive, word-aware, aligned output by default, while choosing explicit visual variants and explicit pipe/data formats without switching components.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-070-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does a default human-mode \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} fit \texttt{c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s} when content would otherwise exceed the terminal?
\item
  Does \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}"} preserve today's content-sized behavior?
\item
  Do wrapped rows keep continuation lines aligned under the correct columns?
\item
  Can callers choose \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}x}, \texttt{a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} as table variants?
\item
  Does \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e} mode still default to TSV?
\item
  Can callers explicitly request CSV, Markdown, TSV, or ASCII grid pipe output?
\item
  Are ANSI styles, OSC 8 links, emoji, CJK, and combining graphemes measured by visible terminal width rather than string length?
\item
  Does \texttt{a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} mode keep row/header/value semantics independent of the visual variant?
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Posture}\label{record-070-accessibility-assistive-posture}

Visual variants must not change the accessible reading contract. Accessible mode should keep a row-oriented header/value narration that is stable even when human output wraps, uses rules, or serializes differently for pipes.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-070-localization-directionality-posture}

The first cycle is not a full bidirectional table layout project. It should keep the existing left-to-right table assumption, but all measurement and wrapping should remain grapheme-aware so localized strings, combining marks, CJK, and emoji do not break alignment.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-070-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

The layout engine should produce a shared fitted table model before rendering. Tests should be able to inspect or prove the resolved widths, wrapped lines, variant renderer output, and pipe serialization independently enough that an agent can explain why a column wrapped or shrank.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-070-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/runtime-truth-wins.md}{Runtime Truth Wins}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are the Spec}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/graceful-lowering-preserves-meaning.md}{Graceful Lowering Preserves Meaning}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/docs-are-the-demo.md}{Docs Are the Demo}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/schemas-live-at-boundaries.md}{Schemas Live At Boundaries}
\end{itemize}

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-070-current-truth}

\texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} currently renders an intrinsic-width Unicode boxed table in human modes:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  columns without explicit \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h} grow to the widest header or cell
\item
  the renderer does not consult \texttt{c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  cells wrap only when a column has an explicit \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h}
\item
  wrapping is grapheme-aware but hard-wraps; it does not prefer word boundaries
\item
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}"} clips text without adding an ellipsis
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e} mode lowers to TSV
\item
  \texttt{a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} mode lowers to \texttt{R\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e}
\end{itemize}

\texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} has the same intrinsic sizing posture: it creates a surface large enough for the table instead of fitting a parent width.

\section{Product Decision}\label{record-070-product-decision}

This should remain a \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} feature, not become a separate \texttt{r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} component.

Add table variants as one API axis, and keep machine/data serialization as a separate axis:

\begin{CodeBlock}
table({
  columns,
  rows,
  layout: 'auto',
  variant: 'ruled',
  pipeFormat: 'tsv',
});
\end{CodeBlock}

Recommended defaults:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}"} for human modes
\item
  \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s} for string rendering when no explicit width is provided
\item
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}"} for human modes
\item
  \texttt{w\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}"} so wrapping prefers whitespace boundaries
\item
  hard-wrap unbreakable tokens rather than losing data
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}"} for \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e} mode
\end{itemize}

Keep an escape hatch:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}"} preserves today's content-sized behavior
\item
  explicit \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h} / \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h} can override the runtime width
\item
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}"} and a future \texttt{o\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}"} can support dense compact output where data loss is acceptable
\end{itemize}

\section{Layout Requirements}\label{record-070-layout-requirements}

Build a shared fitted table model before rendering variants:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Measure headers and cells by visible terminal width, ignoring ANSI and OSC 8 escapes and respecting grapheme widths.
\item
  Compute preferred column widths from content.
\item
  If the preferred table fits the available width, render at natural width.
\item
  If it does not fit, shrink flexible columns toward minimum widths.
\item
  Prefer wrapping cell text at word boundaries.
\item
  Hard-wrap a long unbreakable token only when it cannot fit.
\item
  Preserve alignment for continuation lines by leaving earlier columns blank and padding every column by visible width.
\item
  Recompute from the current width whenever a live TUI rerenders after a terminal resize.
\end{enumerate}

Column options should grow beyond today's fixed \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h}:

\begin{CodeBlock}
type TableColumn = {
  header: string;
  width?: number;
  minWidth?: number;
  maxWidth?: number;
  weight?: number;
  align?: 'left' | 'right' | 'center';
};
\end{CodeBlock}

For \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, the first practical step is explicit \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h} / \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h} support. Parent-surface auto-fit can arrive once parent layout code has a stable way to pass available width down to child surfaces.

\section{Variants To Support}\label{record-070-variants-to-support}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}"}}{}}\label{record-070-variant-box}

The current Unicode boxed table. Keep this as the compatibility visual style, but route it through the fitted table model.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}"}}{}}\label{record-070-variant-ascii-grid}

Portable boxed ASCII table:

\begin{CodeBlock}
+----------+---------+-------+
| Name     | State   | Score |
+----------+---------+-------+
| Alice    | active  | 95    |
| Bob      | pending | 72    |
+----------+---------+-------+
\end{CodeBlock}

This should be available explicitly as a visual variant and as an explicit pipe format, but it should not replace TSV as the default \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e} lowering.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}"}}{}}\label{record-070-variant-ruled}

The desired report style: no outer border, no vertical dividers, heavy header rule, and light row separators.

\begin{CodeBlock}
Name       State     Score
━━━━━━━━━  ━━━━━━━━  ━━━━━
Alice      active    95
─────────  ────────  ─────
Bob        pending   72
\end{CodeBlock}

This variant must support wrapped cells and continuation-line alignment from the first implementation.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}"}}{}}\label{record-070-variant-header-rule}

Compact report style with only a header separator:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Name       State     Score
---------  --------  -----
Alice      active    95
Bob        pending   72
\end{CodeBlock}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}"}}{}}\label{record-070-variant-plain}

Borderless aligned columns:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Name       State     Score
Alice      active    95
Bob        pending   72
\end{CodeBlock}

Use spaces for visual alignment, not tabs. Tabs belong to TSV serialization; space padding is the only reliable way to align ANSI-styled and wide-character terminal content.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}"}}{}}\label{record-070-variant-markdown}

GitHub-flavored Markdown pipe table:

\begin{CodeBlock}
| Name  | State   | Score |
|-------|---------|------:|
| Alice | active  |    95 |
| Bob   | pending |    72 |
\end{CodeBlock}

This is useful both as a human/static variant and as \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}"} when the destination is a README, issue, PR, or docs file. Escape \texttt{|}, backslashes, and multiline cells deliberately.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}"}}{}}\label{record-070-variant-definition}

Two-column field/value output:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Field          Value
━━━━━━━━━━━━━  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
PR             https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/pull/120
State          MERGED
Merged at      2026-05-31T21:30:02Z
\end{CodeBlock}

This can be implemented as a table variant with inferred \texttt{F\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d} and \texttt{V\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e} columns for two-column rows.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}"}}{}}\label{record-070-variant-expanded}

psql-style record inspection:

\begin{CodeBlock}
-[ RECORD 1 ]-------------------------
name   | Alice
state  | active
score  | 95
-[ RECORD 2 ]-------------------------
name   | Bob
state  | pending
score  | 72
\end{CodeBlock}

This is valuable for narrow terminals and many-column records, but it changes the reading mode from row comparison to record inspection. It can follow after the fitted table model and primary variants are stable.

\section{Formats To Support}\label{record-070-formats-to-support}

Keep serializations separate from visual variants:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}"}: default lowest lowering for machine use
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}"}: RFC-style escaped CSV for spreadsheet and shell export
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}"}: docs-friendly pipe table
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}"}: explicit human-readable pipe output
\end{itemize}

TSV should remain the default pipe lowering because \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e} usually means tools, scripts, and data transfer. ASCII grid and Markdown are useful, but they are human presentation formats and should be opt-in.

CSV must quote fields containing comma, quote, CR, LF, or other ambiguous content according to a documented policy. TSV also needs a deliberate escaping or preservation policy for tabs and newlines instead of accidental raw joins.

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-070-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Extract or replace the current table-private width/wrap helpers with a shared fitted table model that can serve all string variants.
\item
  Extend \texttt{T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}n} with optional \texttt{m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h}, \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h}, \texttt{w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t}, and \texttt{a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n}.
\item
  Add \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h} / \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h}, \texttt{v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t}, and word-wrapping options to \texttt{T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Make human modes default to width-aware \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}"} and use \texttt{c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s} when no width is provided.
\item
  Preserve today's content-sized rendering behind \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}"}.
\item
  Render \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}x}, \texttt{a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} from the fitted model.
\item
  Keep TSV as the default pipe lowering, then add explicit CSV, Markdown, and ASCII grid pipe formats with escaping tests.
\item
  Bring \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} to parity for explicit \texttt{w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h} / \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h} once the string model is stable.
\item
  Update DOGFOOD or design-system docs with examples for the human-facing variants.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-070-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A regression proving current intrinsic tables can exceed narrow runtime width, then the new default fits that width.
\item
  A compatibility test proving \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}"} retains old content-sized output.
\item
  Fitted-width tests for fixed, min, max, weighted, and aligned columns.
\item
  Word-boundary wrapping and hard-wrap fallback tests.
\item
  Continuation-line alignment tests for multiline rows.
\item
  ANSI, OSC 8, emoji, CJK, and combining-grapheme alignment tests.
\item
  Snapshot-style tests for \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}x}, \texttt{a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}.
\item
  Pipe-format tests for TSV default, CSV escaping, Markdown escaping, and ASCII grid opt-in lowering.
\item
  Accessible-mode tests proving visual variants do not change semantic row/header/value reading order.
\end{itemize}

\section{Explicit Non-Goals}\label{record-070-explicit-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Do not add \texttt{r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as a separate public component.
\item
  Do not support Org-mode / Emacs table syntax in the first pass.
\item
  Do not make ASCII grid the default \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e} lowering.
\item
  Do not silently truncate data by default.
\item
  Do not redesign \texttt{n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} before the passive \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} model is stable.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Bar}\label{record-070-acceptance-bar}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} defaults to width-aware layout in human modes.
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}"} preserves old content-sized behavior.
\item
  Fixed, minimum, maximum, weighted, and aligned columns are covered by tests.
\item
  Word-boundary wrapping uses shared text wrapping behavior where possible.
\item
  ANSI, OSC 8 links, emoji, CJK, and combining graphemes stay aligned.
\item
  Wrapped rows keep continuation lines under the correct columns.
\item
  \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}x}, \texttt{a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} variants have snapshot-style tests.
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}"}, \texttt{"\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}"}, \texttt{"\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}"}, and \texttt{"\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}"} are covered with escaping tests.
\item
  \texttt{a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} mode preserves semantic row/header/value reading order.
\item
  DOGFOOD or design-system docs show at least \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}x}, \texttt{r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} examples.
\item
  Follow-on work is filed for \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d} if it is not implemented in the first cycle.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-070-retrospective}

Closed by adding a shared fitted string-table model behind \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.

Shipped behavior:

  human-mode \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} now defaults to width-aware \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}"}
\item

\item
  constrained cells wrap at word boundaries by default and hard-wrap only when needed
\item
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}n} supports \texttt{m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h}, \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h}, \texttt{w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t}, and \texttt{a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n}
\item
  visual variants now include \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}x}, \texttt{a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, and \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}
\item

\chapter{DX-038 - BlockLab Rename And Migration}\label{record-071}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-038-blocklab-rename-and-migration.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: "DX-038 - BlockLab Rename And Migration"
legend: DX
lane: design
issue: https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/271

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Linked Issue}\label{record-071-linked-issue}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/271
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-071-sponsored-human}

A Bijou maintainer wants the story and component workbench to have a project-owned name that does not imply affiliation with the browser Storybook product, while keeping the existing workflow understandable for users who already know \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k}.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-071-sponsored-agent}

An agent needs stable names for scripts, Blocks, command intents, surface ids, and docs links. It should not have to infer whether ``storybook'' means Bijou's terminal workbench, the external product, or a generic story-driven workflow.

\section{Hill}\label{record-071-hill}

Rename the current Storybook-labeled workstation to \textbf{BlockLab} across human visible surfaces and future-facing contracts, while preserving a short compatibility path for existing commands.

This is product hygiene, not a legal conclusion. The current name creates avoidable ambiguity because Storybook is an established external product. Bijou can keep story-driven component development while naming its own terminal-native surface differently.

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-071-current-truth}

The current repo exposes a story-driven workstation through:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x}
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  visible labels such as \texttt{B\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k}, \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k}, and \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}
\item
  DOGFOOD Block and registry names such as \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  docs that describe a ``Storybook-style'' workbench
\end{itemize}

The product shape is already useful: it has a story catalog, variants, profile presets, structured docs fields, matrix capture, AppFrame integration, and a text-first index. The naming layer is the weak part.

\section{Name Decision}\label{record-071-name-decision}

Use \textbf{BlockLab} as the product name.

\texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} & \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} \\
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h} & \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h} \\
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y} & \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y} \\
\texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k} & \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b} \\
\texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x} & \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x} \\
\end{longtable}
}

Compatibility aliases should remain for one migration window:

\begin{CodeBlock}
npm run storybook
npm run storybook:index
npm run dogfood:storybook
\end{CodeBlock}

Those aliases should call the BlockLab entrypoints and may print a concise deprecation note if the runtime can do so without polluting deterministic index output.

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Posture}\label{record-071-accessibility-assistive-posture}

The rename must not make the workbench more visual-only. Every renamed surface keeps existing lower-mode facts:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  story id
\item
  story title
\item
  package
\item
  source path
\item
  selected variant
\item
  selected profile
\item
  required mode coverage
\item
  capture matrix status
\end{itemize}

Future \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b} labels should be localizable visible text. Machine tokens such as command ids and event discriminants can use \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}*} but should not be translated.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-071-localization-directionality-posture}

New visible strings must enter \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v} with \texttt{e\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{f\allowbreak{}r}, \texttt{e\allowbreak{}s}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e} rows. The rename should update generated catalog files in the same PR, and \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e} should be run against the branch.

Directionality does not change for this rename. The UI must continue to route localized copy through DOGFOOD's localization port rather than hard-coded view helpers.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-071-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

Agents should be able to tell that \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b} is the canonical surface without scraping UI strings. The rename should update:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Block metadata names and tags
\item
  surface inventory ids and descriptions
\item
  command intents
\item
  story matrix report titles
\item
  deterministic index title
\item
  docs references
\end{itemize}

The compatibility aliases should be treated as command-level affordances, not as canonical product names.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-071-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  GitHub Issues are the live tracker; this design is linked to \#271.
\item
  DOGFOOD localization completeness gates protect new visible strings.
\item
  Blocks own product semantics; components remain leaf rendering vocabulary.
\item
  Text-first outputs stay deterministic for CI, agents, and fixtures.
\end{itemize}

\section{Migration Plan}\label{record-071-migration-plan}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Introduce BlockLab docs language and visible product labels.
\item
  Add \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b} and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x} scripts.
\item
  Keep \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k} as compatibility aliases for one migration window.
\item
  Rename user-visible AppFrame page title and settings label.
\item
  Rename DOGFOOD Block contracts and registry entries from \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} to \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}.
\item
  Rename command intents and surface ids from \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}*} to \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}*}.
\item
  Update localization rows and generated catalogs.
\item
  Update docs, tests, and teardown command tables.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-071-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A focused rename test that expects the default title to be \texttt{B\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b}.
\item
  A framed AppFrame test that expects the page title \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b}.
\item
  A DOGFOOD settings test that expects \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}.
\item
  A Block metadata test that expects \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}.
\item
  A script-registration test proving \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b} and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x} exist and legacy scripts still resolve.
\item
  An i18n completeness run proving every changed visible string has supported locale rows.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-071-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  No direct Storybook compatibility layer.
\item
  No browser runtime.
\item
  No package rename outside the workbench surface.
\item
  No claim about trademark law.
\item
  No removal of compatibility scripts in the first rename PR.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective Target}\label{record-071-retrospective-target}

The rename is successful when humans see \texttt{B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b}, agents see \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}*} contracts, and legacy \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k} commands still work long enough for users to move without friction.

\chapter{DX-039 - BlockLab Product Parity}\label{record-072}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-039-blocklab-product-parity.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: "DX-039 - BlockLab Product Parity"
legend: DX
lane: design
issue: https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/272

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Linked Issue}\label{record-072-linked-issue}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/272
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-072-sponsored-human}

A component author wants BlockLab to feel like a real component development product: searchable, controllable, inspectable, test-aware, and useful for building the next Bijou Block without dropping into the full DOGFOOD docs app.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-072-sponsored-agent}

An agent needs one stable story surface that can produce docs, fixtures, lower-mode captures, interaction playback, visual evidence, source links, and machine-readable reports without scraping terminal frames.

\section{Hill}\label{record-072-hill}

Evolve BlockLab from ``story catalog plus preview'' into a terminal-native component and Block laboratory that borrows the strongest workflows from the current Storybook product without cloning its browser UI.

\section{Source Scan}\label{record-072-source-scan}

Official Storybook documentation reviewed on 2026-06-03:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Args: https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-stories/args
\item
  Controls: https://storybook.js.org/docs/essentials/controls
\item
  Toolbars and globals: https://storybook.js.org/docs/essentials/toolbars-and-globals
\item
  Viewport: https://storybook.js.org/docs/essentials/viewport
\item
  Decorators: https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-stories/decorators
\item
  Docs and Autodocs: https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-docs/autodocs
\item
  MDX and doc blocks: https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-docs/mdx
\item
  Interaction testing: https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-tests/interaction-testing
\item
  Accessibility testing: https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-tests/accessibility-testing
\item
  Visual testing: https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-tests/visual-testing
\item
  Addon types: https://storybook.js.org/docs/addons/addon-types
\item
  Storybook composition: https://storybook.js.org/docs/sharing/storybook-composition
\end{itemize}

The product lesson is not ``make a browser Storybook clone.'' The lesson is that a mature story workbench separates story data, controls, global context, preview, generated docs, addon panels, and test artifacts while keeping them linked by stable story ids.

\section{Current Bijou Truth}\label{record-072-current-bijou-truth}

BlockLab's current pre-rename substrate already has:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y} records with \texttt{i\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y}, \texttt{t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e}, docs, profile presets, variants, source, and tags
\item
  canonical profile presets for \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e}, and \texttt{a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}
\item
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for deterministic text output
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for profile x variant capture
\item
  a three-pane interactive TUI: catalog, preview, and testing
\item
  AppFrame integration and a surface Block contract
\end{itemize}

The missing layer is product workflow.

\section{Protocol Sketch}\label{record-072-protocol-sketch}

\texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y} can grow without breaking existing records by adding optional fields:

\begin{CodeBlock}
interface BlockLabControl {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly kind: 'boolean' | 'number' | 'text' | 'select' | 'color' | 'json';
  readonly defaultValue: unknown;
  readonly options?: readonly unknown[];
}

interface BlockLabGlobals {
  readonly mode?: OutputMode;
  readonly width?: number;
  readonly locale?: string;
  readonly direction?: 'ltr' | 'rtl';
  readonly theme?: string;
  readonly density?: string;
  readonly reducedMotion?: boolean;
}

interface BlockLabPanelReport {
  readonly panelId: string;
  readonly status: 'pass' | 'warn' | 'fail' | 'info';
  readonly facts: readonly ExplanationFact[];
  readonly output: string;
}
\end{CodeBlock}

The first implementation should keep these fields optional and derive defaults from the current profile presets.

\section{Feature Slices}\label{record-072-feature-slices}

\subsection{1. Args/Controls}\label{record-072-argscontrols}

Add serializable controls to stories and a control pane in BlockLab.

Proof:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  controls render in TUI and lower modes
\item
  control changes feed story render input deterministically
\item
  CLI output includes selected args
\end{itemize}

\subsection{2. Globals/Toolbars}\label{record-072-globalstoolbars}

Add global context for mode, width, locale, direction, theme, density, and reduced motion.

Proof:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  global state affects preview context
\item
  lower modes report globals
\item
  locale/direction changes route through DOGFOOD localization ports
\end{itemize}

\subsection{3. Decorators/Harnesses}\label{record-072-decoratorsharnesses}

Add a story harness chain for common setup: AppFrame, providers, mock IO, binding snapshots, theme, and viewport.

Proof:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  harnesses compose without mutating base context
\item
  a story can declare provider data without bespoke preview code
\end{itemize}

\subsection{4. Docs Blocks}\label{record-072-docs-blocks}

Replace fixed markdown assembly with docs block composition.

Proof:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  docs view can show source, controls, lowerings, story matrix, and related stories as separate inspectable blocks
\item
  pipe mode can emit those blocks in deterministic order
\end{itemize}

\subsection{5. Addon-Like Panels}\label{record-072-addon-like-panels}

Introduce panel slots for actions/events, accessibility facts, visual diffs, performance facts, binding state, and source.

Proof:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  each panel has a stable id and lower-mode report
\item
  disabled panels do not affect preview rendering
\end{itemize}

\subsection{6. Interaction Playback}\label{record-072-interaction-playback}

Let stories declare deterministic play steps that can run in BlockLab, CI, and text-first output.

Proof:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED/GREEN tests for one story-local playback
\item
  playback report includes steps, status, elapsed time, and artifacts
\end{itemize}

\subsection{7. Composition}\label{record-072-composition}

Allow BlockLab to import multiple story catalogs.

Proof:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  composed catalogs preserve package/source facts
\item
  duplicate story ids fail loudly
\item
  CLI can filter by package, family, tag, and source
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Posture}\label{record-072-accessibility-assistive-posture}

BlockLab parity must improve lower-mode truth, not just add visual panels. Every product feature needs accessible and pipe output:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  controls list active values
\item
  globals list current context
\item
  panels list status and findings
\item
  interactions list steps and outcomes
\item
  visual reports describe line/cell differences
\item
  docs blocks preserve heading order
\end{itemize}

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-072-localization-directionality-posture}

Controls and globals are visible UI. Labels, panel names, and status text must go through DOGFOOD localization when they appear in DOGFOOD-owned surfaces. Story ids, arg ids, and artifact paths remain machine tokens.

Directionality belongs in globals. RTL preview should be a first-class context state, not a separate story variant unless the variant is semantically different.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-072-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

The text-first command should eventually emit:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x}
\item
  \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}>}
\item
  \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}>}
\item
  \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}>}
\item
  \texttt{b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}>}
\end{itemize}

Each command should produce stable sections that agents can parse without screen scraping. JSON output can be added later, but plain text remains the first evidence surface because it is easier to review in PRs.

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-072-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Protocol tests for optional controls and globals.
\item
  Workbench model tests proving controls, globals, panels, and docs blocks are discoverable without rendering.
\item
  TUI tests proving controls and globals change preview output.
\item
  Lower-mode tests proving pipe and accessible output include args/controls and panel statuses.
\item
  Interaction playback tests using fake clocks and deterministic input.
\item
  Visual artifact tests using fixed-size terminal captures.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-072-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  No browser Storybook runtime.
\item
  No direct addon API compatibility promise.
\item
  No screenshots-only acceptance criteria.
\item
  No story catalog fork separate from DOGFOOD story truth.
\item
  No hidden global registry.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective Target}\label{record-072-retrospective-target}

BlockLab is product-grade when a maintainer can open one terminal workbench, adjust story inputs, switch global context, read generated docs, run playback, inspect a11y/visual/performance findings, and export deterministic evidence for CI or agents.

This follow-up keeps the scope intentionally narrow: fix exactly the two review comments, preserve the v7 closeout behavior, and leave broader table or title treatment redesigns for later cycles.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-073-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A DOGFOOD reader on a medium-width terminal needs the release-title guide to fit the actual viewport instead of drawing a wider box.
\item
  A TUI author using \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} expects readable fitted text by default, matching the word-wrap posture already established by \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  A review agent needs the reported regressions captured as deterministic tests so the branch proves the fix instead of relying on prose.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-073-hill}

A maintainer can run deterministic tests that reproduce both post-merge review comments, then see the title renderer stay within requested widths and \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} preserve word boundaries when fitting string cells.

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-073-current-truth}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}'\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}'\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\}\allowbreak{})} selects the wide renderer even though wide output is 60 columns.
\item
  The new fitted \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} path wraps shrunk string cells through \texttt{w\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, which chunks at hard cell boundaries and can split words such as \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} and \texttt{e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.
\item

\section{Framing}\label{record-074-framing}

Issue \#305 adds a small, runnable side app that proves image browsing and image-to-glyph rendering as a real workflow instead of only as DOGFOOD title art. The app should use a sidebar file explorer, render the selected image in a main preview pane, let the user hot-swap between Braille and ASCII output, and expose enough tuning controls to discuss how image-to-text filters behave.

The app stays intentionally small: it reuses \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for the filesystem browser and \texttt{r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for glyph rendering. Codec support is dependency-free and scoped to formats the repo can test deterministically.

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-074-sponsor-human}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer wants to point Bijou at local assets and quickly inspect how they look as terminal glyph art.
\item
  A designer wants to compare Braille density against ASCII density without restarting the app.
\item
  A contributor wants a concrete example of \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} driving a real side-by-side tool.
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-074-sponsor-agent}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A review agent needs the file browser, selected path, renderer mode, decoded frame, and visible glyph output to be inspectable through tests.
\item
  A future block-promotion agent needs evidence that the file picker can drive a richer app before promoting image browsing into a public block family.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-074-hill}

A user can launch the image viewer, browse supported image files in a sidebar, select an image, and see the main pane render that image as Braille or ASCII glyphs. Pressing \texttt{m} swaps the render mode immediately. The preview pane also supports pan and zoom so a user can inspect image details without leaving the side app. The same pane lets the user preserve sampled image colors, adjust Braille threshold and contrast, and toggle ordered dithering.

| > d icons/                  | |                                            |
|   - Bijou.svg               | |   ⣿⣿⣿⣿⣿⣶⣤...                    |

q quit  Enter open/select  <- parent  m mode  c color  d dither
\end{CodeBlock}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} as a runnable side app.
\item
  Add \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} for dependency-free PNG and PPM decoding.
\item
  Reuse the existing SVG rasterizer for SVG preview.
\item
  Add \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}.
\item

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-074-non-goals}
