\section{Runtime Contract}\label{record-074-runtime-contract}

The app starts in \texttt{a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/} by default. If the user passes a directory, that directory becomes the file-picker root. If the user passes an image file, the file's parent directory becomes the root and the file starts selected.

Supported input formats:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  SVG: rasterized into a transparent RGBA frame at preview resolution.
\item
  PNG: 8-bit, non-interlaced RGB/RGBA.
\item
  PPM/PNM: \texttt{P\allowbreak{}3} and \texttt{P\allowbreak{}6} RGB Netpbm data.
\end{itemize}

Navigation contract:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{j} / \texttt{k}: move file-picker focus.
\item
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}: select focused image or open focused directory.
\item
  \texttt{B\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}: move the file picker to its parent directory.
\item
  Arrow keys: pan the image viewport.
\item
  \texttt{+} / \texttt{=}: zoom in.
\item
  \texttt{-}: zoom out.
\item
  \texttt{0}: reset to fit.
\item
  \texttt{m} / \texttt{T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b}: switch Braille and ASCII rendering.
\item
  \texttt{c}: cycle color mode between monochrome, full color, and foreground-only color.
\item
  \texttt{d}: toggle ordered dithering.
\item
  \texttt{[} / \texttt{]}: lower or raise the Braille threshold.
\item
  \texttt{,} / \texttt{.}: lower or raise contrast.
\end{itemize}

The file picker marks focus with \texttt{>} and the rendered image with \texttt{*}. The preview gutter reports zoom percentage, pan offset, color mode, dithering mode, threshold, and contrast. The initial image and every newly selected image start at \texttt{1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\%} fit, centered horizontally and vertically.

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-074-lower-modes}

The app is interactive-first. Pipe/static smoke only needs to prove startup and first-frame rendering; the selected path and mode remain ordinary model state for tests.

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Posture}\label{record-074-accessibility-assistive-posture}

The file picker remains textual. The preview pane names the selected file, render mode, format, dimensions, and tuning state so the image is not only communicated by glyph art.

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-074-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED: PNG decoder cannot map synthetic RGB/RGBA PNGs into RGBA.
\item
  RED: PPM decoder cannot map \texttt{P\allowbreak{}3} and \texttt{P\allowbreak{}6} RGB data into RGBA.
\item
  RED: image viewer starts with an image selected from the root.
\item
  RED: pressing \texttt{m} does not change Braille mode to ASCII mode.
\item
  RED: pressing \texttt{c} does not preserve sampled light and dark image colors on rendered glyph cells.
\item
  RED: threshold, contrast, and dither controls do not change visible tuning state.
\item
  RED: rendered view does not contain the file picker and preview panes.
\end{itemize}

\section{Validation}\label{record-074-validation}

\begin{CodeBlock}
npx vitest run scripts/image-viewer.test.ts scripts/svg-raster.test.ts packages/bijou-tui/src/raster-glyph.test.ts
npm run typecheck:test
npm run lint
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Follow-On Debt}\label{record-074-follow-on-debt}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add JPEG/WebP support behind an explicit codec adapter decision.
\item
  Decide whether this app should become part of DOGFOOD or stay an example.
\item
  Promote a first-class image/file-browser block only after the side-app shape proves stable.
\item
  Add error-diffusion algorithms such as Floyd-Steinberg or Atkinson once the ordered-dither baseline has enough usage feedback.
\item
  Add palette quantization and custom charset editing if the side app graduates into a broader image-to-text workbench.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DX-042 Shared UI Scene IR And Bijou Render Target}\label{record-075}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-042-shared-ui-scene-ir-and-bijou-render-target.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DX-042 Shared UI Scene IR And Bijou Render Target
legend: DX
lane: cool-ideas
priority: medium
github_issue: 302
status: proposed
keywords:
  - developer-experience
  - ir
  - geordi
  - wesley
  - surface
  - provenance

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DX-developer-experience.md}{DX - Developer Experience}

\section{Linked Work}\label{record-075-linked-work}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  User story: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/302}{\#302}
\item
  Roadmap candidate: Runtime Graph And Scene IR
\item
  This document is a planning artifact only. It records the shared IR boundary for the \#302 idea; it does not claim implementation of the IR, a compiler, or a renderer integration in this PR.
\end{itemize}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-075-decision-summary}

Bijou \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} should be treated as a deterministic terminal render target for a portable UI scene IR, not as the portable IR itself.

The shared IR should sit above Bijou and Geordi:

\begin{CodeBlock}
GraphQL SDL / authored source
  -> Wesley semantic graph and domain law
    -> ui-scene-ir/1
      -> bijou-layout/1
        -> Bijou Surface
          -> terminal cells

      -> geordi-ir/1
        -> Geordi renderer
          -> pixels and render receipts
\end{CodeBlock}

This keeps the final renderer substrates honest. Geordi owns pixel-oriented render proof. Bijou owns terminal cell rendering, input, focus, runtime interaction, and agent-legible surfaces. The shared IR owns portable scene structure, semantic identity, bindings, localization references, theme token references, actions, and source maps.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-075-sponsored-human}

A builder wants to describe a UI scene once and render it through either Geordi or Bijou so that browser/native artifacts and terminal artifacts stay aligned without manually maintaining two different scene descriptions.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-075-sponsored-agent}

An agent wants a source-mapped, inspectable scene contract so it can audit which localized strings, theme tokens, bindings, actions, and rendered cells came from the same authored scene.

\section{Hill}\label{record-075-hill}

A scene authored as a semantic UI contract can lower to both a Geordi render artifact and a Bijou terminal surface, with structural receipts proving that node identity, text keys, token references, bindings, and actions stayed in sync across both targets.

\section{Core Rule}\label{record-075-core-rule}

The portable IR describes scene intent.

Bijou \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} describes rendered terminal output.

Those are different layers:

\begin{CodeBlock}
ui-scene-ir/1
  describes: nodes, text keys, token refs, bindings, actions, source maps

bijou-layout/1
  describes: terminal layout, focus graph, keymap, viewport regions

Bijou Surface
  describes: final cell grid with glyphs, colors, modifiers, opacity, masks
\end{CodeBlock}

Bijou may render a shared scene IR. Geordi may render the same shared scene IR. Neither system should pretend that terminal cells and pixels are the same final substrate.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-075-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Which authored scene node produced this rendered cell or pixel region?
\item
  Which localization key produced this text?
\item
  Which theme token produced this foreground or background color?
\item
  Which action or key binding is attached to this node?
\item
  Which renderer-specific target profile lowered this scene?
\item
  Which target-specific claims are proven, and which are explicit nonclaims?
\item
  Can the Geordi and Bijou outputs prove structural parity without claiming pixel parity?
\item
  Can compile-time checks catch missing localization keys and raw color usage before runtime?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Boundary}\label{record-075-boundary}

This design is about a portable scene contract and renderer-specific lowering.

It is not about:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  replacing Bijou's runtime loop
\item
  replacing Bijou \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}
\item
  making terminal cells behave like pixels
\item
  making Geordi own terminal input or focus
\item
  making Wesley a renderer
\item
  forcing every existing Bijou block to be authored in GraphQL immediately
\item
  claiming pixel-perfect parity between terminal and browser render targets
\end{itemize}

\section{Role Model}\label{record-075-role-model}

\subsection{Wesley}\label{record-075-wesley}

Wesley owns semantic compilation and domain law.

For this design, Wesley can:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  parse GraphQL SDL or another schema-backed authoring source
\item
  validate schema shape
\item
  generate TypeScript and Rust types
\item
  validate localization requirements
\item
  validate style token requirements
\item
  compute schema hashes
\item
  produce or validate \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}
\end{itemize}

Wesley should not render terminal cells or pixels.

\subsection{Shared UI Scene IR}\label{record-075-shared-ui-scene-ir}

\texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} owns portable scene structure.

It should carry enough information for both Bijou and Geordi to lower the same scene while preserving source identity.

It should know about:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  scene node IDs
\item
  node kinds
\item
  semantic roles
\item
  layout intent
\item
  text and localization references
\item
  theme token references
\item
  bindings
\item
  actions
\item
  source maps
\item
  target profile requirements
\end{itemize}

It should not know about:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  terminal escape sequences
\item
  renderer dirty-region internals
\item
  final RGB cell caches
\item
  subpixel antialiasing details
\item
  host-specific input event loops
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Geordi}\label{record-075-geordi}

Geordi owns pixel-oriented render artifacts and receipts.

For this design, Geordi lowers \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} to \texttt{g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, then renders or verifies the pixel artifact under a declared target profile.

Geordi claims:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  explicit pixel geometry
\item
  font and asset requirements
\item
  visual receipt hashes
\item
  target profile facts
\item
  browser/native renderer parity where supported
\end{itemize}

Geordi does not claim:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  terminal focus semantics
\item
  terminal key routing
\item
  cell-level glyph approximations
\item
  Bijou runtime state updates
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Bijou}\label{record-075-bijou}

Bijou owns terminal runtime behavior and terminal render targets.

For this design, Bijou lowers \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} to \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, then renders that layout into a \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.

Bijou claims:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  deterministic terminal cell output
\item
  focus and input routing
\item
  theme token resolution
\item
  localization lowering
\item
  cell-level provenance
\item
  surface receipts
\item
  agent-readable inspection through structured surfaces
\end{itemize}

Bijou does not claim:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  browser pixel parity
\item
  native canvas fidelity
\item
  subpixel antialiasing
\item
  font-pack proof identical to Geordi
\end{itemize}

\section{Relationship Diagram}\label{record-075-relationship-diagram}

\begin{center}
\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[booknode/.style={draw=BookHeading,line width=.6pt,fill=BookPanel,rounded corners=1.5pt,align=center,text width=29mm,minimum height=10mm,inner sep=5pt,font=\small},bookedge/.style={-{Latex[length=2mm]},draw=BookHeading,line width=.65pt},every edge quotes/.style={font=\scriptsize,fill=white,inner sep=2pt,text=BookMuted}]
\node[booknode] (SDL) at (0,0) {Graph\allowbreak{}QL SDL or authored source};
\node[booknode] (W) at (0,-1.6) {Wesley semantic compiler};
\node[booknode] (IR) at (0,-3.2) {ui-scene-ir/1};
\node[booknode] (BIR) at (-3.5,-4.9) {bijou-layout/1};
\node[booknode] (Surface) at (-3.5,-6.5) {Bijou Surface};
\node[booknode] (Terminal) at (-5,-8.2) {Terminal cells};
\node[booknode] (GIR) at (3.5,-4.9) {geordi-ir/1};
\node[booknode] (Pixels) at (1.8,-6.8) {Pixels};
\node[booknode] (GR) at (5.2,-6.8) {Geordi receipt};
\node[booknode] (BR) at (-1.5,-8.2) {Bijou surface receipt};
\draw[bookedge,] (SDL) to (W);
\draw[bookedge,] (W) to (IR);
\draw[bookedge,] (IR) to (BIR);
\draw[bookedge,] (BIR) to (Surface);
\draw[bookedge,] (Surface) to (Terminal);
\draw[bookedge,] (Surface) to (BR);
\draw[bookedge,] (IR) to (GIR);
\draw[bookedge,] (GIR) to (Pixels);
\draw[bookedge,] (GIR) to (GR);
\end{tikzpicture}}
\end{center}

\section{Target Profile Diagram}\label{record-075-target-profile-diagram}

\begin{CodeBlock}
ui-scene-ir/1
  targetProfiles:
    - kind: geordi-pixel
      width: 1280
      height: 720
      colorProfile: truecolor
      claims:
        - pixel geometry
        - font metrics
        - asset hashes

    - kind: bijou-cell
      cols: 120
      rows: 40
      glyphProfile: ansi-unicode
      claims:
        - structural hierarchy
        - cell occupancy
        - token provenance
        - i18n provenance
\end{CodeBlock}

The target profile makes renderer differences explicit. A Bijou terminal render can claim structural parity and cell-level determinism without claiming that it matches Geordi pixels exactly.

\section{Proposed IR Shape}\label{record-075-proposed-ir-shape}

The shared scene IR should be plain data. The first draft can stay intentionally small:

\begin{CodeBlock}
type UiSceneIr = {
  irVersion: 'ui-scene-ir/1';
  id: string;
  sourceHash: string;
  rootNodeId: string;
  nodes: UiNode[];
  bindings: UiBinding[];
  actions: UiAction[];
  tokenUses: UiTokenUse[];
  i18nUses: UiI18nUse[];
  sourceMap: UiSourceMapEntry[];
  targetProfiles: UiTargetProfile[];
};
\end{CodeBlock}

\subsection{Nodes}\label{record-075-nodes}

\begin{CodeBlock}
type UiNode = {
  id: string;
  kind: 'box' | 'text' | 'image' | 'group' | 'list' | 'table' | 'custom';
  role?: string;
  parentId?: string;
  children?: string[];
  layout?: UiLayoutIntent;
  text?: UiTextRef;
  style?: UiStyleRef;
  actions?: string[];
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
};
\end{CodeBlock}

Nodes are semantic scene members. They are not terminal cells and they are not pixel rectangles, even when a renderer later lowers them into cells or rectangles.

\subsection{Text}\label{record-075-text}

\begin{CodeBlock}
type UiTextRef =
  | { kind: 'literal'; value: string }
  | { kind: 'i18n'; key: string; fallback?: string };
\end{CodeBlock}

Literal text should be allowed for fixture work and generated artifacts, but product surfaces should prefer \texttt{i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n} references when they are user-facing.

\subsection{Style}\label{record-075-style}

\begin{CodeBlock}
type UiStyleRef = {
  fg?: { token: string };
  bg?: { token: string };
  border?: { token: string };
  modifiers?: string[];
};
\end{CodeBlock}

The IR should carry token references, not only resolved colors. Renderers can resolve tokens later against dark or light themes. Lower modes can preserve the token name when color is unavailable.

\subsection{Bindings}\label{record-075-bindings}

\begin{CodeBlock}
type UiBinding = {
  id: string;
  targetNodeId: string;
  targetProperty: string;
  source: {
    kind: 'state' | 'query' | 'computed';
    path: string;
  };
  when?: string;
};
\end{CodeBlock}

Bindings are data, not hidden callbacks. They make dynamic surfaces auditable and compile-time-checkable.

\subsection{Actions}\label{record-075-actions}

\begin{CodeBlock}
type UiAction = {
  id: string;
  label?: UiTextRef;
  command: string;
  keybindings?: string[];
  targetNodeId?: string;
};
\end{CodeBlock}

Actions let Bijou preserve focus and input contracts while Geordi can still render the same action affordances as visual artifacts.

\section{Bijou Lowering}\label{record-075-bijou-lowering}

Bijou lowering turns portable intent into a terminal-specific layout contract:

\begin{CodeBlock}
type BijouLayoutIr = {
  irVersion: 'bijou-layout/1';
  sceneHash: string;
  nodes: LayoutNode[];
  focusGraph: FocusGraph;
  keymap: KeyBinding[];
  viewportRegions: ViewportRegion[];
  themeRequirements: TokenRequirement[];
  localeRequirements: I18nRequirement[];
  sourceMap: UiToCellSourceMap[];
};
\end{CodeBlock}

The final render target remains \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.

\begin{CodeBlock}
ui-scene-ir/1
  -> bijou-layout/1
    -> Surface
      -> terminal
\end{CodeBlock}

The \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} can then be inspected, hashed, diffed, serialized for MCP, or recorded in a renderer playback artifact.

\section{Geordi Lowering}\label{record-075-geordi-lowering}

Geordi lowering turns portable intent into a pixel-oriented render contract:

\begin{CodeBlock}
ui-scene-ir/1
  -> geordi-ir/1
    -> browser/native renderer
      -> pixel buffer
      -> receipt
\end{CodeBlock}

Geordi can preserve the same node IDs, token references, localization references, and source maps while resolving geometry and render-profile facts for pixel output.

\section{Cross-Renderer Structural Receipt}\label{record-075-cross-renderer-structural-receipt}

The first proof should not compare pixels to cells. It should compare shared structure.

\begin{CodeBlock}
type SharedSceneReceipt = {
  sceneHash: string;
  sourceHash: string;
  nodeIds: string[];
  i18nKeys: string[];
  tokenRefs: string[];
  actionIds: string[];
  bindingIds: string[];
  outputs: {
    geordi?: {
      irHash: string;
      receiptHash: string;
    };
    bijou?: {
      layoutHash: string;
      surfaceHash: string;
    };
  };
};
\end{CodeBlock}

This answers the important question:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Did both targets render the same authored scene contract?
\end{CodeBlock}

It does not falsely answer:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Are terminal cells pixel-perfect replicas of browser pixels?
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Debug And Provenance Files}\label{record-075-debug-and-provenance-files}

This design connects directly to the proposed stable debug logs:

\begin{CodeBlock}
<repo>/.bijou/debug.i18n.jsonl
<repo>/.bijou/debug.style.jsonl
\end{CodeBlock}

The logs should record first appearance or provenance changes, not every frame.

Example i18n line:

\begin{CodeBlock}
{"scene":"docs.home","node":"hero.title","key":"dogfood.home.title","locale":"en","status":"resolved"}
\end{CodeBlock}

Example style line:

\begin{CodeBlock}
{"scene":"docs.home","node":"hero.title","slot":"fg","token":"semantic.primary","mode":"dark","status":"resolved"}
\end{CodeBlock}

The eventual goal is to catch these issues earlier through IR validation:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  missing localization key
\item
  unsupported locale
\item
  raw color in product surface
\item
  unresolved token
\item
  unsafe token pair
\item
  binding target that does not exist
\item
  action without a command
\end{itemize}

Runtime logs remain useful as proof of what actually appeared.

\section{Authoring Model}\label{record-075-authoring-model}

GraphQL SDL remains the strongest candidate authoring source because Wesley and Geordi already use schema-backed compilation patterns.

The authoring source may look like this in spirit:

\begin{CodeBlock}
type DocsHomeScene
  @ui_scene(id: "docs.home")
  @ui_target(kind: "bijou-cell", cols: 120, rows: 40)
  @ui_target(kind: "geordi-pixel", width: 1280, height: 720) {
  title: String!
    @ui_node(id: "hero.title", kind: "text")
    @ui_text(key: "dogfood.home.title")
    @ui_style(fg: "semantic.primary")

  openAction: String
    @ui_action(id: "docs.open", command: "docs.open", keybindings: ["Enter"])
}
\end{CodeBlock}

This is not final syntax. The important contract is that scene structure, text, style, binding, and action identity are compile-time data.

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-075-lower-modes}

The shared IR should make lower modes more deterministic.

For example, Bijou could render diagnostic modes:

\begin{CodeBlock}
normal:
  Start Here

i18n lowering:
  dogfood.nav.startHere

token lowering:
  semantic.primary on surface.primary.bg

binding lowering:
  docs.currentPage.title <- route.currentPage.title
\end{CodeBlock}

These modes are easier to test than screenshots and more useful to agents than raw escape sequences.

\section{Scope}\label{record-075-scope}

The first implementation slice should include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a design document for \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}
\item
  one tiny fixture scene
\item
  a structural receipt format
\item
  a Bijou lowering proof to \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}
\item
  a Geordi lowering proof or adapter stub if Geordi integration is not yet ready inside this repository
\item
  tests proving node IDs, token refs, i18n keys, actions, and bindings survive lowering
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-075-non-goals}

The first slice should not:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  migrate DOGFOOD wholesale to GraphQL-authored scenes
\item
  replace existing Bijou block APIs
\item
  implement a full Geordi renderer inside Bijou
\item
  require Geordi as a runtime dependency of every Bijou app
\item
  claim pixel/cell parity
\item
  solve every binding expression shape
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-075-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} fixture describes at least one text node, one token reference, one i18n key, and one action.
\item
  Bijou can lower the fixture into a terminal render target without losing node identity.
\item
  The resulting \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} can report a structural receipt or source-map facts tied back to the fixture.
\item
  The design names the distinction between shared IR, Bijou layout IR, and Bijou \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  The design names Geordi as the pixel-proof target and Bijou as the terminal-surface target.
\item
  The validation plan proves structure, not screenshot similarity.
\end{itemize}

\section{Slice Plan}\label{record-075-slice-plan}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Document the shared IR contract and renderer boundaries.
\item
  Add a minimal \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} fixture package or test helper.
\item
  Add Bijou lowering from the fixture to a simple \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  Add structural receipt generation for the fixture.
\item
  Add token and i18n provenance checks against the receipt.
\item
  Add a Geordi integration spike that either lowers to \texttt{g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} or records the adapter boundary needed to do so.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Validation Plan}\label{record-075-validation-plan}

Focused proof should use deterministic fixture tests:

\begin{CodeBlock}
npm test -- --run shared-ui-scene-ir
npm run typecheck:test
npm run lint
\end{CodeBlock}

Future integration proof can add:

\begin{CodeBlock}
npm run dogfood:i18n:check
npm run dogfood:i18n:debt
npm run verify:interactive-examples
\end{CodeBlock}

The key invariant is that a passing test must prove software behavior or inspectable output. A design document alone is not completion proof for the implementation goalpost.

\section{Risks}\label{record-075-risks}

\subsection{Risk: The Shared IR Becomes A Renderer}\label{record-075-risk-the-shared-ir-becomes-a-renderer}

If \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} starts carrying renderer internals, it will become too expensive to author and too vague to validate.

Mitigation: keep final render details in \texttt{g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, and \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.

\subsection{Risk: Bijou Loses Terminal-Native Behavior}\label{record-075-risk-bijou-loses-terminal-native-behavior}

If the IR treats keyboard routing, focus, and terminal viewports as afterthought metadata, Bijou scenes will look portable but feel broken.

Mitigation: make Bijou target profiles carry focus, keymap, and viewport requirements explicitly.

\subsection{Risk: Geordi And Bijou Drift Anyway}\label{record-075-risk-geordi-and-bijou-drift-anyway}

If both lowerings are implemented independently without receipts, drift will come back.

Mitigation: structural receipts compare node IDs, text keys, token refs, bindings, actions, and source hashes.

\subsection{Risk: GraphQL Syntax Gets Overloaded}\label{record-075-risk-graphql-syntax-gets-overloaded}

GraphQL SDL can describe contracts well, but directives can become JSON string dumps if the schema is not designed carefully.

Mitigation: use Wesley domain law to validate directive shape and prefer typed schema contracts over ad hoc JSON blobs.

\section{Open Questions}\label{record-075-open-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Should \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} live in Bijou, Geordi, Wesley, or a small shared package?
\item
  Should Bijou expose \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} as a public artifact or keep it internal until the contract stabilizes?
\item
  Should Geordi consume \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} directly, or should Wesley emit \texttt{g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} as sibling artifacts?
\item
  How much action/focus metadata belongs in the shared IR versus the Bijou target profile?
\item
  Should debug JSONL files be produced by the renderer, by the lowering layer, or by both with different provenance phases?
\end{itemize}

\section{Recommended Next Step}\label{record-075-recommended-next-step}

Create a roadmap-backed issue for \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} and start with one tiny fixture scene. The fixture should prove that Bijou \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} is a render target for the shared IR, while Geordi remains the pixel-proof target.

This document is a planning artifact. It does not claim a GraphQL compiler, portable Bijou IR runtime, browser Dogfood endpoint, Geordi packed-cell target, or Unity endpoint already exists in this repository.

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-076-decision-summary}

Bijou should grow toward a portable block and component semantics layer. Terminal rendering remains a first-class Bijou endpoint, but it should not be the only possible endpoint for Bijou-authored UI.

The intended flow is:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Bijou Blocks + Components GraphQL
  -> Wesley validation and generated DTOs
    -> ui-scene-ir/1
      -> Bijou terminal endpoint
      -> Geordi browser/WebGL/WebGPU endpoint
      -> Geordi image or video witness endpoint
      -> Geordi packed Bijou cell endpoint
      -> future engine endpoints such as GeordiUnityGameEngine
\end{CodeBlock}

The reverse direction should also be possible for visual surfaces:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Figma or other external design source
  -> Geordi IR or compatible scene IR
    -> BijouPackedCellRenderer
      -> PackedBijouCells
        -> Bijou Surface
          -> terminal cells
\end{CodeBlock}

The important shift is this:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Bijou Surface is one render target.
Bijou block and component semantics are the portable product contract.
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-076-sponsored-human}

A developer wants to define an app surface once and render it in a terminal, browser, visual witness, or future game-engine endpoint without maintaining parallel component trees by hand.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-076-sponsored-agent}

An agent wants deterministic UI IR and deterministic render witnesses so it can debug node identity, bindings, localization, theme tokens, focus, actions, and rendered output without scraping screenshots or inferring intent from terminal pixels.

\section{Hill}\label{record-076-hill}

Dogfood can be described by a Bijou-owned semantic UI contract, compiled into a deterministic IR, and rendered through both a terminal endpoint and a browser endpoint, with receipts proving that node IDs, token references, localization keys, actions, bindings, and target-specific outputs came from the same source.

\section{Core Rule}\label{record-076-core-rule}

Bijou owns the meaning of Bijou blocks and components.

Renderers own how that meaning is drawn.

\begin{CodeBlock}
GraphQL source
  describes: author intent

ui-scene-ir/1
  describes: portable semantic UI structure

bijou-layout/1
  describes: terminal layout, focus graph, keymap, and viewports

Bijou Surface
  describes: final terminal cell output

Geordi endpoint IR or prepared target
  describes: browser, image, GPU, packed-cell, or engine render state
\end{CodeBlock}

No endpoint owns the semantic truth of a Bijou component. An endpoint may render or inspect the component, but it must not silently redefine its behavior.

\section{Why This Matters}\label{record-076-why-this-matters}

\subsection{Agent-Legible Debugging}\label{record-076-agent-legible-debugging}

Screenshots are weak debugging artifacts. They show that something looked odd, but they do not directly answer what node, token, string, binding, or target rule produced the output.

IR plus receipts can answer:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Which source node produced this cell, pixel, or engine element?
\item
  Which localization key produced this text?
\item
  Which theme token produced this foreground or background?
\item
  Which action is attached to this focusable element?
\item
  Which endpoint lowered this scene?
\item
  Which target claims are proven, and which are explicit nonclaims?
\item
  Did two endpoints render the same semantic scene?
\end{itemize}

The expected debug artifact should be inspectable by agents:

\begin{CodeBlock}
{
  "scene": "dogfood.docs",
  "node": "nav.guides.startHere",
  "component": "tree.item",
  "textKey": "dogfood.nav.startHere",
  "fgToken": "semantic.nav.item.active.fg",
  "bgToken": "semantic.nav.item.active.bg",
  "action": "dogfood.openDoc",
  "target": "bijou-terminal",
  "cellBounds": { "x": 12, "y": 4, "w": 22, "h": 1 }
}
\end{CodeBlock}

\subsection{Render Anywhere}\label{record-076-render-anywhere}

Bijou-authored UI should be able to leave the terminal:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Bijou Blocks -> IR -> GeordiWebGL
Bijou Blocks -> IR -> GeordiWebGPU
Bijou Blocks -> IR -> GeordiImage
Bijou Blocks -> IR -> GeordiUnityGameEngine
\end{CodeBlock}

This does not mean every endpoint has identical pixels. It means every endpoint renders the same semantic contract under a declared target profile.

\subsection{Render Other UI Into The Terminal}\label{record-076-render-other-ui-into-the-terminal}

Bijou can also become the terminal endpoint for non-Bijou UI sources:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Figma -> Geordi IR -> BijouPackedCellRenderer -> terminal
\end{CodeBlock}

The first claim here is visual portability: can the source be approximated as terminal cells? Interactive portability requires additional semantics: focus, actions, state, localization, accessibility, and key routing.

\section{Bijou Ownership}\label{record-076-bijou-ownership}

Bijou should own portable terminal UI semantics:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  blocks and components
\item
  component identity
\item
  child hierarchy
\item
  layout intent
\item
  state bindings
\item
  actions and command IDs
\item
  focus and key routing intent
\item
  localization references
\item
  theme token references
\item
  accessibility labels and roles
\item
  terminal runtime behavior
\item
  \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} and cell semantics
\item
  packed-cell validation rules when a packed target claims Bijou compatibility
\end{itemize}

Bijou should not own:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Geordi browser renderer internals
\item
  GPU shader dispatch
\item
  image/video export internals
\item
  Unity scene graph adapters
\item
  Figma import specifics
\item
  Bunny geometry kernels
\end{itemize}

\section{Proposed Source Shape}\label{record-076-proposed-source-shape}

GraphQL remains the best initial source-of-truth candidate because it can carry schema-backed fields and directives while letting Wesley generate DTOs and drift checks.

Example shape:

\begin{CodeBlock}
type DogfoodDocsScene
  @bijou_scene(id: "dogfood.docs")
  @ui_target(kind: "bijou-terminal", cols: 160, rows: 48)
  @ui_target(kind: "geordi-browser", width: 1440, height: 900)
  @ui_target(kind: "geordi-packed-bijou-cells", cols: 160, rows: 48) {
  navTitle: String!
    @ui_node(id: "nav.title", kind: "text", component: "heading")
    @ui_text(key: "dogfood.nav.title")
    @ui_style(fg: "semantic.nav.title.fg")

  startHere: String!
    @ui_node(id: "nav.guides.startHere", kind: "text", component: "tree.item")
    @ui_text(key: "dogfood.nav.startHere")
    @ui_style(
      fg: "semantic.nav.item.active.fg"
      bg: "semantic.nav.item.active.bg"
    )
    @ui_action(id: "dogfood.openDoc", command: "dogfood.openDoc", keys: ["Enter"])

  currentPage: String!
    @ui_node(id: "content.currentPage", kind: "markdown", component: "doc.page")
    @ui_binding(path: "docs.currentPage.markdown")
}
\end{CodeBlock}

This syntax is not final. The contract matters more than the directive names: source nodes, text keys, style tokens, bindings, actions, and target profiles must be compile-time data.

\section{IR Shape}\label{record-076-ir-shape}

DX-042 proposes the first \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} shape. This design extends its intent with explicit component portability and endpoint requirements.

\begin{CodeBlock}
type UiSceneIr = {
  irVersion: 'ui-scene-ir/1';
  id: string;
  sourceHash: string;
  rootNodeId: string;
  nodes: UiNode[];
  bindings: UiBinding[];
  actions: UiAction[];
  tokenUses: UiTokenUse[];
  i18nUses: UiI18nUse[];
  sourceMap: UiSourceMapEntry[];
  targetProfiles: UiTargetProfile[];
  portability: UiPortabilityClaim;
};

type UiPortabilityClaim = {
  level: 'portable' | 'terminal-native' | 'visual-only' | 'host-adapter';
  reasons?: string[];
};
\end{CodeBlock}

Portability should be explicit. Some Bijou surfaces may remain terminal-native because they inspect terminal escape behavior, alternate-screen state, or raw cell buffers. Those surfaces are still valuable, but they should not pretend to render everywhere.

\section{Target Profiles}\label{record-076-target-profiles}

The first target profile vocabulary should include:

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Profile
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Output
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Primary owner
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l} & \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} & Bijou \\
\texttt{g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r} & browser canvas/WebGL/WebGPU output & Geordi \\
\texttt{g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e} & RGBA frame, PNG, video witness & Geordi \\
\texttt{g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s} & \texttt{P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s} & Geordi plus Bijou contract \\
\texttt{g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y} & Unity scene or UI graph & Geordi adapter \\
\texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t} & visual scene imported from Figma or similar & Geordi adapter \\
\end{longtable}
}

Every target profile should name supported features. Unsupported features must fail before drawing.

\section{Bijou Terminal Lowering}\label{record-076-bijou-terminal-lowering}

The Bijou terminal endpoint lowers semantic UI IR into terminal runtime facts:

\begin{CodeBlock}
ui-scene-ir/1
  -> bijou-layout/1
    -> Surface
      -> terminal cells
\end{CodeBlock}

\texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} should carry:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  resolved terminal layout regions
\item
  focus graph
\item
  keymap
\item
  viewport regions
\item
  scroll policies
\item
  localized text after i18n resolution
\item
  theme token requirements
\item
  source-map entries from nodes to cells
\item
  target-specific nonclaims
\end{itemize}

The final \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} remains the rendered cell grid. It is not the portable IR.

\section{Packed Cell Lowering}\label{record-076-packed-cell-lowering}

The packed cell endpoint lets Geordi render directly into a Bijou-compatible terminal cell target:

\begin{CodeBlock}
ui-scene-ir/1 or geordi endpoint IR
  -> Geordi packed-cell renderer
    -> PackedBijouCells
      -> Bijou Surface adapter
        -> terminal cells
\end{CodeBlock}

This is useful when a renderer, CPU backend, or GPU backend can produce the terminal-native output directly instead of rendering a large image and then sampling it on the CPU.

The contract should be explicit:

\begin{CodeBlock}
type PackedBijouCells = {
  targetVersion: 'packed-bijou-cells/1';
  widthCells: number;
  heightCells: number;
  cellFormatId: string;
  sampleGrid?: '1x1' | '2x4' | 'custom';
  colorPolicyId: string;
  glyphResolvePolicyId: string;
  cells: PackedBijouCell[];
  facts: RenderFrameFacts;
};

type PackedBijouCell = {
  char: string;
  fg?: Rgb;
  bg?: Rgb;
  modifiers?: string[];
  provenanceNodeId?: string;
  tokenRefs?: {
    fg?: string;
    bg?: string;
  };
};
\end{CodeBlock}

Bijou should validate that a packed-cell buffer is structurally compatible with Bijou cell semantics before presenting it.

\section{Dogfood Proof}\label{record-076-dogfood-proof}

Dogfood is the best flagship proof because it contains:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  document navigation
\item
  panes
\item
  markdown rendering
\item
  theme tokens
\item
  light and dark modes
\item
  localization
\item
  focus
\item
  scrolling
\item
  keyboard actions
\item
  status rows
\item
  drawers
\item
  overlays
\item
  debug panels
\end{itemize}

The intended proof path is:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Dogfood source
  -> Dogfood IR
    -> Dogfood in the terminal
    -> Dogfood in the browser
    -> structural receipts proving semantic parity
\end{CodeBlock}

The first slice should not rewrite all of Dogfood. It should make one page or one pane undeniable.

\section{Structural Receipt}\label{record-076-structural-receipt}

The shared receipt proves semantic parity, not pixel parity:

\begin{CodeBlock}
type PortableUiReceipt = {
  sceneHash: string;
  sourceHash: string;
  nodeIds: string[];
  componentIds: string[];
  i18nKeys: string[];
  tokenRefs: string[];
  actionIds: string[];
  bindingIds: string[];
  outputs: {
    terminal?: {
      layoutHash: string;
      surfaceHash: string;
    };
    browser?: {
      endpointHash: string;
      witnessHash: string;
    };
    packedCells?: {
      targetHash: string;
      surfaceHash: string;
    };
  };
};
\end{CodeBlock}

Endpoint receipts can add target-specific proof:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  terminal cell hashes
\item
  browser pixel probes
\item
  packed-cell hashes
\item
  image frame hashes
\item
  engine object counts
\item
  target profile support matrix
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-076-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

Portable Bijou IR should preserve accessibility metadata even when a renderer does not directly display it.

Required fields should include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  semantic role
\item
  accessible label or i18n key
\item
  focusability
\item
  keyboard action hints
\item
  decorative vs meaningful marker
\item
  directionality and locale posture
\item
  reduced-motion or animation policy where relevant
\end{itemize}

Browser and engine endpoints can map this metadata to their own accessibility systems later. Terminal endpoints can expose it through debug modes, help surfaces, and structured MCP surfaces.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-076-localization-and-directionality-posture}

Product text should enter the IR as localization keys, not resolved ad hoc strings. Render endpoints may resolve keys later against locale bundles, but receipts must preserve which key was used.

Directionality should be target-aware:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  terminal endpoint records whether a region is left-to-right or right-to-left
\item
  browser endpoint can map direction to layout/text properties
\item
  image endpoint records direction metadata in frame facts
\item
  packed-cell endpoint records the resolved order it actually emitted
\end{itemize}

\section{Agent Inspectability}\label{record-076-agent-inspectability}

The IR and receipts should make these questions answerable by file inspection:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  What component rendered this cell?
\item
  What action would fire if the user pressed Enter here?
\item
  Why is this node not focusable?
\item
  Which token produced this color?
\item
  Which localization key produced this text?
\item
  Which target profile rejected this component?
\item
  Did terminal and browser outputs use the same semantic node tree?
\end{itemize}

This is the main reason the IR matters. It turns UI debugging into structured evidence instead of screenshot interpretation.

\section{Scope}\label{record-076-scope}

The first implementation arc should include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  one portable Bijou component fixture
\item
  one GraphQL or JSON source-of-truth fixture
\item
  one \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} output
\item
  one terminal lowering to \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}
\item
  one browser or Geordi endpoint stub
\item
  one structural receipt
\item
  one negative fixture proving fail-loud unsupported target requirements
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-076-non-goals}

The first arc should not:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  migrate all Dogfood pages
\item
  replace existing block APIs
\item
  require Geordi at runtime for every Bijou app
\item
  claim pixel parity between terminal and browser
\item
  implement Unity, Figma, WebGPU, or GPU packed-cell output immediately
\item
  make GraphQL directives the permanent final authoring syntax
\item
  erase terminal-native Bijou components
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-076-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A portable Bijou component can be represented as deterministic IR.
\item
  The IR preserves node IDs, component IDs, token refs, i18n keys, actions, and bindings.
\item
  The same IR can lower to a Bijou \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  A second endpoint stub or fixture can consume the same IR and emit a receipt.
\item
  Receipts prove semantic parity across endpoints.
\item
  Unsupported endpoint requirements fail before drawing.
\item
  The design distinguishes portable components from terminal-native components.
\item
  Dogfood has a concrete first-page or first-pane migration target.
\end{itemize}

\section{Slice Plan}\label{record-076-slice-plan}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Land this design and the Geordi companion design.
\item
  Define a tiny portable component fixture.
\item
  Define the first \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} fixture and canonical JSON rules.
\item
  Add a structural receipt fixture.
\item
  Lower the fixture to a Bijou \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  Add a terminal receipt with source-map facts.
\item
  Add a Geordi browser endpoint stub or fixture consumer.
\item
  Add a fail-loud unsupported target fixture.
\item
  Add a Dogfood page/pane candidate map.
\item
  Emit Dogfood IR witness data beside the current runtime.
\item
  Render one Dogfood pane from IR to terminal.
\item
  Render the same pane through a browser witness endpoint.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Validation Plan}\label{record-076-validation-plan}

Initial validation should be deterministic and file-backed:

\begin{CodeBlock}
npm test -- --run portable-bijou-ir
npm run typecheck:test
npm run lint
npm run docs:inventory
git diff --check
\end{CodeBlock}

Future validation should add:

\begin{CodeBlock}
npm run dogfood:i18n:check
npm run dogfood:i18n:debt
npm run verify:interactive-examples
\end{CodeBlock}

The important proof rule remains: design docs describe intent; executable fixtures and receipts prove behavior.

\section{Risks}\label{record-076-risks}

\subsection{Risk: Bijou Becomes Too Abstract}\label{record-076-risk-bijou-becomes-too-abstract}

If portable IR hides terminal realities, Bijou components may render elsewhere but feel broken in the terminal.

Mitigation: keep \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l} as a first-class endpoint with focus, keymap, viewport, scroll, and cell-source-map requirements.

\subsection{Risk: Geordi Redefines Bijou Semantics}\label{record-076-risk-geordi-redefines-bijou-semantics}

If Geordi endpoints silently reinterpret Bijou components, parity becomes cosmetic.

Mitigation: Bijou owns component semantics; Geordi owns endpoint rendering and receipts.

\subsection{Risk: GraphQL Becomes An Unreadable Directive Dump}\label{record-076-risk-graphql-becomes-an-unreadable-directive-dump}

GraphQL can carry schema-backed contracts, but overly complex directives can turn into JSON blobs.

Mitigation: keep source syntax small, use Wesley validation, and treat early syntax as provisional.

\subsection{Risk: Visual Import Pretends To Be Interactive}\label{record-076-risk-visual-import-pretends-to-be-interactive}

A Figma-to-terminal path can render a visual mockup, but that does not mean it has focus, actions, state, or accessibility.

Mitigation: distinguish visual portability from interactive portability in the target profile.

\section{Recommended Next Step}\label{record-076-recommended-next-step}

Create the smallest possible Dogfood proof:

\begin{CodeBlock}
one Dogfood nav or content pane
  -> portable source fixture
    -> ui-scene-ir/1
      -> Bijou Surface
      -> browser/Geordi endpoint receipt
      -> structural parity receipt
\end{CodeBlock}

That proves the architecture without rewriting Dogfood or overbuilding the compiler.

\chapter{DX-044 GraphQL Authored Bijou Block IR Proof}\label{record-077}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-044-graphql-authored-bijou-block-ir-proof.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DX-044 GraphQL Authored Bijou Block IR Proof
legend: DX
lane: cool-ideas
priority: medium
github_issue: 302
status: landed
keywords:
  - developer-experience
  - graphql
  - blocks
  - ir
  - geordi
  - dogfood
  - render-everywhere

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DX-developer-experience.md}{DX - Developer Experience}

\section{Linked Work}\label{record-077-linked-work}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  GitHub issue: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/302}{\#302}
\item
  Runtime seed: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-042-shared-ui-scene-ir-and-bijou-render-target.md}{DX-042 Shared UI Scene IR And Bijou Render Target}
\item
  Portable endpoint direction: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-043-portable-bijou-blocks-and-multi-endpoint-ir.md}{DX-043 Portable Bijou Blocks And Multi-Endpoint IR}
\item
  Prior block contract: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-031-standard-bijou-blocks.md}{DX-031 Standard Bijou Blocks}
\end{itemize}

This cycle is the first implementation proof after the \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} runtime seed. It should not try to make every Bijou block GraphQL-authored. It should prove one boring, deterministic vertical slice that future Wesley and Geordi work can replace or extend without changing the proof contract.

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-077-decision-summary}

Bijou should treat GraphQL SDL as an authoring surface for portable block semantics, not as a runtime data store and not as a visual scene graph.

The first flow is:

\begin{CodeBlock}
GraphQL SDL fixture
  -> bijou-block/1 artifact
    -> ui-scene-ir/1
      -> Bijou terminal Surface proof
        -> ui-scene-receipt/1
\end{CodeBlock}

The first slice stays inside Bijou. Geordi remains a named endpoint target, but this cycle does not require Geordi repository changes unless the Bijou proof needs a companion endpoint fixture.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-077-sponsored-human}

A Bijou author wants to define a small UI block in a declarative source format and get a deterministic block artifact, scene IR, terminal output, source map, and receipt without hand-maintaining parallel JSON fixtures.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-077-sponsored-agent}

An agent wants to inspect the GraphQL source, generated block artifact, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, terminal cell source map, and receipt hashes to understand exactly which source field produced each visible terminal fact.

\section{Hill}\label{record-077-hill}

Given a constrained GraphQL SDL file for one text-first Bijou block, Bijou can produce a stable \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} artifact, lower it into \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, render it to a terminal \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}, and emit a receipt whose source maps, tokens, i18n keys, actions, bindings, and hashes are deterministic.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-077-playback-questions}

This design is successful only if the committed proof lets a maintainer or agent answer the following questions from repository facts:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Can a reader trace one SDL field through \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, terminal cells, and receipt dependencies?
\item
  Can whitespace-only SDL edits preserve the block artifact hash and scene hash?
\item
  Can unsupported or duplicate identities fail before terminal lowering produces a misleading witness?
\item
  Can an agent inspect source-map, token, i18n, action, and binding facts without scraping a screenshot?
\end{itemize}

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-077-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/schemas-live-at-boundaries.md}{Schemas Live At Boundaries}: the SDL reader rejects unsupported or malformed authoring input before the runtime treats the block artifact as trusted.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/graceful-lowering-preserves-meaning.md}{Graceful Lowering Preserves Meaning}: \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} preserves semantic text, token, i18n, action, binding, and source-map meaning when it lowers to terminal cells.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/buffer-holds-facts.md}{The Buffer Holds Facts}: generated artifacts, receipts, and source maps remain inspectable fact records instead of executable behavior.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are the Spec}: the first slice is complete only when focused tests prove the hash, validation, lowering, and receipt contract.
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope}\label{record-077-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A constrained SDL reader for one block type.
\item
  Directive-like metadata for block identity, target profile, slots, commands, bindings, theme tokens, localization keys, and source positions.
\item
  A public \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} artifact type.
\item
  A compiler function from SDL source to block artifact.
\item
  A lowering function from block artifact to \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}.
\item
  Tests proving whitespace-stable source hashing, artifact stability, IR validation, terminal lowering, source maps, and receipts.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-077-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  No full GraphQL parser dependency in the first slice.
\item
  No Wesley code generation in the first slice.
\item
  No Geordi endpoint implementation in the first slice.
\item
  No arbitrary GraphQL schema execution.
\item
  No nested field resolver runtime.
\item
  No visual layout engine beyond explicit first-slice layout facts.
\item
  No DOGFOOD-wide migration.
\end{itemize}

\section{First SDL Shape}\label{record-077-first-sdl-shape}

The first SDL subset is intentionally explicit:

\begin{CodeBlock}
type ReleaseTitle
  @bijouBlock(id: "release.title", component: "ReleaseTitleBlock")
  @bijouTarget(kind: "bijou-terminal", cols: 40, rows: 5) {
  heading: String!
    @bijouText(id: "heading", x: 2, y: 1)
    @bijouI18n(key: "release.title.heading", fallback: "Bijou")
    @bijouToken(fg: "semantic.title.fg")

  openNotes: String
    @bijouAction(id: "release.openNotes", command: "release.openNotes", key: "Enter")
    @bijouText(id: "open-notes", x: 2, y: 3)
    @bijouI18n(key: "release.title.openNotes", fallback: "Open release notes")
    @bijouToken(fg: "semantic.action.fg", bg: "semantic.action.bg")
}
\end{CodeBlock}

The subset allows only:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  one \texttt{t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e}
\item
  type directives on the type declaration or following indented lines before \texttt{\{}
\item
  scalar fields
\item
  field directives on following indented lines
\item
  string and integer directive arguments
\end{itemize}

That is small enough to parse deterministically without pretending to be a general GraphQL compiler.

\section{Binding Directive Shape}\label{record-077-binding-directive-shape}

Bindings use field directives because they attach authoring source to one renderable field:

\begin{CodeBlock}
status: String
  @bijouText(id: "status", x: 2, y: 3)
  @bijouBind(
    id: "release.status.value",
    kind: "state",
    path: "release.status",
    targetProperty: "text",
    when: "release.visible"
  )
\end{CodeBlock}

The first slice treats binding directives as fact records, not live dataflow. \texttt{k\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d} is intentionally constrained to source categories such as \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}, and \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}. \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h} identifies the external source fact. \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y} defaults to \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t} when omitted. \texttt{w\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n} is optional and records the gating condition that a later runtime or endpoint may evaluate.

\section{Artifact Contract}\label{record-077-artifact-contract}

The first generated artifact is:

\begin{CodeBlock}
bijou-block/1
  id
  component
  sourceHash
  fields[]
    fieldName
    nodeId
    text
    action
    binding
    token refs
    source
  targetProfiles[]
\end{CodeBlock}

\texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} is semantic. It is not the same thing as Geordi IR and it is not the same thing as a final \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.

\section{Lowering Contract}\label{record-077-lowering-contract}

\texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} must preserve:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  source hash
\item
  node ids
\item
  component ids
\item
  i18n keys and fallbacks
\item
  token references
\item
  action ids, commands, keybindings, and targets
\item
  binding facts when present
\item
  source-map facts from SDL field anchors to IR nodes
\item
  target profile facts
\end{itemize}

If the source asks for unsupported target facts, the compiler must fail before lowering.

\section{Source Map Posture}\label{record-077-source-map-posture}

Source strings should be stable and local to the input. The first slice uses semantic anchors instead of line and column positions so formatting-only SDL edits do not change the artifact or scene hash:

\begin{CodeBlock}
release-title.graphql#type.ReleaseTitle.field.heading
\end{CodeBlock}

Absolute paths are not allowed in emitted artifacts. The caller may provide a \texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} option, but the default should be a neutral \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l}.

\section{Agent Inspectability}\label{record-077-agent-inspectability}

The useful debug path should be:

\begin{CodeBlock}
SDL field -> bijou-block/1 field -> ui-scene-ir/1 node -> Surface cell -> receipt
\end{CodeBlock}

An agent should not need a screenshot to answer:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Which SDL field produced this node?
\item
  Which node produced this terminal cell?
\item
  Which i18n key and token refs were used?
\item
  Which action or binding belongs to the rendered text?
\item
  Which hash proves the scene and terminal output?
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility And Localization Posture}\label{record-077-accessibility-and-localization-posture}

This first slice preserves localization keys and fallbacks but does not add new runtime translation behavior. The source author must provide fallback text for renderable text nodes. Directionality is deferred until multiline text and localized layout constraints exist in the IR.

\section{Geordi Posture}\label{record-077-geordi-posture}

Geordi is the likely next endpoint after this Bijou-only proof. The first Geordi-facing shape should be a receipt-compatible endpoint facet, not a semantic replacement for \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}.

Expected later flow:

\begin{CodeBlock}
bijou-block/1
  -> ui-scene-ir/1
    -> Geordi endpoint profile
      -> browser/image/packed-cell witness
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-077-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add this design doc and issue update.
\item
  Add \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} artifact types.
\item
  Add a deterministic constrained SDL compiler.
\item
  Add block-artifact to \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} lowering.
\item
  Add public exports.
\item
  Add a focused fixture test that renders one GraphQL-authored block into a terminal proof.
\item
  Update changelog and issue/PR proof.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-077-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  RED: a whitespace-variant SDL input should produce the same block hash and scene hash.
\item
  RED: missing \texttt{@\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} should fail with a deterministic error.
\item
  RED: a text field with i18n/token/action directives should become one IR text node with matching source-map facts.
\item
  GREEN: terminal proof should render fallback text and include SHA-256 scene, layout, and surface hashes.
\end{itemize}

\section{Closeout}\label{record-077-closeout}

The cycle is landed when:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the design doc exists and links \#302
\item
  \#302 has a cycle comment pointing at the branch and PR
\item
  \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u} exports the first block authoring APIs
\item
  the focused GraphQL-authored block proof is green
\item

\item

\end{itemize}

\chapter{DX-045 GraphQL Block Groups And Debug Facts}\label{record-078}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-045-graphql-block-groups-and-debug-facts.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}

\section{Linked Work}\label{record-078-linked-work}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  GitHub issue: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/302}{\#302}
\item
  Prior slice: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-044-graphql-authored-bijou-block-ir-proof.md}{DX-044 GraphQL Authored Bijou Block IR Proof}
\item
  Runtime seed: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-042-shared-ui-scene-ir-and-bijou-render-target.md}{DX-042 Shared UI Scene IR And Bijou Render Target}
\item
  Portable endpoint direction: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-043-portable-bijou-blocks-and-multi-endpoint-ir.md}{DX-043 Portable Bijou Blocks And Multi-Endpoint IR}
\end{itemize}

DX-044 proved the smallest boring path:

\begin{CodeBlock}
GraphQL SDL
  -> bijou-block/1
    -> ui-scene-ir/1
      -> terminal Surface proof
\end{CodeBlock}

DX-045 turns that proof into a more credible authoring pipeline by adding explicit group nodes and deterministic debug facts. It should still stay inside Bijou; Geordi remains the next endpoint after the semantic artifact is strong enough to hand across a repository boundary.

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-078-decision-summary}

GraphQL-authored Bijou blocks need a hierarchy before Dogfood or BlockLab can use them naturally. The first hierarchy primitive should be a small field-attached group directive, not a general GraphQL execution model.

The next flow is:

\begin{CodeBlock}
GraphQL SDL fixture
  -> bijou-block/1 artifact with groups[]
    -> ui-scene-ir/1 group/text node tree
      -> terminal Surface proof
        -> debug summary facts
          -> ui-scene-receipt/1
\end{CodeBlock}

The debug summary is deliberately fact-shaped. It is not a renderer and not a test snapshot. It gives maintainers and agents one deterministic object that answers what source, artifact, scene, nodes, tokens, i18n keys, actions, bindings, and lower-mode witnesses exist.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-078-sponsored-human}

A Bijou author wants to organize a GraphQL-authored block into named sections without hand-editing JSON IR, then confirm that the rendered terminal output and debug facts still point back to the right source fields.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-078-sponsored-agent}

An agent wants a deterministic summary of the GraphQL-to-IR pipeline so it can reason about a UI failure from source anchors, group ownership, token refs, i18n keys, bindings, actions, hashes, and lower-mode output instead of interpreting screenshots.

\section{Hill}\label{record-078-hill}

Given a constrained GraphQL SDL file with text fields assigned to named groups, Bijou can produce a stable grouped \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} artifact, lower it into a valid \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} group/text node tree, render the text nodes to a terminal \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}, and emit deterministic debug facts that preserve source maps, tokens, i18n keys, actions, bindings, lower-mode witnesses, and hashes.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-078-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Can one SDL group directive become one \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} group and one \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} group node with stable parent/child relationships?
\item
  Can one SDL text field point to its owning group, text node, i18n key, token refs, action, binding, visible cells, and source anchor?
\item
  Can whitespace-only SDL edits preserve the artifact hash, scene hash, and debug summary hash?
\item
  Can lower modes prove the same grouped scene through node ids, i18n keys, and token refs?
\item
  Can unsupported duplicate group ids fail before lowering creates a misleading receipt?
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope}\label{record-078-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a constrained \texttt{@\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{})} directive.
\item
  Add \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}]} to \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} while preserving existing flat-field compatibility.
\item
  Lower block groups into \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} group nodes.
\item
  Preserve deterministic group source-map facts.
\item
  Add a public debug summary helper for the GraphQL block pipeline.
\item
  Add fixture-style tests for grouped SDL, duplicate groups, lower modes, and hash stability.
\item
  Update issue, roadmap, bearing, and changelog evidence.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-078-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  No full GraphQL parser dependency.
\item
  No nested GraphQL execution or resolver runtime.
\item
  No automatic layout engine.
\item
  No Geordi repository changes in this slice.
\item
  No Dogfood-wide migration.
\item
  No browser endpoint.
\item
  No frame-capture file format.
\end{itemize}

\section{SDL Shape}\label{record-078-sdl-shape}

The first grouped SDL shape stays explicit:

\begin{CodeBlock}
type ReleaseCard
  @bijouBlock(id: "release.card", component: "ReleaseCardBlock")
  @bijouTarget(kind: "bijou-terminal", cols: 48, rows: 8)
  @bijouGroup(id: "release.card.header", label: "Header", x: 1, y: 1, width: 46, height: 3)
  @bijouGroup(id: "release.card.footer", label: "Footer", x: 1, y: 5, width: 46, height: 2) {
  heading: String!
    @bijouText(id: "heading", group: "release.card.header", x: 2, y: 1)
    @bijouI18n(key: "release.card.heading", fallback: "Bijou")
    @bijouToken(fg: "semantic.title.fg")

  openNotes: String
    @bijouText(id: "open-notes", group: "release.card.footer", x: 2, y: 5)
    @bijouAction(id: "release.openNotes", command: "release.openNotes", key: "Enter")
    @bijouI18n(key: "release.card.openNotes", fallback: "Open release notes")
    @bijouToken(fg: "semantic.action.fg", bg: "semantic.action.bg")
}
\end{CodeBlock}

Group directives are type directives. Text fields opt into a group with \texttt{@\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{})}. Omitting \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p} preserves the DX-044 behavior and parents the text node to the block root.

The subset allows only:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  one \texttt{t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e}
\item
  type directives on the type declaration or following indented lines before \texttt{\{}
\item
  scalar fields
\item
  field directives on following indented lines
\item
  string and integer directive arguments
\item
  group ids that are unique and cannot collide with the root node or field node ids
\end{itemize}

\section{Artifact Contract}\label{record-078-artifact-contract}

\texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} gains \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}]}:

\begin{CodeBlock}
bijou-block/1
  id
  component
  sourceHash
  rootNodeId
  groups[]
    id
    label
    source
    layout
  fields[]
    fieldName
    nodeId
    groupId
    text
    action
    binding
    token refs
    source
  targetProfiles[]
\end{CodeBlock}

Existing consumers that only read \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}]} remain valid. Lowering owns the new parent-child relationships.

\section{Debug Summary Contract}\label{record-078-debug-summary-contract}

The debug helper should return plain data:

\begin{CodeBlock}
graphql-bijou-block-debug/1
  artifactVersion
  artifactHash
  sceneHash
  rootNodeId
  groups[]
  fields[]
  sourceMap[]
  i18nKeys[]
  tokenRefs[]
  actionIds[]
  bindingIds[]
  lowerModes[]
\end{CodeBlock}

The summary should be stable enough to hash and inspect in tests. It should not include host paths, timestamps, process ids, terminal dimensions from the operator environment, or screenshots.

\section{Accessibility And Lower Modes}\label{record-078-accessibility-and-lower-modes}

Groups must preserve semantic organization even when terminal color and layout are unavailable. Lower modes must still expose:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  node ids for group and text nodes
\item
  i18n keys for localized text
\item
  token refs for styled text
\item
  source anchors for field and group facts
\end{itemize}

No meaning in this slice may depend only on color.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-078-localization-and-directionality-posture}

The compiler continues to require fallback text for renderable i18n text nodes. Groups may carry labels for debug and inspector use, but group labels are not user-facing localized strings in this slice. Directionality remains deferred until multiline text and localized layout constraints exist in the IR.

\section{Agent Inspectability}\label{record-078-agent-inspectability}

The useful debug path should become:

\begin{CodeBlock}
SDL type directive / field directive
  -> bijou-block/1 group / field
    -> ui-scene-ir/1 group / text node
      -> terminal cell source map
        -> debug summary
          -> receipt
\end{CodeBlock}

An agent should be able to answer, from committed facts:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Which SDL directive created this group?
\item
  Which fields belong to this group?
\item
  Which visible cells came from a field in that group?
\item
  Which lower-mode output proves the same scene without color?
\item
  Which hashes bind the artifact, scene, surface, and debug summary?
\end{itemize}

\item

\item
