\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/buffer-holds-facts.md}{The Buffer Holds Facts}: debug output must be serializable fact records, not executable renderer behavior.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are the Spec}: grouped authoring is complete only when focused tests prove the compiler, lowering, lower modes, and debug summary.
\end{itemize}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-079-decision-summary}

DX-044 and DX-045 proved that constrained GraphQL SDL can produce \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, lower into \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, render terminal proof, and emit \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} facts. DX-046 turns that compiler proof into a real DOGFOOD product fixture.

The first DOGFOOD target is \texttt{N\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} from \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}. It is small enough for a release-boundary slice but real enough to carry product semantics: navigation items, selection state, command intents, i18n text, token styling, group structure, terminal proof, and debug facts.

The useful flow is:

\begin{CodeBlock}
NavigationListBlock GraphQL SDL fixture
  -> bijou-block/1 grouped artifact
    -> ui-scene-ir/1
      -> terminal Surface proof
        -> graphql-bijou-block-debug/1 facts
          -> DOGFOOD product facts
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-079-sponsored-human}

A maintainer wants the post-V7 GraphQL block compiler to prove it can describe an actual DOGFOOD surface, not only synthetic release-card examples.

A DOGFOOD reader benefits because the docs navigation surface becomes inspectable from one source contract instead of only from runtime rendering code.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-079-sponsored-agent}

An agent wants to trace one DOGFOOD navigation field from SDL through \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, terminal cells, lower modes, debug summary facts, and receipt hashes without scraping screenshots or reconstructing product intent from rendered text.

\section{Hill}\label{record-079-hill}

Given a checked-in GraphQL SDL fixture for \texttt{N\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}, Bijou can compile it into a deterministic grouped \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} artifact, lower it into a valid \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} scene, render terminal proof, and emit \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} facts that preserve source maps, token refs, i18n keys, actions, bindings, groups, lower-mode witnesses, and hashes.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-079-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Which DOGFOOD product surface is now authored as GraphQL SDL?
\item
  Can a maintainer prove that the fixture is tied to the existing \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} registry entry and \texttt{N\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} component name?
\item
  Can one SDL field be traced through artifact field, scene node, terminal cell source map, lower-mode row, debug fact, and receipt dependency?
\item
  Can debug facts list the DOGFOOD groups, fields, i18n keys, token refs, action ids, binding ids, lower-mode hashes, artifact hash, and scene hash?
\item
  Can failure tests reject missing or broken product facts before terminal proof is generated?
\end{itemize}

\section{Fixture Contract}\label{record-079-fixture-contract}

The fixture should live at \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l} unless implementation finds a stronger local convention.

Expected SDL shape:

\begin{CodeBlock}
type DogfoodNavigationList
  @bijouBlock(id: "dogfood.navigation", component: "NavigationListBlock")
  @bijouTarget(kind: "bijou-terminal", cols: 80, rows: 8)
  @bijouGroup(id: "dogfood.navigation.header", label: "Header", x: 1, y: 0, width: 46, height: 2)

  title: String!

The implementation may adjust coordinates, labels, or token names if existing terminal proof requires it, but the fixture must still preserve:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist

\item

\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-079-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

Meaning must survive without color or borders. The \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}s}, \texttt{i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}s}, and \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}s} lower modes must expose the same DOGFOOD navigation nodes as the normal terminal proof, and the active selection must be identifiable through source maps and binding facts.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-079-localization-and-directionality-posture}

Renderable fields must use \texttt{@\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n} with fallback text. This slice does not add runtime translation behavior or directionality rules; it preserves i18n keys and fallbacks so later locale-aware fixtures can replace the fallback text without changing the artifact contract.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-079-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

The committed facts should let an agent inspect:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  fixture source path and semantic source anchors
\item
  artifact id, component, source hash, and group hierarchy
\item
  scene id, root node, action ids, binding ids, i18n keys, and token refs
\item
  terminal cell source-map entries for visible navigation text
\item
  lower-mode rows and hashes
\item
  debug summary hash, artifact hash, and scene hash
\end{itemize}

No emitted artifact may include absolute local paths, timestamps, process ids, or screenshots.

\chapter{DX-047 - Blocks App Binding Snippets}\label{record-080}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-047-blocks-app-binding-snippets.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
id: DX-047
title: Blocks App Binding Snippets
status: active
lane: asap
priority: medium
github_issue: 342
legend: DX

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DX-developer-experience.md}{DX - Developer Experience}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-080-decision-summary}

DOGFOOD's Blocks docs should show how a block becomes application code, not only how a block is described as metadata. For \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, the bounded repair is to add an app-binding walkthrough centered on the existing \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} fixture:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  show the block contract: model, config, data requirement, and command intents
\item
  show the application state/update path that owns counter state
\item
  show how keyboard actions become command-intent emissions
\item
  show how the app renders the block from model-owned state
\item
  prove the snippet is not stale by compiling a canonical source file and testing that the rendered docs fence matches it exactly
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-080-sponsored-human}

A release-video viewer needs to understand why Blocks are reusable product assemblies rather than screenshots or one-off demos. The Blocks page should let the presenter say ``this is how you wire one into your app'' without leaving DOGFOOD.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-080-sponsored-agent}

An agent needs a deterministic docs witness that can inspect the Blocks section and verify that the app-binding example names the real API pieces: block config, state ownership, command intents, update routing, render invocation, and lower-mode expectations.

\section{Hill}\label{record-080-hill}

After this cycle, a developer can open DOGFOOD's Blocks section and see a complete, real app-binding snippet for \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}, including the state and command routing that make the block interactive.

\section{Problem}\label{record-080-problem}

Issue \#342 came from the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release-video rehearsal. The Blocks section now has useful catalog and preview surfaces, but it still reads like a product taxonomy. It does not yet answer the practical developer question:

\begin{CodeBlock}
How do I bind this block to my application's state and commands?
\end{CodeBlock}

The current ``How to Make Your Own Blocks'' page shows block authoring metadata and a minimal \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} shape. It does not show the application side of the contract: TEA state, update routing, render-time config, and command-intent handling.

\section{Scope}\label{record-080-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a focused app-binding section to the Blocks docs.
\item
  Use \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} as the first example because it already proves bounded state, command intents, interaction keys, and lower-mode output in DOGFOOD.
\item
  Keep the code snippet small enough to read inside the terminal.
\item
  Back the snippet with deterministic tests so API names and command paths do not drift silently.
\item
  Update release-facing signposts and changelog entries for \#342.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-080-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Do not redesign BlockLab.
\item
  Do not build a code editor or tutorial runner.
\item
  Do not pull broad \#302 Runtime Graph / Scene IR product-contract work into this cycle.
\item
  Do not add a new production counter block. \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} remains a DOGFOOD fixture.
\item
  Do not rewrite the standard block catalog.
\end{itemize}

\section{User Experience Contract}\label{record-080-user-experience-contract}

The Blocks docs should show both sides of a block contract:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the reusable block owns metadata, data requirements, command intents, render contract, and lower-mode behavior
\item
  the application owns model state, update decisions, host data, and when to invoke the block
\end{itemize}

The snippet should be readable in DOGFOOD at normal release-video dimensions. It should not require a browser, external docs page, or source-code search to explain the basic integration path.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-080-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Can a viewer see where counter state lives?
\item
  Can a viewer see which key emits which command intent?
\item
  Can a viewer see that the block render input is built from app-owned state?
\item
  Can a viewer see how lower modes stay meaningful when interaction is absent?
\item
  Can a test fail if the docs remove the binding path or let the snippet drift away from real APIs?
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Posture}\label{record-080-accessibility-assistive-posture}

The binding explanation must be useful as text. Code snippets and prose should not rely on color-only emphasis. The lower-mode note should explain what pipe and accessible output preserve from the interactive block.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-080-localization-directionality-posture}

This cycle adds English-source documentation copy only. DOGFOOD already labels English-source Markdown under non-English locales; this cycle should preserve that behavior. No new right-to-left layout behavior is introduced.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-080-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

Agents should be able to inspect:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the rendered Blocks docs text
\item
  the exact snippet source text
\item
  whether the snippet references real exported \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} helpers
\item
  whether the snippet names command-intent routing and lower-mode output
\end{itemize}

The proof should not depend on screenshots.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-080-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Blocks are product-level assemblies, not leaf visual components.
\item
  Application state owns business data; block render functions consume explicit inputs.
\item
  Command intents describe user intent; applications interpret and apply those intents.
\item
  DOGFOOD release claims must be demonstrable inside DOGFOOD.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-080-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a reusable app-binding snippet source for \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} at \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Render that exact snippet in \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}; generated copies must derive from the canonical snippet source.
\item
  Add prose explaining app-owned state, command intent routing, render-time config, and lower-mode output.
\item
  Add focused tests that render the Blocks guide and assert the app-binding section is visible and legible.
\item
  Add compile and source-integrity tests so the snippet cannot drift from the canonical source file or the real helper API.
\item
  Update \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-080-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A DOGFOOD Blocks render test fails unless ``How to Make Your Own Blocks'' includes a visible \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k} app-binding section.
\item
  A snippet integrity test fails unless the documented code matches the canonical source file and references the real counter model, config, command-intent, update, and render helpers.
\item
  Existing CounterDemoBlock preview and intent-key tests continue to pass.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-080-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Blocks docs include at least one complete app-binding snippet.
\item
  The snippet uses real Bijou / DOGFOOD APIs from a canonical source file and is covered by deterministic type and source-integrity proof.
\item
  Interactive block docs explain state ownership and command routing.
\item
  DOGFOOD renders the snippet legibly in the Blocks section.
\item
  The release/video script can explain ``how to use this in your app'' from the Blocks docs alone.
\item
  Issue \#342 is closed by the implementation PR.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-080-retrospective}

To be completed when the PR lands.

\chapter{DX-048 V8 Runtime Graph And Scene IR Contract}\label{record-081}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-048-v8-runtime-graph-scene-ir-contract.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DX-048 V8 Runtime Graph And Scene IR Contract

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DX-developer-experience.md}{DX - Developer Experience}

\section{Linked Work}\label{record-081-linked-work}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Goalpost tracker: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/457}{\#457}
\item
  First artifact proof: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/458}{\#458}
\item
  Packed-cell proof: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/459}{\#459}
\item
  Broad source lineage: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/302}{\#302}
\item
  VISOR coordination surface: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/visor}{flyingrobots/visor}
\item
  Prior Bijou proof: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-046-graphql-authored-dogfood-block-fixture.md}{DX-046 GraphQL Authored DOGFOOD Block Fixture}
\end{itemize}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-081-decision-summary}

\texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} proved a constrained path from GraphQL SDL to \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, terminal proof, grouped debug facts, and DOGFOOD product facts. \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} stabilized the demo and release surface enough to stop treating that path as release bookkeeping.

The V8 work starts by freezing the product contract before implementation continues. DX-048 defines the source, artifact, IR, receipt, source-map, lower-mode, debug, capture, and witness boundaries that \#458 and \#459 must consume.

VISOR is the coordination surface for the proof. Bijou remains responsible for the source-side contracts and the terminal \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} proof. Geordi, Wesley, Bunny, WARP TTD, browser renderers, and native renderers may consume or inform the contract later, but they do not define the first Bijou release gate.

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-081-sponsor-human}

A maintainer wants V8 to become a stable product contract, not a pile of exciting demos. They should be able to ask, ``what exactly crosses from GraphQL Blocks into Bijou Blocks IR and then into render targets?'' and get a versioned, testable answer.

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-081-sponsor-agent}

An agent needs to trace one product fact from a GraphQL source fixture through artifact fields, scene nodes, terminal cells, lower modes, source maps, debug facts, and receipts without scraping rendered text or guessing ownership.

\section{Hill}\label{record-081-hill}

Given a checked-in DOGFOOD GraphQL fixture, Bijou can produce a deterministic artifact bundle with \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, lower-mode witnesses, source maps, receipts, and packed-cell render evidence, and reviewers can replay the full path without any Wesley or Geordi repository changes.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-081-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the GraphQL Blocks source model allowed to express?
\item
  Which facts belong in the \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} artifact and which belong only in the compiler receipt?
\item
  What is the \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} lowering contract and what facts must it preserve?
\item
  Who owns receipt and source-map ownership when a source field fans out into multiple scene nodes or terminal cells?
\item
  Which lower modes are mandatory for a fixture before V8 calls it product proof?
\item
  What debug facts are stable enough for DOGFOOD, VISOR, and future replay tooling to inspect?
\item
  What invalid source cases fail before terminal rendering?
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope}\label{record-081-scope}

This cycle defines the V8 contract and proof boundaries:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  GraphQL Blocks source model:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    fixture identity
  \item
    component identity
  \item
    field identity
  \item
    group identity
  \item
    binding and command-intent identity
  \item
    i18n key references
  \item
    theme token references
  \item
    target render profile
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} artifact semantics:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    stable artifact version
  \item
    deterministic field and group ordering
  \item
    explicit product-fact inventory
  \item
    hashable payload shape
  \item
    no hidden global registry dependency
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} lowering contract:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    stable scene version
  \item
    node identity and role ownership
  \item
    text, style, focus, and geometry facts
  \item
    lower-mode witness fields
  \item
    source-map references back to artifact and source spans
  \end{itemize}
\item
  receipt and source-map ownership:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    source hash
  \item
    artifact hash
  \item
    scene hash
  \item
    packed-cell hash
  \item
    dependency and transform list
  \item
    failure facts for rejected input
  \end{itemize}
\item
  debug fact contract:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} summary facts
  \item
    group, field, i18n, token, action, binding, lower-mode, and hash inventory
  \item
    deterministic error categories
  \end{itemize}
\item
  DOGFOOD round-trip fixture:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    source fixture checked into the repo
  \item
    artifact bundle checked or snapshotted as test evidence
  \item
    terminal \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} proof
  \item
    lower-mode evidence
  \item
    review path documented in DOGFOOD or release-facing docs
  \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-081-non-goals}

This cycle does not:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  implement the \#458 artifact bundle
\item
  implement the \#459 packed-cell adapter
\item
  migrate every DOGFOOD block to GraphQL
\item
  introduce a general GraphQL resolver runtime
\item
  require Geordi, Wesley, Bunny, WARP TTD, browser, or native app changes
\item
  ship BlockLab, Theme Lab, localization workbench, or operator surfaces
\item
  define the final browser or native render target APIs
\item
  move all \#302 lineage issues into \texttt{v\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}
\end{itemize}

\section{Contract Sketch}\label{record-081-contract-sketch}

The minimum accepted artifact bundle should be inspectable as plain facts:

\begin{CodeBlock}
graphql-source/1
  -> bijou-block/1
    -> ui-scene-ir/1
      -> packed-bijou-cells/1
        -> terminal-surface-proof/1
\end{CodeBlock}

Each transition must produce a receipt:

\begin{CodeBlock}
receipt/1 {
  fromVersion
  toVersion
  sourceHash
  outputHash
  dependencyHashes[]
  transformFacts[]
  sourceMapRefs[]
  lowerModeWitnesses[]
  debugFactRefs[]
}
\end{CodeBlock}

The receipt is not a logging nicety. It is the review contract. If a future VISOR, DOGFOOD, WARP TTD, or browser proof cannot name the receipt it consumed, it is not part of the V8 release gate.

\section{Failure Cases}\label{record-081-failure-cases}

The V8 contract must reject:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  duplicate source, field, group, node, binding, or command ids
\item
  missing component identity
\item
  missing product facts for a DOGFOOD witness
\item
  broken i18n key references
\item
  broken theme token references
\item
  source spans that cannot map back from artifact or scene facts
\item
  lower-mode witnesses that omit required role or text facts
\item
  packed cells that cannot map to scene nodes
\item
  debug summaries that omit hashes or dependency facts
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility Posture}\label{record-081-accessibility-posture}

The contract must preserve lower-mode witnesses. Terminal proof alone is not enough. Every accepted DOGFOOD fixture must expose accessible text and role facts through the artifact or scene receipt so reviewers can inspect a non-TTY representation.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-081-localization-directionality-posture}

The GraphQL source may reference i18n keys and source-language fallback copy, but it must not smuggle untracked visible copy into the artifact. V8 must keep localization keys visible in debug facts and receipts so DOGFOOD can explain what translated and what fell back.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-081-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

Agents must be able to inspect the complete source-to-render chain without executing a full app:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  parse the fixture
\item
  read the artifact
\item
  read the scene IR
\item
  read the receipt list
\item
  read the source map
\item
  read debug facts
\item
  run the terminal proof
\item
  compare hashes
\end{itemize}

This is the line between a demo and a product contract.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-081-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Tests Are the Spec
\item
  Runtime Truth Wins
\item
  Docs Are the Demo
\item
  Work Is Issue-Backed
\item
  Release Claims Need Proof
\item
  Facts Before Behavior
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-081-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Land this design packet and post-release BEARING refresh.
\item
  Update \#457 with the contract decision and the \#458 / \#459 pull order.
\item
  Add tests that keep ROADMAP, BEARING, and this design aligned.
\item
  In \#458, introduce the artifact bundle fixture and receipt shape.
\item
  In \#459, validate \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} and adapt it to \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  Only after \#458 and \#459 are stable, promote broader \#302 lineage into V8 implementation scope.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-081-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  WF-130 roadmap tests must require this design packet while \#457 is open.
\item
  Artifact bundle tests in \#458 should fail until \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, receipts, source maps, and debug facts are emitted together.
\item
  Packed-cell tests in \#459 should fail until \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} can map cells back to scene nodes and render a \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} proof.
\end{itemize}

  Follow-on packed-cell proof: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/459}{\#459}
\item
  Broad source lineage: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/302}{\#302}
\item
  Contract design: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-048-v8-runtime-graph-scene-ir-contract.md}{DX-048 V8 Runtime Graph And Scene IR Contract}
\item
  Prior DOGFOOD fixture proof: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-046-graphql-authored-dogfood-block-fixture.md}{DX-046 GraphQL Authored DOGFOOD Block Fixture}
\item
  VISOR coordination tracker: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/visor/issues/1}{flyingrobots/visor\#1}
\end{itemize}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-082-decision-summary}

DX-046 proved that Bijou can compile a checked-in GraphQL SDL fixture into a grouped \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} artifact, lower it into \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, render a terminal proof, and emit deterministic \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} facts. DX-048 then defined the V8 contract boundary that VISOR needs to coordinate across Bijou, WARP TTD, Geordi, Bunny, Wesley, and follow-on render targets.

Issue \#458 should be the smallest implementation bridge between those two facts. It should introduce a deterministic \texttt{v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} object that wraps the existing GraphQL fixture source, \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} artifact, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} scene, debug summary, replay metadata, visual scene facts, and stable hashes. The bundle is a Bijou-emitted proof artifact for VISOR to index; it is not a new VISOR runtime dependency inside Bijou.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-082-sponsored-human}

A maintainer wants one inspectable artifact that says, ``this exact GraphQL fixture produced this exact block artifact, scene IR, debug summary, replay identity, and visual fact set.'' They should not need to reconstruct the proof from scattered test helpers or terminal screenshots.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-082-sponsored-agent}

An agent wants to load one JSON-shaped bundle and trace a source field through artifact facts, scene nodes, debug facts, replay metadata, visual target facts, and stable hashes without executing DOGFOOD or scraping terminal output.

\section{Hill}\label{record-082-hill}

Given the checked-in DOGFOOD GraphQL fixture, Bijou can emit a deterministic \texttt{v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} whose source, normalized \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} facts, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} facts, \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} facts, replay metadata, visual scene facts, and hash inventory are stable across runs and small enough for VISOR, DOGFOOD, and future WARP TTD tooling to inspect.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-082-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Which GraphQL fixture does the bundle represent?
\item
  Which \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} artifact and \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} scene are carried by the bundle?
\item
  Which hashes prove the source, artifact, scene, debug summary, replay facts, visual scene facts, and full bundle?
\item
  Which replay identity can future debugger tooling use without depending on host-local paths, timestamps, process ids, or terminal timing?
\item
  Which visual scene facts can VISOR inspect before \#459 adds packed-cell validation?
\item
  Can a whitespace-only SDL edit preserve the artifact, scene, debug, visual, and bundle hashes where semantics do not change?
\item
  Can malformed source or broken lowering assumptions fail before a bundle is emitted?
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope}\label{record-082-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a public \texttt{v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} fact shape in Bijou.
\item
  Build the first bundle from the existing constrained GraphQL block compiler path.
\item
  Reuse the checked-in DOGFOOD GraphQL fixture unless implementation finds a smaller fixture that still proves the same source-to-scene path.
\item
  Carry the fixture source name, semantic source hash, normalized source hash, \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} artifact, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} scene, \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} summary, replay metadata, visual scene facts, and stable hashes.
\item
  Keep the bundle JSON-serializable, deterministic, and free of absolute local paths, timestamps, process ids, screenshots, and operator terminal state.
\item
  Add focused tests for deterministic output, hash stability, inspectability, and failure cases.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-082-non-goals}

This cycle does not:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  implement \#459 packed-cell-to-\texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} validation
\item
  implement WARP TTD browser UI or debugger sessions
\item
  implement Geordi browser, image, or packed-cell endpoints
\item
  require Bunny graphics, raycast, mesh, camera, shader, or geometry work
\item
  require Wesley DTO generation or a general GraphQL compiler
\item
  generalize every V8 schema shape
\item
  make VISOR a runtime package dependency of Bijou
\item
  add screenshot, video, or frame-capture file formats
\item
  migrate additional DOGFOOD surfaces to GraphQL
\end{itemize}

\section{Bundle Contract}\label{record-082-bundle-contract}

The first accepted bundle should be plain data:

\begin{CodeBlock}
visor-artifact-bundle/1
  bundleVersion
  fixture
    id
    sourceName
    sourceHash
    normalizedSourceHash
  source
    language
    text
  artifacts
    bijouBlock
    uiScene
    debugSummary
  replay
    replayVersion
    scenarioId
    fixtureId
    deterministicSeed
    steps[]
  visual
    visualFactsVersion
    sceneId
    rootNodeId
    targetProfiles[]
    nodeFacts[]
    lowerModes[]
  hashes
    sourceHash
    normalizedSourceHash
    artifactHash
    sceneHash
    debugSummaryHash
    replayHash
    visualFactsHash
    bundleHash
  receipts[]
\end{CodeBlock}

\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h} records the raw source text hash. \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h} records the semantic source hash inherited from the compiled \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} artifact. \texttt{b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h} is computed from the canonical semantic bundle payload with raw \texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t}, raw \texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h} copies, and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h} itself omitted. That lets VISOR inspect exact source text and raw source identity while preserving a stable semantic bundle hash across whitespace-only SDL edits. Hashing must use the same deterministic JSON rules already used by the GraphQL block and scene IR proof path.

\section{Replay Metadata Contract}\label{record-082-replay-metadata-contract}

Replay metadata is identity and intent, not a full debugger session. The first shape should record:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  stable scenario id
\item
  fixture id
\item
  deterministic seed or explicit no-randomness marker
\item
  source, artifact, scene, debug, and visual hashes consumed by the replay
\item
  ordered steps such as compile source, lower artifact, summarize debug facts, and expose visual facts
\end{itemize}

It must not record wall-clock timestamps, process ids, absolute paths, terminal dimensions from the operator environment, or browser state. WARP TTD may later load this metadata, but WARP TTD does not define the \#458 shape.

\section{Visual Scene Facts Contract}\label{record-082-visual-scene-facts-contract}

Visual scene facts summarize the \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1} output for inspection. They are not Geordi render receipts and not \#459 packed-cell facts. The first shape should expose:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  scene id and root node id
\item
  target profile inventory
\item
  node ids, roles, kinds, text facts, group ownership, and source references
\item
  token refs, i18n keys, action ids, and binding ids
\item
  lower-mode hashes and labels
\end{itemize}

That is enough for VISOR to prove what Bijou thinks the visual scene is before future render targets prove how they draw it.

\section{Failure Cases}\label{record-082-failure-cases}

The bundle builder must reject:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  missing source name or fixture id
\item
  source names that are absolute paths
\item
  missing \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, or debug summary facts
\item
  artifact, scene, debug, replay, or visual hash mismatches
\item
  duplicate visual node ids
\item
  lower-mode inventories that omit required node, i18n, or token witnesses
\item
  replay metadata that contains host-local or wall-clock facts
\item
  malformed source that the GraphQL block compiler already rejects
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-082-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

The bundle must preserve lower-mode witnesses and semantic roles so the proof is inspectable without color, terminal glyphs, or screenshots. Visual facts must name text, node ids, i18n keys, token refs, and source refs independently of the normal terminal rendering path.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-082-localization-and-directionality-posture}

Renderable text continues to come from GraphQL \texttt{@\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n} keys plus fallback copy. The bundle must keep i18n keys and fallbacks visible in artifact, scene, debug, and visual facts. Directionality remains deferred until V8 supports localized layout constraints; this cycle must not hide that deferral.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-082-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

The useful inspection path becomes:

\begin{CodeBlock}
GraphQL fixture
  -> visor-artifact-bundle/1.fixture
  -> visor-artifact-bundle/1.artifacts.bijouBlock
  -> visor-artifact-bundle/1.artifacts.uiScene
  -> visor-artifact-bundle/1.artifacts.debugSummary
  -> visor-artifact-bundle/1.visual
  -> visor-artifact-bundle/1.replay
  -> visor-artifact-bundle/1.hashes
\end{CodeBlock}

An agent should be able to answer, from the bundle alone:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Which source field produced this node?
\item
  Which i18n key and token refs belong to this text?
\item
  Which action or binding facts are attached?
\item
  Which target profile was declared?
\item
  Which hash proves the source-to-scene chain?
\item
  Which facts are deliberately not proven until \#459 or a later external endpoint cycle?
\end{itemize}

\item

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-083-decision-summary}

Bijou will consume byte-identical copies of the canonical Keep \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0}, source map, and build manifest. It will validate their versions, identities, references, and pinned digests before lowering the page through a Bijou-owned \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, layout, and \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} path.

The website remains authoritative for page composition and source occurrences. Bijou owns terminal render identities, inspection facts, residuals, and its receipt. Geordi is sibling evidence, not a package dependency or authority.

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-083-current-truth}

Before DX-050, Bijou could lower Bijou-owned scenes and blocks to terminal surfaces, but it could not validate, inspect, or lower the website-owned \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0} family. The canonical ProjectPage specimen existed only in the website repository at revision \texttt{6\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}7}; Bijou had no pinned copy, page target profile, cross-artifact validation, source-to-render map, target receipt, or terminal witness for that family.

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-083-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Pin byte-identical \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0}, and \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0} inputs to website revision \texttt{6\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}7} with exact SHA-256 digests.
\item
  Validate versions, identities, references, dependency digests, root reachability, reading order, and target capabilities before lowering.
\item
  Reject visible unsupported blocks and obstructed or clipped output with a stable diagnostic and no target artifact.
\item
  Residualize only hidden unsupported blocks, with the unsupported block identity preserved in the target map.
\item

\item
  Preserve page, template, source-occurrence, token, reading-order, landmark, and action facts across all supported inspection modes.
\item
  Hold the Code Dojo debt ceiling at \texttt{6\allowbreak{}2} aggregate violations or lower and pass the focused contract, generation, documentation, and full repository gates.
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-083-sponsor-human}

James Ross.

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-083-sponsor-agent}

Codex.

\section{Hill}\label{record-083-hill}

Given the canonical Keep specimen, Bijou emits deterministic terminal inspection evidence that preserves page, template, source-occurrence, token, reading-order, and link identities; assigns every supported visible node a Bijou render identity; residualizes hidden unsupported nodes; and rejects malformed, contradictory, or visibly unsupported inputs.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-083-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

\item
  Which token, reading-order, source, and action facts remain inspectable?
\item
  Which upstream capabilities does Bijou refuse rather than inherit?
\item
  Does repeated lowering emit byte-identical artifacts and receipts?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Scope}\label{record-083-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Vendor the three canonical inputs with provenance and SHA-256 pins.
\item
  Parse and validate the version-zero artifact family fail closed.
\item
  Lower supported ProjectPage blocks to one deterministic \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}.
\item

\item

\item
  Preserve source-map identities without mutating compiler-owned occurrences.
\item
  Reduce Code Dojo debt to \texttt{6\allowbreak{}2} aggregate violations or lower.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-083-non-goals}

\item
  No website runtime or production GraphQL server.
\item
  No mutation of authored page, source-map, or build-manifest authority.
\item
  No Geordi dependency, pixel parity, browser semantics, or HTML claims.
\item
  No general page-family vocabulary or \texttt{/\allowbreak{}0} to \texttt{/\allowbreak{}1} promotion.
\item
  No unsupported-block approximation or silent capability inheritance.
\item
  No redesign of DOGFOOD, the website, or existing \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} behavior.
\end{itemize}

\section{Target Contract}\label{record-083-target-contract}

The target accepts exact UTF-8 bytes for \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0}, and \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0}. It returns Bijou-owned scene, target-map, receipt, and terminal-witness artifacts or one stable diagnostic with a code, input path, and detail.

Supported visible page nodes receive injective render identities. Hidden unsupported nodes receive explicit residuals. Visible unsupported nodes fail closed without target artifacts. Target output records upstream claims as not inherited and binds every output digest to the exact input family.

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-083-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

The terminal witness preserves text, semantic roles, reading order, link destinations, and residual explanations without relying on color alone. It does not claim browser landmarks, accessibility-tree parity, or native links.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-083-localization-and-directionality-posture}

Input text and order are preserved exactly. Token roles remain references, not resolved theme guesses. No new translation authority or bidirectional layout claim is introduced; unsupported direction-sensitive behavior is residualized.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-083-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

An agent can trace input digest to page node, template node, source occurrence, scene node, terminal region, token references, action destination, and receipt without scraping screenshots or executing the website.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-083-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Canonical bytes stay owned by the website at revision \texttt{6\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}7}.
\item
  Every supported visible page node maps to one target identity.
\item
  Every hidden unsupported page node maps to one explicit residual.
\item
  Every visible unsupported page node fails closed before output.
\item
  Render identities are injective and target-owned.
\item
  Reading order, tokens, actions, and source occurrences remain inspectable.
\item
  Unsupported versions, references, blocks, or claims fail closed.
\item
  Generated outputs are deterministic and inventory checked.
\item
  The Code Dojo ceiling falls from \texttt{1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2} to \texttt{6\allowbreak{}2} or lower.
\end{itemize}

The bounded target supports the five ProjectPage block definitions. \chapter{DX-052 NO\_COLOR Is Not a Capability}\label{record-084}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DX-052-no-color-is-not-a-capability.md}\par}\smallskip

\section{Problem}\label{record-084-problem}

Three defects found by an application (\texttt{m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}) that had to work around all three locally before it could ship a readable palette. Each one is a case of bijou answering a question the caller did not ask.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{1. \texttt{N\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R} takes the whole TUI down, not just the colour}{1.  takes the whole TUI down, not just the colour}}\label{record-084-no_color-takes-the-whole-tui-down-not-just-the-colour}

\texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e} (\texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}) resolves in this order:

\begin{CodeBlock}
BIJOU_ACCESSIBLE=1    -> 'accessible'
NO_COLOR / TERM=dumb  -> 'pipe'
!stdout.isTTY         -> 'pipe'
CI                    -> 'static'
stdout.isTTY          -> 'interactive'
\end{CodeBlock}

The second line conflates two unrelated requests. \href{https://no-color.org}{no-color.org} defines \texttt{N\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R} as a statement about \textbf{colour}: ``when present, regardless of its value, prevents the addition of ANSI color''. It says nothing about cursor addressing, alternate screens, or interactivity. bijou reads it as a statement about \textbf{capability}, so a user who exports \texttt{N\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}1} in their shell profile --- a common, reasonable thing to do --- does not get a monochrome TUI. They get no TUI: \texttt{c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e} becomes \texttt{'\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}'}, every component lowers to its plain single-frame form, and \texttt{s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}Q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m} starts returning \texttt{'\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}'}.

Nothing is gained by the conflation, because \textbf{colour is already suppressed by a separate path} --- three of them, in fact, each reading \texttt{N\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R} directly and none consulting \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e}:

\texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} & 54 & \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r} on the resolved theme \\
\texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} & 23 & \texttt{c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\}\allowbreak{})} \\
\texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} & 20 & \texttt{i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} \\
\end{longtable}
}

So removing the line removes the interactivity damage while every \textbf{colour and style} escape stays suppressed. Not every escape: an interactive session by definition emits cursor movement, screen updates and possibly alternate-screen control sequences, and it should --- a monochrome TUI is still a TUI. \texttt{N\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R} asks for no colour, not for no terminal control. The two concerns were never coupled in the implementation; only in the detector.

\texttt{g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s} (\texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s}) already ships a \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e} override for exactly this reason, with a comment saying so. When two first-party consumers independently re-implement a detector, the detector is wrong.

\subsection{2. An unknown status key renders struck through}\label{record-084-an-unknown-status-key-renders-struck-through}

\texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s} (\texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}):

\begin{CodeBlock}
status: (key) => {
  try { return tokenGraph.get(`status.${key}`, mode); }
  catch { return tokenGraph.get('status.muted', mode); }
},
\end{CodeBlock}

\texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d} carries \texttt{[\allowbreak{}'\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}'\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}'\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}'\allowbreak{}]} in \textbf{every} shipped preset --- \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k}, \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a}, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}k}. That is a defensible token: ``muted'' as in retired, done, cancelled. It is the wrong thing to hand back for a key nobody defined.

\texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{})} takes \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g}, not a key union, so the failure is silent and total: a typo, or a key the app forgot to add to its theme, produces text with a line through it. A reader sees ``cancelled''. The app said nothing of the kind. The sibling accessor already does the right thing --- \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} falls back to \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}, a plain token in another group --- so the fix is to make \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} consistent with it and fall back to \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}, which is \texttt{d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m} and nothing else in every preset.

Found in the field: an app declared a \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} helper, dropped the matching status key from its theme as a duplicate, and shipped a painter that resolved to the strikethrough fallback. No check caught it, because no view had called it yet. \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} in \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} has the same fallback and the same problem.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{3. \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} cannot reach \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r} or \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c}}{3.  cannot reach  or }}\label{record-084-extendtheme-cannot-reach-border-or-semantic}

\begin{CodeBlock}
export declare function extendTheme<S, U, G>(base: Theme, extensions: {
  status?: ...; ui?: ...; gradient?: ...; surface?: ...;
}): Theme<...>
\end{CodeBlock}

\texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} has six token groups. \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} can extend four. There is no way to override a border or semantic token through it, which matters because the shipped themes alias heavily across groups: \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} uses \texttt{\#\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}d} for \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r}, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}o}, \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y} \textbf{and} \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g} --- ten aliases of one amber.

An app that calls \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}J\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\}\allowbreak{})} therefore replaces its statuses and silently keeps bijou's amber for every heading, cursor and border. In the case that prompted this, the app's section headings landed ΔE \textbf{0.023} from its own \texttt{w\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g} in OKLab --- indistinguishable --- and the only escape was to abandon \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} and author all six groups by hand.

\section{Non-goals}\label{record-084-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Changing \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d} itself.} Its strikethrough is deliberate and used. Only the \emph{fallback target} moves.
\item
  \textbf{Re-fitting the shipped palettes.} The \texttt{\#\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}d} ten-way alias and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k}'s error/success collapse under protanopia (ΔE 0.059) are real, are what motivated non-goal-adjacent issues, and are filed separately.
\item
  \textbf{Adding OKLCH authoring or a CVD-aware palette audit to bijou.} Also filed separately; \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} covers contrast and reuse but not perceptual separation under simulated colour-vision deficiency.
\item
  \textbf{Typing \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{})} to a key union.} It would catch defect 2 at compile time for typed callers, but it is a wider API change than this cycle wants and would not help JS consumers. Filed as follow-up.
\end{itemize}
