  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-114-retrospective}

Closed by adding \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r} to the built-in theme contract, updating first-party focus-area defaults to consume shell UI tokens, and moving DOGFOOD focused gutter styling into its shell theme vocabulary.

\chapter{DL-013 Design token and theme builder API}\label{record-115}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DL-013-design-token-theme-builder-api.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DL-013 Design token and theme builder API
legend: DL
lane: cool-ideas
priority: medium
github_issue: 308
keywords:
  - design-language
  - themes
  - tokens
  - styles
  - builder-api

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DL-design-language.md}{DL - Design Language}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-115-decision-summary}

Tokens describe semantic color slots in a theme.

Themes own mode-specific token values.

Dark and light are the required first theme modes.

Styles consume resolved tokens at render time.

Styles do not register tokens, own theme values, or decide dark/light mode.

This design records the first official Bijou shape for a Lip Gloss-like builder API without copying Lip Gloss' object model wholesale. Bijou should expose a declarative style builder, but the theme graph must remain explicit because Bijou already treats rendering, lowering, and inspectability as first-class contracts.

The short relationship is:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Theme
  contains modes
    contain token color values

Style
  contains layout and rendering rules
  may reference token ids
  resolves those references through one theme mode during render
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-115-sponsored-human}

A Bijou app author wants to declare semantic colors once and reuse them across dark and light modes so that components can stay visually coherent without passing raw RGB values through every call site.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-115-sponsored-agent}

An agent auditing a Bijou app wants theme tokens and style use to be separable and inspectable so that it can explain whether a rendered cell came from a semantic theme slot, a raw color override, or a lower-mode fallback.

\section{Hill}\label{record-115-hill}

A Bijou app author can define semantic color tokens once inside a theme, provide required dark and light mode values, and apply those tokens through a fluent style builder without allowing styles to become the owner of product theme truth.

\section{Problem}\label{record-115-problem}

Bijou has styleable surfaces, palettes, theme presets, and DOGFOOD chrome, but the authoring API still makes authors think in implementation details too early. A Lip Gloss-like builder can make styling feel natural, but a naive builder can blur three different responsibilities:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  declaring which semantic colors exist
\item
  assigning concrete colors to those semantic colors for dark and light modes
\item
  applying resolved colors and layout rules to rendered content
\end{itemize}

The user-facing syntax should be fluent, but the model should stay strict. Theme data is application and product identity. Style data is component presentation. Token references are the bridge.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-115-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Can a theme define the same token id with separate dark and light values?
\item
  Does a style keep token references unresolved until render receives a theme and mode?
\item
  Can an inspector explain which theme, mode, token id, and lowering profile produced a rendered cell color?
\item
  Do unresolved tokens fail or fall back through an explicit policy instead of silently degrading?
\item
  Does the lower-mode path preserve meaning when truecolor is unavailable?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Scope}\label{record-115-scope}

This spec covers the first color-token API only:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  semantic color token ids
\item
  dark and light theme modes
\item
  theme-local token registration and validation
\item
  token references inside styles
\item
  raw color escape hatches inside styles
\item
  deterministic lower-mode color resolution
\item
  runtime inspectability facts for token resolution
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-115-non-goals}

This slice does not design every future design-token category.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  No spacing tokens yet.
\item
  No typography tokens yet.
\item
  No motion tokens yet.
\item
  No border-shape tokens yet.
\item
  No global mutable token registry.
\item
  No runtime terminal background-color query requirement.
\item
  No implementation of the builder API in this planning slice.
\end{itemize}

Those can become follow-on issues once the color-token and theme-mode contract is landed.

\section{Core Vocabulary}\label{record-115-core-vocabulary}

\subsection{Token}\label{record-115-token}

A token is a semantic color slot inside a theme. It has a stable id such as \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g}, but it does not carry a single universal color by itself. Its value comes from a theme mode.

Good token ids name intent, not pigment:

\begin{CodeBlock}
color.surface.canvas.bg
color.surface.canvas.fg
color.status.danger.bg
color.status.danger.fg
color.chrome.focusGutter
color.chrome.scrollThumb
color.brand.primary
\end{CodeBlock}

Bad token ids encode mode or raw color:

\begin{CodeBlock}
color.dark.red900
color.light.blueAccent
color.hex.ff0000
\end{CodeBlock}

\subsection{Theme}\label{record-115-theme}

A theme is an immutable named collection of modes. It is the owner of token values. A theme can declare that the same token has different concrete colors in dark and light modes.

\subsection{Mode}\label{record-115-mode}

A mode is a named token-value map inside a theme. \texttt{d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} and \texttt{l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} are the required first modes because they cover the highest-value terminal theme split without requiring terminal background probing in the first implementation.

Additional modes can be designed later, for example \texttt{h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a}, or \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}.

\subsection{Style}\label{record-115-style}

A style is an immutable builder for presentation. It can hold foreground, background, border, padding, margin, width, wrapping, alignment, and other rendering rules. When a style uses a token, it stores a token reference rather than a concrete color.

The concrete color is resolved only when rendering receives a theme and mode.

\section{Proposed API}\label{record-115-proposed-api}

The primary API should optimize for the common case: define a theme, define styles that reference semantic tokens, then render with a selected mode.

\begin{CodeBlock}
import {
  defineTheme,
  style,
  tokenRef,
} from '@flyingrobots/bijou';

const theme = defineTheme()
  .id('bijou.default')
  .label('Bijou Default')
  .mode("dark", mode => mode
    .token('color.status.danger.bg')
    .color({ r: 144, g: 0, b: 0 })
    .token('color.status.danger.fg')
    .color({ r: 255, g: 230, b: 230 }))
  .mode("light", mode => mode
    .token('color.status.danger.bg')
    .color({ r: 255, g: 230, b: 230 })
    .token('color.status.danger.fg')
    .color({ r: 144, g: 0, b: 0 }))
  .build();

const warning = style()
  .padding(0, 1)
  .foreground(tokenRef("color.status.danger.fg"))
  .background(tokenRef("color.status.danger.bg"));

const surface = warning.render(surfaceText, { theme, mode: "dark" });
\end{CodeBlock}

The exact authoring names can still move during implementation, but the responsibility split should not.

\section{Token Builder Variant}\label{record-115-token-builder-variant}

The user-proposed token builder shape is useful, but it should be scoped to theme modes rather than become a global registry:

\begin{CodeBlock}
const theme = defineTheme()
  .id('bijou.default')
  .mode('dark', mode => mode
    .token()
    .id('color.status.danger.bg')
    .color({ r: 144, g: 0, b: 0 })
    .register())
  .mode('light', mode => mode
    .token()
    .id('color.status.danger.bg')
    .color({ r: 255, g: 230, b: 230 })
    .register())
  .build();
\end{CodeBlock}

The shorter \texttt{.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{})} form should exist for dense theme files. The longer \texttt{.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} form is useful when an author wants comments, metadata, or validation hooks attached to one token entry.

\section{Why Tokens Are Theme-Scoped}\label{record-115-why-tokens-are-theme-scoped}

Theme-scoped token registration prevents three failure modes:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A token definition cannot silently survive without mode values.
\item
  A style cannot accidentally become the source of product theme truth.
\item
  A future theme inspector can show all missing mode values from one theme object instead of chasing global state.
\end{enumerate}

If Bijou later adds package-level token catalogs, those catalogs should declare allowed ids and descriptions. They should still not own the concrete dark and light mode colors for every consuming app.

\section{Relationship Diagram}\label{record-115-relationship-diagram}

\begin{CodeBlock}
              +------------------+
              | Theme            |
              | id, label        |
              +--------+---------+
                       |
              owns mode maps
                       |
          +------------+------------+
          |                         |
+---------v---------+     +---------v---------+
| Mode: dark        |     | Mode: light       |
| token -> color    |     | token -> color    |
+---------+---------+     +---------+---------+
          |                         |
          +------------+------------+
                       |
                 resolves refs
                       |
              +--------v---------+
              | Style            |
              | fg: tokenRef(...)|
              | bg: tokenRef(...)|
              | layout rules     |
              +--------+---------+
                       |
                 render context
                       |
              +--------v---------+
              | Surface cells    |
              | concrete colors  |
              +------------------+
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Style Builder Surface}\label{record-115-style-builder-surface}

The style builder should feel familiar to authors who know fluent terminal style APIs, while still returning Bijou surfaces and facts.

Candidate methods:

\begin{CodeBlock}
style()
  .foreground(tokenRef('color.text.primary'))
  .background(tokenRef('color.surface.canvas.bg'))
  .bold(true)
  .italic(true)
  .underline(true)
  .padding(1, 2)
  .margin(0, 1)
  .width(40)
  .height(8)
  .maxWidth(80)
  .align('center')
  .border('single')
  .borderForeground(tokenRef('color.chrome.border'))
  .render(surfaceText, { theme, mode: 'dark' });
\end{CodeBlock}

The style builder can support raw colors as an escape hatch:

\begin{CodeBlock}
style().foreground({ r: 250, g: 250, b: 250 });
\end{CodeBlock}

Raw colors should be visible in inspectability facts so an agent can distinguish deliberate hard-coded color from semantic token use.

\section{Resolution Contract}\label{record-115-resolution-contract}

Rendering a token-backed style requires:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a theme
\item
  a mode id
\item
  a lowering profile
\item
  an unresolved-token policy
\end{itemize}

The default unresolved-token policy should fail in development and use a visible fallback in production-like rendering. The fallback must be deterministic and inspectable.

\begin{CodeBlock}
type TokenResolutionFact = {
  tokenId: string;
  themeId: string;
  mode: string;
  source: 'theme' | 'fallback' | 'raw-color';
  requestedColor?: RgbColor;
  resolvedColor: LoweredColor;
  profile: 'truecolor' | 'ansi256' | 'ansi16' | 'mono' | 'plain';
};
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-115-lower-modes}

Color lowering belongs to the resolver, not to each style call site.

The first resolver should support:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r}: preserve RGB
\item
  \texttt{a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}6}: nearest palette index
\item
  \texttt{a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}6}: nearest named ANSI color
\item
  \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o}: intensity and emphasis only
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n}: no color, style facts preserved
\end{itemize}

This keeps the style syntax stable even when output moves from rich terminal to pipe, static snapshot, accessible text, or future frame capture.

\section{Inheritance And Composition}\label{record-115-inheritance-and-composition}

Bijou should support value-style copying and inheritance, but unset rules must stay distinguishable from intentionally raw or token-backed rules.

Candidate API:

\begin{CodeBlock}
const base = style()
  .foreground(tokenRef('color.text.primary'))
  .background(tokenRef('color.surface.canvas.bg'));

const danger = style()
  .inherit(base)
  .background(tokenRef('color.status.danger.bg'))
  .foreground(tokenRef('color.status.danger.fg'));
\end{CodeBlock}

Inheritance should copy only unset rules on the receiver, matching the useful part of Lip Gloss while keeping the resolved-token facts intact.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-115-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

Every rendered token-backed style should be able to expose:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  style id, when provided
\item
  theme id
\item
  mode id
\item
  token ids used
\item
  raw colors used
\item
  fallback tokens used
\item
  lowered output profile
\item
  concrete cell color results
\end{itemize}

This is a Bijou-specific requirement. The goal is not only nice terminal styling, but explainable rendering.

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Reading Posture}\label{record-115-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

Token ids should be semantic enough that an accessible renderer can report meaning even when color is stripped.

For example, \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g} gives better assistive context than \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0}. The style resolver should preserve facts for accessible surfaces even when the final text has no color escape sequences.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-115-localization-directionality-posture}

No localized strings are introduced by this design. Public docs and DOGFOOD examples introduced during implementation must follow the repository localization policy and provide all supported DOGFOOD locales when new localized copy is added. Token ids are logical semantic identifiers and should not encode physical direction, locale, or translated prose.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-115-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/runtime-truth-wins.md}{Runtime Truth Wins}: resolved cell colors and resolver facts are stronger evidence than design prose.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/graceful-lowering-preserves-meaning.md}{Graceful Lowering Preserves Meaning}: color cannot be the only carrier of status, focus, or warning meaning.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are The Spec}: the builder API should land through focused runtime tests, not just examples.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/buffer-holds-facts.md}{Buffer Holds Facts}: rendered cells should preserve token-resolution facts for inspection and replay.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/docs-are-the-demo.md}{Docs Are The Demo}: DOGFOOD examples should exercise the same public builder API as consumers.
\end{itemize}

\section{Compatibility}\label{record-115-compatibility}

The builder should be additive. Existing theme preset and surface APIs should continue to work while the builder is introduced.

Migration can be staged:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add token references and theme builder types.
\item
  Convert one DOGFOOD shell theme path to prove the model.
\item
  Add docs and examples.
\item
  Expand first-party components to accept \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} values.
\item
  Deprecate ad hoc raw color plumbing only after call sites have a builder alternative.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-115-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} creates immutable theme definitions with required dark and light mode maps.
\item
  Theme builders reject duplicate token ids within one mode.
\item
  Theme builders reject themes missing required dark or light mode values for declared tokens.
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{})} is accepted by style color setters.
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} produces immutable styles and does not mutate copied styles.
\item
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\}\allowbreak{})} resolves token-backed colors through the selected mode.
\item
  The resolver emits inspectability facts for token, theme, mode, fallback, and lowering decisions.
\item
  Lower modes prove that token-backed styles render in truecolor, ANSI, mono, and plain profiles.
\item
  DOGFOOD includes one theme-builder example and one style-builder example once implementation lands.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-115-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Token and theme type contracts with focused tests.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} builder with dark/light validation.
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and color-reference resolution.
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} builder for foreground, background, emphasis, padding, width, and render.
\item
  Lower-mode resolver facts and fallback behavior.
\item
  DOGFOOD docs, examples, and package exports.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Implementation Progress}\label{record-115-implementation-progress}

Slices 1 through 3 are the first runtime landing target for issue \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/308}{\#308}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} creates immutable token-theme definitions with required \texttt{d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} and \texttt{l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} mode maps.
\item
  Theme-scoped token registration rejects duplicate token ids within one mode and rejects required modes that omit a declared token.
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} preserve resolution facts for selected theme mode, token id, raw colors, and explicit fallback colors.
\end{itemize}

Slice 4 intentionally tightens the current token vocabulary before adding more syntax:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} now gives every built-in token a per-token ``use when / do not use when'' contract.
\item
  DOGFOOD now uses explicit dark and light shell themes instead of deriving its docs chrome from one title-screen color ramp.
\item
  Focused DogFood preview tests prove that the shell themes keep readable surface text and common semantic roles above the contrast floor in both dark and light postures.
\item
  The next inspectability UX is \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/311}{\#311}, the Theme Inspector drawer: an opt-in \texttt{F\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0} shell drawer that shows token swatches, dark/light values, contrast facts, and future renderer provenance when cell-level token facts exist.
\end{itemize}

Slice 5 promotes contrast from ad hoc tests into a reusable safe-pair contract:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DL-015-theme-safe-pairs-and-contrast-matrices.md}{DL-015} defines foreground/background safe pairs as design-system data.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} builds immutable \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s}, and \texttt{c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} pair matrices.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} can validate pair paths that target token background slots, such as \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g}.
\item
  DOGFOOD exports \texttt{D\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}S} so docs preview tests and the future Theme Inspector drawer consume the same pair contract.
\item
  This slice closes the implementation path for \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/314}{\#314}.
\end{itemize}

The remaining implementation work is the \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} builder, lower-mode resolution proof, package example coverage, and the optional Theme Inspector UX slice.

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-115-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Theme builder rejects missing \texttt{d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} or \texttt{l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} modes.
\item
  Theme builder rejects duplicate mode token ids.
\item
  Style render resolves foreground and background token refs by selected mode.
\item
  Copied styles stay immutable after chained modifications.
\item
  Lower-mode rendering produces deterministic truecolor, ANSI, mono, and plain output.
\item
  Inspectability facts identify theme id, mode id, token id, and fallback status.
\end{itemize}

\section{Roadmap Placement}\label{record-115-roadmap-placement}

This belongs in the Beyond lane as issue \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/308}{\#308} until implementation is scheduled into a versioned release. It should be grouped as the candidate goalpost \texttt{D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} because it crosses design language, runtime rendering, DOGFOOD docs, and public package exports.

\section{Open Questions}\label{record-115-open-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Should \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} accept strings only, surfaces only, or both?
\item
  Should style ids be required for inspectability, or optional metadata?
\item
  Should high-contrast mode land in the first implementation or immediately after dark/light?
\item
  Should token catalogs exist as package-level declarations separate from app-owned theme values?
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-115-retrospective}

This slice is intentionally documentation and roadmap only. The important decision is the object model: tokens belong to themes, themes own modes, and styles consume resolved tokens. Implementation should start with failing runtime tests that prove that split instead of only matching fluent syntax.

\chapter{DL-014 Theme Inspector And Lab}\label{record-116}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DL-014-theme-inspector-and-lab.md}\par}\smallskip

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-116-decision-summary}

Bijou should make theme facts inspectable inside DOGFOOD before the broader mode-aware runtime migration is complete.

This slice adds two bounded surfaces:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  an \texttt{F\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0} Theme Inspector drawer in DOGFOOD
\item
  a \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} / Theme Lab docs page with default palettes, shell-gallery facts, token swatches, and safe-pair diagnostics
\end{itemize}

The first implementation inspects theme tokens only. It does not guess element-level token ownership from final RGB values.

\section{Linked Work}\label{record-116-linked-work}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Parent goalpost: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/308}{\#308}
\item
  User story: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/311}{\#311}
\item
  Related Theme Lab idea: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/315}{\#315}
\item
  Safe-pair contract: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/314}{\#314}
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsored Perspectives}\label{record-116-sponsored-perspectives}

\subsection{Human Perspective}\label{record-116-human-perspective}

A designer-engineer wants to inspect the active theme's token palette from inside a running Bijou TUI so that contrast, token naming, and reuse mistakes can be debugged without leaving the app.

\subsection{Agent Perspective}\label{record-116-agent-perspective}

An implementation agent wants a deterministic DOGFOOD surface and scripted assertions for theme facts so future theme work can be reviewed without relying only on subjective screenshots.

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-116-current-truth}

Bijou has a typed \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} contract with \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s}, and \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t} families. DL-013 added a mode-aware token-theme builder, and DL-015 added safe-pair contrast contracts. DOGFOOD had explicit dark/light themes, but those facts were visible only through settings and tests.

The legacy runtime \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} object is still single-mode. This design works inside that limitation by inspecting concrete runtime themes and documenting the mode migration separately in \#313.

\section{Problem}\label{record-116-problem}

Theme work is hard to evaluate when token choices are buried in code:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  colors can look acceptable in one screen but fail in another surface
\item
  token names and token usage are not visible to the person running DOGFOOD
\item
  safe-pair diagnostics are test-only facts
\item
  dark/light design decisions are not presented as a product surface
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope}\label{record-116-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add first-party \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} presets.
\item
  Retokenize DOGFOOD dark/light shell themes to consume those presets.
\item
  Add a \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} page to DOGFOOD.
\item
  Add an \texttt{F\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0} Theme Inspector drawer to the DOGFOOD docs route.
\item
  Render token swatches grouped by family.
\item
  Show deterministic safe-pair pass counts.
\item
  Add scripted tests for presets, DogFood theme inheritance, F10 behavior, and the Theme Lab page.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-116-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Do not implement full runtime theme/mode separation in this slice.
\item
  Do not make \texttt{F\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0} a global app-frame feature for every consumer app yet.
\item
  Do not implement element-level token overlays without renderer provenance.
\item
  Do not guess token ownership from RGB equality.
\item
  Do not block lower-mode rendering on rich color swatches.
\end{itemize}

\section{Product Shape}\label{record-116-product-shape}

\begin{CodeBlock}
-------------------- DOGFOOD docs shell --------------------+
| Guides  Components  Blocks  Packages  Philosophy  Themes  |
|                                                           |
| +-- themes --------+  +-- docs • Theme Lab --------------+ |
| | > Theme Lab      |  | theme posture                    | |
| |                  |  | shell gallery                    | |
| |                  |  | bijou-dark token swatches        | |
| |                  |  | bijou-light token swatches       | |
| +------------------+  +----------------------------------+ |
| ? Help • / Search • F2 Settings • F10 Theme Inspector     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
\end{CodeBlock}

The quick inspector is a right-side drawer:

\begin{CodeBlock}
                         +-- Theme Inspector --------------+
                         | Active: DOGFOOD / Dark          |
                         | Theme:  dogfood-dark            |
                         | 32/32 safe pairs pass           |
                         |                                  |
                         | SEMANTIC                        |
                         | [swatch] semantic.primary       |
                         | [swatch] semantic.muted         |
                         | SURFACE                         |
                         | [swatch] surface.primary        |
                         | ...                             |
                         | F10/Esc close • ↑/↓ scroll      |
                         +----------------------------------+
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-116-lower-modes}

The inspector and lab are still useful in lower modes because every swatch row also prints the token path and token value text. Color improves scanning, but the token name and diagnostics remain visible without color.

\section{Runtime And API Contract}\label{record-116-runtime-and-api-contract}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{B\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}J\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}K} and \texttt{B\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}J\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}T} are exported from \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u}.
\item
  The presets are registered in \texttt{P\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}S} as \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t}.
\item
  DOGFOOD shell themes keep concrete mode theme names:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    family id: \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d}
  \item
    dark choice id: \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k}, concrete theme name: \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k}
  \item
    light choice id: \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t}, concrete theme name: \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t}
  \end{itemize}
\item
  DOGFOOD clones the default preset values into those shell themes so mutating runtime RGB caches cannot accidentally alias future app-level overrides.
\item
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0} toggles the DOGFOOD-only Theme Inspector drawer after the title screen.
\item
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} closes the drawer.
\item
  \texttt{↑}/\texttt{↓}, \texttt{j}/\texttt{k}, \texttt{d}/\texttt{u}, and \texttt{g}/\texttt{G} scroll the drawer without changing the page behind it.
\item
  \texttt{q} still routes to the normal DOGFOOD quit confirmation and closes the drawer so the confirmation is visible.
\item
  Other keys are bounded and do not drive the page behind the drawer.
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility And Localization}\label{record-116-accessibility-and-localization}

The Theme Lab and quick inspector use DOGFOOD catalog entries for all new user-facing strings. New keys are present in every supported runtime locale: English, German, Spanish, and French. Stable token paths such as \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y} and \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g} remain developer identifiers and are not localized.

\section{Inspectability}\label{record-116-inspectability}

The lab and drawer expose:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  active shell theme label
\item
  runtime theme name
\item
  grouped token paths
\item
  token hex and foreground/background values
\item
  gradient stop values
\item
  color-reuse counts
\item
  safe-pair pass counts
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Slices}\label{record-116-implementation-slices}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} presets and export them.
\item
  Retokenize DOGFOOD dark/light shell themes to consume those presets.
\item

\item

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-116-tests-to-write-first}

\chapter{DL-015 Theme safe pairs and contrast matrices}\label{record-117}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DL-015-theme-safe-pairs-and-contrast-matrices.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DL-015 Theme safe pairs and contrast matrices
legend: DL
lane: cool-ideas
priority: medium
github_issue: 314
keywords:
  - design-language
  - themes
  - tokens
  - contrast
  - accessibility

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DL-design-language.md}{DL - Design Language}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-117-decision-summary}

Theme contrast should be declared as a reusable design-system contract, not as one-off test loops.

Safe pairs name which foreground token paths are expected to be readable on which background token paths. The contract feeds \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, DOGFOOD theme tests, future Theme Inspector swatches, and lower-mode accessibility reports.

The first runtime shape is intentionally compact:

\begin{CodeBlock}
const pairs = defineThemeSafePairs()
  .readable('semantic.primary', 'surface.primary.bg')
  .status('status.error', 'surface.overlay.bg')
  .chrome('ui.cursor', 'surface.secondary.bg')
  .build();
\end{CodeBlock}

Safe-pair background paths may target a token foreground, such as \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}, or a token background slot, such as \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g}.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-117-sponsored-human}

A designer-engineer wants DogFood and first-party themes to prove readable foreground/background combinations so that theme retuning is a design exercise instead of a screenshot guessing game.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-117-sponsored-agent}

An agent auditing a theme wants a stable matrix of safe token pairs so it can identify whether a low-contrast failure is a broken theme value, a missing token, or an unsupported pair that should not have been used by the component.

\section{Hill}\label{record-117-hill}

Bijou can declare safe token pairs once, run the same contrast contract through \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, and reuse the resulting pair matrix in DOGFOOD and future Theme Inspector UX.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-117-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Can a safe pair target \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g} instead of only token foregrounds?
\item
  Does the safe-pair builder reject duplicate foreground/background declarations?
\item
  Can \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} validate a safe-pair matrix without bespoke test code?
\item
  Does DogFood publish its readable/status/chrome pair matrix from the theme module rather than hiding it in tests?
\item
  Can Theme Inspector later display the same pair facts without inventing a second contrast registry?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Scope}\label{record-117-scope}

This slice includes:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} as a fluent builder for safe-pair declarations
\item
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s}, and \texttt{c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} pair classifications
\item
  support for \texttt{.\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g} color-slot paths in \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} contrast pairs
\item
  DOGFOOD dark/light shell pair contracts
\item
  focused tests proving the contract and DogFood usage
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-117-non-goals}

This slice does not implement the Theme Inspector drawer, retune the global default theme values, or replace the legacy single-mode \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} interface. Those are separate follow-on slices.

\section{Safe-Pair Vocabulary}\label{record-117-safe-pair-vocabulary}

\texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} pairs are ordinary text and component foregrounds that must stay legible on a surface.

\texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s} pairs are process, health, timeline, or object-state foregrounds that must stay legible when rendered on a surface.

\texttt{c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} pairs are shell/runtime affordances such as cursor and focus chrome that must remain recognizable on app surfaces.

The kind is not decorative metadata. Future inspectors and reports can group failures by kind so a theme author can distinguish typography problems from status-color problems.

\section{Runtime Contract}\label{record-117-runtime-contract}

\texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} returns a pure builder. Chained calls accumulate immutable pair declarations. \texttt{b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} returns a frozen array of frozen pair objects compatible with \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r}.

Duplicate foreground/background pairs are rejected because duplicate pair rows make reports and inspectors ambiguous.

\texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} resolves contrast pair paths through concrete token color slots:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y} resolves to the token foreground color.
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y} resolves to the surface token foreground color.
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g} resolves to the surface token background color.
\end{itemize}

Missing paths remain errors. Invalid colors remain invalid-color issues from the normal token scan.

\section{DOGFOOD Matrix}\label{record-117-dogfood-matrix}

DogFood declares its safe-pair matrix beside its shell themes.

Readable foregrounds:

\begin{CodeBlock}
semantic.primary
semantic.muted
semantic.accent
semantic.info
semantic.success
semantic.warning
semantic.error
\end{CodeBlock}

Status foregrounds:

\begin{CodeBlock}
status.active
status.pending
\end{CodeBlock}

Chrome foregrounds:

\begin{CodeBlock}
ui.cursor
\end{CodeBlock}

Background slots:

\begin{CodeBlock}
surface.primary.bg
surface.secondary.bg
surface.elevated.bg
surface.overlay.bg
surface.muted.bg
\end{CodeBlock}

That matrix intentionally proves the dense docs shell before broader component retokenization. Additional first-party pairs should be added only when a component needs them as a real contract.

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Reading Posture}\label{record-117-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

Safe-pair checks do not make color sufficient as the only meaning carrier. They prove that color, when present, remains readable. The same components still need text, symbols, structure, or state labels that survive no-color, pipe, and accessible output modes.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-117-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

A future inspector can group safe-pair facts by pair kind:

\begin{CodeBlock}
readable semantic.primary on surface.primary.bg: pass 15.20
status status.pending on surface.overlay.bg: pass 8.40
chrome ui.cursor on surface.secondary.bg: pass 7.10
\end{CodeBlock}

If the renderer later preserves per-cell token provenance, an agent can compare the token pair actually used by a cell against the declared safe-pair matrix.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-117-localization-directionality-posture}

No localized strings are introduced by this design. Token paths and pair kinds are stable developer identifiers and must not encode locale-specific prose or physical direction.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-117-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/runtime-truth-wins.md}{Runtime Truth Wins}: safe pairs are only useful when \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} proves them from concrete theme values.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/graceful-lowering-preserves-meaning.md}{Graceful Lowering Preserves Meaning}: contrast is necessary, but color is not the only meaning carrier.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are The Spec}: the pair builder and DogFood matrix land through focused runtime tests.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/docs-are-the-demo.md}{Docs Are The Demo}: DOGFOOD consumes the same pair contract the docs describe.
\end{itemize}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist

\chapter{DL-016 Mode-aware runtime theme adapter}\label{record-118}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DL-016-mode-aware-runtime-theme-adapter.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: DL-016 Mode-aware runtime theme adapter
legend: DL
lane: bad-code
priority: medium
github_issue: 313
keywords:
  - design-language
  - themes
  - modes
  - app-frame
  - dogfood

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DL-design-language.md}{DL - Design Language}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-118-decision-summary}

Bijou should distinguish theme identity from theme mode at the app-frame boundary.

The existing runtime \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} object is a concrete palette. That stays true for compatibility. The new shape is an adapter around that concrete palette:

\begin{CodeBlock}
FrameShellThemeFamily
  id: "dogfood"
  modes:
    dark  -> Theme("dogfood-dark")
    light -> Theme("dogfood-light")
\end{CodeBlock}

Single-mode shell themes remain valid:

\begin{CodeBlock}
FrameShellTheme
  id: "default"
  theme: Theme("default")
\end{CodeBlock}

The frame resolves both forms into concrete choices before rendering. A choice has a stable id, a family id, an optional mode id, and a resolved concrete theme. This gives settings, inspectors, and DOGFOOD one product identity while keeping the legacy render path stable.

\section{Linked Work}\label{record-118-linked-work}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  User story: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/313}{\#313}
\item
  Token builder foundation: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/308}{\#308}
\item
  Theme Inspector follow-up: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/311}{\#311}
\item
  Theme Lab follow-up: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/315}{\#315}
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsored Perspectives}\label{record-118-sponsored-perspectives}

\subsection{Human Perspective}\label{record-118-human-perspective}

A designer-engineer wants DOGFOOD to present one DogFood theme with dark and light modes so that switching color scheme does not look like switching product identity.

\subsection{Agent Perspective}\label{record-118-agent-perspective}

An implementation agent wants app-frame theme facts to carry both family and mode identity so tests, inspectors, and future provenance tools can prove which semantic theme and concrete mode produced the current cells.

\section{Hill}\label{record-118-hill}

An app can declare a mode-aware shell theme, switch between its dark and light modes through the existing settings drawer, and observe the selected family and mode without breaking consumers that still pass single concrete themes.

\section{Problem}\label{record-118-problem}

DL-013 made theme authoring mode-aware: one theme owns dark and light token values. The runtime still consumes one concrete \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} at a time. PR \#310 therefore had to model DOGFOOD as two independent shell themes:

\begin{CodeBlock}
dogfood-dark
dogfood-light
\end{CodeBlock}

That representation works mechanically, but it teaches the wrong model:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  theme identity and mode identity are conflated
\item
  settings rows mix product themes and color modes in one flat list
\item
  Theme Inspector and Theme Lab cannot report a stable family id
\item
  tests assert \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} as peer themes instead of \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d} plus a selected mode
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope}\label{record-118-scope}

This slice adds the first runtime adapter, not a full replacement for \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e}.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a mode-aware \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y} path beside concrete \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  Resolve shell theme specs into flattened runtime choices.
\item
  Preserve old single-theme specs unchanged.
\item
  Include selected mode facts in \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  Convert DOGFOOD to one \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d} shell theme with \texttt{d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} and \texttt{l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} modes.
\item
  Update Theme Inspector and Theme Lab facts to use family and mode labels.
\item
  Add tests proving mode switching, compatibility, and context isolation.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-118-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Do not replace the concrete \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} interface.
\item
  Do not require every app to adopt mode-aware themes.
\item
  Do not add terminal background-color detection here.
\item
  Do not add element-level token provenance.
\item
  Do not implement Theme Inspector mode preview/apply UX from \#311 in this slice.
\end{itemize}

\section{Runtime Contract}\label{record-118-runtime-contract}

\texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c} accepts either a concrete \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} with \texttt{t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} or a mode-aware \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y} with a non-empty \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} array.

\begin{CodeBlock}
const theme = {
  id: 'dogfood',
  label: 'DOGFOOD',
  modes: [
    { id: 'dark', label: 'Dark', theme: dogfoodDark },
    { id: 'light', label: 'Light', theme: dogfoodLight },
  ],
} satisfies FrameShellThemeSpec;
\end{CodeBlock}

A mode-aware entry resolves into choices:

\begin{CodeBlock}
choice id: dogfood:dark
family id: dogfood
mode id: dark
label: DOGFOOD / Dark
theme: dogfood-dark
\end{CodeBlock}

A legacy entry resolves into one choice:

\begin{CodeBlock}
choice id: default
family id: default
mode id: undefined
label: Default
theme: default
\end{CodeBlock}

The existing frame model can continue storing \texttt{a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}d} as the choice id. Consumers that inspect \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e} get the richer facts:

\begin{CodeBlock}
{
  shellTheme: {
    id: 'dogfood:dark',
    label: 'DOGFOOD / Dark',
    theme: dogfoodDark,
  },
  shellThemeSpec: dogfoodFamily,
  shellThemeId: 'dogfood',
  modeId: 'dark',
  modeLabel: 'Dark',
  ctx,
}
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Settings UX}\label{record-118-settings-ux}

The first implementation keeps one settings row:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Shell theme  DOGFOOD / Dark
\end{CodeBlock}

Activating the row cycles the resolved choices:

\begin{CodeBlock}
DOGFOOD / Dark -> DOGFOOD / Light -> Cabinet of Curiosities -> ...
\end{CodeBlock}

This is intentionally conservative. A later \#311/\#315 slice can split family and mode into separate controls once the app-frame has enough option metadata to render that well.

\section{Compatibility}\label{record-118-compatibility}

Compatibility is a hard requirement:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Existing \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} entries with \texttt{t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} still compile.
\item
  Existing apps that read \texttt{c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} still receive a concrete selected shell theme.
\item
  Mode-aware apps can inspect \texttt{c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c}, \texttt{c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}d}, and optional mode facts for family identity.
\item
  Existing app-frame tests for simple theme cycling keep passing.
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} still receives one concrete resolved theme.
\end{itemize}

\section{Tests}\label{record-118-tests}

The slice is complete when tests prove:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Mode-aware shell themes flatten into stable choices.
\item
  Settings cycling applies a mode choice and reports family/mode facts.
\item
  Old single-mode shell themes still cycle and apply.
\item
  DOGFOOD publishes one \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d} family with \texttt{d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} and \texttt{l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} modes.
\item
  Preview/resolution helpers can inspect a mode choice without mutating the ambient default context until the setting is applied.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-118-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item[$\square$]
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c} supports concrete \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} entries and mode-aware \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y} entries.
\item[$\square$]
  Runtime choice ids distinguish family and mode.
\item[$\square$]
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e} includes optional mode facts.
\item[$\square$]
  DOGFOOD presents one DogFood shell theme family with dark/light modes.
\item[$\square$]
  Legacy single-mode themes remain supported.
\item[$\square$]
  Tests cover mode switching and context isolation.
\end{itemize}

\section{Slice Plan}\label{record-118-slice-plan}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add the design doc and tracker updates.
\item
  Add app-frame mode-aware shell theme types and choice resolution tests.
