\chapter{DL-017 - DOGFOOD Light Theme Readiness}\label{record-119}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DL-017-dogfood-light-theme-readiness.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
id: DL-017
title: DOGFOOD Light Theme Readiness
status: active
lane: asap
priority: medium
github_issue: 341
legend: DL

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DL-design-language.md}{DL - Design Language}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-119-decision-summary}

DOGFOOD's \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} shell theme should be safe to demonstrate in a real terminal without relying on the terminal profile's default background or lucky contrast. For \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, the bounded repair is:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  framed settings, menu, and modal chrome paints explicit light-theme backgrounds
\item
  borders, panel fills, muted copy, selection rows, and action labels remain visually distinct in the Bijou light palette
\item
  the theme doctor covers the chrome-safe pairs that failed the release-video rehearsal by sight
\item
  deterministic tests prove both token-level contrast and rendered shell background ownership
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-119-sponsored-human}

A release-video user needs to switch DOGFOOD into light mode and have the app look deliberate on camera. Settings and quit chrome should not show dark terminal patches, washed-out borders, or action labels that are hard to find.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-119-sponsored-agent}

An agent needs a deterministic witness for light-theme chrome. It should be able to render the DOGFOOD shell in \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t}, inspect actual \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} cell metadata, and fail if settings or modal chrome leaves meaningful cells without a theme-owned background.

\section{Hill}\label{record-119-hill}

After this cycle, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} is release-demo-ready for the current V7 surface: the theme paints its shell chrome, passes explicit chrome contrast diagnostics, and has enough focused proof to keep terminal-default background leaks from silently returning.

\section{Problem}\label{record-119-problem}

Issue \#341 came from the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release-video rehearsal. The light theme looked unfinished around settings and modal chrome: some border/background regions appeared to inherit the terminal's unstyled background, and several low-contrast token pairs made panels, muted text, and selected rows difficult to read.

The dark DOGFOOD theme mostly hides this class of problem because terminal profiles are commonly dark. The light theme needs explicit proof because a terminal-default background leak can look acceptable on one profile and broken on another.

\section{Scope}\label{record-119-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a focused rendered witness for DOGFOOD light-theme settings/menu/modal chrome.
\item
  Fix any shell-rendering path that fails to paint theme-owned backgrounds for the witness.
\item
  Retune the Bijou light palette only where the current tokens make borders, panels, muted text, selection rows, or modal actions unclear.
\item
  Expand DOGFOOD theme safe-pair diagnostics so light-theme chrome tokens are checked by \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Update release-facing docs/changelog so \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} records the light-theme demo-readiness repair honestly.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-119-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Do not solve \#343's full first-party dark/light variant coverage.
\item
  Do not redesign Theme Lab or Theme Inspector.
\item
  Do not add a global dark/light hotkey in this cycle.
\item
  Do not redesign DOGFOOD's layout, typography, or theme family model.
\item
  Do not turn \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} into a broad design-system feature train.
\end{itemize}

\section{User Experience Contract}\label{record-119-user-experience-contract}

The light theme may be calmer than the dark theme, but it cannot be ambiguous. The user should be able to distinguish the app background, panels, borders, muted text, selected rows, scrollbars, and modal actions without changing their terminal profile.

Settings, command-palette menu, and modal surfaces must paint their own backgrounds. Empty frame chrome inside those surfaces should not be transparent unless the transparency is a deliberate tokenized overlay with a deterministic fallback.

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-119-lower-modes}

\subsection{Static Mode}\label{record-119-static-mode}

Static rendered proof should expose actual \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} cells and token-derived foreground/background choices so tests can inspect theme ownership without parsing screenshots.

\subsection{Pipe Mode}\label{record-119-pipe-mode}

Pipe output remains text-first and does not need to encode color proof. The color-specific proof belongs in rendered \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} tests and theme diagnostics.

\subsection{Accessible Mode}\label{record-119-accessible-mode}

No new accessibility contract is introduced. Any action labels or status text made easier to see through color should remain textual, not color-only.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-119-localization-directionality-posture}

This cycle does not add new localization or bidirectional-layout behavior. The theme repair must preserve the selected-locale text path, existing English-source documentation notices, and current left-to-right DOGFOOD chrome geometry.

The rendered witnesses should avoid making assertions about translated copy beyond stable shell titles such as settings, command palette, and quit chrome. If a future right-to-left shell layout changes modal or drawer geometry, it should still inherit the same token-owned background contract.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-119-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

Agents should be able to inspect the repair without screenshots. The important facts are:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  which concrete DOGFOOD shell theme is active
\item
  which shell surface is open: settings drawer, command-palette menu, or quit modal
\item
  whether visible chrome border cells have explicit foreground and background metadata
\item
  which safe-pair token declarations cover the chrome colors
\item
  whether \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} reports any low-contrast chrome pairs for DOGFOOD dark or light modes
\end{itemize}

The proof should stay in \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} metadata and theme-doctor reports so future agents can reason about background ownership deterministically.

\section{Theme Diagnostics}\label{record-119-theme-diagnostics}

The existing DOGFOOD safe-pair matrix should grow beyond primary text/status pairs to cover the light chrome pairs that matter for this bug:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  border tokens against primary, secondary, elevated, overlay, and muted surfaces
\item
  muted text against the same surfaces used by settings and modal panels
\item
  selection/focus gutter foregrounds and backgrounds
\item
  scroll thumb and scroll track visibility
\item
  modal action/status foregrounds against overlay and elevated surfaces
\end{itemize}

The diagnostic is intentionally token-level. Rendered tests prove that chrome uses those tokens; the doctor proves that the token pairs remain readable.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-119-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD light mode should not depend on terminal-profile background color.
\item
  Theme diagnostics should cover app chrome, not just body copy.
\item
  Light-theme repairs must stay compatible with existing dark theme behavior.
\item
  \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} remains a narrow stabilization release.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Plan}\label{record-119-implementation-plan}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add focused failing tests that render DOGFOOD \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} settings drawer, command-palette menu, and quit modal chrome and find unpainted cells in each chrome rectangle.
\item
  Add a focused failing diagnostic test for missing DOGFOOD chrome safe pairs.
\item
  Fix the shell/component path that leaves backgrounds unset, or retune tokens if the renderer already paints but the selected color pair is too weak.
\item
  Expand the DOGFOOD safe-pair matrix to cover chrome-relevant light-theme pairs.
\item
  Run focused rendered tests, theme doctor tests, the DOGFOOD terminal capture smoke path, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}, \texttt{g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}, and the relevant broader suite before review.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-119-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD light-theme settings drawer, command-palette menu, and quit modal renders fail when visible chrome cells inside their overlay rectangles have no background metadata.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\}\allowbreak{})} fails if chrome pairs are omitted or fall below the selected contrast floor.
\item
  Existing dark-theme DOGFOOD shell tests continue to pass.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-119-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Deterministic light-theme chrome witnesses exist for settings drawer, command-palette menu, and quit modal rendering.
\item
  Any unpainted background path found by the witness is fixed.
\item
  Bijou light theme border, panel, muted text, selection, and modal action tokens are readable enough for the DOGFOOD release-video path.
\item
  DOGFOOD theme diagnostics cover the relevant chrome safe pairs.
\item
  The DOGFOOD terminal capture smoke path is run as release-video-path evidence.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} records the demo-readiness fix.
\item
  Issue \#341 is closed by the implementation PR.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-119-retrospective}

To be completed when the PR lands.

\chapter{DL-018 - First-Party Theme Variant Coverage}\label{record-120}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DL-018-first-party-theme-variant-coverage.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
id: DL-018
title: First-Party Theme Variant Coverage
status: active
lane: asap
priority: medium
github_issue: 343
legend: DL

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DL-design-language.md}{DL - Design Language}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-120-decision-summary}

DOGFOOD now has a real AppShell theme-mode toggle, but the theme list still mixes one paired shell family with several landing-art shell presets that do not have light/dark siblings. For \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, the bounded repair is:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  inventory every first-party DOGFOOD shell theme as paired or single-mode through deterministic shell-spec coverage
\item
  keep \texttt{D\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} and \texttt{D\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} as the paired release-demo path
\item
  classify landing-art shell presets as explicit single-mode choices instead of implying that they support a dark/light toggle
\item
  make unsupported theme-mode toggles visible through shell feedback
\item
  prove dark-to-light and light-to-dark toggles deterministically
\end{itemize}

This cycle is about honest mode coverage, not a broad Theme Lab or palette redesign.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-120-sponsored-human}

A DOGFOOD user wants to switch between dark and light modes during a demo and understand why some gallery themes do not toggle. Pressing the inherited AppShell shortcut should either switch the active paired theme or clearly say that the selected theme has no alternate mode.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-120-sponsored-agent}

An agent needs machine-readable evidence for first-party theme coverage. It should be able to inspect the DOGFOOD shell theme list, classify each choice, and assert that unsupported mode switches do not silently no-op.

\section{Hill}\label{record-120-hill}

After this cycle, DOGFOOD's theme path tells the truth: paired themes have dark/light behavior, single-mode themes are classified as single-mode in deterministic shell-spec coverage, and the AppShell mode toggle gives deterministic feedback in both supported and unsupported paths.

\section{Problem}\label{record-120-problem}

Issue \#343 came from the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release-video rehearsal. DOGFOOD exposed theme and mode concepts, then listed several first-party themes without a coherent mode story. That made \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T} look unreliable: it works for the mode-aware DOGFOOD family, but single concrete themes cannot toggle and the user receives no explanation.

The current implementation already has an AppShell-level \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T} command for mode-aware shell theme families. The gap is coverage and honesty around the full DOGFOOD theme inventory.

\section{Scope}\label{record-120-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add first-party shell theme coverage that distinguishes paired families from single-mode concrete themes.
\item
  Do not touch the DOGFOOD app rendering file for visible Theme Lab inventory until its existing raw-string debt is cleaned under the touched-file localization policy.
\item
  Keep the DOGFOOD family as the paired first-party dark/light shell path.
\item
  Keep landing-art shell presets single-mode unless a real light/dark pair is intentionally designed for a given preset.
\item
  Make \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T} on a single-mode theme publish an explicit shell notification instead of silently doing nothing.
\item
  Add deterministic AppShell tests for supported dark-to-light and light-to-dark switching and for unsupported single-mode feedback.
\item
  Add DOGFOOD tests that prove the shell-spec inventory lists paired and single-mode coverage.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-120-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Do not redesign Theme Lab or Theme Inspector.
\item
  Do not create speculative light variants for landing-art palettes.
\item
  Do not change the release-title/landing-art rendering palette.
\item
  Do not add a global theme registry outside the existing AppShell shellThemes contract.
\item
  Do not move Theme Lab provenance, pointer inspection, or full operator surfaces out of the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} horizon.
\end{itemize}

\section{User Experience Contract}\label{record-120-user-experience-contract}

\texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T} is inherited by apps that expose mode-aware shell themes. When the active shell choice belongs to a family with multiple modes, \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T} switches to a sibling mode and posts the existing ``Shell theme set to \ldots{}'' feedback.

When the active shell choice is a concrete single-mode theme, \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T} posts a short settings notification that names the active theme and says it has no alternate mode. The active theme remains unchanged.

The shell spec and settings surfaces must prove:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the active default dark and light presets
\item
  a shell inventory where each first-party choice is classified as \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d} or \texttt{s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e}
\item
  enough concrete labels that users can tell which entries respond to \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T}
\end{itemize}

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-120-lower-modes}

\subsection{Static Mode}\label{record-120-static-mode}

Static tests should assert the same inventory classification from shell specs without requiring screenshot or ANSI scraping.

\subsection{Pipe Mode}\label{record-120-pipe-mode}

No new pipe contract is introduced. The shell theme inventory is diagnostic copy, not an exported data format.

\subsection{Accessible Mode}\label{record-120-accessible-mode}

Mode support must be textual. The user should not need color, swatches, or visual grouping alone to understand whether a theme supports the mode toggle.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-120-localization-directionality-posture}

New user-facing strings should use the existing DOGFOOD or AppShell i18n ports. The tests may assert English source copy, but the source strings must be catalog-discoverable so the localization gates can track them.

Directionality is unchanged. Future visible inventory copy should flow through the current shell layout after the touched DOGFOOD app file is localization clean.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-120-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

Agents should be able to inspect:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  raw DOGFOOD shell theme specs and their mode support
\item
  resolved AppShell theme choices and their \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}d} facts
\item
  shell-spec classification for paired and single-mode choices
\item
  runtime notifications after supported and unsupported \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T} paths
\end{itemize}

The proof should not require screenshots or terminal color sampling.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-120-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Visible controls are a promise: a mode toggle must either work or explain why it cannot.
\item
  Docs are the demo: once the DOGFOOD app rendering file is localization-clean, Theme Lab should explain the actual first-party theme inventory users can select.
\item
  Shell owns shell concerns: mode switching remains AppShell behavior inherited by DOGFOOD and other apps through \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p}.
\item
  Tests are the spec: paired and unsupported paths need deterministic coverage.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Plan}\label{record-120-implementation-plan}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add first-party shell theme support coverage for tests.
\item
  Keep visible Theme Lab inventory out of this cycle until the touched DOGFOOD app file is localization-clean.
\item
  Add AppShell feedback for unsupported mode toggles on single-mode concrete themes.
\item
  Add tests that fail before the implementation:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    DOGFOOD shell specs list \texttt{D\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D} as paired dark/light.
  \item
    DOGFOOD shell specs list landing-art shell presets as single-mode.
  \item
    AppShell toggles paired themes dark -\textgreater{} light -\textgreater{} dark.
  \item
    AppShell \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T} on a single-mode theme leaves the id unchanged and posts explicit feedback.
  \end{itemize}
\item
  Update \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, run focused tests, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}, and \texttt{g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-120-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} for DOGFOOD shell inventory.
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} coverage for supported dark-to-light and light-to-dark \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T} switching.
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} coverage for unsupported single-mode \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T} feedback.
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} coverage for the command-palette theme-mode action.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-120-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Every DOGFOOD first-party shell theme is classified as paired or single-mode.
\item
  DOGFOOD shell-spec coverage proves the first-party theme inventory with mode-support labels.
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T} toggles the paired DOGFOOD family in both directions.
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}T} on a single-mode theme posts explicit feedback instead of silently doing nothing.
\item
  Deterministic coverage proves at least one dark-to-light and one light-to-dark switch path.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} records the theme variant coverage repair.
\item
  Issue \#343 is closed by the implementation PR.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-120-retrospective}

To be completed when the PR lands.

\chapter{DL-019 - Theme Rule Selection And Inspection}\label{record-121}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DL-019-theme-rule-selection-and-inspection.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-121-decision-summary}

Bijou should adopt the strongest ideas from reactive design-token systems without importing an incompatible dependency or replacing the existing runtime theme contract.

The runtime truth remains:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Theme
  -> ResolvedTheme
    -> TokenGraph
      -> ThemeAccessors
        -> terminal cells, lower modes, and DTCG interop
\end{CodeBlock}

This cycle adds a Bijou-native rule layer for theme authoring and inspection:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  selector rules such as best contrast, minimum contrast, most vivid, least vivid, closest color, and ordered choice
\item
  explicit candidate exclusions for reserved roles such as success and error
\item
  structured inspection facts explaining why a rule chose a token
\item
  dependency facts that Theme Inspector and tests can consume later
\item
  compiled output that remains a normal Bijou \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} or token graph entry
\end{itemize}

No \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k} runtime, dev, peer, optional, or generated dependency is added. The external package is useful prior art, but its license and general CSS surface do not belong in Bijou's Apache-2.0 zero-dependency core.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-121-sponsored-human}

A Bijou theme author wants to tune primitive palettes while keeping semantic roles stable. They should be able to say ``choose readable text for this surface'' or ``choose a vivid accent that is not success or error'' instead of manually maintaining every derived hex value.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-121-sponsored-agent}

An agent auditing theme behavior wants deterministic facts for rule inputs, candidate rejection, selected values, dependencies, and contrast proof so it can explain a theme without sampling screenshots or guessing from final RGB values.

\section{Hill}\label{record-121-hill}

A Bijou theme author can define semantic theme roles through pure selector rules, replay the product questions below with tests, compile the rules into the existing theme/token graph contract, and inspect which candidates were considered, rejected, and selected.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-121-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Can a semantic foreground choose a readable color from a primitive palette without hard-coding the final hex value?
\item
  Can a vivid accent selector exclude reserved success and error roles while still proving contrast against its surface?
\item
  Can \texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} explain every candidate read by a rule, including selected, eligible, excluded, invalid, and contrast-failed candidates?
\item
  Can malformed rule inputs fail with the missing target, scope, candidate, or exclusion path instead of silently choosing a surprising color?
\item
  Can the rule layer preserve existing \texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} behavior for callers that only need a resolved \texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e}?
\end{itemize}

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-121-current-truth}

Bijou already has:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a public \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} contract with \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}, \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i}, \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s}, and \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t} token families
\item
  a \texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h} with references, light/dark definitions, transforms, cache invalidation, and subscribers
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for mode-aware token themes
\item
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for token document interop
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} for concrete contrast checks
\item
  DOGFOOD Theme Lab and Theme Inspector surfaces for concrete token facts
\end{itemize}

The missing piece is rule provenance. Today a derived token can be encoded as a manual hex, a direct reference, or a transform. It cannot yet say:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  choose the highest-contrast color from this palette
\item
  choose the first color that reaches a contrast floor
\item
  choose the most vivid color that is still readable
\item
  exclude reserved role tokens from an accent search
\item
  explain which candidates failed and why
\end{itemize}

\section{Problem}\label{record-121-problem}

Manual semantic token maintenance creates drift:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a primitive palette can change while semantic foregrounds stay stale
\item
  a vivid accent may accidentally reuse a destructive or success role
\item
  contrast proof happens after values are chosen instead of during selection
\item
  Theme Inspector can show final values but not why those values won
\item
  tests can assert concrete hex values but not the decision rule behind them
\end{itemize}

The answer is not to replace Bijou's runtime theme model. The runtime model already encodes terminal-specific facts: \texttt{N\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R}, foreground/background tokens, text modifiers, RGB caches, ANSI downsampling, lower-mode behavior, and safe-pair checks.

\section{Scope}\label{record-121-scope}

This cycle adds pure core support for rule-based color selection and inspection.

Included:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  color candidate scopes represented as token paths or explicit color values
\item
  selector functions for contrast, vividness, closeness, ordered position, and minimum contrast
\item
  explicit \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t} exclusions by token path
\item
  selector result facts with candidate pass/fail reasons
\item
  dependency extraction for references and candidate scopes
\item
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h} support for rule definitions if that can land without breaking existing callers
\item
  focused tests for selection, exclusion, dependency, and cycle behavior
\item
  design-system docs and changelog notes
\end{itemize}

Out of scope:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  no external \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k} package integration
\item
  no CSS renderer
\item
  no typography, spacing, motion, or duration token categories
\item
  no Figma adapter
\item
  no Theme Lab redesign in this slice
\item
  no element-level renderer provenance
\item
  no app-frame theme-mode UX changes
\end{itemize}

\section{API Direction}\label{record-121-api-direction}

The first public API should be small and structural. Exact names can move in implementation, but the shape should stay close to this:

\begin{CodeBlock}
const graph = createTokenGraph({
  palette: {
    ink: "#0b1020",
    paper: "#f8fafc",
    cyan: "#38bdf8",
    green: "#22c55e",
    red: "#ef4444",
  },
  surface: {
    primary: { fg: "#f8fafc", bg: { ref: "palette.ink" } },
  },
  semantic: {
    primary: bestContrastWith(
      { ref: "surface.primary.bg" }, // token background slot
      scope("palette"),
    ),
    accent: mostVivid(scope("palette"), {
      against: { ref: "surface.primary.bg" },
      minContrast: 4.5,
      not: ["palette.green", "palette.red"],
    }),
  },
});
\end{CodeBlock}

If the fluent helper API is too large for the first slice, the serialized graph definition may use plain discriminated data instead:

\begin{CodeBlock}
semantic: {
  primary: {
    rule: "best-contrast-with",
    target: { ref: "surface.primary.bg" },
    candidates: { kind: "scope", path: "palette" },
  },
}
\end{CodeBlock}

Slot-path references ending in \texttt{.\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g} are part of this cycle's contract. A reference such as \texttt{\{\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\}} resolves the background color of the \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y} token while \texttt{\{\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\}} keeps the existing foreground-reference behavior.

The graph should expose inspection facts separately from resolved values:

\begin{CodeBlock}
const fact = graph.inspect("semantic.accent", "dark");
\end{CodeBlock}

The returned fact should be structured enough for tests and future Theme Inspector rows:

\begin{CodeBlock}
semantic.accent
  rule: most-vivid
  selected: palette.cyan (#38bdf8)
  dependencies: surface.primary.bg, palette.ink, palette.paper, palette.cyan,
    palette.green, palette.red
  rejected:
    palette.paper - eligible, not selected
    palette.green - excluded
    palette.red - excluded
    palette.ink - contrast below 4.5
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Selector Vocabulary}\label{record-121-selector-vocabulary}

The initial selector vocabulary should cover the high-value color decisions. Selectors that compare against a target put the target first. Selectors that rank only a candidate collection put the collection first.

\texttt{b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})} chooses the candidate with the highest contrast ratio against the target. Equal scores keep candidate order.

\texttt{m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\}\allowbreak{})} chooses the first candidate that clears the requested contrast ratio, using deterministic candidate order.

\texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})} chooses the highest-chroma candidate, with optional \texttt{a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}, and \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t} constraints. First-slice chroma is the deterministic RGB channel spread: \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{})}. If \texttt{m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t} is present, \texttt{a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t} is required.

\texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})} chooses the lowest-chroma candidate, with the same optional constraints and the same \texttt{m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t} rule.

\texttt{c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})} chooses the closest candidate to a target color. The first slice uses squared RGB distance and keeps candidate order for equal distances.

\texttt{n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{})} chooses a candidate by ordered position. Integer indices use array-style ordering, negative integers count from the end, and out-of-range integers clamp to the nearest valid candidate. Fractional indices clamp to \texttt{0} through \texttt{1} and use \texttt{r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{})}.

\section{Runtime Contract}\label{record-121-runtime-contract}

Selectors are pure. They do not read process state, filesystem data, terminal facts, or clocks.

Selector helpers return plain \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} data. The token graph evaluates that intermediate rule definition, and the existing \texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} path still returns a resolved \texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e}.

Rule failures are deterministic:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  missing target, explicit candidate, candidate-scope, and exclusion paths throw with the missing path
\item
  vividness selectors throw when \texttt{m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t} is set without \texttt{a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}
\item
  no minimum-contrast candidate throws unless the selector defines an explicit fallback
\item
  cycles remain cycle errors
\end{itemize}

Inspection dependencies include target and \texttt{a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t} references plus every candidate path read from explicit candidate lists or scopes, whether the candidate was selected, eligible-but-not-selected, excluded, invalid, or below the contrast floor.

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-121-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

Selector rules improve color quality, but they do not make color sufficient as the only meaning carrier. The same graceful-lowering rule applies:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  no-color output must keep text, symbols, or structure
\item
  pipe output must not depend on swatches
\item
  accessible output must name state and intent
\end{itemize}

Contrast-aware selection is proof that a chosen color is readable when color is available. It is not proof that the UI is accessible by itself.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-121-localization-and-directionality-posture}

No user-facing localized copy is required for the core rule primitives. Rule ids, token paths, candidate paths, and inspection facts are developer-facing identifiers.

Future DOGFOOD Theme Inspector prose that explains rule facts must flow through the DOGFOOD localization catalog. Token paths remain stable identifiers and are not localized.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-121-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

Inspection facts are a first-class product requirement. An agent should be able to assert:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  which selector rule resolved a token
\item
  which references and candidate scopes the rule read
\item
  which candidate won
\item
  which candidates were rejected
\item
  whether a candidate failed contrast, was excluded, or was the wrong type
\item
  which downstream token paths depend on the resolved token
\end{itemize}

These facts should not require terminal rendering, screenshot analysis, or RGB equality guessing.

\begin{itemize}
