\item
  \texttt{m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} rejects candidates below the minimum ratio and selects the first passing candidate.
\item
  \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} respects \texttt{a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}, and \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t} exclusions.
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} chooses the muted readable candidate.
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} are deterministic.
\item
  selector definitions participate in graph dependency inspection.
\item
  circular selector references still fail deterministically.
\item
  existing graph reference and transform tests keep passing.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-121-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Bijou has no dependency on \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k}.
\item
  Theme selectors are pure core functions.
\item
  Token graph rule definitions resolve to existing \texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e} objects.
\item
  Inspection facts explain selected and rejected candidates.
\item
  Exclusions by token path prevent reserved roles from winning accent rules.
\item
  The new API exports from \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u}.
\item
  Design-system docs show the primitive -\textgreater{} semantic rule -\textgreater{} UI token workflow.
\item
  Local validation includes focused theme tests, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}.
\item
  Code Dojo debt remains verifiable through \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}t} and \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}y}; this cycle does not claim the repo goalpost unless that aggregate report reaches \texttt{1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2} or lower.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-121-retrospective}

To be completed when the cycle lands.

\chapter{DL-020 - Dogfood Rule-Authored First-Party Themes}\label{record-122}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DL-020-dogfood-rule-authored-first-party-themes.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
id: DL-020
title: Dogfood Rule-Authored First-Party Themes
status: active
lane: cool-ideas
priority: medium
github_issue: 446
legend: DL

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DL-design-language.md}{DL - Design Language}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-122-decision-summary}

DL-019 added Bijou-native theme selector rules and inspection facts. This cycle uses that system inside Bijou's own first-party defaults instead of keeping the new rule layer as a demo-only API.

The public runtime contract remains unchanged:

\begin{CodeBlock}
rule-authored preset definitions
  -> TokenGraph
    -> concrete Theme
      -> ResolvedTheme
        -> terminal rendering, DTCG interop, and inspectors
\end{CodeBlock}

No external design-token dependency is introduced. The work is a narrow dogfood pass over Bijou-owned themes only.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-122-sponsored-human}

A Bijou theme maintainer wants to adjust primitive palette choices and trust the system to derive readable semantic roles, accents, borders, and UI affordances without manually copying final hex values across every token family.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-122-sponsored-agent}

An agent auditing first-party themes wants deterministic provenance facts for why default theme tokens were selected, so it can review rule behavior instead of reverse-engineering intent from literal hex equality.

\section{Hill}\label{record-122-hill}

\texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} are authored from primitive palette definitions plus selector rules, materialize to the existing \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} shape, and expose rule inspection facts that explain their first-party semantic choices.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-122-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Can Bijou-owned defaults use selector rules while preserving the public \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} object shape and registry keys?
\item
  Can tests prove first-party semantic choices through \texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} rather than only final hex assertions?
\item
  Can DTCG round trips, resolver behavior, RGB caches, and gradient consumers keep working with compiled rule-authored presets?
\item
  Can third-party and legacy themes stay literal compatibility fixtures in this slice?
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope}\label{record-122-scope}

Included:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a small first-party preset authoring layer that compiles token graph definitions into \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e}
\item
  rule-authored \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t}
\item
  tests for compiled values, registry identity, and rule inspection provenance
\item
  docs/changelog updates that make dogfooding explicit
\end{itemize}

Out of scope:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  external \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k} integration
\item
  public breaking changes to \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e}
\item
  rewriting \texttt{c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a}, \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}k}, \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d}, or \texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n}
\item
  Theme Lab UI redesign
\end{itemize}

\section{Runtime Contract}\label{record-122-runtime-contract}

Preset compilation must be pure and deterministic. It cannot read process state, terminal facts, filesystem data, clocks, or network data.

The compiled object remains a normal \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e}. Existing consumers can continue to read \texttt{t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x}, \texttt{t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s}, \texttt{t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}, and surface tokens without knowing how first-party themes were authored.

The preset authoring layer records the original rule definitions against the compiled \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} identity. \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} uses those definitions when present, so \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h} remains rule-authored for first-party presets. Cloned themes and DTCG imports fall back to concrete token graphs.

Tests may assert rule ids, selected candidate paths, dependencies, and selected hex values from the same resolved graph inspectors consume.

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-122-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

This slice improves color choice but does not make color the only carrier of meaning. Existing labels, text structure, \texttt{N\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R} behavior, and lower-mode rendering remain the accessibility contract.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-122-localization-and-directionality-posture}

This slice does not add DOGFOOD user-facing copy. Rule ids, token paths, design document prose, and changelog entries are developer-facing documentation and stable identifiers. Future DOGFOOD UI that renders these facts must use the localization catalog.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-122-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

The primary agent-facing value is provenance. An audit should be able to inspect \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t} and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t}, see the selector rule, enumerate candidates, and explain exclusions without comparing screenshots or final hex equality.

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-122-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add a small preset compiler that materializes graph definitions into \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  Move \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k} and \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} into rule-authored preset modules.
\item
  Preserve first-party rule definitions through \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Keep literal legacy and third-party presets unchanged.
\item
  Update docs and changelog after the tests prove the behavior.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-122-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a red provenance test showing literal defaults expose \texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n} inspection instead of \texttt{r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}
\item
  a dark-theme accent test proving \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d} selects \texttt{b\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}
\item
  a light-theme primary text test proving \texttt{m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h} selects \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}
\item
  existing preset and DTCG tests proving resolved values stay compatible
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective / Closeout Notes}\label{record-122-retrospective-closeout-notes}

Close this cycle when CI is green, CodeRabbit is green, review threads are resolved, and the PR summary records the rule probe values.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-122-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/runtime-truth-wins.md}{Runtime Truth Wins}: compiled presets and inspection facts come from executing the graph.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are the Spec}: dogfood behavior lands through deterministic tests.
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/docs-are-the-demo.md}{Docs Are the Demo}: the docs record that Bijou's defaults use the system they document.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{DL-021 - Dogfood Theme Token Usage Proof}\label{record-123}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DL-021-dogfood-theme-token-usage-proof.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
id: DL-021
title: Dogfood Theme Token Usage Proof
status: active
lane: asap
priority: high
github_issue: 448
legend: DL

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DL-design-language.md}{DL - Design Language}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-123-decision-summary}

DL-019 and DL-020 made theme rule provenance real, but DOGFOOD still has to make that truth visible. The Theme Inspector must not look like an unthemed debug drawer that merely lists colors. It should prove which active theme tokens are powering the docs shell and keep its own chrome readable in light and dark shells.

The runtime truth remains the existing DOGFOOD docs shell:

\begin{CodeBlock}
active docs shell theme
  -> docs visual theme
    -> docs chrome tokens
      -> terminal cells and Theme Inspector usage proof
\end{CodeBlock}

No external design-token integration is added. This is a narrow DOGFOOD usage pass over the inspector and its immediate theme proof surface.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-123-sponsored-human}

A DOGFOOD reader comparing dark and light themes wants to see the active theme affect the app they are looking at, not just a detached list of hex values.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-123-sponsored-agent}

An agent auditing theme behavior wants deterministic rendered evidence that the inspector chrome, summary copy, usage rows, palette labels, and scroll chrome all come from active DOGFOOD theme tokens.

\section{Hill}\label{record-123-hill}

The Theme Inspector renders readable themed chrome in DOGFOOD dark and light shells, shows a live usage proof for DOGFOOD docs surfaces, and keeps the full palette as reference data rather than implying every reference color is already visible in the surrounding app.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-123-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does the inspector border, background, title, summary, and close hint use active docs theme tokens instead of fallback styling?
\item
  Does light mode preserve readable foreground/background contrast inside the inspector summary and usage proof?
\item
  Can the inspector show both the active shell palette and the specific DOGFOOD docs tokens currently used by the app?
\item
  Can tests fail if the inspector regresses to unstyled summary copy or loses the usage proof?
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope}\label{record-123-scope}

Included:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  theme the Theme Inspector drawer chrome through the active docs visual theme
\item
  add a compact DOGFOOD usage proof section before the reference palette
\item
  style inspector summary and palette chrome with explicit theme tokens
\item
  add focused DOGFOOD preview tests for light-mode readability and usage proof
\item
  update changelog and localization catalogs for new visible copy
\end{itemize}

Out of scope:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  replacing the theme engine
\item
  adding a design-book dependency
\item
  restyling every DOGFOOD docs pane in this slice
\item
  changing third-party theme presets
\item
  adding element-level provenance for every rendered cell
\end{itemize}

\section{Runtime Contract}\label{record-123-runtime-contract}

The usage proof is derived from the same active shell theme id that drives the docs page. It must not maintain an independent color table. If the active shell theme changes, the inspector summary, usage proof, reference palette labels, drawer border, surface, and scrollbar update from that same model state.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-123-localization-and-directionality-posture}

All new visible DOGFOOD copy is catalog-backed and participates in the existing DOGFOOD i18n completeness, check, and debt gates.

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-123-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a light-theme inspector regression that proves the active summary and close hint are styled with readable foreground/background cells
\item
  a usage-proof regression that proves the inspector renders live DOGFOOD docs token rows instead of only the reference palette
\end{itemize}

\section{Closeout Notes}\label{record-123-closeout-notes}

Close this cycle when local DOGFOOD preview tests, DOGFOOD i18n gates, lint, and relevant Code Dojo checks are green, and the PR summary names the before/after behavior from the screenshots.

\chapter{DL-022 - Theme Lab Editor Graph UX}\label{record-124}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/DL-022-theme-lab-editor-graph-ux.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
id: DL-022
title: Theme Lab Editor Graph UX
status: active
lane: asap
priority: high
github_issue: 450
legend: DL

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/DL-design-language.md}{DL - Design Language}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-124-decision-summary}

DL-019 and DL-020 made theme rule provenance inspectable, and DL-021 made the DOGFOOD Theme Inspector prove that its chrome consumes active theme tokens. The Theme Lab still reads like a static reference page. This cycle turns it into a bounded editor surface with visible controls and a live token graph that updates from the same in-memory draft theme when a color changes.

The runtime truth for this slice is:

\begin{CodeBlock}
active DOGFOOD shell theme
  -> editable DOGFOOD-local draft
    -> selected editable color slot
      -> derived theme token rows
        -> live token relationship graph
\end{CodeBlock}

No external design-token package or design-book dependency is added. The useful idea is the relationship graph and immediate feedback loop, implemented through Bijou's existing theme and terminal surface contracts.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-124-sponsored-human}

A DOGFOOD user opening \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} wants something that behaves like an editor, not a read-only list. They need a focused color row, obvious keyboard controls, a current hex value, and a graph that changes when the color changes.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-124-sponsored-agent}

An agent auditing theme behavior needs deterministic model functions and scripted preview tests that prove a color edit updates the editor state, rendered token values, and graph rows in the same frame.

\section{Hill}\label{record-124-hill}

Theme Lab exposes a first editing pass for active DOGFOOD theme colors. A user can move between editable colors, nudge RGB channels, reset the draft, and see a live graph of token relationships and changed colors without leaving the docs shell.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-124-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does the Theme Lab show editing affordances rather than only static swatches?
\item
  Can the selected editable row move deterministically with keyboard input?
\item
  Does changing a channel update the selected hex value and the rendered token graph in the same frame?
\item
  Does reset restore the draft graph to the active theme values?
\item
  Are all new visible labels catalog-backed?
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope}\label{record-124-scope}

Included:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a DOGFOOD-local theme draft model that clones the active shell theme
\item
  editable rows for a bounded set of high-signal tokens
\item
  deterministic key handling for selection, channel choice, nudging, and reset
\item
  a live graph renderer that shows token nodes, dependency edges, and edited nodes from the current draft
\item
  deterministic invalid-input handling: RGB channel nudges clamp to \texttt{0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}5}, unsupported keys are ignored, and this first pass exposes no free-form hex parser that could accept malformed color text
\item
  focused preview tests for editing state and graph updates
\item
  changelog and DOGFOOD i18n catalog updates
\end{itemize}

Out of scope:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  saving custom themes to disk
\item
  mutating exported preset constants
\item
  importing or integrating design-book
\item
  mouse or pointer editing
\item
  full authoring for every third-party preset
\item
  replacing \texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h}, \texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e}, or the existing DOGFOOD shell theme model
\end{itemize}

\section{Runtime Contract}\label{record-124-runtime-contract}

The editor state is owned by the DOGFOOD docs model. It is not a global theme registry and it does not mutate \texttt{B\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}J\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}K}, \texttt{B\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}J\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}T}, or shell theme constants.

The renderer must consume one draft object for all Theme Lab editor output:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  editor row swatches
\item
  selected color hex
\item
  channel values
\item
  graph nodes
\item
  graph edges
\item
  palette preview rows
\end{itemize}

If a color changes, the graph changes because it is projected from the draft theme, not because the graph keeps its own color cache.

This slice does not feed the draft into \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h} or replace the runtime \texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h} exposed by \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t}. The docs shell still observes the active runtime theme through the normal context path, while Theme Lab builds a local presentation graph from the unsaved draft. That keeps third-party \texttt{o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} guidance intact: unsaved editor previews are local to Theme Lab, and any future persisted theme must re-enter the canonical context and token-graph path.

\section{Editable Slots}\label{record-124-editable-slots}

The first pass edits a deliberately small set of active DOGFOOD runtime tokens:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g}
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}g}
\item
  \texttt{b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}
\item
  \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r}
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r}
\end{itemize}

Those slots are enough to prove text, surface, border, cursor, and status feedback without pretending this is a full theme persistence product.

\section{Graph Shape}\label{record-124-graph-shape}

The graph is textual and terminal-native. It should show:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  token path
\item
  current hex or foreground/background pair
\item
  edited marker when the draft differs from the active theme
\item
  dependency-style edges for major families, such as:
\end{itemize}

\begin{CodeBlock}
semantic.accent #7aa7e8 *
  -> border.secondary
  -> ui.cursor
  -> ui.focusGutter
surface.primary.bg #171827
  -> surface.primary
  -> ui.focusGutter.bg
\end{CodeBlock}

\texttt{A\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}B} means the preview treats \texttt{B} as a consumer or dependent of editable source \texttt{A}. It does not mean runtime derivation has been committed to \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h}.

The graph is not renderer provenance. It explains theme-token relationships and draft changes only.

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-124-lower-modes}

Swatches are optional visual assistance. The selected row, current hex, RGB channels, edited marker, graph node names, and graph edge labels remain visible as text.

\section{Localization Posture}\label{record-124-localization-posture}

All new Theme Lab labels, control hints, and graph section headings are DOGFOOD catalog keys in every supported runtime locale. Token paths and hex values are developer identifiers and are not localized. English \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t} fallbacks are permitted as developer scaffolding and runtime resilience only; generated catalog entries for the new keys must still exist before merge.

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-124-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a pure editor-model test proving selection, channel nudge, and reset behavior
\item
  a graph projection test proving an edited token is marked and carries the new hex value
\item
  a same-frame coherence test proving a channel nudge updates the selected hex and the rendered graph node from the same draft state
\item
  a DOGFOOD preview test proving Theme Lab renders editor controls and the live graph after scripted key input
\end{itemize}

\section{Closeout Notes}\label{record-124-closeout-notes}

Close this cycle when the focused Theme Lab tests, DOGFOOD i18n gates, Code Dojo changed-file gates, lint, and relevant preview checks are green. The PR summary should explicitly name the before/after behavior: static reference page to editable color lab with live graph feedback.

\part{Localization}

\chapter{LX-001 --- bijou-i18n Runtime Package}\label{record-125}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/LX-001-bijou-i18n-runtime-package.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/LX-localization-and-bidirectionality.md}{LX --- Localization and Bidirectionality}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-125-why-this-cycle-exists}

Bijou now has doctrine for localization and bidirectionality, but no runtime package boundary that applications or shell surfaces can actually consume.

If we want \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n} to be a real localization tool, the first step is not spreadsheets.

The first step is a clean, in-memory runtime package.

This cycle intentionally narrows scope to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n}
\item
  runtime catalogs
\item
  locale and direction
\item
  runtime-safe lookup and references
\item
  formatting seams
\end{itemize}

It does \textbf{not} try to ship spreadsheet workflows yet.

\section{Human users}\label{record-125-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-125-primary-human-user}

A builder who wants to localize Bijou shell or app content without inventing their own ad hoc runtime i18n substrate.

They are asking:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  where does locale live?
\item
  where does direction live?
\item
  how do I register catalogs?
\item
  how do I look up a message or resource?
\item
  how do I do this without filesystem or service assumptions?
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-125-human-hill}

A builder can install and use a real \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n} runtime package entirely in memory, with a clean catalog model and no spreadsheet baggage.

\section{Agent users}\label{record-125-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-125-primary-agent-user}

An agent that needs to inspect or generate localized UI against explicit runtime contracts instead of hidden string tables.

They are asking:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  what is the active locale?
\item
  what is the active direction?
\item
  what keys and namespaces exist?
\item
  how do references resolve?
\item
  what happens when a translation is missing?
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-125-agent-hill}

An agent can reason about localized runtime content through explicit catalog, locale, direction, and lookup APIs instead of implicit English defaults.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-125-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder installs \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n}.
\item
  They create an in-memory catalog with namespaced keys.
\item
  They load the catalog into a runtime.
\item
  They resolve messages and resources by key.
\item
  They switch locale and observe fallback behavior.
\item
  They read direction from the same runtime without inventing a second seam.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Agent playback}\label{record-125-agent-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent inspects the runtime package API.
\item
  It can enumerate or at least reason about namespaces, ids, locale, and direction.
\item
  It resolves a message key with interpolation values.
\item
  It resolves a resource/data key.
\item
  It observes missing-translation fallback and explicit missing-key behavior.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Linked invariants}\label{record-125-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are the Spec}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/graceful-lowering-preserves-meaning.md}{Graceful Lowering Preserves Meaning}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/docs-are-the-demo.md}{Docs Are the Demo}
\end{itemize}

\section{Invariants for this cycle}\label{record-125-invariants-for-this-cycle}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  runtime package must work entirely in memory
\item
  runtime package must not assume spreadsheets, files, services, or persistence
\item
  runtime package must expose direction as first-class metadata
\item
  runtime package must be string-first but not string-only
\item
  runtime package must support runtime-safe references without becoming a spreadsheet interpreter
\end{itemize}

\section{Deliverable}\label{record-125-deliverable}

Introduce a new package:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n}
\end{itemize}

With a minimal but real runtime surface:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  catalog types
\item
  key types
\item
  locale direction types
\item
  in-memory runtime / adapter
\item
  message lookup
\item
  generic resource lookup
\item
  fallback behavior
\item
  formatter hooks or default formatters
\end{itemize}

\section{Proposed API direction}\label{record-125-proposed-api-direction}

The exact names can still evolve, but the first slice should be close to:

\begin{CodeBlock}
type LocaleDirection = 'ltr' | 'rtl' | 'auto';

interface CatalogKey {
  readonly namespace: string;
  readonly id: string;
}

type CatalogEntryKind = 'message' | 'resource' | 'data';

interface I18nCatalogEntry<T = unknown> {
  readonly key: CatalogKey;
  readonly kind: CatalogEntryKind;
  readonly sourceLocale: string;
  readonly values: Readonly<Record<string, T>>;
  readonly fallbackValue?: T;
}

interface I18nRuntime {
  readonly locale: string;
  readonly direction: LocaleDirection;
  loadCatalog(catalog: I18nCatalog): void;
  unloadCatalog(namespace: string): void;
  t(key: CatalogKey, values?: Record<string, unknown>): string;
  resource<T = unknown>(key: CatalogKey): T | undefined;
}
\end{CodeBlock}

The first slice does not need every possible authoring feature. It does need a clean runtime shape.

\section{Tests to write first}\label{record-125-tests-to-write-first}

\subsection{Cycle-owned playback tests}\label{record-125-cycle-owned-playback-tests}

Under \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  package exists and can be imported
\item
  in-memory catalogs can be loaded and unloaded
\item
  messages resolve by namespaced key
\item
  missing locale values fall back to source locale
\item
  runtime exposes locale and direction together
\item
  resource lookup supports non-string values
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Package-local unit tests}\label{record-125-package-local-unit-tests}

Under \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  missing-key behavior is explicit
\item
  namespace unload removes lookups cleanly
\item
  interpolation works for simple scalar values
\item
  runtime-safe references resolve or fail clearly
\end{itemize}

\section{Risks}\label{record-125-risks}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  over-designing the runtime around tooling concerns too early
\item
  under-designing the runtime into string-only helpers
\item
  leaking layout or UI overflow policy into the i18n package
\item
  trying to implement tooling and runtime together in one cycle
\end{itemize}

\section{Out of scope}\label{record-125-out-of-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  spreadsheet import/export
\item
  stale detection
\item
  pseudo-localization
\item
  RTL shell mirroring implementation
\item
  shell integration beyond light proving imports
\end{itemize}

\chapter{LX-002 --- bijou-i18n Tools Package}\label{record-126}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/LX-002-bijou-i18n-tools-package.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/LX-localization-and-bidirectionality.md}{LX --- Localization and Bidirectionality}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-126-why-this-cycle-exists}

LX-001 deliberately shipped only the runtime half of localization:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  in-memory catalogs
\item
  locale and direction
\item
  message/resource lookup
\item
  runtime-safe references
\end{itemize}

That was the right first move, but a real localization system also needs workflow tooling.

This cycle exists to build the first real \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s} package.

It should give Bijou a provider-neutral authoring and translation workflow surface without dragging spreadsheets or files into the runtime package.

\section{Scope of this cycle}\label{record-126-scope-of-this-cycle}

This first tooling slice intentionally narrows scope to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  authoring catalog types
\item
  source hashing
\item
  stale translation detection
\item
  provider-neutral tabular export/import rows
\item
  reference validation and normalization
\item
  compilation into runtime catalogs
\item
  pseudo-localization helper
\end{itemize}

It does \textbf{not} include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Google Sheets integration
\item
  Excel integration
\item
  CSV file parsing
\item
  filesystem adapters
\item
  remote catalog publishing
\end{itemize}

Those can come later if justified.

\section{Human users}\label{record-126-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-126-primary-human-user}

A builder or localization maintainer who needs to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  track changed source strings
\item
  export only missing/stale work
\item
  import translated rows cleanly
\item
  validate references before runtime
\item
  compile authoring catalogs into runtime catalogs
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-126-human-hill}

A builder can manage localization workflow data entirely in memory through one clean tooling package, without having to invent stale detection or spreadsheet row formats from scratch.

\section{Agent users}\label{record-126-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-126-primary-agent-user}

An agent helping maintain localization catalogs and workflow data.

They need to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  detect stale translations
\item
  understand which rows need work
\item
  import reviewed rows safely
\item
  validate references before shipping
\item
  generate pseudo-localized stress content for layout review
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-126-agent-hill}

An agent can reason about localization workflow state explicitly through authoring catalogs and tabular rows, instead of diffing arbitrary JSON blobs or hidden spreadsheets.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-126-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder has authoring catalogs in memory.
\item
  They change an English source string.
\item
  The tooling marks affected translations stale automatically.
\item
  They export only missing/stale rows into a generic tabular shape.
\item
  They import completed rows back in.
\item
  They compile the result into runtime catalogs.
\item
  They load those runtime catalogs into \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n}.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Agent playback}\label{record-126-agent-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent reads authoring catalogs.
\item
  It identifies stale or missing translations by source hash.
\item
  It exports review rows for a target locale.
\item
  It imports updated rows.
\item
  It validates references and catches broken/cyclic ones before runtime.
\item
  It generates pseudo-localized output to stress UI copy.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Linked invariants}\label{record-126-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are the Spec}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/graceful-lowering-preserves-meaning.md}{Graceful Lowering Preserves Meaning}

  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/docs-are-the-demo.md}{Docs Are the Demo}
\end{itemize}

\section{Invariants for this cycle}\label{record-126-invariants-for-this-cycle}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  tooling must stay separate from the runtime package
\item
  tabular workflow support must be provider-neutral
\item
  stale detection must be automatic, not manual bookkeeping
\item
  reference-heavy catalogs must fail clearly before runtime
\item
  pseudo-localization is a tooling concern, not a runtime concern
\end{itemize}

\section{Deliverable}\label{record-126-deliverable}

Introduce a new package:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s}
\end{itemize}

With the first workflow surface for:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  authoring catalogs
\item
  translation rows
\item
  stale detection
\item
  import/export
\item
  compilation
\item
  pseudo-localization
\end{itemize}

\section{Proposed API direction}\label{record-126-proposed-api-direction}

The first slice should be close to:

\begin{CodeBlock}
interface AuthoringCatalog { ... }
interface AuthoringCatalogEntry { ... }
interface TranslationRow { ... }

function hashSourceValue(value: unknown): string;
function markStaleTranslations(catalogs: readonly AuthoringCatalog[]): readonly AuthoringCatalog[];
function exportTranslationRows(catalogs: readonly AuthoringCatalog[], locale: string): readonly TranslationRow[];
function importTranslationRows(catalogs: readonly AuthoringCatalog[], rows: readonly TranslationRow[]): readonly AuthoringCatalog[];
function compileCatalogs(catalogs: readonly AuthoringCatalog[]): readonly I18nCatalog[];
function pseudoLocalize(value: string): string;
\end{CodeBlock}

Exact names can still move, but the responsibilities should not.

\section{Tests to write first}\label{record-126-tests-to-write-first}

\subsection{Cycle-owned playback tests}\label{record-126-cycle-owned-playback-tests}

Under \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  package exists and can be imported
\item
  changed source strings mark existing translations stale
\item
  export returns only missing/stale rows for a locale
\item
  imported rows merge back and compile into runtime catalogs consumable by \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n}
\item
  pseudolocalization visibly lengthens text for layout stress
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Package-local unit tests}\label{record-126-package-local-unit-tests}

\chapter{LX-003 --- Spreadsheet Adapters and Catalog Exchange Workflows}\label{record-127}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/LX-003-spreadsheet-adapters-and-catalog-exchange-workflows.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/LX-localization-and-bidirectionality.md}{LX --- Localization and Bidirectionality}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-127-why-this-cycle-exists}

LX-002 gave Bijou a real localization tooling core:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  authoring catalogs
\item
  source hashing
\item
  stale detection
\item
  provider-neutral translation rows
\item
  runtime catalog compilation
\item
  pseudo-localization
\end{itemize}

That solved in-memory workflow logic, but not the exchange problem. Real localization work still has to move through:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  spreadsheet-shaped review workflows
\item
  structured handoff bundles
\item
  typed values and references that survive export/import without turning into mush
\end{itemize}

This cycle exists to add a provider-neutral exchange layer to \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s}.

\section{Scope of this cycle}\label{record-127-scope-of-this-cycle}

This cycle intentionally covers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a spreadsheet-friendly workbook model
\item
  typed export/import for translation rows
\item
  a serializable catalog-bundle format for authoring catalogs
\item
  reference-safe encoding/decoding for message/resource/data values
\item
  validation at the exchange boundary
\end{itemize}

It does \textbf{not} include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  CSV parsing
\item
  XLSX parsing
\item
  Google Sheets integration
\item
  filesystem adapters
\item
  remote services
\item
  runtime i18n changes
\end{itemize}

The goal is to define the exchange seam that those adapters can target later.

\section{Human users}\label{record-127-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-127-primary-human-user}

A localization maintainer who needs to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  export translatable work into a spreadsheet-like shape
\item
  import reviewed translations safely
\item
  move full authoring catalogs across tools or repos
\item
  preserve typed values and references without inventing a bespoke format
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-127-human-hill}

A builder can move localization workflow data through spreadsheet-like and bundle-like formats without losing type/reference fidelity or writing their own ad hoc serialization rules.

\section{Agent users}\label{record-127-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-127-primary-agent-user}

An agent helping with localization maintenance and exchange.

It needs to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  generate workbook-shaped review payloads
\item
  read imported workbook data back into typed translation rows
\item
  exchange full authoring catalogs in a stable serializable form
\item
  validate malformed exchange data before it reaches runtime compilation
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-127-agent-hill}

An agent can reason about localization exchange through explicit workbook/bundle contracts instead of reverse-engineering spreadsheet columns or raw JSON blobs.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-127-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder has authoring catalogs in memory.
\item
  They export stale or missing work for \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e} into a workbook-shaped review payload.
\item
  A translator or tool edits the workbook rows.
\item
  The builder imports the workbook back into translation rows and merges it into the authoring catalogs.
\item
  They export the full catalogs as a serializable bundle for storage, transport, or staged review.
\item
  They import the bundle back and compile it into runtime catalogs.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Agent playback}\label{record-127-agent-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent reads authoring catalogs.
\item
  It exports a workbook for a target locale.
\item
  It can inspect typed cells and references explicitly instead of guessing.
\item
  It imports workbook rows back into translation rows.
\item
  It exports/imports full catalog bundles for handoff or normalization.
\item
  It validates malformed references or invalid encoded values before compilation.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Deliverable}\label{record-127-deliverable}

Extend \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s} with exchange APIs for:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item

\item
  typed cell encoding/decoding
\item
  serializable catalog bundles
\item
  bundle export/import
\end{itemize}

\section{Proposed API direction}\label{record-127-proposed-api-direction}

The first slice should be close to:

\begin{CodeBlock}
interface ExchangeWorkbook { ... }
interface ExchangeSheet { ... }
interface ExchangeRow { ... }
interface CatalogBundle { ... }

function exportTranslationWorkbook(
  catalogs: readonly AuthoringCatalog[],
  locale: string,
): ExchangeWorkbook;

function importTranslationWorkbook(
  workbook: ExchangeWorkbook,
): readonly TranslationRow[];

function exportCatalogBundle(
  catalogs: readonly AuthoringCatalog[],
): CatalogBundle;

function importCatalogBundle(
  bundle: CatalogBundle,
): readonly AuthoringCatalog[];
\end{CodeBlock}

Exact names can still move, but the responsibilities should not.

\section{Tests to write first}\label{record-127-tests-to-write-first}

\subsection{Cycle-owned playback tests}\label{record-127-cycle-owned-playback-tests}

Under \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}/}:

\item

\item

\item
  malformed workbook/bundle payloads fail clearly
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Package-local unit tests}\label{record-127-package-local-unit-tests}

Under \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  typed value encoding/decoding preserves strings, objects, arrays, booleans, null, and refs
\item
  workbook import rejects malformed headers or invalid encoded values
\item
  bundle import rejects malformed catalog payloads
\item
  workbook rows remain string-cell-safe
\end{itemize}

\chapter{LX-004 --- Provider Adapters for Workbook and Bundle Exchange}\label{record-128}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/LX-004-provider-adapters-for-workbook-and-bundle-exchange.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/LX-localization-and-bidirectionality.md}{LX --- Localization and Bidirectionality}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-128-why-this-cycle-exists}

LX-003 established the provider-neutral exchange seam in \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  spreadsheet-friendly workbooks
\item
  serializable catalog bundles
\item
  typed value encoding/decoding
\end{itemize}

That seam is useful, but still abstract. Real workflows need concrete adapters that can move those formats through common external media.

This cycle exists to prove the seam with the smallest honest adapter layer:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  delimited text for sheets (\texttt{c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v} / \texttt{t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v})
\item
  JSON for catalog bundles
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope of this cycle}\label{record-128-scope-of-this-cycle}

This cycle intentionally covers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  serializing an \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t} to TSV
\item
  parsing an \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t} from TSV
\item
  serializing an \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t} to CSV
\item
  parsing an \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t} from CSV
\item
  serializing a \texttt{C\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} to JSON
\item
  parsing a \texttt{C\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} from JSON
\end{itemize}

It does \textbf{not} include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  filesystem helpers
\item
  XLSX
\item
  Google Sheets
\item
  remote services
\item
  multi-file workbook orchestration
\end{itemize}

The point is to prove the adapter surface without bringing in provider/platform coupling yet.

\section{Human users}\label{record-128-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-128-primary-human-user}

A localization maintainer who needs to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  hand off one exchange sheet to external tooling in a real delimited text format
\item
  bring edited rows back from that format
\item
  move full catalog bundles through a serializable JSON representation
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-128-human-hill}

A builder can export a sheet to a real CSV/TSV string, import it back, and move full authoring bundles through JSON without inventing one-off parsing logic.

\section{Agent users}\label{record-128-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-128-primary-agent-user}

An agent maintaining localization workflows.

It needs to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  emit delimited review sheets that non-Bijou tooling can consume
\item
  parse those sheets back safely
\item
  serialize and deserialize full catalog bundles for transport or review
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-128-agent-hill}

An agent can move localization exchange data through explicit adapter APIs instead of hand-rolling CSV escaping or JSON bundle parsing in each workflow.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-128-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder exports a translation workbook for \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  They take the sheet and serialize it to TSV or CSV.
\item
  Another tool edits the serialized rows.
\item
  The builder parses the edited sheet back into an \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t}.
\item
  They import the workbook rows and merge them into authoring catalogs.
\item
  They serialize a full catalog bundle to JSON and later restore it back into authoring catalogs.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Agent playback}\label{record-128-agent-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent exports a workbook.
\item
  It serializes the sheet to TSV or CSV for an external review tool.
\item
  It parses the edited sheet back.
\item
  It serializes full catalog bundles to JSON for handoff or snapshotting.
\item
  It restores bundles from JSON and feeds them back into the tooling core.
\end{enumerate}

\end{itemize}

\section{Deliverable}\label{record-128-deliverable}

Extend \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s} with adapter APIs for:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t} \textless-\textgreater{} \texttt{c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v}
\item
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t} \textless-\textgreater{} \texttt{t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v}
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} \textless-\textgreater{} \texttt{j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}
\end{itemize}

\section{Proposed API direction}\label{record-128-proposed-api-direction}

The first slice should be close to:

\begin{CodeBlock}
type DelimitedFormat = 'csv' | 'tsv';

function serializeExchangeSheet(
  sheet: ExchangeSheet,
  format: DelimitedFormat,
): string;

function parseExchangeSheet(
  name: string,
  input: string,
  format: DelimitedFormat,
): ExchangeSheet;

function serializeCatalogBundleJson(bundle: CatalogBundle): string;
function parseCatalogBundleJson(input: string): CatalogBundle;
\end{CodeBlock}

Higher-level helpers can be added later if needed, but this cycle should prove the core adapter surface.

\section{Tests to write first}\label{record-128-tests-to-write-first}

\subsection{Cycle-owned playback tests}\label{record-128-cycle-owned-playback-tests}

Under \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  exported workbook sheets roundtrip through TSV and still import into runtime-consumable catalogs
\item
  exported workbook sheets roundtrip through CSV even with commas, quotes, and newlines in cells
\item
  catalog bundles roundtrip through JSON and still restore full authoring catalogs
\item
  malformed CSV/TSV/JSON payloads fail clearly
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Package-local unit tests}\label{record-128-package-local-unit-tests}

Under \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  CSV quoting/escaping is correct
\item
  TSV preserves tabs/newlines through quoting rules
\item
  parsers reject ragged rows
\item
  JSON bundle parser rejects malformed versioned payloads
\end{itemize}

\section{Risks}\label{record-128-risks}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  under-testing delimiter edge cases
\item
  accidentally normalizing away exact cell payloads
\item
  letting adapter helpers grow into file I/O abstractions
\item
  making JSON bundle parsing too permissive
\end{itemize}

\section{Out of scope}\label{record-128-out-of-scope}

  file reads/writes

\item
  Google Sheets
\item

\item
  service adapters of any kind
\end{itemize}

\chapter{LX-005 --- Rich Spreadsheet and Filesystem Adapters}\label{record-129}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/LX-005-rich-spreadsheet-and-filesystem-adapters.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/LX-localization-and-bidirectionality.md}{LX --- Localization and Bidirectionality}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-129-why-this-cycle-exists}

LX-004 proved the first concrete adapter seam in \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  CSV sheet adapters
\item
  TSV sheet adapters
\item
  JSON bundle adapters
\end{itemize}

That still leaves a practical gap for real automation and tooling:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  reading and writing those formats from the filesystem
\item
  handling whole workbooks instead of one sheet string at a time
\end{itemize}

This cycle exists to add the Node-specific filesystem layer on top of the existing exchange seam.

\section{Scope of this cycle}\label{record-129-scope-of-this-cycle}

This cycle intentionally covers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a new Node-specific package for filesystem helpers
\item
  reading/writing one \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t} file in CSV or TSV
\item
  reading/writing one \texttt{C\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} JSON file
\item
  reading/writing a workbook directory made of:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    a manifest file
  \item
    one sheet file per sheet
  \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

It does \textbf{not} include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  XLSX
\item
  Google Sheets
\item
  remote services
\item
  zip packaging
\item
  changing the pure \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s} exchange model
\end{itemize}

The point is to make the current exchange seam practical in Node without dragging platform concerns into the core tooling package.

\section{Human users}\label{record-129-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-129-primary-human-user}

A builder or localization maintainer who needs to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  save exchange sheets to disk
\item
  read edited sheets back from disk
\item
  store and reload full catalog bundles
\item
  hand off or restore complete workbooks as a directory artifact
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-129-human-hill}

A builder can persist workbook and bundle exchange artifacts through one small Node helper package, without hand-writing file I/O or inventing an ad hoc workbook directory format.

\section{Agent users}\label{record-129-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-129-primary-agent-user}

An agent automating localization workflows.

It needs to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  write sheets and bundles to disk
\item
  read them back deterministically
\item
  stage workbook directories for review workflows
\item
  reason about paths and formats explicitly instead of shelling out to one-off scripts
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-129-agent-hill}

An agent can automate localization exchange through explicit Node adapters instead of rebuilding CSV/TSV/JSON file orchestration in every workflow.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-129-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder exports a workbook in memory.
\item
  They write it to a directory on disk in TSV or CSV form.
\item
  A tool or person edits the sheet files.
\item
  The builder reads the workbook directory back into memory.
\item
  They import the workbook rows and merge the updates.
\item
  They also save and restore full catalog bundles as JSON files.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Agent playback}\label{record-129-agent-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent exports a workbook.
\item
  It writes the workbook to a directory for review.
\item
  It later reads the workbook directory back.
\item
  It writes and reads catalog bundle files as deterministic JSON artifacts.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/invariants/tests-are-the-spec.md}{Tests Are the Spec}

\section{Invariants for this cycle}\label{record-129-invariants-for-this-cycle}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  filesystem concerns must stay out of the pure \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s} package
\item
  Node helpers must build on the existing workbook/bundle seam instead of replacing it
\item
  directory formats must be explicit and versioned
\item
  file helpers must be deterministic about sheet ordering and file names
\item
  richer spreadsheet providers remain out of scope
\end{itemize}

\section{Deliverable}\label{record-129-deliverable}

Introduce a new package:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e}
\end{itemize}

With Node filesystem helpers for:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t} files (\texttt{c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v} / \texttt{t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}v})
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} files (\texttt{j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n})
\item
  workbook directories (\texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s})
\end{itemize}

\section{Proposed API direction}\label{record-129-proposed-api-direction}

The first slice should be close to:

\begin{CodeBlock}
function writeExchangeSheetFile(path: string, sheet: ExchangeSheet, format?: DelimitedFormat): Promise<void>;
function readExchangeSheetFile(path: string, format?: DelimitedFormat): Promise<ExchangeSheet>;

function writeCatalogBundleFile(path: string, bundle: CatalogBundle): Promise<void>;
function readCatalogBundleFile(path: string): Promise<CatalogBundle>;

function writeExchangeWorkbookDirectory(
  path: string,
  workbook: ExchangeWorkbook,
  format: DelimitedFormat,
): Promise<void>;

function readExchangeWorkbookDirectory(path: string): Promise<ExchangeWorkbook>;
\end{CodeBlock}

Exact names can still move, but the responsibilities should not.

\section{Tests to write first}\label{record-129-tests-to-write-first}

\subsection{Cycle-owned playback tests}\label{record-129-cycle-owned-playback-tests}

Under \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  workbook directories roundtrip through disk and still import back into runtime-consumable catalogs
\item
  bundle files roundtrip through disk and restore full authoring catalogs
\item
  file helpers infer format from extension where appropriate
\item
  malformed manifests or missing sheet files fail clearly
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Package-local unit tests}\label{record-129-package-local-unit-tests}

Under \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  sheet files preserve CSV/TSV content exactly
\item
  workbook directory manifest is versioned and deterministic
\item
  unsupported extensions fail clearly
\item
  missing files fail clearly
\end{itemize}

\section{Risks}\label{record-129-risks}

\item

\item
  accidentally making the helpers non-deterministic

\item
