\chapter{LX-006 --- XLSX Localization Adapters}\label{record-130}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/LX-006-xlsx-localization-adapters.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/LX-localization-and-bidirectionality.md}{LX --- Localization and Bidirectionality}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-130-why-this-cycle-exists}

LX-005 made the exchange seam practical on disk through:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  CSV / TSV sheet files
\item
  JSON bundle files
\item
  workbook directories with a manifest
\end{itemize}

That still leaves a common real-world localization format uncovered:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{.\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}x} workbook exchange
\end{itemize}

This cycle exists to add a true spreadsheet provider adapter on top of the existing workbook seam without dragging spreadsheet-library concerns into the pure runtime/tools packages.

\section{Scope of this cycle}\label{record-130-scope-of-this-cycle}

This cycle intentionally covers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a dedicated XLSX adapter package
\item
  serializing an \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k} to XLSX bytes
\item
  parsing XLSX bytes back into an \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  deterministic handling of workbook sheet order and required workbook columns
\end{itemize}

It does \textbf{not} include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Google Sheets
\item
  remote services
\item
  filesystem helpers for XLSX paths
\item
  changing the pure \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s} workbook model
\item
  changing bundle JSON exchange
\end{itemize}

The point is to prove the provider seam with one richer spreadsheet format first.

\section{Human users}\label{record-130-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-130-primary-human-user}

A localization maintainer who needs to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  hand a workbook to translators in a true spreadsheet format
\item
  import edited spreadsheets back into the existing Bijou exchange flow
\item
  keep using the same workbook schema regardless of carrier format
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-130-human-hill}

A maintainer can export and import localization workbooks as \texttt{.\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}x} files without losing typed exchange values or inventing a second workbook model.

\section{Agent users}\label{record-130-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-130-primary-agent-user}

An agent automating localization exchange.

It needs to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  export workbook bytes suitable for XLSX workflows
\item
  parse returned XLSX workbook bytes deterministically
\item
  stay on the same workbook seam as CSV / TSV / filesystem helpers
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-130-agent-hill}

An agent can automate true spreadsheet exchange without shelling out to ad hoc conversion scripts or bypassing the Bijou workbook model.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-130-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer exports a German translation workbook.
\item
  They serialize it to an XLSX blob.
\item
  A spreadsheet editor changes translated values.
\item
  The maintainer parses the XLSX blob back into an \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k}.
\item
  They import the rows and merge the translations back into authoring catalogs.
\item
  The resulting runtime catalogs resolve the edited translations correctly.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Agent playback}\label{record-130-agent-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent exports an \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k}.
\item
  It serializes that workbook to XLSX bytes for review or delivery.
\item
  It later parses returned XLSX bytes back into an \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k}.
\item
  It imports the workbook rows and compiles catalogs without losing typed values, refs, or sheet ordering.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Invariants for this cycle}\label{record-130-invariants-for-this-cycle}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  spreadsheet-provider logic must stay out of \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  XLSX adapters must preserve the existing workbook schema instead of inventing a new one
\item
  workbook sheet order must remain deterministic
\item
  required translation workbook columns must remain explicit
\item
  service-backed adapters remain out of scope for this cycle
\end{itemize}

\section{Deliverable}\label{record-130-deliverable}

Introduce a new package:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}x}
\end{itemize}

With XLSX adapters for:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k} -\textgreater{} XLSX bytes
\item
  XLSX bytes -\textgreater{} \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k}
\end{itemize}

\section{Proposed API direction}\label{record-130-proposed-api-direction}

The first slice should be close to:

\begin{CodeBlock}
function serializeExchangeWorkbookXlsx(workbook: ExchangeWorkbook): Uint8Array;
function parseExchangeWorkbookXlsx(input: Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer): ExchangeWorkbook;
\end{CodeBlock}

Exact names can still move, but the responsibilities should not.

\section{Tests to write first}\label{record-130-tests-to-write-first}

\subsection{Cycle-owned playback tests}\label{record-130-cycle-owned-playback-tests}

Under \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  XLSX workbooks roundtrip through bytes and still import back into runtime-consumable catalogs
\item
  the new package exports only the XLSX-focused workbook adapters
\item
  typed values and refs survive the roundtrip when workbook rows are edited after parsing
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Package-local unit tests}\label{record-130-package-local-unit-tests}

Under \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  workbook sheet order is preserved
\item
  required columns survive serialization and parsing
\item
  missing required headers fail clearly
\item
  non-string cell values are normalized back into the exchange row shape correctly
\end{itemize}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/LX-008-localize-shell-chrome-and-dogfood.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/LX-localization-and-bidirectionality.md}{LX --- Localization and Bidirectionality}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-131-why-this-cycle-exists}

LX-001 through LX-006 built the localization substrate:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  runtime catalogs
\item
  tools and exchange workflows
\item
  filesystem helpers
\item
  XLSX adapters
\end{itemize}

But the humane shell and DOGFOOD still ship mostly hardcoded English copy.

This cycle exists to prove that the i18n work is real in product surfaces:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  shell chrome
\item
  shell overlays and drawers
\item
  DOGFOOD landing and onboarding copy
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope of this cycle}\label{record-131-scope-of-this-cycle}

This cycle intentionally covers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a shell-level i18n seam for \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}
\item
  localized shell-owned defaults such as:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    command palette title
  \item
    default search title
  \item
    settings drawer title
  \item
    quit confirm copy
  \item
    footer notification cue and shell drawer footer hints
  \end{itemize}
\item
  DOGFOOD-localized copy for:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    landing footer and prompt
  \item
    search/settings labels
  \item
    empty-state onboarding copy
  \item
    settings row labels, descriptions, and feedback
  \end{itemize}
\item
  one visible direction-aware shell behavior driven by i18n direction metadata
\end{itemize}

It does \textbf{not} include:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  full generic bidirectional layout support across every shell surface
\item
  localizing every example in the repo
\item
  provider/service adapters
\item
  persistence
\end{itemize}

The point is to prove the localization runtime in the shell and DOGFOOD without pretending RTL support is solved everywhere.

\section{Human users}\label{record-131-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-131-primary-human-user}

A builder or end user working in a non-English locale.

They need to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  see shell controls and onboarding copy in their locale
\item
  trust that shell labels, footer hints, and settings copy are not locked to English
\item
  see at least one shell behavior react to logical direction instead of physical left/right assumptions
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-131-human-hill}

A non-English user can enter DOGFOOD and immediately see localized shell/UI copy, while a builder can point to DOGFOOD as proof that Bijou localization is not theoretical.

\section{Agent users}\label{record-131-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-131-primary-agent-user}

An agent integrating or validating localized Bijou surfaces.

It needs to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  load catalogs into the shell and docs proving surface
\item
  verify localized strings at the rendered shell boundary
\item
  reason about direction-aware shell behavior through explicit runtime metadata
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-131-agent-hill}

An agent can localize shell chrome and DOGFOOD through explicit i18n contracts instead of editing hardcoded English strings in place.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-131-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A builder creates a localized runtime.
\item
  They launch DOGFOOD in that locale.
\item
  The landing footer and prompt use localized copy.
\item
  After entering the docs, the shell drawer titles, search surface, footer hints, and settings copy use localized copy too.
\item
  In an RTL locale, at least one shell drawer placement mirrors logically instead of staying physically fixed.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Agent playback}\label{record-131-agent-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent loads shell and DOGFOOD catalogs into an i18n runtime.
\item
  It passes that runtime into the shell/docs app.
\item
  It verifies localized shell strings in rendered frames.
\item
  It verifies pseudo-localized copy appears in DOGFOOD.
\item
  It verifies direction metadata changes a visible shell behavior.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{itemize}

  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} must own shell-localized defaults instead of pushing shell copy responsibility entirely to apps

\section{Deliverable}\label{record-131-deliverable}

Introduce:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a shell i18n seam in \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i}
\item
  a canonical shell catalog for frame-owned copy
\item
  DOGFOOD-localized catalogs and runtime wiring
\end{itemize}

So that shell chrome and DOGFOOD can run against locale/direction metadata instead of hardcoded English strings.

\section{Proposed API direction}\label{record-131-proposed-api-direction}

The first slice should be close to:

\begin{CodeBlock}
interface CreateFramedAppOptions<PageModel, Msg> {
  readonly i18n?: I18nRuntime;
}
\end{CodeBlock}

With:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a built-in frame-shell catalog exported from \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i}
\item
  DOGFOOD creating and using an i18n runtime, loading both shell and docs catalogs
\end{itemize}

Exact names can still move, but the responsibilities should not.

\section{Tests to write first}\label{record-131-tests-to-write-first}

\subsection{Cycle-owned playback tests}\label{record-131-cycle-owned-playback-tests}

Under \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}/}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a localized framed app shows translated shell-owned titles and hints
\item
  DOGFOOD renders pseudo-localized shell/docs copy when supplied localized catalogs
\item
  an RTL runtime changes a visible shell behavior such as drawer anchor placement
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Package-local tests}\label{record-131-package-local-tests}

In existing package/example test surfaces:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  shell quit/search/settings defaults use localized copy when an i18n runtime is provided
\item
  DOGFOOD settings/landing/onboarding copy comes from catalogs rather than hardcoded strings
\end{itemize}

\section{Risks}\label{record-131-risks}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  only partially localizing shell surfaces and leaving confusing English islands
\item
  adding an i18n seam that DOGFOOD does not actually prove
\item
  claiming direction-awareness without any visible shell behavior change
\item
  threading translator functions everywhere instead of defining one shell-localized seam
\end{itemize}

\section{Out of scope}\label{record-131-out-of-scope}

\begin{itemize}

\item
  full generic RTL layout mirroring across every component
\item
  persistence
\item
  service-backed localization workflows
\item
  every example app in the repo
\end{itemize}

    default search title
  \item
    settings title and footer hint
  \item
    notification-center title, footer hint, and footer cue label
  \item
    help title and hint
  \item
    quit-confirm title, body, and footer hint
  \item
    shell mode labels
  \end{itemize}
\item
  DOGFOOD-localized catalogs and runtime wiring for:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    landing prompt and footer
  \item
    onboarding / empty-state copy
  \item
    localized search/settings surfaces
  \item
    settings-row labels, descriptions, value labels, and feedback toasts
  \end{itemize}
\item
  visible direction-aware shell behavior:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    settings drawer resolves to logical \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t}
  \item
    notification center resolves to logical \texttt{e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d}
  \item
    the settings drawer visibly mirrors under RTL
  \end{itemize}
\item
  cycle-owned playback coverage in:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
  \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Drift from ideal}\label{record-131-drift-from-ideal}

This cycle proved the shell/runtime seam cleanly, but it did not finish every English island.

Still intentionally incomplete:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  help-overlay keybinding descriptions still mostly fall back to English strings
\item
  notification history/body copy is only partially localized
\item
  direction awareness is real but still narrow; only a subset of shell drawer placement is mirrored so far
\end{itemize}

That drift is acceptable for LX-008 because the point of the cycle was to prove that shell localization and direction metadata are real in product surfaces, not to declare shell localization complete.

\subsection{Debt spawned}\label{record-131-debt-spawned}

Spawned:

  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/method/graveyard/legacy-backlog/LX-009-localize-shell-help-notification-and-directional-surfaces.md}{LX-009 --- Localize Shell Help, Notification, and Directional Surfaces}

\chapter{LX-019 --- Localization Port Contract}\label{record-132}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/LX-019-localization-port-contract.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/LX-localization-and-bidirectionality.md}{LX --- Localization and Bidirectionality}

\section{Why This Cycle Exists}\label{record-132-why-this-cycle-exists}

Bijou already has a runtime catalog engine, formatter ports, catalog loaders, string-table tooling, and DOGFOOD locale preference ports. Those pieces make localization possible, but DOGFOOD still tends to pass the concrete i18n runtime through rendering code and ask it for naked strings.

That is too low-level for the long-term architecture.

Views, blocks, and docs surfaces should ask an application-facing localization port for a localized object:

\begin{CodeBlock}
const title = localization.resolve({
  key: { namespace: 'bijou.dogfood', id: 'blocks.preview.title' },
});
\end{CodeBlock}

The result should preserve runtime truth:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the requested key
\item
  selected locale
\item
  direction
\item
  entry kind
\item
  translated / fallback / missing status
\item
  localized value
\item
  issues and facts for tooling
\end{itemize}

The view should not know how catalogs were loaded, where JSON files live, which CSV source produced them, or how fallback catalogs were attached.

\section{Core Rule}\label{record-132-core-rule}

Localization in Bijou is a port/adapter boundary.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Ports live where the localization vocabulary lives.
\item
  Adapters live where the external dependency lives.
\item
  Composition lives at the app boundary.
\item
  Views receive localized objects, not filesystem, catalog, or runtime machinery.
\end{itemize}

\section{Boundary}\label{record-132-boundary}

This cycle is about the application-facing localization port contract and DOGFOOD wiring.

It is not about:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  expanding translation coverage
\item
  adding a localization dashboard
\item
  adding a translation workbench
\item
  changing the CSV string-table workflow
\item
  loading every locale at runtime
\item
  implementing remote localization services
\item
  making blocks fetch localization data directly
\item
  replacing the lower-level i18n runtime
\end{itemize}

\section{Vocabulary}\label{record-132-vocabulary}

\subsection{Localization Port}\label{record-132-localization-port}

The app-facing port that resolves a localization request into a structured localized object.

It should answer:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Given this key and interpolation values, what localized object should this view
render in the selected locale?
\end{CodeBlock}

It should not answer:

\begin{CodeBlock}
Where are the catalog files?
How do I read the filesystem?
How do I compile CSV rows?
How do I persist locale preferences?
\end{CodeBlock}

\subsection{Localized Object}\label{record-132-localized-object}

The immutable result returned by the localization port.

It contains:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  key
\item
  locale
\item
  direction
\item
  fallback locale
\item
  entry kind
\item
  resolution status
\item
  value
\item
  issues
\item
  facts
\end{itemize}

The value may be a message string, data payload, or resource payload depending on the catalog entry kind.

\subsection{Runtime Adapter}\label{record-132-runtime-adapter}

An adapter that wraps \texttt{I\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} and exposes it through \texttt{L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t}.

The runtime continues to own catalog state, fallback behavior, locale switching, references, and formatting. The port makes that behavior consumable by application code without leaking the runtime surface everywhere.

Runtime convenience methods that remain public, such as \texttt{t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, should behave like stable API functions instead of receiver-sensitive object methods. Callers may pass or destructure these helpers without preserving a JavaScript \texttt{t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s} binding; the runtime state remains closure-owned at the adapter boundary.

\subsection{Node / Filesystem Adapters}\label{record-132-node-filesystem-adapters}

Adapters that read selected-locale generated JSON catalogs from disk belong in \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e} or application composition code.

They should return catalogs or construct runtime-backed localization ports. They should not redefine the generic localization port contract.

\section{Package Split}\label{record-132-package-split}

The contract belongs in \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n}:

\begin{CodeBlock}
packages/bijou-i18n
  LocalizationPort
  LocalizationRequest
  LocalizedObject
  LocalizationStatus
  LocalizationIssue
  LocalizationFact
  createRuntimeLocalizationPort()
\end{CodeBlock}

Node/file adapters stay in \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e}:

\begin{CodeBlock}
packages/bijou-i18n-tools-node
  CSV and TSV string-table files
  generated runtime catalog JSON files
  selected-locale catalog directory loaders
\end{CodeBlock}

DOGFOOD composition lives in \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s}:

\begin{CodeBlock}
examples/docs
  selected locale resolution
  English fallback catalog attachment
  development missing-marker policy
  runtime-backed LocalizationPort assembly
\end{CodeBlock}

Views and block previews should receive the port or localized objects. They should not receive filesystem loaders, CSV data, generated catalog paths, or provider handles.

\section{Expected Flow}\label{record-132-expected-flow}

\begin{CodeBlock}
CSV source string table
  -> generated per-locale JSON catalogs
  -> selected-locale catalog loader adapter
  -> I18nRuntime
  -> LocalizationPort
  -> LocalizedObject
  -> DOGFOOD / Blocks / shell surfaces
\end{CodeBlock}

The fallback posture remains:

\begin{CodeBlock}
production:
  selected locale value
  -> English fallback catalog

non-production:
  selected locale value
  -> loud missing-localization object
  -> English fallback only when missing markers are disabled
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{DOGFOOD Implications}\label{record-132-dogfood-implications}

DOGFOOD should keep the concrete runtime at the composition boundary because the frame shell still consumes \texttt{I\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e} and the app still needs locale activation. Ordinary DOGFOOD text lookup should move behind \texttt{L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.

The app may still hold both:

\begin{CodeBlock}
const runtime = createI18nRuntime(...);
const localization = createRuntimeLocalizationPort(runtime);
\end{CodeBlock}

But render helpers should prefer:

\begin{CodeBlock}
localization.resolve({
  key: { namespace: 'bijou.dogfood', id: 'settings.language.label' },
});
\end{CodeBlock}

over:

\begin{CodeBlock}
runtime.t({ namespace: 'bijou.dogfood', id: 'settings.language.label' });
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-132-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n} exports a first-class localization port contract.
\item
  Runtime lookup helpers stay receiver-independent so app code can pass them around without binding \texttt{t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  The runtime adapter returns immutable localized objects.
\item
  Localized values enforce the portable JSON-shaped catalog boundary with deterministic errors for cyclic graphs, symbol-keyed properties, non-enumerable properties, accessors, class instances, functions, symbols, and bigint values.
\item
  Localized objects preserve key, locale, direction, kind, status, value, issues, and facts.
\item
  Missing selected-locale translations remain inspectable as missing localization results in non-production posture.
\item
  Production fallback remains explicit through fallback catalogs.
\item
  DOGFOOD text helpers use the localization port rather than direct runtime string lookups.
\item
  DOGFOOD still keeps catalog loading and locale activation at the app composition boundary.
\end{itemize}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-132-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Port resolution returns a localized object for a translated message.
\item
  Port resolution reports fallback status when selected-locale catalogs omit a value and fallback catalogs provide one.
\item
  Port resolution reports missing status and marker value when missing-marker policy is enabled.
\item
  Resource/data entries return localized object values without converting them to strings.
\item
  Localized objects and their issue/fact arrays are immutable.
\item
  DOGFOOD text lookup consumes \texttt{L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t} and does not call \texttt{I\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} directly.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-132-retrospective}

Not started.

\chapter{LX-020 - DOGFOOD Locale Demo Readiness}\label{record-133}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/LX-020-dogfood-locale-demo-readiness.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
id: LX-020
title: DOGFOOD Locale Demo Readiness
status: active
lane: asap
priority: high
github_issue: 340
legend: LX

\end{RecordMeta}

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/LX-localization-and-bidirectionality.md}{LX - Localization and Bidirectionality}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-133-decision-summary}

DOGFOOD should stop presenting non-English locale selection as if the whole app is fully translated. For \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, the honest release-demo contract is:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  core app chrome and release-demo navigation do not show missing localization placeholders
\item
  English-source documentation is labeled as such when selected locale content is intentionally unavailable
\item
  localization debt remains visible to maintainers without leaking broken UI into the user-facing demo path
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-133-sponsored-human}

A release-video user needs DOGFOOD to survive a non-English locale switch without looking broken. Missing localization markers, accidental English chrome, and unclear partial-translation behavior make the shipped story feel unfinished.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-133-sponsored-agent}

An agent needs deterministic localization witnesses that distinguish three states:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  selected-locale translation exists and is rendered
\item
  selected-locale translation is intentionally unavailable and the app presents an English-source notice
\item
  selected-locale translation is missing by accident and should fail the gate
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-133-hill}

After this cycle, DOGFOOD's non-English demo path is truthful enough for a release video: switching locales does not expose missing-placeholder strings in major app chrome, and documentation surfaces clearly explain when they remain English-source content.

\section{Problem}\label{record-133-problem}

Issue \#340 came from the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release-video rehearsal. DOGFOOD can switch to non-English locales, but much of the app still renders English copy or missing localization markers. Existing i18n gates prove debt is counted, not that the presentation path is demo-ready.

The current debt ratchet is useful, but it is not sufficient for user-facing release claims:

\begin{CodeBlock}
dogfood-i18n-debt: ok (2772 raw strings; baseline 2772; 78 missing Markdown localizations; baseline 78)
\end{CodeBlock}

That output tells maintainers the known debt did not grow. It does not tell a viewer why non-English DOGFOOD still shows English documentation.

\section{Scope}\label{record-133-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Audit the launch, navigation, settings, status/footer, and major tab chrome for the supported non-English DOGFOOD locales.
\item
  Add deterministic coverage that fails when the release-demo path renders visible missing-localization placeholders.
\item
  Add or update DOGFOOD copy so intentionally English-source documentation is labeled clearly when the selected locale lacks translated Markdown.
\item
  Keep the existing debt ratchet intact; this cycle strengthens the presentation contract around it.
\item
  Update release-facing docs/changelog so \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} describes the localization posture honestly.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-133-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Do not translate the full DOGFOOD documentation corpus in this cycle.
\item
  Do not build a localization workbench or dashboard.
\item
  Do not change the CSV/XLSX localization workflow.
\item
  Do not hide known debt from maintainer tooling.
\item
  Do not broaden \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} into the V8/V9 localization operations surface.
\end{itemize}

\section{User Experience Contract}\label{record-133-user-experience-contract}

For non-English locales, DOGFOOD may show English documentation only if the UI makes that fallback explicit. The user should not have to infer whether English copy is a bug, an untranslated source document, or a missing catalog entry.

Major app chrome should be localized or explicitly excluded from the release demo path. Missing-placeholder strings are not acceptable on the demo path.

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-133-lower-modes}

\subsection{Static Mode}\label{record-133-static-mode}

Static DOGFOOD render helpers should be able to render a selected-locale path and expose whether missing placeholders appear in visible output.

\subsection{Pipe Mode}\label{record-133-pipe-mode}

Pipe/smoke output should remain deterministic and suitable for release evidence. Locale-specific output checks must avoid terminal-profile assumptions.

\subsection{Accessible Mode}\label{record-133-accessible-mode}

English-source notices should be text, not color-only styling. Screen readers and terminal readers should receive the same partial-localization status.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-133-localization-directionality-posture}

This cycle treats localization status as product truth. The app may still carry known translation debt, but the release-demo path must make that debt explicit instead of looking accidentally broken.

No new right-to-left layout contract is introduced. Direction metadata should continue to flow from the selected locale through the existing localization port/runtime path.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-133-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

Agents should be able to inspect:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  which locale was selected
\item
  whether a rendered string came from selected-locale content, fallback content, or an English-source documentation notice
\item
  whether missing localization markers appeared in the tested output
\end{itemize}

The proof should be executable through focused tests and existing DOGFOOD i18n commands, not through screenshots alone.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-133-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD visible release claims must be true in the app.
\item
  Known localization debt must stay counted by the ratchet.
\item
  Missing localization placeholders must not appear in the release-demo path.
\item
  English-source documentation fallback must be explicit to users.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Plan}\label{record-133-implementation-plan}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add focused failing tests that render representative non-English DOGFOOD paths and assert no visible missing-localization placeholders are present.
\item
  Identify the release-demo chrome surfaces that should be localized now.
\item
  Add an English-source documentation notice for intentionally untranslated Markdown/documentation surfaces.
\item
  Update catalog entries or DOGFOOD copy for the scoped chrome surfaces.
\item
  Preserve the existing \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}t}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e} gates.
\item
  Update changelog and any release-facing wording needed to avoid overclaiming full DOGFOOD translation.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-133-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A non-English DOGFOOD launch/render path fails if visible missing localization markers appear.
\item
  A selected non-English documentation path renders an explicit English-source notice when translated Markdown is unavailable.
\item
  Locale switching keeps major app chrome free of accidental missing markers.
\item
  Existing debt-ratchet behavior still reports known raw-string and Markdown localization debt.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-133-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Non-English release-demo path has deterministic missing-placeholder coverage.
\item
  Major DOGFOOD chrome on that path is localized or explicitly excluded from the release-demo claim.
\item
  English-source documentation fallback is visible and textual.
\item
  Existing i18n debt gates remain green.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} records the demo-readiness fix.
\item
  Issue \#340 is closed by the implementation PR.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-133-retrospective}

To be completed when the PR lands.

\chapter{LX-021 DOGFOOD String Debt Ratchet}\label{record-134}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/LX-021-dogfood-string-debt-ratchet.md}\par}\smallskip

\section{Status}\label{record-134-status}

Implemented.

\section{Tracker}\label{record-134-tracker}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  GitHub Issue: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/415}{\#415}
\item
  Pull Request: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/pull/416}{\#416}
\end{itemize}

\section{Legend}\label{record-134-legend}

\begin{itemize}

\item
  Linked legend: LX, Localization and Bidirectionality
\item
  Sponsor human: James Ross
\item
  Sponsor agent: Codex
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-134-hill}

DOGFOOD must stop treating raw visible strings as harmless residue. This cycle removes a material slice from the raw-string baseline by moving selected component story copy behind the existing DOGFOOD localization catalog workflow.

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-134-current-truth}

Live counts on \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n} at \texttt{a\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  DOGFOOD raw-string debt: \texttt{2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}1}
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s} raw-string debt: \texttt{1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}1}
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}s} raw-string debt: \texttt{6\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}1}
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p} raw-string debt: \texttt{2\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}8}
\item
  missing Markdown localizations: \texttt{7\allowbreak{}8}
\item
  aggregate Code Dojo debt: \texttt{9\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}1}
\end{itemize}

Target for this cycle:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item

\section{User Experience Contract}\label{record-134-user-experience-contract}

Converted story copy must still read as the same DOGFOOD demonstration. The localized text may use conservative translations, but it must not replace visible content with placeholder keys or intentionally untranslated fallback rows.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-134-localization-and-directionality-posture}

This cycle uses the existing DOGFOOD localization port. It does not introduce a new directionality model. Any converted copy should continue to flow through \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t} so locale selection, fallback interpolation, and catalog checks remain centralized.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-134-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

The PR must make the changed keys easy to audit:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  catalog IDs should be grouped by the story surface they serve
\item
  fallback copy should remain adjacent to the rendered usage
\item
  final debt counts should be recorded in this design doc or the PR summary
\end{itemize}

  No broad theme-lab, landing-page, or navigation redesign.
\item
  No placeholder localization rows.
\item
  No Code Dojo baseline increases.
\item
  No release-version scope.
\item
  No rebase, amend, force push, or draft PR.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-135-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Did aggregate Code Dojo debt fall to \texttt{8\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}0} or lower?
\item

\item

\item
  Did the touched DOGFOOD surface still pass focused smoke or preview tests?
\end{enumerate}

\section{User Experience Contract}\label{record-135-user-experience-contract}

The DOGFOOD app must render the same visible product behavior after the split. Navigation rows, guide rows, landing behavior, theme selection, and preview panes must preserve their current semantics unless this design explicitly says otherwise.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-135-localization-and-directionality-posture}

Any visible string converted during this slice must use the existing DOGFOOD localization port and catalog workflow. Moving raw strings to a new module is not a debt reduction unless the raw-string inventory proves the total count went down.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-135-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

The split should create named modules that reveal responsibility from their file names. Reviewers should be able to tell which code owns app row rendering, standard block preview data, or other extracted behavior without scrolling through the full DOGFOOD app file.

\section{Problem}\label{record-136-problem}

The Code Dojo baseline is enforceable, but the repository is not yet living at the standard. The remaining DOGFOOD block and capture surfaces still rely on unsafe casts, implicit string formatting, unchecked reads, and raw user-facing strings. They are also product-facing proof surfaces, so cleanup must preserve rendered behavior and lower-mode truth instead of applying mechanical lint silencing.

\section{Scope}\label{record-136-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Remove at least \texttt{5\allowbreak{}0} counted ESLint findings from the selected DOGFOOD block and capture cluster.
\item
  Prefer checked reads, local type guards, explicit \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{})} formatting, and precise return types over assertions.
\item
  Reduce touched raw DOGFOOD strings by removing non-user-facing literals, de-duplicating code tokens, or using catalog-backed lookups when product copy is actually touched.
\item
  Update measured baselines only after validation proves the new counts.
\item
  Update Code Dojo and changelog documentation with landed numbers.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-136-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Aggregate Code Dojo debt is \texttt{7\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}5} or lower.
\item
  ESLint baseline is \texttt{3\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}7} or lower.
\item
  Touched DOGFOOD i18n debt is reduced without adding new missing translations.
\item
  Touched files remain under their current file/context baselines.
\item
  Issue \#419, this design doc, and the pull request are cross-linked.
\end{itemize}

\part{Workflow and delivery}

\chapter{WF-001 --- Adopt the Legends/Cycles Workflow}\label{record-137}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/WF-001-adopt-cycle-workflow.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/WF-workflow-and-delivery.md}{WF --- Workflow and Delivery}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-137-why-this-cycle-exists}

Bijou has been mixing multiple planning models:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  roadmap milestones
\item
  strategy notes
\item
  specs
\item
  ad hoc backlog capture
\end{itemize}

That makes it harder for both humans and agents to tell:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  what is active
\item
  what is backlog
\item
  where design truth lives
\item
  where tests tied to a cycle should go
\end{itemize}

This cycle establishes the workflow itself as a first-class repo artifact.

\section{Human users}\label{record-137-human-users}

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-137-primary-human-user}

A maintainer or contributor who needs to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  capture ideas
\item
  pick the next piece of work
\item
  understand active design intent
\item
  see what tests belong to a cycle
\item
  record debt and follow-on work honestly
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-137-human-hill}

A human maintainer can open the repo and understand:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  what a legend is
\item
  what a cycle is
\item
  where backlog items live
\item
  where active design docs live
\item
  where cycle-specific tests live
\end{itemize}

without reverse-engineering tribal process from old roadmap prose.

\section{Agent users}\label{record-137-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-137-primary-agent-user}

A coding/design agent working inside the repo who needs to:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  discover the current planning model quickly
\item
  know where to place new design docs
\item
  know where to place cycle-owned tests
\item
  know which invariants must be linked and protected
\item
  know how to spawn backlog debt instead of silently drifting
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-137-agent-hill}

An agent can enter the repo and, with minimal context, place design, tests, backlog fallout, and changelog updates in the right locations without reinforcing the old \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p} drift.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-137-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer has a new idea.
\item
  They create one file in \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/}.
\item
  They decide to start the work.
\item
  They move that file into \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/}.
\item
  They enrich the cycle doc with hills, playbacks, invariants, and test intent.
\item
  They write failing tests under \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/} or the relevant cycle directory.
\item
  They land the work.
\item
  They record drift and spin out any debt into fresh backlog items.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Agent playback}\label{record-137-agent-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent reads \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/WORKFLOW.md}{Bijou Workflow}.
\item

\item
  The agent checks linked invariants.
\item
  The agent discovers the active cycle doc in \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/}.
\item

\chapter{WF-003 --- Replace smoke:examples:* With smoke:dogfood}\label{record-138}

\section{Sponsor human}\label{record-138-sponsor-human}

A maintainer preparing \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} and needing the repo's release smoke contract to match the repo's stated DOGFOOD-first docs posture.

\section{Sponsor agent}\label{record-138-sponsor-agent}

An agent that must answer, from repo artifacts alone:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  what release smoke actually runs before \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}
\item
  whether DOGFOOD or the broad \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/} tree is the public proving surface
\item
  which scripts and workflows witness that answer
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-138-hill}

The public \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} smoke contract now belongs to DOGFOOD.

The workspace scripts, release-readiness gauntlet, CI workflow, release-dry-run workflow, publish workflow, and release docs all agree that DOGFOOD is the release-facing smoke surface.

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-138-why-this-cycle-exists}

\href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-025-make-dogfood-the-only-human-facing-docs-surface.md}{DF-025} made the repo posture sharp: DOGFOOD, not \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}, is the only human-facing docs surface for \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}.

But the release contract was still lying:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} still exposed \texttt{s\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}*} as the main smoke family
\item
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s} still ran \texttt{s\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l}
\item
  CI, release dry-runs, and publish verification still fanned out the old examples lanes
\item
  repo docs still talked about moving smoke to DOGFOOD as future work
\end{itemize}

That meant the repo could teach one surface while releasing against another.

\subsection{Primary human user}\label{record-138-primary-human-user}

A maintainer or reviewer checking whether \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} is ready to release.

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-138-human-hill}

A human can inspect the package scripts, workflows, and release docs and see one coherent answer: DOGFOOD is the release-facing smoke surface.

\section{Agent users}\label{record-138-agent-users}

\subsection{Primary agent user}\label{record-138-primary-agent-user}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-138-agent-hill}

An agent can recover the DOGFOOD smoke contract from repo artifacts alone without guessing whether examples are still canonical.

\section{Decision}\label{record-138-decision}

\texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release smoke belongs to DOGFOOD, not the broad \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/} tree.

Bijou should therefore:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  expose DOGFOOD smoke as the public smoke family
\item
  run DOGFOOD smoke in local release readiness
\item
  fan DOGFOOD smoke out in CI and release workflows
\item
  describe example smoke as secondary/internal rather than release canonical
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}

\item

\item
  Update release docs, backlog/signpost docs, and examples posture docs so they stop describing DOGFOOD smoke as future work.
\item
  Promote \texttt{W\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3} into \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/} and prune the now-empty \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}/} lane again.

\section{Sponsor human}\label{record-139-sponsor-human}

A maintainer preparing the next public Bijou release.

\section{Sponsor agent}\label{record-139-sponsor-agent}

An agent that must answer, from repo artifacts alone:

\item

\item
  what is deferred

\section{Hill}\label{record-139-hill}

The next Bijou release is a deliberate, inspectable decision rather than an accretion of unreleased work.

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-139-why-this-cycle-exists}

Since \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, Bijou has accumulated a large and mixed wave of work:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  runtime engine architecture and implementation slices
\item
  humane shell behavior and shell introspection
\item
  DOGFOOD growth into a real proving surface
\item
  new localization packages and workflow tooling
\item
  design-language doctrine and reusable review surfaces
\item
  release, workflow, and repo-signpost hardening
\end{itemize}

That progress is real, but it created release ambiguity:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{[\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}]} in \texttt{C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} is not yet a clean \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D} release boundary
\item
  the repo had long-form release docs, but they still lived under \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/}
\item
  the workspace contains new i18n packages, but the automated npm publish matrix still only covers the older five published packages
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/method/graveyard/legacy-backlog/up-next/RE-007-migrate-framed-shell-onto-runtime-engine-seams.md}{RE-007} is important follow-on architecture work, but the repo had not yet answered whether it is a release blocker
\end{itemize}

This cycle exists to make those choices explicit.

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-139-agent-hill}

An agent can recover the next release boundary, version, and readiness criteria from the repo itself without relying on chat memory or vague interpretation of \texttt{[\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}]}.

  After reading this cycle and the release docs, can a maintainer explain why the next release is \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} instead of a patch or a new major?
\item
  Can a maintainer see that \texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}7} is explicitly deferred rather than silently assumed to be a blocker?
\item
  Can an agent find versioned long-form release docs in \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}/}?
\item
  Can a release operator name the unresolved blockers before tagging?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility / assistive reading posture}\label{record-139-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

This cycle is documentation-first. The important requirement is that the release shape remains legible in plain markdown and does not depend on tables, screenshots, or GitHub-specific UI to understand the decision.

\section{Localization / directionality posture}\label{record-139-localization-directionality-posture}

The release includes localization work, so the docs must not pretend that the repo is still English-only by design. The prose remains English for now, but the release shape must explicitly acknowledge the new i18n packages and the publish-matrix gap around them.

\section{Decision}\label{record-139-decision}

\subsection{Target version}\label{record-139-target-version}

The next release should be \textbf{\texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}}, stable.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{Why \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}}{Why }}\label{record-139-why-4.1.0}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the release has a strong additive feature story across multiple public surfaces
\item
  it is much larger than a patch release
\item
  it does not present a clear enough breaking boundary to justify \texttt{5\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}
\item
  it is the first release after \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} that turns Bijou from ``surface toolkit with a framed shell'' into a more coherent application/runtime platform
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{In scope for \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}}{In scope for }}\label{record-139-in-scope-for-4.1.0}

\subsubsection{Headline themes}\label{record-139-headline-themes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  runtime engine work through \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/RE-006-formalize-component-layout-and-interaction-contracts.md}{RE-006}
\item
  humane shell work through \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/HT-004-promote-explicit-layer-objects-and-richer-shell-introspection.md}{HT-004}
\item
  typed framed-shell and cleanup-capable command improvements through \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-001-type-framed-app-messages-and-updates-end-to-end.md}{DX-001} and \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DX-002-reconcile-cmd-typing-with-cleanup-and-effect-patterns.md}{DX-002}
\item
  DOGFOOD completion through \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/DF-019-raise-dogfood-coverage-floor-to-100-percent.md}{DF-019}
\item
  localization packages and localized shell/docs work through \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/LX-008-localize-shell-chrome-and-dogfood.md}{LX-008}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}7} decision}{ decision}}\label{record-139-re-007-decision}

\texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}7} is \textbf{not} a blocker for \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}.

It remains an important architectural follow-on, but waiting for it would blur a coherent and already substantial release behind one more runtime slice. \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} should ship the runtime-engine story through \texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}6} and then let \texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}7} become follow-on work for the next line.

\section{Hill}\label{record-140-hill}

The \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} i18n package story is no longer ambiguous.

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-140-why-this-cycle-exists}

\href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/WF-004-shape-the-next-release.md}{WF-004} made \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} an explicit, inspectable release decision, but it also surfaced a real contradiction:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the workspace and long-form release docs already treated the i18n packages as part of the \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} story
\item
  the automated publish workflows still only packed and published the older five-package surface
\end{itemize}

That meant the repo could not honestly answer a simple question:

Are the i18n packages part of the public \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release or not?

This cycle exists to close that gap in code, docs, and tests.

\section{Decision}\label{record-140-decision}

The four i18n packages are part of the planned public \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release.

Bijou should therefore:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  pack them in the tag publish verification workflow
\item
  dry-run publish them in the release dry-run workflow
\item
  publish them from the real tag-driven npm workflow
\item
  describe them as real \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release artifacts in repo docs
\end{itemize}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-141-why-this-cycle-exists}

\href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/WF-004-shape-the-next-release.md}{WF-004} chose \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, and \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/WF-005-close-4-1-0-i18n-publish-surface-gap.md}{WF-005} closed the i18n publish-surface gap.

But the short-form release surfaces were still drifting:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the root \texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} still led with a \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} ``What's New'' section
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} still treated \texttt{[\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}]} as a vague bucket instead of an explicit \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D} release slice
\item
  the compare links still implied \texttt{v\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} was the previous release
\item
  \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} itself never got a dedicated changelog section
\end{itemize}

That meant the repo had long-form release docs but still lacked an honest short-form release cut.

\subsection{Boundary decision}\label{record-141-boundary-decision}

The current \texttt{[\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}]} section is the planned \texttt{4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release slice.
