\chapter{WF-009 - Keep Release PRs Under Automated Review File Limits}\label{record-142}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/WF-009-keep-release-prs-under-automated-review-file-limits.md}\par}\smallskip

Legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/WF-workflow-and-delivery.md}{WF - Workflow and Delivery}

\section{Sponsor human}\label{record-142-sponsor-human}

A maintainer preparing release-boundary work that may span many packages, docs, examples, tests, and backlog notes.

\section{Sponsor agent}\label{record-142-sponsor-agent}

An agent executing the METHOD loop through pull, implementation, commit, push, PR, and merge without producing a PR too large for automated review.

\section{Hill}\label{record-142-hill}

Release-boundary work is sliced into reviewer-sized PRs before the final release sync, so automated review, CI, and human inspection all see bounded changes.

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-142-why-this-cycle-exists}

CodeRabbit skipped PR \#65 because the diff exceeded its 150-file cap. PR \#69 also reached the danger zone: the local pre-push hook warned about 23 commits, and CodeRabbit selected 149 files for processing.

The issue is not that large releases are bad. The issue is that a large release must be composed from smaller reviewable precursor PRs instead of arriving as one oversized branch.

\section{Playback questions}\label{record-142-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Can an operator identify when a release branch must be split before PR?
\item
  Can an agent choose the next release-boundary slice without relying on chat memory?
\item
  Can a reviewer see whether a PR is intentionally a precursor slice or a final release sync?
\item
  Can the final release PR stay mostly about version, changelog, long-form release docs, and release validation rather than hiding unrelated features?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility / assistive reading posture}\label{record-142-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

This is workflow documentation. It must remain useful in plain markdown, terminal readers, MCP document summaries, and copied text. The policy uses short numbered rules instead of relying on diagrams.

\section{Localization / directionality posture}\label{record-142-localization-directionality-posture}

No localized runtime behavior changes. The guidance should avoid idioms that make the release process harder to translate later.

\section{Agent inspectability / explainability posture}\label{record-142-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

The slicing threshold and required response live in repo docs, not chat memory:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/WORKFLOW.md}{docs/WORKFLOW.md}
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/release.md}{docs/release.md}
\item
  this cycle doc
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-goals}\label{record-142-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  changing branch protection
\item
  disabling CodeRabbit
\item
  forcing every tiny fix into its own PR
\item
  tagging or publishing \texttt{v\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}
\end{itemize}

\section{Decision}\label{record-142-decision}

Bijou release work should use precursor PRs whenever a branch is likely to exceed automated review limits.

The practical thresholds are:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  hard stop: more than 140 changed files before opening a PR
\item
  caution: more than 10 commits on one branch
\item
  caution: unrelated legends or cycle families mixed in one branch
\item
  caution: generated snapshots or docs mixed with unrelated runtime changes
\end{itemize}

When a threshold is hit, split by cycle or product surface:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  runtime engine
\item
  TUI shell and interaction
\item
  core components
\item
  DOGFOOD and docs proof
\item
  backlog/release-lane bookkeeping
\item
  release version/changelog/tag prep
\end{itemize}

The final release PR should be boring. It should primarily contain version bump, changelog, release docs, release-readiness proof, and any final metadata adjustments that cannot land earlier.

\section{Implementation outline}\label{record-142-implementation-outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Add PR sizing discipline to the short workflow guide.
\item
  Add release-boundary slicing guidance to the release process.
\item
  Update stale release facts while editing the release process so the docs point at \texttt{v\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} as the next shaping lane.
\item
  Keep the v6 backlog lane linked to this pulled cycle.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests / validation}\label{record-142-tests-validation}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}
\item
  \texttt{g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k}
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-142-retrospective}

Closed by documenting PR slicing thresholds in the workflow guide, adding release-boundary sizing rules to the release process, and updating stale release posture from \texttt{v\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} to \texttt{v\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}.

\chapter{WF-122 - Cross-Platform Contributor Path}\label{record-143}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/WF-122-cross-platform-contributor-path.md}\par}\smallskip

Linked issues: \#122, \#135, \#136

Linked legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/WF-workflow-and-delivery.md}{WF - Workflow and Delivery}

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-143-sponsor-human}

A TypeScript contributor on macOS, Linux, or Windows who wants the core Bijou build and test path to work without first installing a Unix shell.

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-143-sponsor-agent}

A workflow verification agent that can inspect CI, package scripts, and local commands to prove which parts of the repo are portable and which are intentionally platform-hosted.

\section{Hill}\label{record-143-hill}

Bijou's contributor-facing scripts are Node-first, and CI proves the core build and focused unit-test path on at least one non-Linux platform.

\section{Scope}\label{record-143-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Replace avoidable Bash and POSIX shell usage in root contributor scripts.
\item
  Add a non-Linux CI lane for build, typecheck, and focused unit tests.
\item
  Document which workflows remain Linux/Bash-hosted because they are release, benchmark, or terminal-capture lanes rather than the first contributor path.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-143-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Can a Windows contributor run the core root scripts without WSL-only shell behavior?
\item
  Does CI prove at least one non-Linux build/typecheck/unit lane?
\item
  Can a reviewer tell which remaining Bash paths are intentional workflow infrastructure?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Reading Posture}\label{record-143-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

The docs must name the platform support posture plainly in README and CONTRIBUTING without hiding it in workflow YAML.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-143-localization-directionality-posture}

No runtime localization changes.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-143-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

The proof lives in \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}l}, script source, and \texttt{w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t} output.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-143-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Contributor-facing commands should be portable when Node can provide the same behavior.
\item
  Platform-specific shell remains acceptable for release and benchmark lanes when the host choice is explicit.
\end{itemize}

\section{Decisions}\label{record-143-decisions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n} becomes \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s} and removes workspace \texttt{d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/} directories plus workspace \texttt{.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o} files without shell globs.
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} becomes \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s}, preserving the existing workspace version bump and internal dependency pinning behavior.
\item
  CI keeps the full supported Node 20/22 lane on Ubuntu and adds Node 22 focused unit coverage on macOS and Windows.
\item
  The repository development floor is \texttt{\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} after the Vitest 4.1 toolchain moved through Vite 8/Rolldown APIs that cannot start on Node 18 or earlier 20/22 minors.
\item
  Existing release, publish, benchmark, retry, and hook shell scripts remain explicit shell-owned infrastructure. They are not the Day 0 contributor path.
\end{itemize}

\section{Verification}\label{record-143-verification}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s}
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t}
\item
  focused CI-equivalent unit tests listed in \texttt{.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}l}
\end{itemize}

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-143-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}

\chapter{WF-123 - Issues-First Method Intake}\label{record-144}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/WF-123-issues-first-method-intake.md}\par}\smallskip

Linked issues: \#123, \#124, \#153

Linked legend: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/WF-workflow-and-delivery.md}{WF - Workflow and Delivery}

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-144-sponsor-human}

A Bijou maintainer or contributor who needs to propose, triage, and follow work without learning the historical filesystem backlog first.

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-144-sponsor-agent}

A Method bookkeeping agent that must keep GitHub Issues, labels, design docs, witness evidence, retros, changelog notes, and PR closure references aligned.

\section{Hill}\label{record-144-hill}

Bijou uses GitHub Issues as the live work tracker while keeping repository docs as the durable evidence ledger for designs, witnesses, retros, and shipped history.

\section{Why This Cycle Exists}\label{record-144-why-this-cycle-exists}

The deep-dive audit found that the old backlog-first docs made Day 0 contributors and agents read historical planning files before they could tell where active work lives. The Method direction has changed: raw intake belongs in GitHub Issues, and labels carry live tracker state.

Bijou should follow that model without deleting historical evidence.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-144-playback-questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Can a contributor open one GitHub issue and understand which labels describe lane, type, priority, and legend?
\item
  Can a maintainer see that \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/}, \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}/}, and \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}/} are evidence and archive surfaces, not the first intake path?
\item
  Can an agent distinguish live issue state from historical repo files during context recovery?
\item
  Can a PR still point to design, witness, retro, changelog, and issue evidence after implementation work lands?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Reading Posture}\label{record-144-accessibility-assistive-reading-posture}

The guidance must remain plain Markdown with short tables and direct issue template references. The important reader task is deciding where to open or triage work, not parsing a process essay.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-144-localization-directionality-posture}

This is repository workflow documentation. No runtime localization behavior changes.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-144-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

The live state is inspectable through GitHub issue labels. Repo files remain inspectable evidence:

  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/} for shaped cycle intent

\end{itemize}

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-144-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}

\item
  Labels are tracker metadata; issue body and PR evidence carry the narrative.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{WF-125 Draft-first cycle start workflow}\label{record-145}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/WF-125-draft-first-cycle-start-workflow.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: WF-125 Draft-first cycle start workflow
legend: WF
lane: design
priority: medium
keywords:
  - workflow
  - method
  - draft-pr
  - design-thinking

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-145-framing}

Issue \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/279}{\#279} changes the Bijou cycle loop from ``open the pull request at ship time'' to ``open a draft pull request at cycle start.'' The intent is to make issue, branch, design doc, and PR state visible before implementation expands, while keeping the final ready-for-review and merge gates strict.

The work follows a Design Thinking loop:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  observe that cycle work can stay invisible until late implementation
\item
  frame draft PRs as early coordination artifacts rather than merge-ready review artifacts
\item
  prototype the new loop in Method, Workflow, Contributor, Agent, and issue template docs
\item
  prove the policy with a workflow regression that reads those docs
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-145-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Maintainers who need early visibility into the branch and linked artifacts.
\item
  Contributors who need one explicit start-of-cycle checklist.
\item
  Agents that need a deterministic order for sync, branch, shape, push, draft PR, and work-in-progress labeling.
\item
  Reviewers who should see draft context early without treating it as ready.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-145-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A contributor can start a cycle by syncing the merge target, creating a \texttt{c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}>} branch, shaping the issue and design doc, committing and pushing that shape, opening a draft PR, and applying \texttt{w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  A reviewer can distinguish an early draft coordination PR from a ready PR that has passed implementation, validation, and self-review.
\item
  A maintainer can run one workflow regression that prevents the docs and issue template from drifting back to the old ``PR only at ship'' loop.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-145-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does every workflow surface say to run \texttt{g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h} and sync the merge target before branching?
\item
  Does the cycle branch start from the synced target instead of stale local state?
\item
  Does the shaping commit include the GitHub Issue and design doc before implementation work begins?
\item
  Does a draft PR to \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n} exist before implementation starts?
\item
  Does the issue carry \texttt{w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s} while the branch or draft PR is actively carrying it?
\item
  Does the draft PR move to ready only after implementation, validation, and self-review?
\end{itemize}

\section{Workflow Contract}\label{record-145-workflow-contract}

\begin{CodeBlock}
git fetch
sync merge target branch
checkout cycle/<cycle_name>
write or update GitHub Issue
write docs/design/<cycle>.md
stage + commit + push shaping artifact
open draft PR to main
link issue + design doc + draft PR
apply work-in-progress to issue
do RED/GREEN cycle work
validate + self-review
mark PR ready for review
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Implementation Notes}\label{record-145-implementation-notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{A\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} owns the short agent recovery protocol.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} owns the doctrine and cycle-state diagram.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} owns the operator checklist.
\item
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} owns contributor-facing expectations.
\item
  \texttt{.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}l} owns the issue-form acceptance text.
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} freezes the contract.
\end{itemize}

\section{Tests}\label{record-145-tests}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} adds a regression that reads \texttt{A\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and the Method work-item issue template.
\item
  The RED pass failed because \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} did not contain the new \texttt{g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h} and draft-PR cycle-start language.
\item
  The GREEN pass updates the docs and normalizes Markdown whitespace in the regression so wrapped prose can still carry exact policy sentences.
\end{itemize}

\section{Closeout}\label{record-145-closeout}

The cycle is landed when:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the workflow docs require merge-target sync before branching
\item
  the workflow docs require a draft PR to \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n} at cycle start
\item
  the issue template requires issue, design doc, and draft PR links
\item
  the draft PR is marked ready only after implementation, validation, and self-review
\item
  the WF-001 regression, docs inventory, lint, and whitespace checks pass
\item
  the pull request closes \#279
\end{itemize}

\section{Framing}\label{record-146-framing}

GitHub is the live tracker for Bijou work. After the V7 Product Truth closeout, the post-merge Codex review follow-up, and this tracker-sync cleanup, the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} milestone should be issue-complete: zero open milestone items and twenty-seven closed milestone items.

The repository mirrors did not fully follow that state. \texttt{B\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{R\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and the WF-126 regression still describe the pre-merge V7 closeout with \#245, \#246, and \#281 as open work. That creates the exact tracker/docs drift the Method calls out as bad code.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-146-sponsored-users}

\chapter{WF-128 Safe GitHub Comments And Milestone Item Mirrors}\label{record-147}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/WF-128-safe-gh-comments-and-milestone-items.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: WF-128 Safe GitHub Comments And Milestone Item Mirrors
legend: WF
lane: bad-code
priority: medium
issues:
  - https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/287
  - https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/288
keywords:
  - github
  - comments
  - roadmap
  - milestone
  - workflow

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-147-framing}

Two small workflow defects came out of the V7 closeout:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  review comments can be corrupted when Markdown literals are passed through a shell-interpolated \texttt{g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}"\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}"} argument
\item
  roadmap release snapshots can be misread when GitHub milestone totals include pull requests as milestone items while nearby prose says ``issues''
\end{itemize}

Both are process bugs. They do not change runtime behavior, but they do affect the reliability of review evidence and release bookkeeping.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-147-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer posting self-review, Code Lawyer, or activity-summary comments needs a command pattern that preserves Markdown literally.
\item
  A release maintainer reading \texttt{R\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} needs to know whether the snapshot counts GitHub milestone items or issue-only rows.
\item
  A review agent needs executable repo tests that catch unsafe comment examples and ambiguous milestone-count language before the pattern spreads.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-147-hill}

A maintainer can post Markdown-heavy GitHub comments and reconcile release snapshot rows without relying on memory: \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} state the safe conventions, and WF-128 tests prove those conventions stay visible.

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-147-current-truth}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Issue \#287 records that a PR \#284 self-review comment was polluted when Markdown backticks inside a double-quoted \texttt{-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}y} argument were evaluated by the shell.
\item
  Issue \#288 records that V7 tracker-sync work had to count milestone PRs \#278 and \#280 to match GitHub milestone totals.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} do not currently name the \texttt{-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} / literal-heredoc path for review comments.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} says GitHub milestones and issue labels are live tracker state, but the release snapshot columns are named only \texttt{O\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n} and \texttt{C\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}, which makes item counts look like issue-only counts.
\end{itemize}

\section{Product Shape}\label{record-147-product-shape}

\subsection{Safe Comment Posting}\label{record-147-safe-comment-posting}

\begin{CodeBlock}
Workflow review step
  self-review / Code Lawyer / activity summary
    |
    v
  gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --body-file - <<'EOF'
  Markdown stays literal:
  - `commands`
  - $()
  - tables
  EOF
\end{CodeBlock}

The rule is intentionally boring: if a GitHub comment body contains Markdown, commands, backticks, \texttt{\$\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, tables, or copied review output, post it through \texttt{-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e} with a quoted heredoc or a real file.

\begin{CodeBlock}
GitHub milestone page / API
  open milestone items   = issues + pull requests assigned to milestone
  closed milestone items = issues + pull requests assigned to milestone

ROADMAP release snapshot
  Open Items / Closed Items
  Completed lineage includes milestone PR rows when PRs contribute to totals.
\end{CodeBlock}

\chapter{WF-129 Path-Gate DOGFOOD CI}\label{record-148}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/WF-129-path-gate-dogfood-ci.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: WF-129 Path-Gate DOGFOOD CI
legend: WF
lane: bad-code
priority: medium
issue: https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/293
keywords:
  - ci
  - dogfood
  - path-gates
  - iteration-time
  - workflow

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-148-framing}

The CI loop is intentionally conservative, but ordinary workflow/documentation PRs currently run DOGFOOD-heavy gates even when they do not touch DOGFOOD, runtime components, localization, or CI scripts. That makes rapid-fire cycles pay duplicate install/build/smoke costs before review can close.

This cycle adds a CI change classifier so DOGFOOD-specific checks run when they are relevant and skip when a PR is unrelated to DOGFOOD. Pushes to \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n} and tag workflows remain full-strength.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-148-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  A maintainer iterating on workflow documentation needs PR CI to avoid DOGFOOD smoke work when the branch cannot affect DOGFOOD.
\item
  A release maintainer needs \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n} pushes and tags to continue running the full DOGFOOD proof path.
\item
  A review agent needs the path-gating contract to be visible in the workflow file and covered by a regression test.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-148-hill}

A contributor can open a PR that only changes non-DOGFOOD docs or workflow bookkeeping and see DOGFOOD-heavy CI lanes skipped, while any PR touching DOGFOOD, packages, localization, DOGFOOD scripts/tests, or CI workflows still runs DOGFOOD proof.

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-148-current-truth}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h} runs DOGFOOD i18n, test typecheck, full Vitest, and interactive example smoke before every push.
\item
  \texttt{.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}l} runs DOGFOOD coverage and i18n policy inside the Ubuntu Node 22 \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t} job for every PR.
\item
  \texttt{.\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}l} runs separate DOGFOOD landing/docs smoke jobs for every PR, with their own checkout, install, and build.
\item
  The latest main CI run after PR \#291 had a \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})} critical path just under two minutes, plus separate DOGFOOD smoke jobs.
\end{itemize}

\section{Product Shape}\label{record-148-product-shape}

\subsection{CI Classifier}\label{record-148-ci-classifier}

\begin{CodeBlock}
CI
  changes
    dogfood = true on main pushes and tags
    dogfood = true on PRs touching:
      .github/workflows/**
      package.json
      package-lock.json
      packages/**
      examples/docs/**
      scripts/dogfood-*
      scripts/smoke-dogfood*
      tests/cycles/DF-*
      tests/cycles/*dogfood*
      docs/DOGFOOD.md
      docs/design/DF-*
      docs/legends/DF-*
      docs/method/legends/DF-*
\end{CodeBlock}

\subsection{Gated DOGFOOD Proof}\label{record-148-gated-dogfood-proof}

\begin{CodeBlock}
test (22)
  always: build, lint, npm test
  when dogfood-relevant: DOGFOOD coverage + DOGFOOD i18n policy

Smoke DOGFOOD (landing/docs)
  when dogfood-relevant: run checkout, install, build, and smoke command
  otherwise: keep check names present and skip expensive smoke steps
\end{CodeBlock}

\section{Runtime And API Contract}\label{record-148-runtime-and-api-contract}

This cycle changes CI workflow behavior only. It does not change package APIs, runtime behavior, DOGFOOD rendering, localization catalogs, or release workflows.

\section{Lower Modes}\label{record-148-lower-modes}

No TUI output changes are included.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist

  Static mode: not applicable.
\item
  Pipe mode: not applicable.
\item
  Accessible mode: not applicable.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{WF-130 Roadmap Goalpost Policy}\label{record-149}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/WF-130-roadmap-goalpost-policy.md}\par}\smallskip

\section{Linked Legend}\label{record-149-linked-legend}

WF - Workflow and Delivery

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-149-decision-summary}

Adopt a Bijou roadmap planning system that maps GitHub milestone items into versioned releases, candidate goalposts, umbrella issues, user-story issues, slice budgets, release gates, and proof requirements.

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-149-sponsor-human}

A maintainer wants to see the current release path and backlog shape without reconstructing it from memory, stale Markdown, and raw GitHub lists, so that release planning can stay issue-backed and inspectable.

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-149-sponsor-agent}

An agent needs a documented roadmap hierarchy and issue-template fields so it can classify work as ordinary issues, goalpost umbrellas, or user stories without inventing planning structure in each turn.

\section{Hill}\label{record-149-hill}

By the end of this cycle, Bijou has a release-packet policy, a GitHub-backed roadmap snapshot, issue-template fields for roadmap roles and slice budgets, and tests that prevent the docs from drifting back to draft-first cycle language.

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-149-current-truth}

Verified against \texttt{o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n} on 2026-06-06 after PR \#304 merged.

Current anchors:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  GitHub milestone \texttt{v\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}: 0 open, 30 closed milestone items.
\item
  GitHub milestone \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}: 0 open, 27 closed milestone items.
\item
  GitHub milestone \texttt{B\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d}: 29 open, 1 closed milestone item.
\item
  Open unmilestoned issues: \#249 and \#306.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} is a stub.
\item
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{A\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and WF-001 tests still describe draft-first cycle PRs.
\end{itemize}

\section{Problem}\label{record-149-problem}

Bijou has strong issue intake and cycle docs, but it lacks the intermediate roadmap structure that explains how individual issues become release-scale goalposts. The docs also contain stale draft-first language that conflicts with current repo instructions.

\section{Scope}\label{record-149-scope}

This cycle includes:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  defining the release-packet contract under \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}
\item
  refreshing \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} from live GitHub milestone and issue data
\item
  grouping the open Beyond backlog into candidate goalposts
\item
  adding roadmap role, linkage, slice budget, and release-gate fields to the Method work-item issue form
\item
  aligning operator docs to non-draft PRs at cycle start
\item
  adding tests that prove the policy and the non-draft alignment
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-149-non-goals}

This cycle does not:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  create new release milestones
\item
  move GitHub issues between milestones
\item
  create umbrella issues for the candidate goalposts
\item
  close or rewrite the existing Beyond issues
\item
  implement any product features from the candidate goalposts
\end{itemize}

\chapter{WF-131 Roadmap Forward-Looking Refresh}\label{record-150}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/WF-131-roadmap-current-reality-refresh.md}\par}\smallskip

\section{Linked Legend}\label{record-150-linked-legend}

WF - Workflow and Delivery

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-150-decision-summary}

Refresh \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} so they describe the forward post-\texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release horizon instead of implying the complete \texttt{v\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} and \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} milestone lanes still need release-readiness work before tagging. The refresh now also selects the forward train: \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} next, no planned feature \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, \texttt{v\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} for the Runtime Graph and Scene IR product contract, and \texttt{v\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} for Product Workbench and operator surfaces.

\section{Sponsor Human}\label{record-150-sponsor-human}

A maintainer noticed that the roadmap felt significantly outdated and asked for it to reflect current reality.

\section{Sponsor Agent}\label{record-150-sponsor-agent}

An agent needs the roadmap to distinguish live tracker truth from historical release lineage so it can select the next slice without treating already complete zero-open release lanes as active release targets.

\section{Hill}\label{record-150-hill}

By the end of this cycle, the roadmap names \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} as the latest shipped public release, records that \texttt{v\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} was skipped as a public package release, treats complete milestone lanes as lineage, selects \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} as the next public release target, says there is no planned \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} feature train, organizes \texttt{v\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} and \texttt{v\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, surfaces unmilestoned triage and open pull requests, and preserves deterministic tests for the GitHub-backed counts.

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-150-current-truth}

Verified against GitHub on 2026-06-13.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Latest public release tag: \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}.
\item
  \texttt{v\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} was skipped as a public package release; its zero-open milestone lane is complete tracker lineage.
\item
  GitHub milestone \texttt{v\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}: 0 open, 30 closed milestone items.
\item
  GitHub milestone \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}: 0 open, 27 closed milestone items.
\item

\end{itemize}

\section{Problem}\label{record-150-problem}

The roadmap's numerical snapshot was recently synced, but the surrounding release narrative still read as if V7 had not shipped and as if v6/v7 release-readiness validation remained the next release-facing action. It also spent too much space on past milestone inventory when the useful work now is choosing the next release candidate from \texttt{B\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d}. That contradicts \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, which already names \texttt{7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} as the latest shipped release and says the older v6/v7 milestones are retained as lineage.

\section{Status}\label{record-151-status}

  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}f} for release workflow readiness.
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}f} for DOGFOOD docs-surface coverage.
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}x} for localization debt and scanner behavior.
\end{itemize}

\section{Sponsors}\label{record-151-sponsors}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Human sponsor: James Ross.
\item
  Agent sponsor: Codex.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-151-hill}

Before \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} is cut, release readiness should be inspectable as a milestone-specific report and DOGFOOD i18n debt should cover newly added docs modules by default.

\section{Problem}\label{record-151-problem}

The repo already has \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s}, but the command is mostly a validation gauntlet. It does not produce a milestone-aware readiness report that proves tracker closure, WIP-label cleanup, release-document posture, and package smoke coverage before a release tag.

The DOGFOOD i18n debt ratchet also depends on a hand-maintained source list. New \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} modules can introduce visible strings without participating in the debt baseline.

\section{Scope}\label{record-151-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Keep \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s} as the single release readiness command.
\item
  Add an optional milestone report mode that can be run before tagging, for example \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}.
\item
  Classify tracker, docs, release-packet, and package-smoke readiness using deterministic fixture-testable data.
\item
  Discover DOGFOOD TypeScript debt sources from \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} by default, with documented exclusions for tooling-only files.
\item
  Preserve per-surface i18n debt counts so ratchet output stays actionable.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-151-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Do not move broad V8/V9 product work into \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}.
\item
  Do not require GitHub access for the default no-argument local gauntlet.
\item
  Do not replace the GitHub release dry-run workflow; the local report should point to the existing workflow boundary.
\item
  Do not burn down the current DOGFOOD raw-string debt in this cycle.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-151-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} explain why a release is or is not ready before running expensive local gates?

  Can a new \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} module introduce visible copy without increasing the DOGFOOD i18n debt ratchet?
\item
  Are remaining release-process gaps documented instead of silently implied?
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility / Assistive Posture}\label{record-151-accessibility-assistive-posture}

No runtime UI accessibility behavior changes. The new readiness report is plain text plus a Markdown table so it can be copied into release PRs and read by terminal or screen-reader workflows.

\section{Localization / Directionality Posture}\label{record-151-localization-directionality-posture}

\#312 directly strengthens localization guardrails. It does not localize existing raw DOGFOOD copy; it makes the current raw-string debt baseline honest across newly discovered DOGFOOD modules.

\section{Agent Inspectability / Explainability Posture}\label{record-151-agent-inspectability-explainability-posture}

The release-readiness report classifies each gate as pass/fail with a concise summary. The i18n debt scanner continues to report counts by source surface so agents can identify which DOGFOOD module moved the ratchet.

\section{Linked Invariants}\label{record-151-linked-invariants}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Release tags require issue-complete tracker posture and release evidence.
\item
  DOGFOOD visible strings must either be cataloged, counted as known debt, or explicitly excluded as non-product tooling.
\item

\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-152-hill}

Before \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} ships, Bijou's development dependency graph should resolve the patched \texttt{e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}@\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1} release so GitHub and npm audit no longer report the known \texttt{e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}@\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} security advisories.

\section{Problem}\label{record-152-problem}

\texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t} reports the lockfile-resolved \texttt{e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}@\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} package against two GitHub advisories:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{G\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r} (\texttt{h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h}), patched in \texttt{0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1}.
\item
  \texttt{G\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r} (\texttt{l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w}), patched in \texttt{0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1}.
\end{itemize}

The package is present through development tooling, not Bijou runtime API:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}@\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}4} accepts \texttt{e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}@\allowbreak{}\textasciitilde{}\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}.
\item
  \texttt{v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}@\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}8} pulls \texttt{v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}@\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}6}, whose optional peer accepts \texttt{e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}@\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}.
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope}\label{record-152-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Update the package lock so \texttt{e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d} resolves to \texttt{0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1}.
\item
  Avoid broad package churn or unrelated runtime dependency changes.
\item
  Record the security patch in the unreleased changelog.
\item
  Keep \texttt{v\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} bounded: this is an urgent dependency-security repair, not a new feature slice.
\end{itemize}

\tightlist
\item
  Issue: \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/364}{\#364}

\item

\end{itemize}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-153-decision-summary}

\texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o} made the standards debt visible and ratcheted, but the ESLint debt is still the dominant exception class. The stored ESLint ceiling is \texttt{5\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}5}, while a live type-aware ESLint run on \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n} reports \texttt{5\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}1} findings. The first cleanup pass should convert that already observed shrink plus targeted high-yield fixes into a lower enforceable ceiling.

This cycle deliberately starts with bounded test and tooling clusters instead of broad DOGFOOD example rewrites. The DOGFOOD files also carry localization and code-size tripwires, so they need their own carefully shaped pass.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-153-sponsored-human}

A maintainer wants the new standards posture to burn down real lint debt now, not merely document it as a future aspiration.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-153-sponsored-agent}

An agent needs a concrete first ratchet target with inspectable before/after counts, so later cycles can keep reducing the ceiling without guessing which violations are already paid down.

\section{Hill}\label{record-153-hill}

Reduce live type-aware ESLint findings from \texttt{5\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}1} to at most \texttt{4\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0}, then continue the same bounded cleanup pass to at most \texttt{4\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0} when the first target is comfortably met. Lower the official ESLint and aggregate Code Dojo debt ceilings so future work cannot regain the cleaned-up violations.

\section{Scope}\label{record-153-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Target high-yield ESLint clusters first:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    docs-preview tests under \texttt{s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
  \item
    app-frame tests under \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
  \item
    single-rule test files such as \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
  \end{itemize}
\item
  Prefer typed test helpers and guard functions over repeated casts.
\item
  Update \texttt{s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} to the new live count and per-rule counts.
\item
  Update \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} and the \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}x} ceiling.
\item
  Keep the aggregate debt reduction at least 50 violations below the current \texttt{5\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}8} ceiling.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-153-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Do not soften, disable, or narrow ESLint rules.
\item
  Do not raise any Code Dojo ceiling.
\item
  Do not mix unrelated product behavior changes into the cleanup.
\item
  Do not tackle DOGFOOD mega-file refactors in this first pass unless a touched file's policy requires it.
\item
  Do not try to clear all ESLint debt in one oversized branch.
\end{itemize}

This cycle mostly pays down static-analysis debt in already covered surfaces. When a cleanup changes runtime behavior or helper contracts, add a focused regression test before the fix. For purely type-safety rewrites, the RED signal is the existing ESLint finding and the GREEN signal is the lowered live ESLint count plus the relevant existing focused suite.

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-154-decision-summary}

\texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o} made the standards debt enforceable. WF-134 proved the ratchet can burn down real violations, but \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n} still has thousands of counted exceptions. This cycle raises the bar from minimum 50-count goalpost reductions to a 1000-count burndown pass.

The long-term goal is uncompromising:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  zero ESLint errors
\item
  zero Code Dojo warnings, errors, or issues
\item
  zero files violating length restrictions
\end{itemize}

This cycle is not allowed to move that goalpost by weakening rules, excluding files, or raising baselines.

\section{Sponsored Human}\label{record-154-sponsored-human}

A maintainer wants the repository to stop treating the standards as symbolic and make a visible move toward real compliance.

\section{Sponsored Agent}\label{record-154-sponsored-agent}

An agent needs a concrete large burndown target, live count evidence, and clear guardrails so cleanup work stays reviewable instead of becoming a broad semantic rewrite.

\section{Hill}\label{record-154-hill}

Reduce aggregate Code Dojo debt from \texttt{4\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}0} to \texttt{3\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}0} or lower with real cleanup. Lower the official ratchet ceilings to the new live counts so future work cannot regain the violations.

\section{Scope}\label{record-154-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Target high-yield, mechanically reviewable ESLint clusters first:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    non-null assertions that can become local guards or reusable helpers
  \item
    unsafe \texttt{a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}y} and unsafe assertion clusters in tests and scripts
  \item
    template-expression findings with explicit string formatting
  \item
    stale async wrappers and unused values where the fix is local
  \end{itemize}
\item
  Reduce file/context debt when touched files exceed the current threshold.
\item
  Keep changes clustered by surface so validation can be focused.
\item
  Update \texttt{s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} only after live counts prove the reduction.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-154-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Do not disable, soften, or narrow ESLint rules.
\item
  Do not raise any Code Dojo ceiling.
\item
  Do not exclude files from Code Dojo or ESLint.
\item
  Do not make risky product behavior changes for static-analysis convenience.
\item
  Do not split mega-files purely by line count unless the ownership boundary is obvious and tests can cover the move.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-154-retrospective}

Completed with a measured aggregate Code Dojo debt reduction from \texttt{4\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}0} to \texttt{2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}8} (\texttt{-\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}2}). The stored ESLint baseline now records \texttt{1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}6} live findings, down from \texttt{4\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}7} (\texttt{-\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}1}), and the next aggregate target is \texttt{2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8} or lower. Follow-on passes covered mechanically reviewable clusters across tests, scripts, examples, MCP docs, DOGFOOD, app-frame surfaces, render/surface helpers, table/markdown parsing, geometry, benchmarks, runtime helpers, i18n helpers, and TUI input/action surfaces.

The latest pass removed app-frame action/input-shell assertion debt, bench CLI formatting debt, focus-map text formatting debt, key parser regex/assertion debt, and node style test regex debt. Touched file/context budgets stayed below their stored ceilings, two file/context exceptions have been removed, and the latest app-frame core/overlay pass removed retained-layout non-null assertions, shell-command handler narrowing casts, combo-key formatting debt, and framed-app runtime bridge assertions. The binding cluster then removed runtime brand casts, unchecked generic snapshot casts, descriptor clone assertions, and unchecked fixture casts from the core binding contract and tests. The runtime/schema cluster removed TUI runtime binding brand casts, command dispatch narrowing debt, schema-block brand casts, schema bind-output assertions, and extracted inert schema data cloning into a focused helper.

\section{Scope}\label{record-161-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Replace non-null assertions, unsafe assertions, \texttt{a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}y} escapes, unchecked dynamic reads, and implicit interpolation with typed helpers, checked reads, explicit formatting, or narrowed runtime guards.

\item
  Preserve DOGFOOD docs/example runtime behavior.
\item
  Lower \texttt{s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} only after live counts prove the reduction.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-161-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}

  ESLint rules, Code Dojo thresholds, hooks, and CI policy must not weaken.

\section{Scope}\label{record-163-scope}

\section{Context}\label{record-165-context}

WF-145 landed the Respecting the Dojo burndown at \texttt{1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}3} aggregate Code Dojo violations. The next ratchet must cut at least \texttt{5\allowbreak{}0} more violations and set the ceiling to \texttt{1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}3} or lower.

The active objective remains zero ESLint errors, zero Code Dojo warnings/errors/issues, and zero length-restriction violations. This cycle is a bounded cleanup slice toward that endpoint.

\section{Goal}\label{record-165-goal}

Reduce aggregate Code Dojo debt from \texttt{1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}3} to \texttt{1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}3} or lower by eliminating at least \texttt{5\allowbreak{}0} live findings with behavior-preserving TypeScript fixes.

Implementation should choose the highest-yield slice that can pass the focused Code Dojo and DOGFOOD gates without weakening standards. If DOGFOOD docs files are touched, visible-copy policy failures are part of the work rather than an excuse to raise baselines.

\section{Scope}\label{record-165-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Replace unsafe assertions, non-null assertions, unchecked dynamic reads, fake async commands, stale unused values, and implicit interpolation with typed helpers, checked reads, explicit formatting, or narrowed runtime guards.
\item
  Preserve DOGFOOD docs behavior, package runtime behavior, and public APIs.
\item
  Lower ratchet artifacts only after live counts prove the reduction.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-165-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  ESLint rules, Code Dojo thresholds, hooks, and CI policy must not weaken.
\item
  File/context, mock-ban, and code-size ceilings must not rise.
\item
  DOGFOOD visible-copy cleanup is in scope only for files deliberately touched by the selected slice.
\item
  Exception churn cannot stand in for real cleanup.
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-170-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

This is standards cleanup. Any touched rendered or terminal output must preserve existing text, focus, lower-mode, and screen-reader semantics unless a test explicitly proves an accessibility improvement.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-170-localization-and-directionality-posture}

Avoid DOGFOOD copy edits unless the slice intentionally updates localization catalogs. If DOGFOOD-facing strings are touched, run the DOGFOOD i18n gates and hold the raw-string and missing-localization ratchets flat or lower.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-170-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

The selected files, rule deltas, and validation commands must be captured in this design doc or the PR summary so the next agent can audit what changed without re-running broad discovery first.

\section{Scope}\label{record-171-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Select a focused cleanup slice from current ESLint or Code Dojo offenders.
\item
  Prefer real type, data-shape, and control-flow fixes over suppressions or cosmetic baseline churn.
\item
  Keep touched file/context, mock-ban, code-size, and DOGFOOD localization ratchets flat or lower.
\item
  Update \texttt{s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} after the live count is proven lower.

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-171-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

This is standards cleanup. Any touched rendered or terminal output must preserve existing text, focus, lower-mode, and screen-reader semantics unless a test explicitly proves an accessibility improvement.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-171-localization-and-directionality-posture}

Avoid DOGFOOD copy edits unless the slice intentionally updates localization catalogs. If DOGFOOD-facing strings are touched, run the DOGFOOD i18n gates and hold the raw-string and missing-localization ratchets flat or lower.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-171-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

The selected files, rule deltas, and validation commands must be captured in this design doc or the PR summary so the next agent can audit what changed without re-running broad discovery first.

  Use \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s} and focused ESLint probes to select a slice that can remove at least \texttt{5\allowbreak{}0} findings.
\item
  Write focused regressions only where cleanup exposes a behavior or module boundary risk.
\item
  Replace unsafe assertions, non-null assertions, implicit coercions, fake async shapes, and nondeterministic test clocks with typed helpers and explicit control flow.
\item
  Ratchet the ESLint baseline and aggregate Code Dojo ceiling after the live count is proven lower.
\item
  Update docs and changelog with final counts and the next target.
\end{enumerate}

\item
  Update docs and changelog with final counts and the next target.
\end{enumerate}
