\section{Implementation Notes}\label{record-175-implementation-notes}

WF-156 removes \texttt{5\allowbreak{}3} live ESLint findings, lowering the ESLint baseline from \texttt{2\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}5} to \texttt{1\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2} and the aggregate Code Dojo debt from \texttt{6\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}3} to \texttt{5\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}0}.

Touched cleanup clusters:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  TUI runtime, app-frame test support, notifications, browsable list, DAG pane, and string layout helpers.
\item
  Core block-tree rendering, grapheme sanitization, and timer spoken formatting.
\item
  Create-app CLI package parsing and npm pack output parsing.
\item
  Release readiness tracker parsing, release metadata tag handling, and smoke canary manifest/npm-pack/env handling.
\end{itemize}

Per the operator's temporary waiver for touched-file size ratchets during this slice, existing file/context and code-size entries for touched legacy-large files were refreshed. The counted file/context and code-size totals do not grow.

Known remaining top ESLint clusters after this pass include i18n runtime, PR review status, i18n filesystem/localization helpers, MCP docs tooling, and small TUI/core tests. The next goalpost target is \texttt{5\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0} aggregate violations or lower.

\section{Scope}\label{record-175-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Select focused cleanup clusters from current ESLint or Code Dojo offenders.
\item
  Prefer real type, data-shape, deterministic-test, and control-flow fixes over suppressions or cosmetic baseline churn.
\item
  Continue shrinking oversized files when that contributes to the same standards objective.
\item
  Keep counted file/context, mock-ban, code-size, and DOGFOOD localization totals flat or lower. If the operator explicitly waives touched-file size ratchets, record any refreshed legacy-large ceilings in this design doc.
\item
  Update \texttt{s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} after the live count is proven lower.

\section{Implementation Notes}\label{record-176-implementation-notes}

WF-157 removes \texttt{5\allowbreak{}2} live type-aware ESLint findings, lowering the ESLint baseline from \texttt{1\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2} to \texttt{1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0} and the aggregate Code Dojo ceiling from \texttt{5\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}0} to \texttt{5\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8}.

Cleanup clusters:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  i18n runtime-adjacent boundaries: story protocol index guards, catalog filesystem parsing, authoring-tool record handling, and localized value clone/freeze validation.
\item
  MCP docs examples: replace docs-only renderer assertions with local JSON-shape coercion helpers for guided flow, preference list, and stats panel examples.
\item
  TUI/core tests and helpers: keybinding/action visibility checks, drawer invalid-input coverage, runtime support typing, subapp command mapping, binding-frame invalid input coverage, DOGFOOD block registry invalid-input and immutability checks, flex/pager numeric formatting, navigable-table repeat loops, notification row guards, motion reconciliation narrowing, and split-pane grapheme guards.
\item
  Examples: mark top-level app launches as intentionally floated with \texttt{v\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d}.
\end{itemize}

Per the operator's temporary waiver for touched-file size ratchets, existing file/context entries for touched legacy-large files were refreshed to their current measured line/byte counts. No new counted file/context, mock-ban, or code-size entries were added.

\section{Scope}\label{record-176-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Select focused cleanup clusters from current ESLint or Code Dojo offenders.
\item
  Prefer real type, data-shape, deterministic-test, and control-flow fixes over suppressions or cosmetic baseline churn.
\item
  Continue shrinking oversized files when that contributes to the same standards objective.
\item
  Keep counted file/context, mock-ban, code-size, and DOGFOOD localization totals flat or lower. If the operator explicitly waives touched-file size ratchets, record any refreshed legacy-large ceilings in this design doc.
\item
  Update \texttt{s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} after the live count is proven lower.

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-176-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

This is standards cleanup. Any touched rendered or terminal output must preserve existing text, focus, lower-mode, and screen-reader semantics unless a test explicitly proves an accessibility improvement.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-176-localization-and-directionality-posture}

Avoid DOGFOOD copy edits unless the slice intentionally updates localization catalogs. If DOGFOOD-facing strings are touched, run the DOGFOOD i18n gates and hold the raw-string and missing-localization ratchets flat or lower.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-176-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

The selected files, rule deltas, and validation commands must be captured in this design doc or the PR summary so the next agent can audit what changed without re-running broad discovery first.

\section{Implementation Notes}\label{record-177-implementation-notes}

WF-158 removes \texttt{5\allowbreak{}3} live type-aware ESLint findings, lowering the ESLint baseline from \texttt{1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0} to \texttt{5\allowbreak{}7} and the aggregate Code Dojo ceiling from \texttt{5\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}8} to \texttt{4\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}5}.

Cleanup clusters:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Core forms and tests: preserve empty-answer default semantics while replacing unsafe fallback chains, add explicit numeric formatting in fuzz fixtures, and remove control-character regex literals from prompt/progress tests.
\item
  DOGFOOD and cycle tests: replace visible frame-text fallbacks with nullish checks, remove unnecessary conversions, and keep rendered text assertions behaviorally equivalent.
\item
  Bench and smoke helpers: type GC sample arrays, make JSONL parsing return \texttt{u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}n}, document intentional no-op sinks, and remove needless async wrappers.
\item
  TUI helpers: replace non-null assertions with checked reads in command palette, file picker, panel focus, input stack, status bar, cell glyph, CSS parser, and app-frame layout traversal.
\item
  Core components: remove unnecessary fallbacks from already-required string inputs, unify DAG overloads, and keep runtime viewport overlay typing direct.
\end{itemize}

Per the operator's temporary waiver for touched-file size ratchets, existing file/context entries for touched legacy-large files were refreshed to their current measured line/byte counts. No new counted file/context, mock-ban, or code-size entries were added.

\section{Scope}\label{record-177-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Select focused cleanup clusters from current ESLint or Code Dojo offenders.
\item
  Prefer real type, data-shape, deterministic-test, and control-flow fixes over suppressions or cosmetic baseline churn.
\item
  Continue shrinking oversized files when that contributes to the same standards objective.
\item
  Keep counted file/context, mock-ban, code-size, and DOGFOOD localization totals flat or lower. If the operator explicitly waives touched-file size ratchets, record any refreshed legacy-large ceilings in this design doc.
\item
  Update \texttt{s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} after the live count is proven lower.
\end{itemize}

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-177-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

This is standards cleanup. Any touched rendered or terminal output must preserve existing text, focus, lower-mode, and screen-reader semantics unless a test explicitly proves an accessibility improvement.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-177-localization-and-directionality-posture}

Avoid DOGFOOD copy edits unless the slice intentionally updates localization catalogs. If DOGFOOD-facing strings are touched, run the DOGFOOD i18n gates and hold the raw-string and missing-localization ratchets flat or lower.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-177-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

The selected files, rule deltas, and validation commands must be captured in this design doc or the PR summary so the next agent can audit what changed without re-running broad discovery first.

\section{Implementation Notes}\label{record-178-implementation-notes}

WF-159 removes \texttt{5\allowbreak{}1} live type-aware ESLint findings, lowering the ESLint baseline from \texttt{5\allowbreak{}7} to \texttt{6} and the aggregate Code Dojo ceiling from \texttt{4\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}5} to \texttt{4\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}4}.

Cleanup clusters:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  i18n runtime and localization port: remove unchecked caller-selected generic value claims from the runtime boundary, return unknown catalog data until a caller narrows it, and make interpolation avoid implicit object stringification.
\item
  Tests and fixtures: replace scattered non-null assertions, unsafe matcher assignments, malformed active-binding input casts, fuzz fixture casts, and deterministic clock conditionals with typed guards or explicit runtime invocation.
\item
  Theme and TUI helpers: make browsable-list render options generic, resolve theme status tokens through map lookups, preserve deprecated helper exports through star re-exports, and avoid unsafe token-graph casts.
\item
  Script and parser utilities: validate package metadata JSON, parse design-system headings/fields with checked captures, and keep PR-status helper debt isolated for a later split.
\end{itemize}

Per the operator's temporary waiver for touched-file size ratchets, existing file/context entries for touched legacy-large files were refreshed to their current measured line/byte counts, and existing code-size ceilings for the touched i18n runtime files were refreshed as well. No new counted file/context, mock-ban, or code-size entries were added.

\section{Scope}\label{record-178-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Select focused cleanup clusters from current ESLint or Code Dojo offenders.
\item
  Prefer real type, data-shape, deterministic-test, and control-flow fixes over suppressions or cosmetic baseline churn.
\item
  Continue shrinking oversized files when that contributes to the same standards objective.
\item
  Keep counted file/context, mock-ban, code-size, and DOGFOOD localization totals flat or lower. If the operator explicitly waives touched-file size ratchets, record any refreshed legacy-large ceilings in this design doc.
\item
  Update \texttt{s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}, \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} after the live count is proven lower.

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-178-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

This is standards cleanup. Any touched rendered or terminal output must preserve existing text, focus, lower-mode, and screen-reader semantics unless a test explicitly proves an accessibility improvement.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-178-localization-and-directionality-posture}

Avoid DOGFOOD copy edits unless the slice intentionally updates localization catalogs. If DOGFOOD-facing strings are touched, run the DOGFOOD i18n gates and hold the raw-string and missing-localization ratchets flat or lower.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-178-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

The selected files, rule deltas, and validation commands must be captured in this design doc or the PR summary so the next agent can audit what changed without re-running broad discovery first.

\chapter{WF-162 Respecting the Dojo Ratchet 162}\label{record-181}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/WF-162-respecting-dojo-ratchet-162.md}\par}\smallskip

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-181-decision-summary}

Cut \texttt{1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0} counted Code Dojo debt items from the merged \texttt{2\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2} baseline and land the next Respecting the Dojo checkpoint at \texttt{1\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2} aggregate violations or lower.

\section{Hill}\label{record-181-hill}

WF-161 exhausted most of the low-risk oversized test/spec split pool. The repo still carries structural debt in file/context and code-size ledgers, so this cycle has to combine remaining deterministic test decomposition with production, tooling, and example module extraction.

The goal is not cosmetic movement. The resulting ledgers must describe less debt because large files were split into smaller, coherent modules without weakening public behavior, tests, or standards.

\section{Current Truth}\label{record-181-current-truth}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Aggregate Code Dojo debt: \texttt{2\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2}
\item
  File/context baseline: \texttt{2\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}7}
\item
  Mock-ban baseline: \texttt{0}
\item
  Code-size baseline: \texttt{4\allowbreak{}5}, including \texttt{3} hard-limit files
\item
  ESLint baseline: \texttt{0}
\item
  Required target for this cycle: \texttt{1\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2} aggregate violations or lower
\item
  Tracker issue: \#439
\end{itemize}

\section{Scope}\label{record-181-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Split the remaining over-threshold deterministic test/spec files that are safe to decompose.
\item
  Extract enough production, tooling, and example modules to remove the remaining counted debt needed for a \texttt{1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0} item aggregate reduction.
\item
  Keep original module entrypoints as compatibility facades when public import paths are part of the package surface.
\item
  Refresh Code Dojo file/context and code-size ledgers from live files.
\item
  Lower \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}x} to the measured live count.
\item
  Update \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}.
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  No product feature work.
\item
  No release-version work.
\item
  No behavior/API breakage.
\item
  No rebase, amend, force push, or draft PR.
\item
  No large-file marker escape hatches and no standards carveout expansion.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Strategy}\label{record-181-implementation-strategy}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Finish the deterministic test split pool.}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    Split the remaining over-threshold test/spec files into focused threshold-sized specs.
  \item
    Preserve all assertions and snapshots.
  \item
    Prefer semantic describe-group boundaries over arbitrary line cuts.
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Extract high-yield code-size modules.}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    Target modules where one extraction removes both a file/context entry and a code-size entry.
  \item
    Keep stable public files as facades that re-export or delegate to focused internals.
  \item
    Avoid broad rewrites inside domain logic unless tests pin the behavior.
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Extract file/context-only modules when needed.}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    Target self-contained data, fixtures, option tables, test support helpers, parser/render helper clusters, and CLI workflow helpers.
  \item
    Keep each new file below \texttt{1\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}0} lines and \texttt{1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0} bytes.
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Ratcheting and proof.}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    Regenerate the file/context baseline from live files.
  \item
    Remove code-size entries only when live files are below the ratchet limit or have been replaced by smaller modules.
  \item
    Lower the aggregate debt ceiling to \texttt{1\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2} or lower.
  \end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}

\section{Implementation Outcome}\label{record-181-implementation-outcome}

The cycle lands exactly at \texttt{1\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2} aggregate Code Dojo violations:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  File/context baseline: \texttt{1\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}6}
\item
  Mock-ban baseline: \texttt{0}
\item
  Code-size baseline: \texttt{2\allowbreak{}6}, including \texttt{3} hard-limit files
\item
  ESLint baseline: \texttt{0}
\end{itemize}

The reduction combines:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Remaining deterministic test and test-support splits, including app-frame, runtime-interactive, textarea, PTY-driver, DOGFOOD light-theme, docs-preview, and test adapter support files.
\item
  Declaration-boundary module extraction for standard-blocks, theme helpers, packed-cell, component metadata, TUI navigation/layout helpers, transition shaders, block metadata, schema blocks, selection, binding lifecycle, DAG pane, focus area, raster glyphs, layout envelopes, overlays, GraphQL blocks, viewport, binding, and notifications.
\item
  Compatibility facades at the original import paths so public consumers keep stable module entrypoints while implementations move into smaller part files.
\end{itemize}

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-184-decision-summary}

Complete issue \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/480}{\#480} by removing all \texttt{2\allowbreak{}5} files that are counted in both the file/context and code-size ledgers. The combined \texttt{5\allowbreak{}0}-violation reduction lowers aggregate Code Dojo debt from \texttt{6\allowbreak{}2} to \texttt{1\allowbreak{}2} or lower.

Deliver the goalpost through bounded review tranches. Each tranche preserves public entrypoints as typed compatibility facades, proves that its extracted module family remains outside runtime import cycles, and lowers only the live ledger entries it actually removes.

\section{Hill}\label{record-184-hill}

The repository has \texttt{3\allowbreak{}7} file/context violations and \texttt{2\allowbreak{}5} code-size violations. All \texttt{2\allowbreak{}5} code-size offenders are also file/context offenders. Removing those double-counted roots behind stable facades therefore satisfies the next mandatory \texttt{5\allowbreak{}0}-violation goalpost without weakening a threshold, adding an exception, or changing public behavior.

The first tranche starts with five of the smaller double-counted roots:

\section{Scope}\label{record-184-scope}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Bind the exact \texttt{2\allowbreak{}5} double-counted roots in deterministic cycle evidence.
\item
  Deliver those roots through bounded review tranches.
\item
  Start tranche A with the five smaller roots named in this design.
\item
  Preserve every selected public import path and export name.
\item
  Keep mutable module state inside one implementation module unless an explicit port makes cross-module ownership safe.
\item
  Keep overload declarations beside their implementation.
\item
  Preserve source-debt identity across extracted implementation parts.
\item
  Prove every changed split family remains absent from runtime import cycles.
\item
  Remove ledger entries only after the live size gates accept the facade and extracted modules.
\item
  Lower the package debt ceiling only to the measured live result.
\item
  Update the exception ledger, changelog, roadmap, bearing, and cycle evidence in every tranche.
\end{itemize}

\section{Non-Goals}\label{record-184-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  No Profunctor Page feature implementation.
\item
  No public API or behavior redesign.
\item
  No opportunistic repair of pre-existing runtime cycles tracked by \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/476}{\#476}.
\item
  No new standards exception or large-file marker.
\item
  No weakened threshold or aspirational ledger edit.
\item
  No release tag or publication.
\end{itemize}

The exact target roots, tranche boundaries, live threshold checks, runtime-cycle proof, aggregate ceiling, and current documentation agree. A successor can identify every compatibility facade and implementation part without reconstructing the goalpost from commit history.

\section{Retrospective And Closeout}\label{record-184-retrospective-and-closeout}

Open. Tranche A landed in \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/pull/484}{\#484}. Five compatibility facades now delegate to focused contract, state, execution, and adapter modules; all facade exports remain stable, every family file is within the strict context threshold, focused behavior suites pass, and repository runtime-cycle analysis reports no cycle touching a changed family. The live ledgers move from \texttt{3\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2} to \texttt{3\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}2}.

Tranche B landed through \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/pull/486}{\#486}. It applies the same bounded extraction to the TUI runtime, performance gradient, scripted driver, DAG renderer, and TUI-app skeleton. Their public facades preserve the original exports while explicit family manifests bind the focused implementation modules used for size and runtime-cycle evidence. The review witness also binds behavior that the extraction initially drifted: same-column DAG detours, middleware-replaced render targets, the original noise permutation, empty DAG badges, and initialization-inclusive harness time. The live ledgers move again to \texttt{2\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}2}. Fifteen double-counted roots remain before the overall \texttt{6\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2} goalpost can close.

Tranche C is implemented in \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/pull/487}{\#487}. The canonical example app, Notifications, Image Viewer, PR review-status tool, and framed-app renderer remain stable facades over focused implementation families. Exact public-export and family manifests bind the compatibility surface, strict context thresholds, and runtime-cycle proof. Review hardening shares compact notification geometry between rendering and hit testing, preserves RGB-only active-tab backgrounds, localizes the default frame title, keeps divider graphemes intact, removes an orphan image-viewer mode message, and adds bounded caches for derived active-tab tokens and rendered image previews. The preview cache binds its entries to the source path, modification time, byte size, viewport, mode, and tuning so a source-file rewrite invalidates stale output. The live ledgers move to \texttt{2\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}2}; ten double-counted roots remain before the overall \texttt{6\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2} goalpost can close.

Tranche D is implemented in \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/pull/488}{\#488}. \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}, DOGFOOD i18n-debt analysis, framed-app overlays, \texttt{u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1}, and the terminal differ remain stable public facades over the exact family manifests locked by the tranche contract. Every family member stays within \texttt{1\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}0} lines and \texttt{1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0} bytes, and repository runtime-cycle analysis finds no cycle touching the changed families. The \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} witness preserves allocation-free numeric RGB writes and covers negative source-origin clipping. The DOGFOOD scanner retains \texttt{2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}7} raw strings and \texttt{7\allowbreak{}8} missing Markdown localizations while excluding its own implementation family. The live ledgers now measure \texttt{1\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}2}; no public API or rendering redesign entered scope. Five double-counted roots remain for tranche E.

Tranche E is implemented in \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/pull/489}{\#489}. The TUI runtime, table, framed-app, DOGFOOD application, and DOGFOOD story catalog remain stable public facades over the exact family manifests locked by the tranche contract. Every family member stays within \texttt{1\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}0} lines and \texttt{1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0} bytes, and repository runtime-cycle analysis reports no cycle touching the changed families. The story catalog preserves all \texttt{4\allowbreak{}2} ordered story definitions; its typed package identity lowers the split localization lineage from \texttt{1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}3} to \texttt{1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}7} raw strings. The live ledgers reach \texttt{1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2}, completing the WF-165 \texttt{6\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2} goalpost without weakening a threshold or redesigning a public surface.

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-185-decision-summary}

Clear every npm advisory from the resolved workspace dependency graph before the \texttt{v\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} release-preparation cycle begins. Coordinate the now-insufficient Dependabot pull request \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/pull/467}{\#467} inside this issue-backed cycle instead of merging a patch level that remains vulnerable.

\section{Hill}\label{record-185-hill}

Bijou should enter release preparation with a deterministic lockfile that resolves every currently reported package to a patched version, passes the complete Node 20 and Node 22 verification matrix, and produces a zero-advisory \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t} result.

  No audit suppression, ignore rule, or accepted vulnerable version.
\item
  No version bump, release tag, GitHub Release, npm publication, or milestone closure.
\item
  No Code Dojo exception removal; the final \texttt{1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0} goalpost follows this security cycle.
\end{itemize}

\section{Dependency And Compatibility Contract}\label{record-185-dependency-and-compatibility-contract}

The change is acceptable only when:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n} is reproducible from the declared workspace manifests;
\item
  the resolved graph contains no version covered by the current advisories;
\item
  the existing \texttt{@\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}k} public usage compiles and its MCP tests pass;
\item
  Node 20 and Node 22 repository tests remain green;
\item
  the full Code Dojo and DOGFOOD smoke gates remain green;
\item
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w} exits successfully.
\end{itemize}

The package-manager lockfile is authoritative for resolved versions. The live npm advisory service is authoritative for the release audit result.

\section{Tests To Write First}\label{record-185-tests-to-write-first}

The deterministic RED proof reads the lockfile and rejects the vulnerable resolved versions named above. It must fail on the merge-base lockfile before the update and pass afterward.

The external advisory proof is:

\begin{CodeBlock}
npm audit --audit-level=low
\end{CodeBlock}

The clean-install compatibility and product proof is executed in this order:

\begin{CodeBlock}
npm ci
npm audit --audit-level=low
npm run build
npm run typecheck:test
npm run lint
npm run lint:eslint
npm run code:size
npm run test:run
npm run code-dojo:ci
npm run smoke:dogfood
npm run docs:inventory
npm run docs:design-system:preflight
npm run verify:interactive-examples
\end{CodeBlock}

That sequence proves that a clean install from the committed lockfile preserves the repository's supported execution surface. Hosted CI repeats \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i} and the full repository test lane on both supported runtimes as the \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/.github/workflows/ci.yml}{\texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})} matrix jobs}, and runs the two DOGFOOD smoke jobs independently.

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-185-retrospective}

The security pass had to be refreshed against live advisory truth rather than the original shaping snapshot. The first carried lock attempt still admitted newer \texttt{f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i}, Hono, and \texttt{i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s} advisories and predated the \texttt{n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d} advisory. Its regression could therefore false-green. Raising the executable floors and binding the root Hono override made the clean-install promise real.

\texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y} also demonstrated why audit success is not the complete proof: it temporarily pruned the manifest-required SheetJS entry and reported zero vulnerabilities, while \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i} correctly rejected the inconsistent lock. Regenerating through \texttt{n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y} restored that entry; the repeated clean install, audit, full \texttt{9\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}0} file / \texttt{4\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}4} test suite, DOGFOOD smoke, documentation preflight, and interactive examples then passed. Hosted Node 20/22 evidence, \#467 disposition, and the final \#482 closeout remain merge-bound acceptance steps.

\section{Decision Summary}\label{record-186-decision-summary}

Restore one explainable release model across GitHub milestones, \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/5b10cb89165b76673ffc60da59d7de5a531e55e9/docs/ROADMAP.md}{\texttt{R\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}}, and \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/5b10cb89165b76673ffc60da59d7de5a531e55e9/docs/BEARING.md}{\texttt{B\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}}.

Milestones own release horizons. Labels own work posture. Goalpost issues own dependency ordering inside a horizon. Documentation mirrors those authorities; it does not create a competing queue.

The current \texttt{v\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} milestone mixes a landed Runtime Graph and Scene IR contract, an active dependency-security blocker, an additive open Theme Lab pull request, and twenty-one unfinished perceptual-colour and product-surface issues. The unfinished colour campaign includes changes explicitly identified as semver-major. It belongs before the next major release, \texttt{v\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0}, rather than becoming a second product contract inside V8.

This cycle therefore:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  returns \texttt{v\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} to Runtime Graph release closeout and dependency security;
\item
  preserves \texttt{v\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} as replay, capture, debugger, graph, and render evidence;
\item
  preserves \texttt{v\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} as quality automation and reliability hardening;
\item
  makes \texttt{v\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} the Product Workbench \textbf{and Sapphire Design Language} major, including interaction recipes and the State Atlas;
\item
  keeps \texttt{v\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0} for renderer and host integration, including the Geordi native-GPU cell host;
\item
  removes stale title and label residue created by earlier Beyond-to-version promotion;
\item
  assigns every open pull request to its evidenced release horizon.
\end{enumerate}

No issue closes in this cycle. No implementation priority is inferred merely from a milestone move.

\section{Hill}\label{record-186-hill}

A maintainer or agent can answer all of these from the live tracker and receive the same answer from the repository documentation:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  What blocks V8?
\item
  Which work is evidence follow-through rather than release closeout?
\item
  Which visual changes belong to the next semver-major boundary?
\item
  Which ideas are committed, imminent, debt, or optional?
\item
  Which open pull requests participate in each release horizon?
\item
  What must be reconciled before an overlapping pull request can merge?
\end{itemize}

The answer must not require reading historical comments, inferring semantics from an issue number, or treating a \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s} label as a release commitment.

\section{Authority Model}\label{record-186-authority-model}

\subsection{Milestone: Release Destination}\label{record-186-milestone-release-destination}

A versioned milestone answers: \textbf{if this work lands, which release boundary owns it?}

A milestone does not mean every issue is committed or next. That posture comes from \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}*}, \texttt{w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s}, priority, design, and goalpost labels.

\subsection{Lane: Commitment And Intake Posture}\label{record-186-lane-commitment-and-intake-posture}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}x}: not yet shaped;
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p}: imminent pull;
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e}: known debt or structural risk;
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s}: optional or uncommitted exploration;
\item
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e}: committed release-boundary work.
\end{itemize}

An issue should carry one current lane. Historical \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t} residue does not coexist with the current lane model.

\subsection{Goalpost: Dependency And Outcome Authority}\label{record-186-goalpost-dependency-and-outcome-authority}

Goalpost issues such as \#501 own dependency ordering within a release horizon. Moving a goalpost and its children between release horizons does not reorder the children. It changes the release boundary that may claim them.

\subsection{Documentation: Human-Readable Mirror}\label{record-186-documentation-human-readable-mirror}

\texttt{R\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} records release horizons, gates, and snapshot totals. \texttt{B\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d} records current execution gravity. Neither file overrides live GitHub state.

\section{Migration Ordering}\label{record-186-migration-ordering}

The mutation order prevents documentation from claiming unperformed tracker state:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  publish this design and the non-draft cycle PR;
\item
  update milestone descriptions;
\item
  move the V9 cohort and \#507;
\item
  assign PR \#492 and PR \#511;
\item
  normalize titles, lanes, and \#249 priority;
\item
  comment every release-horizon move;
\item
  take a fresh milestone-item snapshot;
\item
  update \texttt{R\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, \texttt{B\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}, changelog, and tests to that snapshot;
\item
  verify GitHub read-back and repository gates;
\item
  update the cycle issue and PR only for material discrepancies.
\end{enumerate}

If any mutation fails, stop and read back the affected issue before retrying. Do not assume a partial batch succeeded.

\section{Rollback And Recovery}\label{record-186-rollback-and-recovery}

GitHub issue and milestone edits are individually reversible. The durable migration table in this design identifies every intended source and target.

If review rejects the model:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  issues can be moved back using the same explicit table;
\item
  titles can regain their previous prefix from GitHub history;
\item
  labels can be restored individually;
\item
  documentation changes can be superseded by a normal follow-up commit;
\item
  no force operation, rebase, amend, or history rewrite is required.
\end{itemize}

Issue comments remain as provenance and should not be deleted. A rollback comment should explain the superseding decision.

\section{Accessibility And Assistive Posture}\label{record-186-accessibility-and-assistive-posture}

This is planning and workflow work. It changes no rendered interface. The roadmap explicitly keeps accessibility and capability-degradation work inside the V9 State Atlas and colour-distinctness stories rather than treating them as optional polish.

The issue migration comments and repository documentation remain readable as plain Markdown without colour, diagrams, or screenshots.

\section{Localization And Directionality Posture}\label{record-186-localization-and-directionality-posture}

No localized product copy or runtime directionality behavior changes. V9 continues to own the localization dashboard, portable preferences, translation workbench, and structured multilingual changelog stories.

Milestone descriptions use concise English tracker metadata; they do not become application-facing strings.

\section{Agent Inspectability And Explainability Posture}\label{record-186-agent-inspectability-and-explainability-posture}

An agent can inspect:

\item
  release-horizon comments;
\item

\end{itemize}

No agent must infer release scope from issue-number ranges, historical \texttt{[\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}]} prefixes, or branch names.

\section{Hill}\label{record-187-hill}

Surface rendering in Bijou goes from ``every cell is a heap-allocated object with string colors'' to ``every cell is 10 bytes in a flat typed array with numeric RGB.'' The DOGFOOD landing benchmark is at parity or faster than the pre-RE-008 baseline, and the architecture enables zero-allocation rendering for any component that opts into \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-187-playback-questions}

\subsection{Human}\label{record-187-human}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item[$\boxtimes$]
  Does the DOGFOOD landing render at least as fast as before?
\item[$\boxtimes$]
  Are all 2816 existing tests still passing?
\item[$\boxtimes$]
  Is the \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} convenience API preserved and documented?

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent}\label{record-187-agent}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item[$\boxtimes$]
  Is the packed buffer the source of truth, with Cell{[}{]} as lazy decode?
\item[$\boxtimes$]
  Does the differ operate on bytes, not strings?
\item[$\boxtimes$]
  Does blit copy bytes directly between packed buffers?
\item[$\boxtimes$]
  Are side-table chars (emoji, grapheme clusters) handled correctly?
\end{itemize}

\section{What Shipped}\label{record-187-what-shipped}

\subsection{Architecture}\label{record-187-architecture}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Packed cell encoding} (\texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}): 10-byte layout per cell --- uint16 char, 3B fg RGB, 3B bg RGB, 1B flags bitfield, 1B alpha/presence. Side table for multi-codepoint graphemes outside the BMP.
\item
  \textbf{Lazy dirty bitmap}: \texttt{U\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y} bitmap (1 bit per cell) tracks which cells need decoding from the buffer. Writes mark dirty; reads decode on demand.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} API}: Zero-allocation writes --- char code + numeric RGB directly into the buffer. No hex parsing, no Cell object.
\item
  \textbf{Packed blit}: 10-byte memcpy per cell with side-table re-encoding for cross-surface grapheme clusters.
\item
  \textbf{Template-stamp fill/clear}: Encode once, copy bytes to every position.
\item
  \textbf{Direct ANSI emission}: Differ reads RGB bytes from the buffer and emits \texttt{\textbackslash{}\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{};\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{};\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{};\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{};\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}m} directly, with a style-byte hash cache. Bypasses chalk and StylePort entirely on the hot diff path.
\item
  \textbf{Numeric theme tokens}: \texttt{T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}B} / \texttt{b\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}B} pre-parsed at theme resolution time.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Slices (19 commits)}\label{record-187-slices-19-commits}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Packed-cell byte encoding module
\item
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} backed by \texttt{U\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y} + eager sync
\item
  Route all direct cell mutations through \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}
\item
  Packed byte-comparison differ
\item
  Grayscale middleware on packed bytes
\item
  Lazy dirty bitmap (replace eager sync)
\item
  Zero-alloc hex parsing (charCode arithmetic, lookup table)
\item
  Inline hex→RGB, FULL\_MASK fast path, numeric theme tokens
\item
  Direct ANSI SGR emission with cached style-byte hash
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} API + perf-gradient demo migration
\item
  Packed byte-copy blit
\item
  Template-stamp fill, clear, clone
\item
  Component migration: surface-text, box-v3, separator-v3
\item
  Component migration: overlay dim, flex/overlay bg inheritance
\item
  Component migration: table-v3, alert-v3
\item
  Component migration: notification, css/text-style
\item
  Component migration: badge, focus-area, preference-list, canvas, differ
\end{enumerate}

\section{Accessibility and Assistive Reading}\label{record-187-accessibility-and-assistive-reading}

No user-facing changes. The packed buffer is internal; all public APIs return the same Cell objects and string output as before.

\section{Localization and Directionality}\label{record-187-localization-and-directionality}

No changes. Character encoding handles the full Unicode BMP directly and uses a side table for astral/multi-codepoint graphemes.

\section{Agent Inspectability and Explainability}\label{record-187-agent-inspectability-and-explainability}

The \texttt{P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} interface and \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} API are exported and documented. Agents can query surface dimensions, read cells via \texttt{g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, and use the packed buffer for performance-sensitive rendering.

\section{Non-goals}\label{record-187-non-goals}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Changing the public Cell interface or breaking component APIs
\item
  Removing hex color support from the convenience \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} API
\item
  Pre-allocated output buffer for stdout (deferred to future work)
\item
  Eliminating the Cell{[}{]} layer entirely (the lazy decode + dirty bitmap keeps backward compatibility with minimal overhead)
\end{itemize}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-189-why-this-cycle-exists}

The Showcase app is the most visible ``complex'' implementation of Bijou. If it contains anti-patterns (e.g., hardcoded colors, loose typing, or mixed architectural concerns), it will mislead developers into adopting those same bad habits.

As the \textbf{EXPERT Bijou BigBro}, I must audit this app to: - Identify and backlog ``sludge'' for correction. - Propose refactors that align with the \textbf{Hexagonal} and \textbf{TEA} pillars. - Ensure it serves as a ``Humane'' reference for others.

\section{Hill}\label{record-190-hill}

Project Big Extraction starts by killing a hard-limit monolith instead of preserving legacy-large files as permanent habitat.

\texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} is currently a \texttt{2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}7} line / \texttt{9\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0} byte DOGFOOD block registry monolith with \texttt{1\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}1} exports. The cycle turns it into a small compatibility facade backed by focused modules, preserving existing consumers while removing the hard-limit file from the active monolith list.

\chapter{HT-002 --- Layered Focus and Interaction}\label{record-191}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/HT-002-layered-focus-and-interaction.md}\par}\smallskip

\emph{Cycle for defining how Bijou shells should treat focus layers, dismiss order, and input ownership as one coherent stack}

Legend:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad902f6bf219326409e7f743a5a1d6517dbc/docs/legends/HT-humane-terminal.md}{HT --- Humane Terminal}
\end{itemize}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-191-why-this-cycle-exists}

Bijou has accumulated multiple shell-owned surfaces:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  help
\item
  search
\item
  command palette
\item
  settings
\item
  notifications
\item
  quit confirm
\item
  page-owned modals
\end{itemize}

They currently route input by branch order. That is workable until it is not: the moment two layers disagree about \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c}, footer hints, or control ownership, the shell starts feeling brittle.

This cycle exists to define a calmer model:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  layers behave like a stack
\item
  the topmost layer owns input
\item
  the topmost layer owns the visible controls
\item
  dismiss actions pop layers before they trigger broader shell behavior
\end{itemize}

The purpose of this cycle is design, not implementation. The follow-on runtime refactor will come in the next cycle.

\section{Human users / jobs / hills}\label{record-191-human-users-jobs-hills}

\subsection{Primary human users}\label{record-191-primary-human-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  operators inside framed Bijou apps
\item
  first-time DOGFOOD users who open layered shell surfaces
\item
  builders trying to understand why \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c}, \texttt{T\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b}, and footer hints behave the way they do
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human jobs}\label{record-191-human-jobs}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Understand which layer currently owns input.
\item
  Dismiss the thing in front of me without accidentally quitting the app.
\item
  Trust the footer and help hints to describe the active controls truthfully.
\item
  Move back to the underlying pane without guessing whether hidden controls are still live.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-191-human-hill}

A user can open and close layered shell surfaces without ever feeling that \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} or the footer lied about what would happen next.

\section{Agent users / jobs / hills}\label{record-191-agent-users-jobs-hills}

\subsection{Primary agent users}\label{record-191-primary-agent-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  agents navigating framed apps through deterministic key sequences
\item
  agents inspecting shell state for playbacks, tests, or UI generation
\item
  agents trying to decide which controls are valid without scraping visual chrome heuristically
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent jobs}\label{record-191-agent-jobs}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Determine the active interaction layer without reconstructing branch order from source.
\item
  Read the active input map for the topmost layer.
\item
  Predict what \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c}, navigation keys, and shell shortcuts will do right now.
\item
  Derive truthful control hints from the same source that governs routing.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-191-agent-hill}

An agent can inspect or infer a single active layer stack and know which input map is live, what controls are truthful, and what dismissal will do next.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-191-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A user is in DOGFOOD docs and opens component search with \texttt{/}.
\item
  Search pushes a search layer onto the shell stack.
\item
  The search layer's input map becomes active, and the footer updates to search-specific controls.
\item
  The underlying pane controls disappear from the footer because they are no longer truthful.
\item
  The user presses \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c}.
\item
  The search layer dismisses and pops off the stack.
\item
  The previously focused docs pane becomes active again, along with its pane controls.
\item
  The user presses \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} again.
\item
  No dismissible overlay remains, so the shell now interprets \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} as a quit request and opens quit confirm.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Agent playback}\label{record-191-agent-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  An agent enters a framed app and requests the current shell layer state.
\item
  The shell reports a base workspace layer plus one topmost settings drawer layer.
\item
  The active input map is the settings drawer map, not the underlying pane map.
\item
  The agent derives visible controls from that topmost input map and ignores stale pane-local hints.
\item
  The agent sends \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c}.
\item
  The shell pops the settings layer and restores the workspace layer and its active pane input map.
\item
  The agent sends \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} again.
\item
  With no dismissible overlay left, the shell opens quit confirm instead of silently quitting or dispatching to a stale pane action.
\end{enumerate}

\end{itemize}

\section{Proposed direction}\label{record-191-proposed-direction}

\subsection{Layer model}\label{record-191-layer-model}

Treat shell and page interaction surfaces as a stack of explicit layers:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  base workspace layer
\item
  pane-local modal layer
\item
  shell search/palette layer
\item
  shell help layer
\item
  shell settings layer
\item
  shell notification center layer
\item
  shell quit-confirm layer
\end{itemize}

The stack is logical, not merely visual. Only the topmost layer owns input.

\subsection{Input maps}\label{record-191-input-maps}

Each layer should provide or select an input map that describes:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the keys it handles
\item
  the dismissal behavior it owns
\item
  the controls that can be shown in the footer/help
\item
  whether it is dismissible, blocking, or review-only
\end{itemize}

This makes the input map do three jobs from one source of truth:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  routing
\item
  visible controls
\item
  agent-readable interaction state
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Dismiss order}\label{record-191-dismiss-order}

Dismissal should be top-down and unsurprising:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  If a dismissible layer is open, \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} dismisses that layer.
\item
  If the topmost layer is not dismissible, \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} does nothing or follows that layer's explicit contract.
\item
  Only when no dismissible layer remains should \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} fall back to the shell quit request.
\end{enumerate}

\texttt{q} and \texttt{C\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}C} can remain explicit quit affordances, but they should still respect text-entry exceptions and shell-owned quit policy.

\subsection{Visible controls}\label{record-191-visible-controls}

Footer and help hints should be derived from the topmost input map, not copied from whichever branch happened to handle the last render.

This means:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a search layer shows search controls
\item
  a modal shows modal controls
\item
  an inactive pane does not keep advertising its keys when covered
\item
  when a layer pops, the previous active map becomes visible again
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent-visible semantics}\label{record-191-agent-visible-semantics}

The shell should eventually expose enough structured layer state that tests, playbacks, and agents do not need to infer ownership from rendered text alone.

Candidate shape:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  ordered active layers
\item
  topmost input map id
\item
  dismissibility
\item
  active control hints
\item
  owning region or surface id
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation outline}\label{record-191-implementation-outline}

This cycle is design-only. The intended implementation follow-on is:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Introduce a shell layer model in \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Convert search/help/settings/notifications/quit confirm into explicit layer descriptors.
\item
  Promote or adapt input maps so each layer drives both routing and visible controls.
\item
  Make \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} follow top-down dismiss semantics.
\item
  Prove the behavior through DOGFOOD and shell regressions.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests to write first}\label{record-191-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  cycle doc regression asserting the new Humane Terminal cycle, invariant, and doctrine links exist
\item
  shell behavior regressions proving top-down dismiss order once implementation begins
\item
  footer/help regressions proving visible controls come from the topmost input map
\item
  DOGFOOD playback proving search dismissal restores the underlying pane controls before quit is possible
\end{itemize}

\section{Risks / unknowns}\label{record-191-risks-unknowns}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  page-owned modals and shell-owned layers currently live in different conceptual buckets
\item
  not every existing key path is modeled as an input map yet
\item
  some layers may want special \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} behavior beyond simple dismissal
\item
  the eventual public API for agent-readable layer state needs to be useful without overfitting the current shell internals
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-191-retrospective}

This cycle deliberately stops at doctrine and interaction model definition.

What it clarified:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} bugs are symptoms of missing layer semantics, not isolated routing accidents
\item
  the shell needs a topmost-layer model, not more special-case branch ordering
\item
  input maps are a promising shared seam for routing, footer truth, and agent visibility
\end{itemize}

Drift and follow-on:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  the runtime still routes most shell layers ad hoc today
\item
  that follow-on has now landed as \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/design/HT-003-implement-layer-stack-and-input-map-routing.md}{HT-003 --- Implement Layer Stack and Input Map Routing}
\end{itemize}

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-192-why-this-cycle-exists}

HT-002 established the right direction:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  layers should behave like a stack
\item
  the topmost layer should own input
\item
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} should dismiss topmost layers before quitting
\item
  visible controls should come from the active input map
\end{itemize}

But the runtime was still routing shell surfaces through raw branch order.

This cycle exists to make that doctrine real enough to stop the \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c}/footer class of bugs from reappearing constantly.

\section{Human users / jobs / hills}\label{record-192-human-users-jobs-hills}

\subsection{Primary human users}\label{record-192-primary-human-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  framed-app operators moving through search, settings, help, notifications, and quit confirm
\item
  DOGFOOD users switching between pane work and shell-owned layers
\item
  builders relying on \texttt{c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} defaults instead of reinventing shell logic
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human jobs}\label{record-192-human-jobs}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Dismiss the thing on top without accidentally triggering something beneath it.
\item
  Trust the footer to describe the active controls instead of stale underlying controls.
\item
  Understand when a page-owned modal is blocking the workspace.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-192-human-hill}

The shell behaves like a calm stack of layers instead of a pile of conditionals: dismissal is unsurprising and footer hints are truthful.

\section{Agent users / jobs / hills}\label{record-192-agent-users-jobs-hills}

\subsection{Primary agent users}\label{record-192-primary-agent-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  agents driving framed apps by key sequences
\item
  agents validating shell behavior through playbacks
\item
  agents that need a structured way to infer what the shell considers active
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent jobs}\label{record-192-agent-jobs}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Inspect the active shell layer order from model state instead of reverse-engineering branch order.
\item
  Predict whether a key will dismiss, route to the page modal, or fall through to the workspace.
\item
  Derive visible controls from the topmost layer, not by parsing terminal chrome heuristically.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-192-agent-hill}

An agent can inspect a frame model and understand the current shell/page layer stack well enough to predict \texttt{E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c} and footer behavior reliably.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-192-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}

\item

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

  Expose a public \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} helper for tests/agents.

What landed:

  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} in the public TUI API

\item

\section{Why this cycle exists}\label{record-193-why-this-cycle-exists}

HT-003 made the shell stack real enough for routing, dismissal, and truthful footer hints.

But the layer model was still intentionally thin:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  most layer objects were inferred from booleans
\item
  layer titles still lived in overlay render helpers
\item
  footer hints still came from separate shell branches
\item
  help overlay content still special-cased underlying layer kinds instead of consuming richer layer metadata
\end{itemize}

This cycle exists to make the layer object itself a better unit of truth for humans, agents, and shared shell code.

\section{Human users / jobs / hills}\label{record-193-human-users-jobs-hills}

\subsection{Primary human users}\label{record-193-primary-human-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  framed-app operators moving between workspace, settings, help, notification review, palette search, and quit confirm
\item
  DOGFOOD users relying on the shell to explain what is active
\item
  builders expecting shell overlays to feel coherent instead of pieced together
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Human jobs}\label{record-193-human-jobs}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Trust a shell layer to own its own title and controls instead of seeing mismatched chrome.
\item
  Open help and get the controls for the layer beneath it without stale workspace leakage.
\item
  Move between shell layers without the footer and overlay titles feeling like they come from different systems.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Human hill}\label{record-193-human-hill}

Each shell layer feels like a real object with its own identity and controls, not a boolean plus a pile of helper branches.

\section{Agent users / jobs / hills}\label{record-193-agent-users-jobs-hills}

\subsection{Primary agent users}\label{record-193-primary-agent-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  agents inspecting framed-app model state
\item
  agents generating deterministic playbacks for shell layers
\item
  agents that need to know which controls belong to the active or underlying layer
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Agent jobs}\label{record-193-agent-jobs}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Inspect the active and underlying layer objects directly instead of reverse-engineering footer/help logic.
\item
  Read a layer title and control ownership from the same place the shell uses.
\item
  Determine whether a layer has its own help source, hint source, and dismissal semantics.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Agent hill}\label{record-193-agent-hill}

An agent can inspect a frame model and obtain richer explicit layer objects with enough metadata to reason about titles, controls, and help ownership without parsing rendered chrome heuristically.

\section{Human playback}\label{record-193-human-playback}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

  A user opens settings in a framed app.
\item

  \item
    workspace
  \item
    settings
  \item
    search
  \end{itemize}
\item
  The search layer object includes its title and hint source.
\item
  The underlying settings layer object includes its help source.
\item
  The agent can predict both the visible footer controls and the help overlay content from those layer objects.

\tightlist
\item
  Promote the public layer descriptor into a richer explicit layer object with:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    stable id
  \item
    title
  \item
    hint source
  \item
    help source
  \end{itemize}
\item
  Let \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} accept metadata overrides for individual layers.
\item
  Export richer active/underlying layer helpers for shell introspection.
\item
  Drive shell footer hints from the active layer object instead of a separate footer-branch helper.
\item
  Drive help-overlay content from the underlying layer object's help source instead of hard-coded kind branching.
\item
  Route shell overlay titles through the same layer metadata where feasible.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Tests to write first}\label{record-193-tests-to-write-first}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  cycle doc regression for HT-004 and its follow-on backlog item
\item
  unit regression proving \texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} returns richer layer metadata when supplied
\item
  regression proving active/underlying layer helpers expose that richer metadata
\item
  shell regression proving help opened over settings renders settings controls, not stale workspace controls
\end{itemize}

\section{Risks / unknowns}\label{record-193-risks-unknowns}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  page-owned layers are still limited to the existing \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p} seam rather than a full page-provided layer registry
\item
  shell overlay bodies may still have some layout-specific logic even after titles and control metadata move onto layer objects
\item
  the first explicit layer object model may still be derived rather than literally pushed/popped as runtime objects
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-193-retrospective}

What landed:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  richer explicit layer objects with title, hint-source, and help-source metadata
\item
  exported active/underlying layer helpers for shell introspection
\item
  footer and help resolution driven from layer metadata instead of ad hoc branching
\item
  overlay titles routed through explicit layer objects where the shell owns the surface
\end{itemize}

What did not land:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  a full page-provided layer registry beyond \texttt{m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p}
\item
  a literal pushed/popped runtime collection of first-class layer instances stored on the frame model
\item
  agent-facing control projection beyond the richer exported layer helpers
\end{itemize}

Follow-on:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
