\end{itemize}

\chapter{HT-007 Focus Map Surface}\label{record-194}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/HT-007-focus-map-surface.md}\par}\smallskip

\begin{RecordMeta}
title: HT-007 Focus Map Surface
legend: HT
lane: design

\end{RecordMeta}

\section{Framing}\label{record-194-framing}

Focus behavior in complex shells and multi-pane workstations is difficult to reason about from runtime output alone. The humane terminal story is stronger when focus ownership is inspectable and explainable.

HT-007 adds a pure focus map report and surface helper. The first slice accepts focus facts from an app or shell, detects basic focus-health issues, and renders plain text or a bounded \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.

\section{Sponsored Users}\label{record-194-sponsored-users}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  App authors debugging tab order and focus ownership.
\item
  Maintainers investigating multi-pane focus regressions.
\item
  Agent workflows that need focus facts as deterministic text.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hills}\label{record-194-hills}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  A developer can render the current focus map with focused node, owner, region, tab order, and disabled state.
\item
  A maintainer can detect multiple focused nodes, missing focused node, focused-disabled nodes, and duplicate tab indexes.
\item
  A test can render the report as a \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e} for docs or debug panes.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Playback Questions}\label{record-194-playback-questions}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Does the helper preserve focus ownership and tab order in the report?
\item
  Does the focused node stand out in text output?
\item
  Does issue detection catch no focus, multiple focus, disabled focus, and duplicate tab indexes?
\item
  Does the surface helper render a bounded report?
\item
  Does \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i} export the focus map API from the source barrel?
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}\label{record-194-requirements}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Add \texttt{f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}?\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Add \texttt{f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}?\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Add \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  Support node id, optional owner, optional role, optional rect, optional tab index, focusable, focused, and disabled flags.
\item
  Keep the first slice pure; it must expose focus truth, not invent a second focus system.
\end{itemize}

\section{Acceptance Criteria}\label{record-194-acceptance-criteria}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Focused RED tests fail before implementation and pass after.
\item
  Text output includes focused node, ownership, tab order, and issues.
\item
  Surface output respects supplied width and height.
\item
  Docs and changelog describe the helper.
\end{itemize}

\section{Implementation Outline}\label{record-194-implementation-outline}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Implement the helper in \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Export it from \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Keep report ordering deterministic: tab index first, then id.
\end{itemize}

\section{Drift Check}\label{record-194-drift-check}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Scope stayed pure and report-only; the helper consumes focus facts supplied by an app or shell instead of creating a competing focus manager.
\item
  The first issue set covers foundational focus invariants. Richer trap and dead-island detection remains a follow-up because it needs parent/edge facts that are not part of this slice.
\item
  Ordering is deterministic: tab index first, then node id.
\end{itemize}

\section{Playback}\label{record-194-playback}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} returns ordered nodes, focused node ids, and structured issues for missing focus, multiple focused nodes, focused-disabled nodes, and duplicate tab indexes.
\item
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} renders owner, role, rect, tab order, focusable, focused, and disabled state, with focused node rows prefixed by \texttt{*}.
\item
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})} renders the same report as a bounded \texttt{S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}.
\item
  \texttt{@\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i} exports the focus map API from its source barrel.
\end{itemize}

\section{Retrospective}\label{record-194-retrospective}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  This pairs cleanly with the layout and input-routing inspectors: layout shows where regions are, input routing shows how events moved, and the focus map shows who currently owns focus.
\item
  App-provided focus facts are the right boundary for the first slice. Inferring focus from rendered text would create brittle diagnostics and hide the runtime truth the helper is meant to expose.
\end{itemize}

\section{Backlog Context}\label{record-195-backlog-context}

The 2026-04-14 audit pass found that Bijou's terminal-safety story is still split across several public text entry points.

\section{Problem}\label{record-195-problem}

The plain-text bridges sanitize control sequences before they reach terminal output, but several public surface-native helpers still accept raw strings and write them directly into cells or OSC sequences.

Current evidence: - \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} - \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} - \texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}

That means an app can appear ``safe'' because some paths sanitize terminal text while other paths still allow destructive control bytes to survive into interactive/static output.

\section{Desired outcome}\label{record-195-desired-outcome}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Define one shared trusted/untrusted text boundary for public text-bearing APIs.
\item
  Route \texttt{b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, surface-text helpers, \texttt{h\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{})}, and transitive callers through that boundary.
\item
  Add regression coverage for CSI, OSC, DCS, BEL, and mixed escape payloads.
\item
  Document when callers should use plain text, trusted styled text, or explicit ANSI parsing.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Why ASAP}\label{record-195-why-asap}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  This is the single most important remaining ship-readiness risk from the 2026-04-14 audit.
\item
  The repo is otherwise release-green, which makes this a high-leverage hardening task instead of speculative cleanup.
\end{itemize}

\section{Hill}\label{record-195-hill-1}

Every public text-bearing helper passes through one auditable terminal-safety contract before it becomes cells or terminal control output.

\chapter{Design Records}\label{record-196}

\noindent{\footnotesize\color{BookMuted}\path{docs/design/README.md}\par}\smallskip

This directory preserves technical decisions and implementation evidence. Current scope and release order live in GitHub issues and milestones; Linear is the chosen execution tracker, pending connection and workspace/team selection.

Write a design record when a change needs a durable technical decision. Name the problem, scope, non-goals, observable contract, acceptance checks, prerequisites, and validation plan. Link the work item and PR. Update the record with actual results when the change lands.

Existing cycle identifiers and templates preserve historical provenance. New work does not require METHOD ceremonies, sponsor fields, a cycle branch name, or an advance shaping commit. Keep existing filenames stable for linked evidence.

The complete design corpus is also available as the \href{https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/blob/1853ad90/docs/book/README.md}{Design Book}, with LaTeX source, a PDF edition, TikZ diagrams, and actual DOGFOOD cell specimens.
